1031833: Industrial waste from the cosmos—metallic slag asteroids are the leftover cores of shattered worlds. 1031835: Pure metallic ingots drifting through space, these asteroids are nature's own refined metal bars. Ingot asteroids are a common source of Iridosmine Nodules.
1031837: Primitive water-bearers from stellar formation, these comet-like asteroids hold preserved secrets in their hydrated sulfide cores. 1031839: Delicate spheres of frozen volatiles, dewdrop asteroids glisten with crystalline methane ice preserved at near-absolute-zero temperatures. 1031841: Still glowing with primordial organic heat, ember asteroids contain pristine kerogen—complex carbon polymers that have remained unaltered since formation. These dark, coal-like bodies hold valuable chemical building blocks. Ember asteroids are a common source of Primitive Kerogen Matrix.
1031843: Shimmering with rainbow-like iridescence, glint asteroids sparkle with veins of complex aromatic hydrocarbons. 1031845: Dark as coal dust and deeply primordial, soot asteroids are coated in prebiotic tholin nodules—tar-like organic compounds formed through radiation chemistry. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} recently sacked one of its employees after a routine inspection revealed a large amount of indecent pictures stored in his personal database.  Sadly, this ex-employee wasn't all too pleased with our 
decision, and has resorted to camping outside of our headquarters and harassing our customers.  Fortunately though, we dug up some old offenses this guy made and revealed them to the authorities, who promptly lowered his security rating quite a bit.  In effect, he's fair game.  Please warp over to the location on the bookmark I'm about to give you and squash this little pest.  I doubt he will survive for long, as some of our customers are 
heavily armed.  So hurry up and take him out if you want your reward.

We've been gathering information from our agents within the Cartel to prepare ourselves for a possible attack on our assets. So far, we've found out only that they are planning a major offensive against a target within {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, possibly to occur today. While the target remains unknown to us, we've managed to discover the meeting point of some of their forces. I want you to gather whatever help you can muster, fly out to the meeting points, and deliver a devastating blow to their fleet. That should deter them from any attack inside {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and send them a message they won't soon forget.

Just don't forget what you're up against. We have no idea how many ships are out there ― all we know is where five of their rendezvous points are. Destroy any and all targets you can find there, then report back to me. If there're too many of them out there, then get some help; I'm sure some of our other agents in the vicinity would be willing to give you a hand.

A CONCORD scout drone was just spotted in this system by one of our men. As usual, these drones should always be eliminated before they cause any damage. I'm not sure why this lone drone has entered our territory. Might just be an accident, or maybe it's on some secret mission.

Either way, I'd like you to head out there and get rid of it before it manages to escape. Leave no trace of it behind. Don't be long!
127560:
Today is a sad day, {[character]player.name}. One of our freelancers, working on a simple reconnaissance job in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, was brutally murdered by Guristas thugs while on duty. He was well liked in {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, and we will miss his loyal service to us greatly.

Now, you might be thinking, "How does this affect me?" Well I'll tell you. We aren't letting this outrage go unpunished. I want the people behind this brutal murder taken care of immediately. I will supply you with a bookmark to their hideout, which is heavily guarded by Guristas fighters. Head out there and avenge your colleague by destroying their habitation module; it's the primary residence of their leaders. Leave no pirate survivors behind.

Oh, and one other thing: They have an asteroid colony out there which is used to house their workers, miners, and such. I suggest you leave them in one piece, for we have no quarrel with them. We'll send a personnel transport to pick them up shortly after you return, as long as you have eliminated all of the pirates.

The convoy that was destroyed was carrying a very valuable artifact which must be retrieved at all cost. It is sealed in a booby-trapped special delivery package. I require you to head out there and look for it, if fortune shines on us today then the attacker and our artifact will still be close by. From there they have been launching attacks on our convoys and outposts nearby, some of which have been totally overrun. I request that you fly to the station ruins and eliminate their hive.

Rogue drones are a constant menace to our assets. They have no allegiance to any nation that we know of and their only purpose seems to be expansion and destruction of anything in their path. Once they have started infesting a system, it is very hard to exterminate the infestation for good. But it is possible to reduce the threat they pose by destroying their hives, fortunately.

As you well know, {[character]player.name}, we have an unfortunate amount of illegal Angel Cartel activity in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Well I believe we have found a target that will cripple their operations here for quite some time.

After countless hours of investigation, our agents have finally discovered their primary armory facility. This is a storage facility for their ship modules and weaponry for ground troops, and would explain how quickly their lost equipment is replaced in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

We believe that if we strike hard and fast, and take out this armory before they know what hit 'em, then we stand a good chance of seriously damaging their supply of spare weaponry, which will greatly impede their operations in this sector. Of course you are the pilot that I feel is most suited for this job, {[character]player.name}. Just remember, we get one shot at this. If you fail, they will undoubtedly relocate their armory and be far more prepared for us next time. So don't screw this one up!
127637:
We've been wondering for some time now why the Guristas strikes on our convoys have been so well timed and coordinated, considering our people usually take the utmost caution when it comes to security and secrecy. But I think we've found the answer.

Some time ago our surveillance team stumbled across a hidden Guristas base located in a deadspace pocket not far from here. We didn't think much of it at first ... until we actually sent in one of our undercover agents to investigate. He did not return with his life, but we did manage to salvage his report from the wreckage of his ship. And from what he discovered, the area is being used to cover up a gigantic telescope, which the Guristas are apparently using to spy on our assets here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. This telescope is so powerful that it's illegal to use in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space without a permit, and those are hard to come by. The interference from the deadspace pocket hides it from our scanners, but it is still able to scan everything outside. An ingenious method of espionage, don't you think?

Your task is simple. Since we've located the base already, all we require you to do is warp over there and destroy it. But although it may sound simple, you should expect heavy resistance. They wouldn't leave such vital equipment lightly guarded. Good luck, {[character]player.name}.
127638:
I just received news of a grave incident that occurred in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} a few hours ago. A convoy carrying our esteemed CEO was ambushed by an unusually large and organized pirate strike force. But fortune shone on us tonight, for due to the extraordinary bravery of our CEO's valiant escort team, he managed to escape unharmed, although slightly traumatised as you might expect. We lost many good men in this unfortunate incident, including the commander of our escort team ... may he rest in peace.

Now, I'll get right to the point. We believe the pirates managed to capture some of the crew of the cruiser that was escorting our CEO, for we found the wreckage of their ship close by the encounter location, but there was no trace of the bodies of most of the crew. {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} special forces have been called in and are scouring the area for any sign left behind by the pirates, who so far remain at large. We'd like you to help out in the investigation. We know of a popular pirate hideout in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. I´ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom: Please search the area for any clues, and if you take any prisoners, bring them back for interrogation.

127640: So what's this important stuff you keep yammering about?
127641: I will do my best, you can count on that.
127642: Good!  I'm sure we can count on you.
127643:
Well done, {[character]player.name}. I see that, since you managed to bring back the missing crew members, my theory was correct. After we've given them proper trauma counseling, we'll ask them about any leads they may have stumbled upon during their time in captivity.

And don't you leave just yet. I have another assignment waiting for you!
127644: Well, it is better to know up front that you are not up to the challenge.  Perhaps the next recruit will have the intestinal fortitude that we require.
127645: Did you really think a sissy like me could handle something like this?  Please.
127646: I am very disappointed.  And you came so highly recommended, too.
127647: Good, I knew I could count on you.  But just one other thing, I have a feeling that these mercs will fight for their leader, to the death.  Be prepared for a grueling fight.  If you fail, we might not get another chance at this, so do your very best.  That is all I expect of you, friend of {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle}.
127648:
I've heard good things about you, {[character]player.name}. They say you are a loyal servant of {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle}, and that you have served us well in the past. I hope that my information is correct, for our sake ... and for yours.

The reason I sent for you is simple, we have visitors, and we need someone to give them a 'warm' welcome. These particular visitors are up to something, but we don't know what yet. And that's where you come in.

Bring us their leader. We need him for interrogation ... and to discover the meaning behind their activities here. Your job is a simple one, and I expect the one we seek here in no less than a day.

They are hauled up in an asteroid belt not far from here, incidently in a deadspace pocket which is blocking our long-range scanners. I will supply you to a bookmark to the acceleration gate leading into it.
127649: Good work, {[character]player.name}, you have served us well as always.  We will begin the interrogation of our prisoner immediately.  I also presume you left the structure they were building intact, we'd like to investigate it.  Whatever they were building out there, it would almost certainly become a threat to our assets in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127650:
While we are interrogating the prisoner you captured, I'd like you to clear up the remnants of the merc forces you defeated in your last mission. I want you to enter the deadspace pocket from a different angle this time, using the other acceleration gate leading into it should put you right next to their base. It's a jumble of structures inside small asteroids connected to each other, which we call an asteroid colony. Destroy it and report back to me.

I'm sure the mercenaries still have a few ships left at their disposal, so be prepared for a fight. Their remaining forces, crippled from your last strike at them, should not cause you any serious problems.

127652:
We've finally finished with the interrogation of the prisoner you captured in a previous mission, and our suspicions were confirmed. It took some ... convincing, to extract the information we needed from the poor, misguided soul. Which is quite ordinary, considering him being an undercover operative of the Amarr Empire. And a high ranking one at that.

Now you might ask, how could we possibly know that he is high ranking? After all, the Empire is very thorough when it comes to purging all records of the people who join their intelligence agency, to keep it from falling into the 'wrong' hands. Agents such as these tend to 'vanish', as if they had never existed. Quite difficult to track down, I tell you.

But when a large group of Amarrian cruisers appears at our doorstep, demanding the release of a certain individual ... well it's not hard to put 2 and 2 together.

This small fleet of imperial ships was spotted entering the same deadspace pocket which we sent you into on your two previous missions. They are here to investigate the disappearance of their agent, and are most likely ready for a fight. And I expect you to make sure they leave our space, feet first.

We also have reason to believe that they have control over a small outpost inside the asteroid belt. On your last two trips there we gave you bookmarks to two acceleration gates into the vast deadspace area our enemy has been hiding in. Well there is a 3rd gate which we just recently discovered, and we suspect the imperial raid force is located in there, planning their next move. Our sources tell us that their leader brought with him documents detailing their orders from the Empress. We would very much like to get our hands on these documents. Destroy their ships if you can, but your primary objective is to retrieve the reports from their leader. They might be located with him on his ship, or inside their base. Find them and bring them to me, this will be your final assignment for a while.
127653: I have the reports you asked for, and I have taken care of the imperial scum.  Now I expect my reward.
127654: Excellent, {[character]player.name}.  Your success will not go unnoticed within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle}.

127656:
I have some grave news, {[character]player.name}. A squadron of imperial ships just managed to lay waste to one of our supply depots in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. This was a hit and run attack, aimed at our drug smuggling business into the Amarr territories. I can understand their attacks inside their own sovereign space, but this cowardly act must not go unpunished.

The squadron is still located in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We managed to block off all exits leading out of the system, and our ships are just waiting for the order to attack. I want you to personally deal with them, {[character]player.name}, and save us from possible casualties. Do this and you shall be well rewarded.

127664:
I need you for a simple courier mission, {[character]player.name}, as well as another job afterwards. It's fairly straight forward, nothing you wouldn't be able to handle.

Recently we acquired a heap load of sensitive Gallente Federation logs, which we want transferred to this station a.s.a.p.. We've made a deal with their government to return this data over to them, without breaking the seal covering the container which they came in, in exchange for a few million LUX. Now all we need is you to bring the stuff here, and then meet their agents at a rendezvous point for the payment.

Meet them there and retrieve the payment they promised us, then report back to me.  If they try anything funny, then you have my permission to defend yourself.

127668:
The Gallente attacked you on sight? Interesting ... I expected as much, they have not been known to deal with us when their back is against the wall, so to speak. Well we have other uses for these logs anyway, blackmailing their citizens will fetch us a much better price.

You've done your job, take your reward and enjoy yourself.
127669:
I call upon you, {[character]player.name}, for an important task that I need accomplished. We have had numerous cases recently of rogue Minmatar miners exploiting our natural resources in the area. Our gangs have made sure most of them left our space feet first, but there is this one group of them that has caused us great pains. They have apparently brought with them a small group of highly skilled Minmatar Fleet pilots, who apparently will defend them with their lives. We can't afford to lose any more of our ships, so I ask you to do us a favor and eliminate the escort ships guarding the miners.

Once you have eliminated the Fleet vessels, my boys will come in and clean up the rest of the mess. Your objective is not to destroy the miners, but I won't hold it against you if you do.

127671:
I have some bad news, {[character]player.name}. The Republic wasn't all too pleased with our attack on the last batch of miners they sent here, which you took part in. Apparently they sent in some reinforcements to the area, to stage a counter-offensive. They must have been deployed nearby already, as it took them a very short time to get here.

I require you to take care of them. We can't afford to lose more ships in these never-ending skirmishes with their forces. Our lines are already thinning from constant battles with freelancers intent on exploiting our valuable resources.

Once you have eliminated the threat they pose, return to me for your reward.

127673: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}.  You've done us a great service by taking care of this business.  This won't be forgotten.
127674:
I have a very important and risky assignment for you, {[character]player.name}. Considering your reputation, I'm sure you can handle it.

A few weeks ago, we discovered that the Caldari State was up to something big inside {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, but we didn't know what. Even the officers we have on our payroll among their navy didn't know what was going on. Then, just recently, one of our patrols stumbled upon an encoded signal coming from an area inside {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We traced the signal and sent a squadron of our best men to investigate, but we soon lost Comlink contact with them; they never came back.

We're almost positive that the State is building a massive military base where that signal came from, probably from where they intend on launching a major offensive against our positions here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. Now, I'd say we have the travel routes through the systems in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} covered pretty well, so this expedition of theirs must be costing them a fortune. If we strike hard and fast before they manage to complete the project, we might be able to convince them that such a foolhardy operation is not in their best interests.

But I'd like to reassure you of one thing, {[character]player.name}. I have no intention of sending you headfirst into the center of their operations ― that would be suicide even for someone with your skills. However, what I'd like you to do is take care of a heavily fortified outpost located on the outskirts of the territory in which their forces are located. They have a number of these outposts guarding their territory, and by removing some of them we hope to open up their defenses enough for us to launch a full-scale attack at their headquarters. Because it's located in the middle of a large deadspace pocket, we haven't been able to do so thus far.

Now, all you have to do is destroy the control tower at the center of the outpost. By doing that, you effectively render the outpost useless, at least till they manage to erect a new tower. By that time, though, our forces will have moved in for the final attack.

Luck be with you, {[character]player.name}.

127676: Excellent work! Our forces are gathering even as we speak in preparation for the final attack. And it's all thanks to your quick work on that control tower.
127677: Just make sure you remember to use all of the acceleration gates leading into the deadspace pocket to reach your target. There will probably be a couple defensive perimeters blocking your way to the control tower, so you will have to get by the Navy ships guarding those areas before you proceed to your target.
127678: After checking our logs, we noticed that only some of the prisoners you brought back were part of the crew that was captured after the pirate raid on our convoy. The rest apparently are former members of one of the pirate ships you destroyed, who managed to escape from the blast that destroyed their vessel. I need them transferred to some colleagues of mine at another station for further interrogation; hopefully the specialists there will be able to extract the information we need to track down who was behind the ambush on our CEO.
127679: I'll do it in no time. Now please update me on how the investigation is going.
127680: Unfortunately we only have a few vague leads at the moment, nothing I can disclose to you at this time.  Get back to me after you have finished your current mission and perhaps I'll have some information for you then.
127681: I won't argue with such logic.  I will find someone else, then.
127682: I cannot accept.  This matter is too important to be entrusted to one such as I.
127683: Great work once again, {[character]player.name}. But I need you back here urgently for another assignment; something terrible just happened. I'll get you posted once you are ready.
127684:
We urgently need help intercepting a group of kidnappers who just managed to snatch the niece of our CEO while she was visiting her uncle in this very system. We believe the perpetrators were a gang of mercenaries led by a felon working for an illegal organization called the Darkonnen. I'll fill you in on the details of that organization in your mission journal.

What I need you to do is capture this agent of theirs, alive if possible. We must have him here for interrogation, for we suspect he is the missing link between the kidnapping and those who are truly responsible for this heinous crime. We need to get to the bottom of which organization stands behind these grave assaults against our people. And it so happens that we know the whereabouts of a certain pirate who has had many dealings with a Darkonnen agent in the past; we hope this pirate will be able to lead you to the agent. The only catch is that he will most likely require a bit of "convincing" on your part before he parts with the needed information. I'll upload the bookmark to his location into your NeoCom; once you have extracted the information from the middleman, I expect you to find the Darkonnen agent and bring him back to me.

127687: Well, I did not say every job would be sunshine and pleasurehalls. Perhaps you are more suited for the garbage-hauling missions?
127688: No, this does not interest me.
127689:
Well done. We will proceed immediately to interrogating the prisoner, so expect some results soon. Our interrogators can be quite ... convincing.

And don't go anywhere: I have another assignment for you.
127691:
So good to see you, {[character]player.name}. I've been on a pretty tight schedule for the past two weeks, ever since we discovered the strange, and increasing, Sansha activity in the system. Our CEO demands an explanation, yet we still don't know enough about the situation to determine what's really going on. And that's where you come in.

Sanshas activity on this scale in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is unheard of, and quite frankly we aren't well enough prepared at the moment to deal with any major conflict with the Nation. Not only that, but those damned zombies give us the creeps, and news of their appearance around here has sent parts of the populace into a state of panic. People are leaving this station already, making my superiors ... less than content if you know what I mean. We're losing good people because of this unacceptable situation and we need to put an end to it.

The first thing I want you to do is undertake a reconnaisance mission for us into an area where we have witnessed most of the Sanshas activity. We've already lost a few patrols that ventured into this area, so be careful. If you do find any Sanshas ships out there, eliminate them. We don't want any prisoners, interrogating the creatures won't do us any good. Report your findings to me a.s.a.p.

127695: Because of your successful reconnaissance mission, we've managed to narrow down the location of the main Sanshas activity a bit. 127698:
After reviewing the intel we received from the spy drones which you transferred for us in your last mission, we managed to pinpoint the location of a military outpost they are building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It appears to be a part of a defensive perimeter that they are setting up around their territory, which has elevated our fears that they have actually managed to erect a large colony inside our solarsystem.

But for now let's keep our sights on the current task, to breach a hole in their defensive wall. We believe that the outpost in question hasn't been fully built, and therefore will be a fairly easy target for you if it's defensive installations aren't complete. Contact with the spy drones was cut off before we could fully analyze the Sansha forces in the area. But one thing's for sure, there will most certainly be guards nearby, and they will have to be dealt with. You will receive a bookmark to the location of the outpost, and your instructions are simple, destroy the habitat of their construction workers. That should slow them down a bit. Good luck.

This leaves us with very few options. But after brainstorming possible solutions to our problem, I came up with a devious plan.

We have in our possession so called 'spy drones', straight from our science labs, which attach themselves to a nearby ships hull and emits a low frequency signal which is picked up by one of our beacons which are strewn around {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, which in turn sends a high frequency signal to our control tower in {[location]agentStationID.name}.

Now we know that an agent of the Sansha's Nation regularly picks up shipments of Ectoplasm at a certain station near here. If we can place the spy drone into his next shipment, this might allow us to track his ship to its destination.

Our men have placed beacons throughout our constellation, so everything is in place. All you need to do is take these crates filled with ectoplasm, and our spy drones, to the station specified in your journal, our agents there will take care of the rest. With luck we'll soon know the location of the Sansha base.

127728:
Our intelligence team has just informed us of new evidence that apparently points to the girl being held in a Blood Raider stronghold in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. According to our information, she is being held in their chapel and is going to be sacrificed in the near future in one of their bloody rituals. We must see that she is returned to her family safely before those despicable Blood Raider fanatics murder her.

There is a fundamental problem, however; the Blood Raiders are fully aware of our intention to free her and have sent in a fleet of their battleships to guard their outpost. Now, I certainly do not expect you to fight against such odds, but I firmly believe you capable of infiltrating their base, rescuing the girl, and escaping with your ship intact.

We have located a series of acceleration gates leading straight to the chapel. Once you arrive at the final room, all you have to do is destroy the chapel and retrieve the girl from the ejected safety capsule. (All of their chapels have this mechanism in place to save their priests from death should the structure be obliterated.) If we send in a fleet of ships, the Blood Raiders will simply kill her as soon as they realize they have lost. We need to hit them fast and hard, with a small force, before they know what hit them. That is the only chance we have of getting her out of there alive.

Now, if you do not find the girl alive after destroying the chapel, then active your warp drive immediately and get out of there! I wouldn't want to lose you needlessly, {[character]player.name}. But rest assured, should you fall, then I will personally make sure the Raider scum pay the price. Good luck.

127733:
Nice work. This victory of yours will undoubtedly be a serious blow to the Blood Raider leader responsible for the outpost's defenses. I'm sure he will be sacrificed in one of their rituals as punishment ― ha! A fitting end to one of those bloodthirsty maniacs.

I am also very pleased to inform you that our CEO's niece is now in our custody. We found her alive and well in a capsule floating around this very station. Apparently they drugged her, and she remembers hardly anything since her capture. But I can't help but wonder at how fortunately this all ended ... I have a nagging suspicion that someone else was behind all of this and played us like fools.

But enough of this, let us rejoice at a job well done. Our CEO sends his utmost gratitude, as well as a special bonus reward from his own coffers, which he hopes you will enjoy.
127734:
I just received news of a grave incident that occurred in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} a few hours ago. A convoy carrying our esteemed CEO was ambushed by an unusually large and organized pirate strike force. But fortune shone on us tonight, for due to the extraordinary bravery of our CEO's valiant escort team, he managed to escape unharmed, although slightly traumatised as you might expect. We lost many good men in this unfortunate incident, including the commander of our escort team ... may he rest in peace.

Now, I'll get right to the point. We believe the pirates managed to capture some of the crew of the cruiser that was escorting our CEO, for we found the wreckage of their ship close by the encounter location, but there was no trace of the bodies of most of the crew. {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} special forces have been called in and are scouring the area for any sign left behind by the pirates, who so far remain at large. We'd like you to help out in the investigation. We know of a popular pirate hideout in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. I´ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom: Please search the area for any clues, and if you take any prisoners, bring them back for interrogation.

I need them transferred to some colleagues of mine at another station for further interrogation; hopefully the specialists there will be able to extract the information we need to track down who was behind the ambush on our CEO.

127749:
We urgently need help intercepting a group of kidnappers who just managed to snatch the granddaughter of our CEO while she was visiting him in this very system. We believe the perpetrators were a gang of mercenaries led by a felon working for an illegal organization calling themeselves the "Komni Corporation."

What I need you to do is capture this agent of theirs, alive if possible. We must have him here for interrogation, for we suspect he is the missing link between the kidnapping and those who are truly responsible for this heinous crime. We need to get to the bottom of which organization stands behind these grave assaults against our people. And it so happens that we know the whereabouts of a certain pirate who has had many dealings with this Komni agent in the past; we hope this pirate will be able to lead you to the agent. The only catch is that he will most likely require a bit of "convincing" on your part before he parts with the needed information. I'll upload the bookmark to his location into your NeoCom; once you have extracted the information from the middleman, I expect you to find the Komni agent and bring him back to me.

127782:
Our intelligence team has just informed us of new evidence that apparently points to the girl being held in a Guristas stronghold in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. According to our information, she is being held in their central control tower, to be executed if their demands are not met. We must see that she is returned to her family safely before those lunatics murder her.

There is a problem, however; the Guristas are fully aware of our intention to free her and have sent in a fleet of their battleships to guard their outpost. Now, I certainly do not expect you to fight against such odds, but I firmly believe you capable of infiltrating their base, rescuing the girl, and escaping with your ship intact.

We have located a series of acceleration gates leading straight to the chapel. Once you arrive at the final room, all you have to do is destroy the control tower and retrieve the girl from the ejected safety capsule. (All of their towers have this mechanism in place to save their ranking officers from death should the structure be obliterated.) If we send in a fleet of ships, the Guristas will simply kill her as soon as they realize they have lost. We need to hit them fast and hard, with a small force, before they know what hit them. That is the only chance we have of getting her out of there alive.

Now, if you do not find the girl alive after destroying the tower, then active your warp drive immediately and get out of there! I wouldn't want to lose you needlessly, {[character]player.name}. But rest assured, should you fall, then I will personally make sure those dirtbags pay the price. Good luck.

127807:
I just received news of a very grave incident that just occured in the system {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} a few hours ago. A convoy carrying our esteemed CEO was ambushed by an unusually large and organized pirate strike force. But fortune shone on us tonight, for due to the extraordinary bravery of our CEO's valiant escort team, he managed to escape unharmed, although slightly traumatised as you might expect. We lost many good men in this unfortunate incident, including the commander of our escort team ... may he rest in peace.

Now I'll get right to the point. We believe the pirates managed to capture some of the crew of the cruiser which was escorting our CEO, as we found the wreckage of their ship close by the encounter location, lacking the bodies of most of the crew. {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} special forces have been called in and are scouring the area for any traces left behind by the pirates, which so far remain at large. We'd like you to help out in the investigation. We know of a popular pirate hideout in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}, please search the area for any clues which might help us, and bring any prisoners you manage to acquire back to us for interrogation.

Apparently he had been contacted by an agent from the Odamian Renegades, a criminal organization which has been making quite a name for itself recently in these parts, and paid a vast sum of money to kidnap our CEO's niece. A foolhardy task, but he did manage to pull it off and transfer her into the hands of the criminals.

Also the data disc you transported in your last mission has revealed even more to us. It contained the precise meeting points between the kidnappers and the Odamian agent for the past few weeks, as well as the exact coordinates for the next meeting which is to take place any minute now. I'd like you to fly over there yourself and ambush the Odamian goons at that location. Try to be quick, I don't know how long they will stay there waiting for their contact to arrive.

127830:
Our intelligence team has just informed us of fresh new evidence, which apparently points to the girl being held in a Serpentis stronghold in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. According to our sources she is being held in the Central Hub structure of the base, where she will be executed if their demands aren't met. It is our civic duty to see to it that she is returned to her family safely before those despicable Serpentis villains murder her.

There is a fundamental flaw with our plan however, the Serpentis are fully aware of our intention to free her and have sent in a fleet of their battleships to guard their outpost. Now I certainly do not expect you to fight against such odds, but I firmly believe you capable of infiltrating their base, rescuing the girl and escaping with your ship, and life, intact.

We have located a series of acceleration gates leading straight to the Central Control Hub. The Serpentis fleet guarding it will be expecting a large force of attackers, which will give you the advantage should you fly in there with a fast, agile ship, to avoid direct confrontation. Once you arrive at the final area, all you have to do is destroy the Central Control Hub and retrieve the girl from the ejected safety capsule, all of their Control Hubs have this mechanism to save their high-ranking personnel from death should the structure be obliterated. We hope that they consider the girl important enough to save in this way as well. If not ... well there is not much other choice. If we send in a fleet of ships they will simply kill her when they realize they have lost. We need to hit them fast and hard, before they know what hit them. That is the only chance we have of getting her out of there alive.

Now, if you do not find the girl alive after destroying the Central Control Hub, then active your warp drive immediately and get out of there! I wouldn't want to lose you needlessly, {[character]player.name}. But rest assured, should you fall then I will personally make sure the pirate scum pay the price. Good luck.

127835:
Nice work. This will undoubtedly be a serious blow to the Serpentis leader responsible for the outpost's defenses. I'm sure he will be severely punished by Sarpati for failing in his duties.

127836:
We need urgent help with intercepting a group of vile kidnappers who just managed to snatch the niece of our CEO while she was visiting her uncle in this very system. We believe the perpetrators were a gang of mercenaries led by a felon working for the illegal organization, the Odamian Renegades. I'll fill you in on the details of that organization in your mission journal.

What I need you to do is capture this agent of theirs, alive if possible. We must have him here for interrogation, as we suspect he is the missing link between the kidnapping and those who are truly responsible for this heinous crime. We need to get to the bottom of which organization stands behind these grave assaults against our people. And it so happens that we know the whereabouts of a certain pirate who has had many dealings with this Odamian agent in the past, who we hope will be able to lead you to him. The only catch is he will most likely require a bit of 'convincing' on your part before he parts with the needed information. I'll upload the bookmark to his location into your NeoCom, once you have extracted the information from the middleman then I expect you to find the Odamian agent and bring him back to me.

127842: The Odamian Renegades named themselves after the system where their organization was founded, in the Gallente controlled Placid region.  The founders themselves were mostly made up of adventurers traveling from the Gallente capital system, Luminaire, searching for fame and fortune in the frontier.  There they came into contact with Dakeur Hullan, a charismatic pirate veteran who had been working for the Serpentis organization until an unfortunate incident saw him outlawed from their territory, with a sizeable bounty on his head.  Despite his misfortunes, Dakeur still had numerous contacts throughout the criminal world, both inside Serpentis and Gallente controlled space.  With Dakeurs experience within the underworld of the Gallente Federation and his co-founders surprising piloting skills, the Odamian Renegades quickly garnered a reputation as a powerful and infamous drug smuggling syndicate within the Gallente territories.

I need them transfered to some colleagues of mine at another station for further interrogation, hopefully the specialists there will be able to extract out of them the information we need to track down who was behind the ambush on our CEO.
127855: I'll do it in no time.  Now please keep me updated on how the investigation is going.

127860:
Okay, we have a situation here. A serious situation. A week ago, we detected a small Amarrian presence right next to the ruins of an old military station. Since then, they have been expanding in numbers; yesterday we found out that they have built an outpost. We believe they are trying to retrieve something from the station, something they could use against us.

Go, destroy the outpost and the ships protecting it. You will be well rewarded, I assure you.
127861: The outpost is destroyed and the infidels eliminated. You mentioned a reward?
127862: This mission is damn near impossible! I can't do it.
127863: Very well, then, pilot. I'll give this to somebody more competent.
127864:
I just received news of a grave incident that occurred in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} a few hours ago. A convoy carrying our esteemed CEO was ambushed by an unusually large and organized pirate strike force. But fortune shone on us tonight, for due to the extraordinary bravery of our CEO's valiant escort team, he managed to escape unharmed, although slightly traumatised as you might expect. We lost many good men in this unfortunate incident, including the commander of our escort team ... may he rest in peace.

Now, I'll get right to the point. We believe the pirates managed to capture some of the crew of the cruiser that was escorting our CEO, for we found the wreckage of their ship close by the encounter location, but there was no trace of the bodies of most of the crew. {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} special forces have been called in and are scouring the area for any sign left behind by the pirates, who so far remain at large. We'd like you to help out in the investigation. We know of a popular pirate hideout in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. I´ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom: Please search the area for any clues, and if you take any prisoners, bring them back for interrogation.

127872: I am very disappointed.  And you came so highly recommended, too.

Now we've received a broken distress signal, only moments ago, from one of our civilian convoys traveling to a supply depot in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I fear it has been attacked by these same pirate forces. Please undock immediately and get over there before it's too late! I'll supply you with a bookmark to their exact coordinates. Now hurry!

127877:
Yes, the interrogation went well. We managed to find out who he was working for. Apparently he had been contacted by a Maru Rebel agent and paid a vast sum of money to kidnap our CEO's daughter. A foolhardy task, but he did manage to pull it off and transfer her into the hands of the criminals.

Also, the data disc you transported in your last mission has revealed even more to us. It contained the precise meeting points between the kidnappers and the Maru agent for the past few weeks, as well as the exact coordinates for the next meeting, which is to take place very soon now. I'd like you to fly over there yourself and ambush the Rebel goons at that location. Be quick: I don't know how long they will wait for their contact to arrive.

Good work. I'm surprised, however, that you didn't find any survivors in the wreckage. Pirates usually don't fight to the death unless something big is at stake.

Oh, hey, don't you take off just yet. If you're willing, I have another assignment for you.
127884: As I've already mentioned, while we were scrambling to defend our convoys from those Sansha's Nation pilots, a few of their assault troopers broke into our prison module and managed to escape with your prisoners. Our interrogation was not complete and we still don't know where their base is located, so we must get them back. We know where their ships are headed, though, and we need you to intercept them before they manage to jump out of this system. This might be our last chance of getting them before they vanish into deep space, so please hurry!

127887:
Our intelligence team has just informed us of new evidence that apparently points to our CEO's daughter being held in a Sansha stronghold in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. According to our information, she is being held in the base's Central Communication Tower; they will execute her if their leaders' demands aren't met. We must see that she is returned to her family safely before those mindless zombies murder her.

There is a big problem, however; the Sansha leaders are fully aware of our intention to free her, so they've sent in a fleet of battleships to guard their outpost. Now, I certainly do not expect you to fight against such odds, but I firmly believe you capable of infiltrating their base, rescuing the young woman, and escaping with your ship intact.

We have located a series of acceleration gates leading straight to the Communication Tower. Once you arrive at the final room, all you have to do is destroy the tower and retrieve her from the ejected safety capsule. (All of their towers have this mechanism in place to save their leaders from death should the structure be obliterated.) If we send in a fleet of ships, they will simply kill her as soon as they realize they have lost. We need to hit them fast and hard, with a small force, before they know what hit them. That is the only chance we have of getting her out of there alive.

Now, if you do not find the woman alive after destroying the tower, then active your warp drive immediately and get out of there! I wouldn't want to lose you needlessly, {[character]player.name}. But rest assured, should you fall, then I will personally make sure the Raider scum pay the price. Good luck.

127892:
Nice work. This will undoubtedly be a serious blow to the Sansha leader responsible for the outpost's defenses. I'm sure he will be severely punished by Sansha for failing in his duties. The Communication Tower also serves as a ‘mother-brain' of sorts for a large portion of the Sansha fleet, with it destroyed their forces will be paralyzed for some time to come.

I am also very pleased to inform you that our CEO's niece is now in our custody. We found her alive and well in a capsule floating around this very station. Apparently they drugged her, and she remembers hardly anything since she was captured. But I can't help but wonder at how fortunate this all ended ... I have a nagging suspicion that someone else was behind all of this and played us like fools.

But enough of this, let us rejoice at a job well done. Our CEO sends his utmost gratitude, as well as a special bonus reward from his own coffers which he hopes you will enjoy.
127893:
We urgently need help intercepting a group of kidnappers who just managed to snatch the daughter of our CEO while she was visiting her father in this very system. We believe the perpetrators were a gang of mercenaries led by a felon working for the Maru Rebels. I'll fill you in on the details of that organization in your mission journal.

What I need you to do is capture this agent of theirs, alive if possible. We must have him here for interrogation, for we suspect he is the missing link between the kidnapping and those who are truly responsible for this heinous crime. We need to get to the bottom of which organization stands behind these grave assaults against our people. And it just so happens that we know the whereabouts of a certain pirate who has had many dealings with a Maru agent in the past; we hope he will be able to lead you to the agent. The only catch is that he will most likely require a bit of "convincing" on your part before he parts with the needed information. I'll upload the bookmark to his location into your NeoCom; once you have extracted the information from the middleman, I expect you to find the Maru agent and bring him back to me.

Well done. We will proceed immediately to interrogating the prisoner, so expect some results soon. Our interrogators can be quite ... convincing.

And don't go anywhere: I have another assignment for you.
127899: The Maru Rebels were once part of a gang of pirates who turned into a sinister terrorist network claiming to fight for Minmatar freedom. In fact, they're little more a ruthless gang of criminals dealing in the black market, smuggling, and extortion and blackmail, even sometimes working as hired assassins. Their official agenda is to murder as many citizens of the Amarr nations as possible ― i.e., Amarr Empire, Ammatar, and Khanid Kingdom ― hoping to force them to withdraw eventually from historically Minmatar systems currently under Amarr control. The Minmatar Republic leadership has denounced them as being cutthroats and criminals even though they support Republic goals, and has put up a sizable bounty on their leader's head. But even so, the Rebels do maintain some support within the Minmatar Republic, which has allowed them certain freedoms other criminal networks do not have.

I'm reluctant to send you, since this may be a trap, but I really have no choice. If I send someone else, though, I could be compromising the investigation. So I ask you, please head out to the bookmarked location which was given to me through the anonymous transmission. Be sure to record anything said to you and save it into your ship's database, and then return with it to me.

127917:
I'm happy to announce that we just spotted a transport ship owned by the Archaeological Agency of Caille University not far from a stargate in this system. It is being escorted by some rather menacing Navy ships, and therefore we've been a bit wary to attack it. I'm sure it got lost and took a wrong jump somewhere along its travel route, no sane captain of a civilian transport ship would travel through these parts on purpose.

You probably guessed it but I'd like you to do the dirty work. Fly off to their current location and eliminate the escort. If the transport freighter puts up a fight then destroy it as well, but try to bring back as many of its passengers as you can. These civilian transport ships can be a goldmine for those in the kidnapping / ransom business, if you know what I mean. I'm sure the Gallenteans will pay a handsome amount of LUX for their precious archaeologists, if taken alive.

They seem to be looting the wreckage and creating some sort of modified Megathron battleship. If you could go and eliminate this threat, we will reward you nicely.

127937:
After you delivered the data chip in your last mission, I've been flooded with reports of Gallente Navy sightings in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. A number of our gangs have been wiped out, and it's not considered safe anymore for a pirate to venture too far out into space in these parts. I'm positive that this new offensive is the direct result of the data chip we sent falling into the hands of the Navy generals. They know what we're up to and it's only a matter of time before the Gallente media get a hold of the story.

I didn't expect the Navy to venture this close to our station, after all we've threatened to kill the prisoners. But they seem intent on keeping their distance, this is just a ploy of theirs to frighten us. But by disrupting our trade routes and ambushing our patrols in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, all they accomplish is raising the price on our demands.

I want you to head out into the outer reaches of this system and eliminate 4 Navy groups. After we have given them the taste of defeat, then it will be time to deliver our new demands. Off you go.

We can't let them start building that outpost!  I want you to personally see to it that their convoy and all of the ships defending the area are destroyed immediately.
127945: Consider the building preparations for that outpost officially terminated.
127946: Your last strike against the Navy forces in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} sent them into a disarray.  That should keep them in check for a day or two.  Meanwhile, I'd like you to bring our new demands to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  This time they better comply, or we might just go through with all of our threats.  We've already decapitated one of the prisoners, which we believe to be a personal aid of Karzath.  The footage has been compiled into the data disk along with our demands.

127950: Nice job mate.  Now let's keep our fingers crossed and hope those bastards cave in to our threats.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127951: I'm glad you're back {[character]player.name}.  The Gallente Navy have gone mad!  They've sent an entire fleet of ships to attack this station.  They must be utterly insane, if even one of them steps foot in here the prisoners heads will roll!  I need you to undock at once and meet the Navy head on before they get within firing range of the station, bring everyone you can, I suspect you'll need all the help you can get.  You'll be supplied with a bookmark of course, now get moving!

I have personally ordered the execution of all of the prisoners save our prized possession, Karzath Pinazi.  The picture of the beheadings will be sent straight to the Gallente media.  This should teach them a lesson.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127954:
Rejoice, {[character]player.name}, the Federation have finally caved in. They have vowed to meet our demands once the prisoner and his cargo have been transferred safely to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, where their agents will pick it up. Ironically enough, we have no idea what cargo they were jammering about, everything that was on board the cargo ship containing the archeologists you captured originally was destroyed along with the ship. No wonder they were so adamant at retrieving whatever it was they were after. Karzath Nuoki was only a smokescreen, whatever he was transporting towards Gallente space was extremely valuable. It's unfortunate we will never find out what it was, as I'm sure you never saw anything suspicious in the wreckage of the cargo ship other than the stranded archeologists ... but just to be on the safe side, I had some of my men search your hangar just in case you have been less than honest with us. No hard feelings I hope.

And as you probably guessed, I want you to do the honors of transporting the prisoner to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, where our agents will hand him along with a cargo container filled with various junk to our Gallente 'friends'. Once this final assignment has been completed, I ... err we will be able to enjoy the fruits of our hard work. In other words, I'll be rich!

The piece of Neophite that I received in exchange for the prisoner will fetch me an absurd price on the black market.  And the look on the faces of the Gallente agents who picked him up, after they rummaged through the cargo container ... simply priceless!
127957: The Republic needs you! Communications have been down all day, I need you to go and get me today's status reports, I have a feeling something big is going to happen today.
127958: The Republic needs you! Communications have been down all day, I need you to go and get me today's status reports, I have a feeling something big is going to happen today.
127961: I'm sorry, it's too hard, I can't do it.
127962: Those reports you just delivered to me were of great importance, it seems as though the Amarrians have made a huge mistake and want us to correct it for them. Before I can tell you more I need you to pass this info on to a nearby agent.
127963:
Those messages you delivered were essential, thank you. The Amarrians screwed up and want us to clean up their mess, what a day.

One of their generals has gone crazy. He ignored orders, broke communications with his commanding officers and then disappeared into thin air. They believe he might be heading our way, apparently he thinks an all-out war has started and wants to be a part of it. Anyway I'll have someone take care of the rest, thank you.
127964: I want nothing to do with this.
127965: Any more news on the Amarr troubles?
127966: I will give this to somebody more competent.
127967: I'll fetch that data chip for you in no time.
127968: Seems like those Amarrians you took out were just scouts, we're not quite sure where this fugitive is hiding. What we do know is the presence of another similar nearby scout outpost. Perhaps if you went there you could get some information out of them as to the whereabouts of our target. We need to find him as soon as possible, before he is able to strike.
127969: You disappoint both me and the Republic, shame on you.
127971: I am proud of you, nice work.
127973: I can't do it, it's too hard!
127974: I don't care, give me something else.
127975:
I've got a lucrative mission for you this time, {[character]player.name}. I need a convoy taken out and looted in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Sounds rather standard, but before you go running off I'd like to explain the situation a bit.

There is a merchant corporation near here, which is basically a small offshoot of the Caldari mega-corporation Sukuuvestaa, who own the vast majority of it's shares. These Sukuuvestaa merchants like to transport all sorts of goods throughout the {[location]agentRegionID.name} region, and regularly pay tribute to us for protection. But sadly sometimes their cargo is simply too enticing.

This convoy is loaded with Caldari consumer electronics, and only guarded with the standard Sukuuvestaa hired mercenary ships, as the Caldari Navy do not frequent these parts. You can't imagine how eager some of the people in these parts are at getting these things. And the price they are willing to pay ... well, it's something that we simply can't pass up so easily. For that reason I want the convoy destroyed and looted, and make sure you are discreet. I don't want any witnesses at the scene to survive, nor any equipment that might record what transpired. As long as the Caldari do not know who attacked their ships, the most they will probably do is send more combat ships with the next convoy.

Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Because of the success in your previous mission, my superiors have one extra task for you. The Sukuuvestaa seem to be completely oblivious as to who attacked their last convoy through this area, and have accepted their loss as merely a freak occurrence. A most fortunate turn of events for us, but there is just one more target that we simply cannot let pass through our grasp. Our cargo scanners in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} spotted some extremely expensive material in one of the latest Sukuuvestaa convoys traveling through {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. We simply must get our hands on that Neophyte, I don't care how many ships it takes. Just do it.

I'll supply you with a bookmark to the current location of the convoy. It seems to have stopped in a deadspace area in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}, perhaps for repairs. Strike it hard and fast with everything you got, and bring me that Neophyte! Don't bother showing your face back here before the task is complete!

This piece of Neophyte will fetch us a fortune! And of course we have you, {[character]player.name}, to deal with any Caldari Navy threat that might materialize as a result. And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127980:
Now that we have the Neophyte, I need it transported to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Don't ask why, just do it.

Watch out for any Navy vessels on the way. Now that they know who was behind the latest heist, they're bound to be on the lookout for any ship loyal to {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle}.
127981:
I have an urgent task for you this time, {[character]player.name}. The Caldari Navy have started a campaign of revenge attacks on our assets here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. They don't have the manpower to launch a full scale assault on us, but they do have various agents here and there setting up booby traps for our ships. This escapade is becoming a tad expensive, so we need to do something before it gets out of hand.

The first thing I want you to do is fly to one of our supply depots in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Caldari have set up a trap there for any incoming ships, which has already cost us a fortune. Destroy the Caldari forces manning the guns, then report back to me. And stay away from our supply depot, they don't take kindly to un-invited visitors, ally or not.

127984:
The Caldari Navy continue to harass us. They are famous for overreacting when it comes to minor incidents involving their fellow corporations. But I'm confident this will die down after you have completed your next mission.

The Caldari have sent a high profile agent of theirs, Whelan Machorin into {[location]agentConstellationID.name} to conduct a campaign of terror against our people. He must be stopped, at all costs. Kill him and bring me his head, which I will have stuck on a stake for all our men to view at their pleasure.

127986:
From data we've collected, the Caldari Navy forces have set up some kind of constellation scanner in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name} to monitor our activities in preparation for a sneak attack. We believe this is what has allowed them to use their small force in these areas so effectively. This also allows them to more effectively monitor the movements of the Caldari convoys flying through here and respond faster to any attacks.

I want you to destroy this high-tech telescope of theirs. It will be heavily guarded, so this is no small task for even you, {[character]player.name}. Once you have completed your mission, we will have dealt a devastating blow to the Caldari Navy plans in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, which I doubt they will recover from anytime soon.

127988:
We have a problem, for the past few weeks the Blood Raiders have been growing increasingly aggressive. They seem to have set up a small base nearby and every few days our convoys, miners and even military personel get attacked. This structure also serves as sacrifical grounds for the Covenant and they believe it to be holy, hence extremely tight security.

My superiors told me to find somebody competent to deal with the threat, and that's why I'm asking you. I suggest you find someone to help you with this, as I fear you will not return should you go alone.
127989: Make haste, before they kill even more innocents!
127990: Not a problem, I'll take care of it.
127991: I'm not risking myself for that.
127992:
I have an assignment for you this time that you'll probably enjoy, {[character]player.name}. Some of our fighters recently stumbled upon a rogue settlement in a cluttering of asteroids in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. The settlers are of Minmatar origin, and apparently are here to steal some of our precious arkonor ore. We can't have that, now can we ...

You have been entrusted with the task of eliminating these pests. We know that they have a small militia guarding their fledgling colony, but that should be no trouble for an experienced vet as yourself.

Once you have destroyed the settlement, capture any survivors and bring them to me. They'll fetch us a decent price on the black market, alive or dead.

127994: Hmmph, the prisoners you captured look a bit scrawny to me.  I guess they must have evacuated the old and young first, which seem to be the only ones who survived the destruction of their colony.  We'll have to make due ... but this is a slight disappointment nonetheless.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127995: We have been informed by agents of the Minmatar Republic that they have sent an encoded data disc to {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}, with information that must be transported to our leaders at all cost.  I have personally taken it upon me to investigate this information, and I'd like you to get the disc for me.  A simple task, just don't lose it on your way back, or I'll have your head delivered to me on a silver platter!  Understand?!

127997: Good work.  I'll take a look at the disc's contents immediately.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
127998:
After decyphering the data disc, we learned that the Minmatar Republic have issued a direct threat against us in retaliation for our attack on the colony in a recent mission of yours, {[character]player.name}. They claim there will be dire consequences if we do not hand over the prisoners you captured. Unfortunately I've already had these prisoners executed and either turned into biomass or sold their organs, so we have no option but to decline their request.

Now we have to prepare for their attack. Reports have indicated that 3 Fleet squadrons have entered our territory, probably heading to where they believe the captives are being held. We must prevent them from reaching their destination in full force.

One of our spies alerted us to an old secret military installation in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}, guarded by Minmatar ships, which contains a large stockpile of weapons and ship modules. Apparently this was normally used by Minmatar Freedom Fighters to resupply their fighter ships after successfull attacks against our slave pens and drug convoys. This armory of theirs must be destroyed, before they can utilize it in their military offensive. Do this for me and you shall be well rewarded.
127999: The destruction of the Minmatar armory should be a serious blow for any long-term military offensive in the area.  Keep up the good work, {[character]player.name}.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
128000:
Your last attack on the Minmatar armory seems to have missed one of the targets that I hoped would be there. Yaekun Ogdin is a long-time enemy of ours, and self proclaimed 'freedom fighter'. His vicious attacks on our slave traders has resulted in a huge loss of revenue. To top it off, he obliterated at least five of our major drug convoys in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} in retaliation for our attack on the Minmatar settlement.

I have coordinates to Yaekun's other hideout, in a deadspace pocket in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. If you find him there, show no mercy.
128001:
The Minmatar squadrons have arrived in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, and they mean business. We've been avoiding them thus far, but we can't ignore the threat they pose any longer. We aren't aware of their destination, but our spies have managed to locate them in a remote deadspace pocket in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. Apparently they've been moving through deadspace to escape detection and our long-range artillery, although it would be foolish of them to expect to remain completely undetected in our backyard.

There is not much that I can tell you about their forces, other than the fact their commander is a seasoned veteran of the Minmatar Fleet. I am not familiar with their combat ability, and therefore I would advise you to hit them with everything you have. Do not underestimate them, bring everyone you can muster with you. This is no small task, even for you, {[character]player.name}.
128002:
You never cease to amaze me, {[character]player.name}. This victory of yours will send a powerful message to the Republic, their Fleet has no business in these parts. As long as we can keep our territory free of military threat, our people will prosper.

I bid you farewell, I have no need of further assistance ... for the time being.
128003: I will take care of these Minmatar dogs, you have my word {[character]agentID.name}.
128005:
Good of you to stop by, {[character]player.name}! And you couldn't have chosen a better time to show up ― I've got some things that need to be taken care of, and you seem like the perfect pilot for the job.

It has been my goal for the past two decades to terraform this beautiful planet, Otomainen V, which we locals call Oshuron. Its temperature is extremely hostile to human life at present, but I believe its position in the solar system and its abundant supply of frozen H20 and CO2 makes it perfect for terraforming. I've even come to the conclusion that scientists residing in this once prosperous community here, in Rush Town, had plans to start the terraforming themselves, but never got around to it before the exodus.

To start the process, I need to acquire a form of extremely simple microorganism that has the ability to survive the terrible conditions on the icy planet. I've located a number of hot springs far beneath the surface that are ideal for harvesting microorganisms, and I believe they will eventually cause a chain reaction on the planet that will lead to a thickening of the atmosphere and thence to global warming.

Now, I´m sure you´re thinking, "Where do I fit into your marvelous scheme?" Well, all I need you to do is bring this stack of sealed containers, filled with old goods I scavenged from the ruins in the area, to an acquaintance of mine at {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. Once that task is complete, I will receive a passcard to a stash of viral agents that have been genetically modified to withstand extreme temperatures, which is exactly what I need to start the terraformation process. But enough of that.

Finish your first task and then I will tell you what to do next. Just don't lose the passcard!!

128007: Excellent! Now make sure you have Tsuna's passcard in your possession before your next assignment. You'll need it.
128008: Oh, and if you're on time, I might even give you some LUX for your troubles!
128009:
Alright, now that we have the passcard, it's time to get the goods. The viral agents that I need are located in a small secluded area near our moon, guarded by Mordu's ships. The Legionnaires were hired by Tsuna Qayse, an obnoxiously wealthy Caldari State citizen who happens to be a major shareholder in the Nugoeihuvi Corporation. She hired the mercenaries to protect her assets, which include the viral agents you are to retrieve for me. My source within the Mordu's Legion ― the same person who provided us with the passcard ― tells me Qayse intends to sell the viral agents on the black market. Unfortunately I don't have the kind of money she's asking for, but that's where you come in.

I want you to fly to her compound in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} and retrieve the stash. You might encounter some resistance from Mordu's guards within the complex, but just try avoiding any direct confrontation. The viral agents are located in a secure location within a high-tech science laboratory in the first area of the complex. The passcard will get you through the acceleration gate.

When you find the science labs, destroy them and retrieve the viral agents. They won't be harmed in the explosion, as they are protected by a safety evacuation system, according to my source. Find the ejected container after the labs have been obliterated, and grab them. Bring them back to me immediately, and just ignore the Legionnaires who may attack you as you attempt to destroy the science labs. Sounds simple, doesn't it!?

You'll be well rewarded for your efforts.

Magnificent! I just can't wait to test my theory...!

Now, don't you look at me like that. I never said my plan was foolproof. I've only done, er, preliminary calculations on the effects these viral agents will have on the planet, true ... but it's worth a try! And if this works, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will make a fortune, and maybe I'll be able to redeem myself within the scientific community!

Oh, and don't you leave just yet ― I have another assignment waiting for you.
128012: Infiltrate Tsuna Qayse's compound in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} and retrieve the potent viral agents, then bring them to {[character]agentID.name}.
128014:
Wonderful! However, now that I have the viral agents, I need a way to transport them down to the planet's surface. I'd like a small ship, one that´s easy to fly and can maneuver handily in the harsh atmosphere of the planet. A shuttle will do nicely. I only know how to fly the Caldari one, so you'll have to bring me that specific type.

Don't tarry, my life's work depends on this!

I only know how to fly the Caldari one, so you'll have to bring me that specific type.

Don't tarry, my life's work depends on this!

128018:
Alright, now that I have the shuttle, there's just one more thing I need before I can get started. To infest the hot springs with these microorganisms, I will need to get to them through an enormous ice sheet. The only way to do that is to have an extremely powerful drill. And I know just the place to acquire one. Well, actually, four.

Jorek Lephny is an old mining tycoon who has been operating in the asteroid belts and moon orbiting Otomainen V for quite some time. The old coot has a mining outpost equipped with a hoard of high-tech drilling equipment, among other things. These drills should do the trick for me, but I need at least four of them in case of breakage or malfunction, which is quite likely due to the scope of the task at hand. The only problem is this: Lephny is extremely paranoid, and we had a falling out of sorts a few years back when I, er, borrowed some of his minerals to construct my lab equipment. He has also had to deal with many pirate attacks through the years and, as a consequence, recently hired a seasoned mercenary veteran from the Mordu's Legion to protect his assets. This mercenary operates a battleship, and he might pose some problems for you if Lephny refuses to hand over the drilling parts willingly.

You will find Lephny's mining outpost in a small asteroid belt near here. There is an acceleration gate close by, inside Rush Town, which will send you to it. Once there, use any means necessary to get those drilling parts! They are located inside the mining outpost itself. Good luck.

I am now on the verge of starting my project, but there is one last hindrance to be eliminated. There is a suspicious-looking craft hovering by a lone rock formation near here. I've tried hailing it, but I get no response. The ship is registered to Ratei Jezzor, whom I have never seen before in these parts. I'm convinced he is an agent working for Caldari Customs, here to spy on us.

I'd like you to take care of him for me, {[character]player.name}. This task will be the last one I give you, I am sure, before I'm on my way into the great annals of history. Just make certain he doesn't bother me when I make my descent to the planet. My life's work depends upon it!

When you finish this final job, you will have done me a great service that I can probably never repay in full. But I hope you'll like my gift ― it's an ultra-rare mineral that I scavenged from one of the ruins here in Rush Town. I have no use for it, but you might.

Dead after those blasted Guristas scoundrels attacked the remnants of this once prosperous community. Dead after the metal walls of these beastly stations caved in from the assault.

But then Old Michi stumbles upon an old pirate he remembers from his younger years. A devilish man, who had a fancy for Old Michi's lost love he did. This troublesome pirate scoffed at Old Michi he did, and claimed his lost love was still alive! But reveal her location he did not. Old Michi will pay handsomely for that information. 128054:
Before you begin I'd like to explain a few things to you, {[character]player.name}. I am {[character]agentID.name}, of the Mercantile Club, which is a prominent corporation within the Caldari State. I came here with a little over 130 other settlers on a project put together by our Chief Operative, Anken Aronainen. Most of the others are miners or engineers, which are here to complete our building project in the area. We are building a small structure which is to serve as the Mercantile Club's headquarters in Otomainen. It is to serve as the meeting place between various State officials of this solarsystem. More you need not know.

The project has just started, but we've run into a few problems already. First of all, it was our intention to use the surrounding asteroid belts as a means to acquire minerals for maintaining our structures, as well as components for building extensions to them once we have imported the neccessary equipment and facilities. The problem is this run-down craphole, which was supposed to be abandoned, apparently has some rather stingy inhabitants. One of them is a crazy old miner called 'Jorek Lephny', who refuses any sort of deal with us to share the vast wealth of asteroids near here, which he claims as his own.

His license ran out ages ago, so we decided to ignore him and mine the area anyway. That's when we encountered his equally insane friend, Markus. Markus is ... or was ... part of Mordu's Legion, and was hired by Lephny who has made quite a fortune since he started strip mining the area. Markus is on a contract for Lephny to protect his assets from random pirate assaults, which I take it he has to deal with on occasion. However, I didn't expect him to attack law abiding citizens of the State ... but I was wrong. He destroyed our Badger and all our mining equipment on board, but allowed the miners to escape on the ejected capsule.

This is of course a treasonous act, and should be dealt with appropriately. I requested military aid from my superiors, but for some reason they would rather I use hired freelance mercenaries to do the job. Something about the legal implications ... anyway here is where you come in. Use one of the stargates in Rush Town to get to the asteroid belt where Lephny is currently stationed at. Find Lephny, and bring him to me. I will make sure he is brought to a mental institution where he belongs. I don't expect you to go up against Markus, he's way too powerful. Once Lephny has been take care of, I'm sure Markus will leave.

We've been scouting the area's near here and have come across an abundance of outlaws. These pirates are a bit strange for city slickers like me, they wear very old fashioned garments and carry spurs (on their boots) instead of insignias as an identification marker. And they seem even more bold than their compatriots deeper within Caldari space, attacking us without warning. A few of our ships have been destroyed, and it's probably only a matter of time before they strike at our position here in Rush Town.

The toughest of the lot that we've encountered so far seem to be the pirates carrying the 'outlaw' spurs. They fly cruiser class ships, and are quire deadly. I can't afford to hire you on a permanent basis, {[character]player.name}, so I'll have to make due with clearing the area for us. You can find most of the outlaws hauled up near Otomainen II's moon. I don't care where you find them, just eliminate as many as you can. Bring back 40 of the outlaw spurs and I'll reward you with an ancient treasure map we discovered in one of the ruins here. I haven't been able to make heads or tails of the map, but someone with your experience might be able to make use of it. Good luck.
