128531:
Well done on that tag-collecting business. These Sniper ID slices now hold a place of honor in my collection. That blood splatter on one of them, man, that was pure genius! Makes it so deliciously eerie! I feel like we're really bonding here, uh... what´s your... oh, yeah, {[character]agentID.name}. No, wait, that´s me. Ehh, {[character]player.name}, right? This might be the beginning of something beautiful, I tell you.

I have such a good feeling about you I'm even willing to let you in on one of my many schemes: A while ago, I came into the possession of some forged transit documents from the Amarr Empire. I have a bit of skill in forgery myself, so I altered them a bit to make them look like imperial orders instructing the bearer to head to a certain location here in Ani for colonization purposes. These Amarrians are always looking to expand, so it's easy to bait a group of wannabee colonists into thinking they have in their hands official permission to settle here. As if the Empire had any say in who settles here and who not? Bah, the fools!

Needless to say, the location here in Ani is in the middle of nowhere; just some old rogue drone hive long since cleaned out. I've already taken out several settlers in the past myself, but with you and me getting on so well, I thought I'd give you a shot at it.

It's nasty business, I can tell you, killing innocent Amarr civilians in cold blood when they're only looking for a place to call home. But I know you have the stomach for it. After all, how innocent can they be, with the blood of my ancestors on their hands? Kill them all, and good riddance to them is what I say. Spit in their eye as they die, mother, father, child and all. Show me you got the guts and I'll reward you with a rare BPC.

Oh, one more thing. Bring the forged documents back to me. This little trap is too sweet not to spring a few more times before they get suspicious.

128533: Yea, I'm lookin' for work.  What you got?
128534:
I am in charge of Urban Management's annual census gathering operation here in Hjoramold. My team flies between settlements in every corner of the system and gathers information on the population count. Then we process this information and finally send it to our headquarters in Abudban along with our report.

Sounds like a pretty simple and straight forward job, eh? And in the more civilized areas of Republic space, it is. But out here you never know what can happen. Every year some disaster strikes, and this year is no exception.

Two of my team have gone missing in addition to one getting stranded in an asteroid belt on her way back, due to her ship breaking down. Needless to say, I need some help getting them back.

First I'd like you to go looking for Kardimo Palettan, one of the workers who went missing. He's my cousin twice removed, and we've known each other since we were kids. I would be terribly unhappy if something has happened to him.

He was on duty near Hjoramold X, collecting census data from some of the bio-dome settlements on the moons there, when he was beset by local thugs. We have a very strict policy here in Urban Management to stay well clear of all pirate infested areas, so we weren't expecting this. Seems one of the local gangs, calling themselves the 'Maru Rebels', thought Kardimo was trespassing on their territory and decided to punish him. I just hope he's still alive. I suggest you scour the area around Hjoramold X's moons, hopefully the Maru will have a base there somewhere. If you find him or any clues leading to him, then return to me for your reward.

128537: Look for a 'Maru Prison Facility' near Hjoramold X's moons, and rescue Kardimo Palettan.
128539:
The other census worker who's having problems is currently stranded on Hjoramold XIII due to an unexpected rogue drone attack. Those drones seem to be randomly attacking all travelers going to and from the planet. The pilots are so scared Kyra, the census taker, can't even find a single one to transport her off XIII. I'd like you to eliminate this threat ASAP so that Kyra can finally get her ass back to base. Republic security forces are taking too damn long to get the job done.

The only thing I need you to do is destroy the Searcher Drone. That will render the drone squad unable to scan all areas around the planet and should allow travelers safe passage as long as they avoid the dust cloud the buggers have been hiding in.

128542:
The last issue I need you to deal with is our stranded census worker, Yttora Lyn. She was sent into the infamous 'Gas Storm' of Hjoramold, which is really a massive gas cloud that orbits Hjoramold's star. Her objective was to take census of the populace in an asteroid colony located deep inside that hostile territory, a pretty dangerous task considering various pirate groups tend to use the area as a hideout. Not to mention it's been infested with rogue drones for years.

The last transmission I received from her was a call for help. Her ship apparently broke down not far from the colony, and as a result she's stranded there for at least a week, when the next convoy arrives. I'd like you to get her out of there ASAP, {[character]player.name}, we can't just leave her there with the psychopaths inhabiting that colony for a week!

If you're careful, you will be able to avoid contact with the pirates. But I warn you, the acceleration gates in the Gas Storm are old and crude and have drifted quite far from the beacons originally placed next to them. Due to the lack of interest in the area, nothing has been done to rectify the situation. So I suggest you head out there on a pretty fast ship, if you want to stay sane that is heh heh.

The last transmission I received from her was a call for help. Her ship apparently broke down not far from the colony, and as a result she's stranded there for at least a week, when the next convoy arrives. I'd like you to get her out of there ASAP, {[character]player.name}, we can't just leave her there with the psychopaths inhabiting that colony for a week!

If you're careful, you will be able to avoid contact with the pirates. But I warn you, the acceleration gates in the Gas Storm are old and crude and have drifted quite far from the beacons originally placed next to them. Due to the lack of interest in the area, nothing has been done to rectify the situation. So I suggest you head out there on a pretty fast ship, if you want to stay sane that is heh heh.
128544: I'm sorry to see that Yttora didn't make it out alive.  She was one of my favorite subordinates, always joyful and energetic.  She was also always available for the risky missions, and I guess her luck finally ran out.  A sad day indeed, {[character]player.name}, but at least now we know what happened to her.
128545:
As you may know, Ihakana and the surrounding systems are completely infested by Gurista pirates. In my work for Internal Security in this system, I've had a number of deputies under me, every single one of whom has fallen prey to these dirty dogs. Fiderer, my last deputy, was a particularly good lad, and I hated to see him go down to those bastards.

I'm always on the lookout for people who know their way around a fight. If you're interested, I can deputize you: Plenty of work to be done around here.

If you feel like proving your mettle, there's a small Gurista forward base in this area that's been no end of trouble for quite a while now. It's not a large outpost as outposts go, but according to our intelligence it plays host to some very powerful Gurista cronies, people not to be trifled with. If you can go in there and eliminate the Gurista force, I'd be much obliged. I'd also be likely to have more work for you.
128546:
Okay, listen up. I have some more Gurista butt for you to kick. Yeah, I thought you'd be happy.

There's another outpost in one of the outlying systems where the Guristas have a nice little drug lab going. This is a slightly bigger target than the last one we hired you to take out, so expect more opposition. Break through their defenses, destroy the outpost's storage silo, and get back to me for your reward.

Get to it, deputy.
128547: Uhm, ok.  Well, I'm here looking for something interesting to do ...
128548:
I'm in a bit of a hard spot at the moment. I work for the Minmatar Freedom Fighters on the side, and a few days ago I was conducting a daring mission in Hjoramold, where I hacked into the Joint Harvesting station's mainframe and planted some grade-A Black Ice. Unfortunately the mainframe sported some grade-AAA watchdogs, which promptly alerted the station authorities to what I was up to. And they complained to the Republic security forces which have launched a formal investigation.

Joint Harvesting may be very unpopular amongst the public, but the government won't risk their multi-billion LUX deal to save my ass, I'm sure of it. I'm afraid there will be a lengthy jail term waiting for me if I turn myself in, so I've decided to go into hiding till this blows over. But hiding in Hjoramold is not easy, especially since Joint Harvesting have decided to send hired mercenaries after me.

So I gotta find a way to leave this system without being spotted by the local security forces or Joint Harvesting's people. So your first job is to find me a cloaking device. And you're in luck, I know of a rogue drone that carries such a device. It's not compatible with most standard ships, but I'm confident I can modify it to work. It's worth a try at least.

Look for a 'searcher drone'. The last I heard it was spotted near one of Hjoramold's outermost planets.

128550: I see it's damaged.  Must have happened when you destroyed the drone.  We'll see if I can fix it up.  In the meantime though, I have more work for you.
128551:
You've done us all a great service. Take this shield booster blueprint copy - our own design, no matter what anyone tells ya - and make yourself some cash... or fly around with the best damn booster this side of the nearest Gist complex.

In any case, Internal Security thanks you for your service, deputy. It's been a pleasure.
128552:
I have a report here on my desk stating that the Guristas have been training a special frigate wing for hit-and-run operations in the vicinities of Ihakana and Friggi. Intelligence has given us the location of one of the training bases for this frigate wing, and we intend to put a dent in this little scheme of theirs.

I need you to go out to the next system, where the base is, kill the detachment of frigates being trained there, and destroy their training bunkers. Beware: The instructors are accomplished pilots, and there may be a battleship or two guarding the facilities. Go in with caution. Good luck.
128553:
The second thing I need you to do is get me an ID Card Generator. I need a fake ID Card where I'm going, and getting one ain't easy. Despite my skills, I haven't been able to make a generator that works, believe me I've tried. But I know a person who knows a person who has a friend who has one ... get my drift? The name of this person is Ketta Tommin, and she is one of Maru's commanders. The Maru are a really bad lot, pretending to fight for the same cause as us Freedom Fighters but in reality they're nothing but criminals.

Anyway, this Ketta is rumored to have an ID Card Generator, but you'll probably have to kill her to acquire it. She resides in a deadspace pocket within Hjoramold, and the entrance to her lair is inside one of the asteroid belts near here. Check each of the main asteroid belts in Hjoramold, you should find it somewhere around there. Just don't go unprepared, she's a tough little cookie.

128555: She put up quite a fight didn't she, {[character]player.name}?  I'm surprised you made it back here in one piece.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
128556: The third item I need is a powerful afterburner, to help me escape from a tight situation.  After all, since I'm headed into low secure space I'm gonna need all the speed I can get.  Those gates out there tend to be closely watched by pirates ... and I don't intend to donate my hard-earned equipment to their hangar floors, if you get what I mean.  Get me a 10MN afterburner module, and I'll give you a generous reward.

128558: Yes, this afterburner will really come in handy.  Good work, {[character]player.name}.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
128559:
Before I can head out of Hjoramold I need those hired merc goons that Joint Harvesting sent after me taken care of. They recently attacked a secret Freedom Fighter outpost near here, and it really pains me to think about the harm I've caused the organization by my failure. If you destroy those responsible for the attack, then at least my comrades will be avenged.

I can supply you with a bookmark to the exact location of the base. The last I heard those merc scum are still roaming the area, looking for me. They are being led by an Amarrian, Kaldar Nagoth, who'm you'll have to deal with. Good luck.

128561: You've been a great help to the Freedom Fighter cause, {[character]player.name}, and I can't thank you enough. I'll be off soon, and I'll make sure my comrades hear of your valiant deeds against the vile Amarr scum. Despite the Republic's stance towards Joint Harvesting, I'm sure deep down inside even the most left-wing of the government will agree to our actions here in Hjoramold. The Amarr must not be allowed to remain within Minmatar space in any shape or form! Peace.
128562: I have a job for you, {[character]player.name}. I became quite concerned today when we lost contact with our commanders in one of the Holy Grounds within Hjoramold, which my people have sworn to protect. I do not have enough pilots on hand to deal with this matter. Investigate the site and report your findings to me. If you find any hostiles there, such as rampaging rogue drones or pirates, then eliminate them at once. Do this and take the blessings of the Kulutor with you.
128563:
There certainly is, and that's why you're here. I have a job for you, {[character]player.name}.

My people, the Kulutor, differ from other Brutor folk; we tend to be seen as "radicals" because of our willingness to merge our ancient traditions with modern views and to embrace new technologies that our conservative brethren dismiss as "unnecessary" and "tainted." Some even go so far as to accuse us of being sympathetic to Amarrian concerns, which is of course rubbish ― the Amarr Empire has conformed probably least of all the major nations to the modern-era culture that we see spreading throughout the free territories. If we are liberal traditionalists, they are radical conservative hegemonists. But enough of political theory: That is not why you're here.

Because of our views, we Kulutor have made many enemies. Therefore, I became quite concerned today when we lost contact with our commanders in one of the Holy Grounds within Hjoramold, which my people have sworn to protect. Many of my people are still returning from the Matar tribal meeting I mentioned earlier, so I do not have enough pilots on hand to deal with this matter. I would like you to investigate the site and report your findings to me. If you find any hostiles there, such as rampaging rogue drones or pirates, then eliminate them at once. Do this and take the blessings of the Kulutor with you.
128564:
I am shocked yet relieved at these tidings, {[character]player.name}. Shocked that our Maru cousins would sink so low as to attack an ancient and holy site that has been part of our Minmatar heritage for generations. Even the Nefantar traitors avoid any conflict in the vicinity of these sites.

However, I am also relieved that the perpetrators were not members of the Brutor tribe. It would have pained me a great deal to learn my own blood stood behind such a cowardly attack. Given your efficiency in this task, I have another assignment for you, if you're willing.
128565: I'm intrigued by your vision. Is there some way I can support this cultural rennaissance?
128566: I want no part in these internecine squabbles. Count me out!
128567: Well, I am sorry, but it is no surprise to me, really. Not all are as open-minded as us Kulutor.
128568: While I scrounge for information on the Maru here in Hjoramold, I would like you to fetch a top-secret report for me that I ordered from our headquarters in Abudban.
128569:
I will need time to think about what our next course of action should be. My first thought is to launch a strike against the Maru, but considering how little I know of them, I believe some research is in order.

While I scrounge for information on the Maru here in Hjoramold, I would like you to fetch a report I ordered from our headquarters in Abudban. It contains some top-secret information on the Maru organization which I don't have clearance to access through the database of the local security forces here in Hjoramold.
128570: Here is the Maru report you requested, {[character]agentID.name}.
128571: Anything else I can do to help your cause?
128572: Ah, yes, excellent, {[character]player.name}. My thanks. If you don't mind waiting while I peruse this, I suspect I'll have another assignment for you momentarily.
128574:
• Acquire the keycard to enter Sispur's Estate from Famon Gurch in the Carnival in Barkrik.
  • Enter Sispur's Estate using the keycard and acquire the security data logs from Sispur's Control Tower. You will probably have to destroy the control tower to access the logs, for its entrance is very securely monitored.
  • Report back to Nabur Verkort with the security logs.
128575:
Apparently Ketta Tommin, a Maru Rebel commander, has been seen visiting Sispur's Estate in Hjormaold several times in the past few weeks. As far as I can see, there are two clues that point directly to her as far as the Maru attack is concerned: First of all, it's well known that Ketta organizes most Maru operations in Hjoramold, which would make her the most likely canditate for being the architect of their terrorist attack; secondly, Ketta was spotted on numerous occasions in the pilgrim camp within the Hjormaold holy site shortly before the attack, which strikes me as odd since she is not exactly known for being the religious type.

I have a feeling that Ketta's trip to Sispur has something to do with your encounter with the Maru. Sispur is one of the staunchest opponents of my campaign to modernize the Brutor, and he therefore has a motive for instigating this attack against us. The Maru themselves have no reason to attack us, so I suspect they've done so only at Sispur's bidding.

I want you to bring me Sispur's security camera logs; there's a good chance they'd prove Sispur's involvement with Ketta's agents in Hjoramold. Once I have the digital recordings of his security cameras, I will hopefully be able to prove that Ketta was working for Sispur, and thus cause him considerable embarrassment.

Your first problem is getting into Sispur's estate. You need a keycard to access the acceleration gate leading further into his estate, and this keycard is not easy to acquire. I suggest you pay a visit to Famon Gurch, a sleazy dog of a merchant who resides in the Carnival in Barkrik. He has often been seen in Sispur's company, and I would be surprised if he didn't have a keycard into the estate.
128576:
While you were off getting the reports I requested, I was busy collecting information from various Matar pilgrims who had recently visited our holy site. A few of them have had dealings with the Maru before, and from one in particular I learned something very interesting: Apparently Ketta Tommin, a Maru Rebel commander, has been seen visiting Sispur's Estate in Hjormaold several times in the past few weeks. Her business there was obviously meant to be kept secret, for Ketta always entered the estate discreetly in a Native Freshfood freighter supposedly carrying food supplies. The pilgrim I spoke to is a Brutor mercenary who works for Sispur. Even though I technically hold a position of authority within the greater Brutor tribe, it took me some time to convince him to fill me in on all the details.

Now, you might be wondering what Ketta Tommin has to do with the Maru attack on our holy site. As far as I can see, there are two clues that point directly to her as far as the Maru attack is concerned: First of all, it's well known that Ketta organizes most Maru operations in Hjoramold, which would make her the most likely canditate for being the architect of their terrorist attack; secondly, Ketta was spotted on numerous occasions in the pilgrim camp within the Hjormaold holy site shortly before the attack, which strikes me as odd since she is not exactly known for being the religious type.

I have a feeling that Ketta's trip to Sispur has something to do with your encounter with the Maru. Sispur is one of the staunchest opponents of my campaign to modernize the Brutor, and he therefore has a motive for instigating this attack against us. The Maru themselves have no reason to attack us, so I suspect they've done so only at Sispur's bidding.

I want you to bring me Sispur's security camera logs; there's a good chance they'd prove Sispur's involvement with Ketta's agents in Hjoramold. It pains me to have to do this, but I can't sit idly while my people are threatened in their own holy places. I do hope you will try to keep the loss of life to a minimum; I do not wish my Brutor brethern harmed, if possible, though I realize you must defend yourself if you are attacked by Sispur's or Ketta's forces. Once I have the digital recordings of his security cameras, I will hopefully be able to prove that Ketta was working for Sispur, and thus cause him considerable embarrassment.

Your first problem is getting into Sispur's estate. You need a keycard to access the acceleration gate leading further into his estate, and this keycard is not easy to acquire. I suggest you pay a visit to Famon Gurch, a sleazy dog of a merchant who resides in the Carnival in Barkrik. He has often been seen in Sispur's company, and I would be surprised if he didn't have a keycard into the estate.
128577:
Once again you've done me a great favor, {[character]player.name}. With these data recordings in my possession, Sispur will have no choice but to yield to my demands. No doubt it will gain me tremendous favor with the Brutor elite. But don't mention this to anyone: As long as it's our little secret, Sispur and his cronies will be powerless to stop me!

Hahahahaaa!
128578:
As you may be aware, the Ani constellation is beset by smugglers as well as dealers in all sorts of illicit goods. Most of the merchandise that comes through here goes to the criminal organizations, who've had this place in their clutches for far too long.

Our plan is to change that, but it's going to take a while. Every day, literally tons of arms, drugs, and even slaves are smuggled through the Nakugard ingress, whence they are taken to various parts of the constellation to be sold. Space is a big place, and hard to police, but we do what we can as we always have ― and any help from capsuleers such as yourself is much appreciated.

Yesterday, I received an encrypted message from one of my deep cover agents. It appears that one Atek Vandano, a notorious fixer loosely affiliated with the Angel Cartel's Gist division, has been establishing contacts in Ani. We're not sure what he's up to, but Command believes this is something that needs to be nipped in the bud if we're to be able to maintain any semblance of control over this place down the line.

But first thing's first. I need you to take a copy of the brief down to some associates of mine at the Sisters of EVE Bureau in Inder. We need to make sure all our operatives in the region are informed of what's going on so we can begin formulating a counter-plan if necessary. Report back to me when you're done and we'll take it from there.
128579:
Look at that ugly structure over there. They call it the Culture Recess and its solemn decay fits my mood perfectly these days. Once I was a proud member of the Sister's research efforts. I had my own lab and staff and every day I woke up with joy in my heart for what wonders I would discover. But the Sister's are a bickering lot; don't let the outer facade of calm and serenity fool you. Behind closed doors you can find fierce rivalry and constant jostling for a higher place in the pecking order. I was adept at playing their games of backstabbing and politics, but not adept enough. One day I found myself out of a job.

I was offered a lowly assistant's position on an insignificant little project. I refused to take it and have been a renegade sister since. But I still hope to regain my former stature within the Sisterhood. If I'm to have any hope of ousting my rivals I must make a crashing entrance, showcasing something magnificent. So here, in the shadow of this ruined monument to past follies, I aim to rebuild my career. I will make a discovery so grand, so momentous, that the Sister's will be forced to accept me back in on my own terms.

Yet I'm finding it hard to do this alone. Material things have never interested me, so I haven't squandered my life savings on something trivial like most. Now I can put my money and my belongings to good use. I'm interested in hiring pilots with the skills and talents to aid me in my task.

If you're interested, I want to hire you for a small job that is too dangerous for a mere scientist such as myself. Over in the Traun system you can find the ruins of an old Nefantar fortress. The Angel Cartel currently holds it and has launched an effort to restore it. Just before I left the Sisters one of our informants within the cartel reported that the repair drones in the old fortress discovered a stash of ancient tablets with strange, indecipherable markings on them. The Angels haven't bothered with the tablets beyond storing those the drones return with in their repair stations.

Now here's the interesting part. A few years ago I was working on a project that compelled me to dig through the ancient history of the Nefantar tribe, from times long before the Amarrians ever arrived in Minmatar space. While traveling in Hjoramold, the tribe's ancestral home, I came upon several tablets with runic inscription, filled with very thought provoking information. I can't go into details here, but it is the key to my work.

I suspect that the tablets the Angels discovered in Traun might be more of these runic tablets. If so, then those tablets could give me a breakthrough in my research efforts. I need someone well versed in the art of war to retrieve those tablets in Traun for me. I will reward you well if you're willing to take this on.

128581:
My research is going well. My decision to hire independent pilots has paid off really well. But I fear it might also have backfired somewhat by putting too much heat on me. The Sisters have become aware of my whereabouts and what I'm trying to achieve. While I doubt it, one of my rivals could decide to dent my efforts my sending some thugs here to rough me up and destroy my work. The physical risk does not concern me all that much, but if I lose my work I have nothing.

I always like to be on the safe side, so I've made backup copies of my research. I need to get them to a safe place. First, I considered placing them in a depository box in a bank, but me hiring such a box is too easy to track down. Maybe I'm being paranoid, but you never know. So instead I've opted to hire a low-key storage room in a remote system to stash my backup copies in.

Obviously, I can't go there myself, I might be followed. But they would never bother with someone such as you, so you're an ideal candidate for the job. Take my stash to the Ragnarg system and by the time you return I'm sure I will have something more interesting, less paranoid, for you to do.

128583:
I'm ready to take my research to the next level. But to do so I must get my hands on some decent science instruments. Without a big corp behind me, the manufacturers of these items won't even speak to me. I've been scouring the second hand market, but not found anything of value. My work will soon stall if I don't get this stuff.

I received an interesting tidbit from a former colleague of mine, one of the few still talking to me. It seems one of the secret research labs the Sisters are running in Lanngisi just had a serious accident and was abandoned. I don't know the extent of the accident, but do know that some lethal substances leaked out. I'm sure the place is already crawling with scavengers, but if we move quickly we might get something good.

It's funny, only a few weeks ago I would be shattered by these news, but now I hardly feel anything. All I care about is how I can exploit this disaster to my own advantage. I guess I just have learnt that to succeed in this harsh world, one must be extra tough. My sheltered life has never exposed me to this world until now, but I feel I'm coping well.

Enough about that. If you're willing to go over to the contaminated research lab and see if you can find any science instruments, I'm sure I can find something suitable to reward you with upon your return. It doesn't matter if the items are broken, just get me a few and I'm sure I can make something out of them. If the facility itself doesn't yield anything you might have to take out some of the scavengers there and see if they cough something interesting up. Just make sure to blow up everything you see there to make sure you get all the salvagable items.

It doesn't matter if the items are broken, just get me a few and I'm sure I can make something out of them. If the facility itself doesn't yield anything you might have to take out some of the scavengers there and see if they cough something interesting up. Just make sure to blow up everything you see there to make sure you get all the salvagable items.
128585:
Thanks to you my research is back on track. I feel like I'm getting close to something big. You remember those tablets you got me awhile ago? I've managed to get some sense out of them and the information I've gleaned points to one place in particular that might hold the key to this whole thing. Unfortunately, that place is not exactly accessible. It lies deeper in the same complex that you found the tablets in, in the Traun system. This place I'm talking about is an ancient portal of some sorts. Sadly, it has long since ceased to function. I'm also beginning to suspect that it wasn't built by the Nefantars themselves, but some other, more elusive, civilization. I'm not sure exactly where it lies, but it is an immense structure, so it can't be all that hard to locate.

I need pieces of the damaged portal. If you can get them for me I would be eternally grateful. Just to show you how serious I am, I'm offering you a very rare BPC as a reward when you return with a few pieces of the damaged portal. Needless to say, you can expect trouble there, so be prepared.

Why, hello to you stranger. It's good to see a friendly face out here. Or at least someone not shooting at me. I'm Dr. Tikrest, by the way. Some call me Ramakell, but I prefer to be called the Professor. In case you haven't heard of my work, I'm a renown sociologist.

So, what is a famous and handsome sociologist such as me doing out here in the middle of nowhere, you might be asking yourself? I don't want to befuddle you with all the technical terminology of my trade, so let me put it simply. I have a reason to believe that a mysterious human civilization lived here in the Ani constellation thousands and thousands of years ago. Yes! I know it's hard to believe, but a famous and intelligent person such as me wouldn't make such a claim unless I was absolutely sure. A few of my more narrow-minded colleagues have scorned this idea of mine, so I'm out here to prove them wrong.

What I'm going to do is build an immense radio antenna capable of detecting the most miniscule signals from deep space. My theory is that such a powerful civilization as this one presumably was must have used some pretty powerful communication devices. Well, there still might be some fractions of signals left out there floating in space, waiting for someone renown and brilliant like me to pick them up.

Unfortunately, my work hasn't launched under the most auspicious of portents. On my very first day out here, I was set upon by a brigand of the most obnoxious and foul-mouthed nature. Neither my illustrious career nor my most eloquent rhetoric sufficed to fend him off and he took off with my portable power generator. The scoundrel was flying a frigate, but he might be anywhere in the constellation by now. Damn Angels! What is the world coming to when renown and charming sociologists like me can't go about their business without having some young punks and upstarts harassing them? Not to mention making lout and insidious remarks that are totally unfounded. The nerve of these pirates! Well, I wont stand for it. I'm not only renown, but also wealthy. I'll pay you good money for hunting down that punk and bring me back my portable power generator.

128589:
Allow me to congratulate you once more on retrieving that power generator for me. It is invaluable for my work here. Your efficiency might almost suffice to make you a passable sociologist one day. But enough about that.

As I've already explained to you, I need to build an immense antenna to have any hope of catching a glimpse into past. To my frustration, the pitiful antennas available on the market are nowhere near being sufficient to meet my needs. But a renown and resourceful sociologist like me doesn't let a little fact like that stop him. I've already placed an order with the firm Boundless Creations for them to custom make an antenna for me. It is being built at their factory over in the Hek system. Their work has progressed at an admiring rate, but they refuse to deliver it to me here. So I'm in need of a courier to fetch me my antenna. Of course, a renown and respected person such as myself can't be bothered with such a trivial matter. But if you are interested, I will give you good money. I've learnt that when dealing with independent pilots such as yourself, money will convince people to do most anything.

128591:
This is all coming together nicely, I must say. We have accomplished much, you and me, and now we're on the brink of success that might change the world of sociology forever. Doesn't it brighten your otherwise mundane existence to be a part, albeit a small one, in something as great as this? No need to thank me though, for a renown and modest sociologist such as me, fame and success is all it takes to fuel what little vanity I have.

But we're not quite there yet. I'm still in need of a good signal amplifier to work alongside my new antenna. The one I brought was nowhere near up to the task and literally melted when I started feeding it the signals from the antenna. Luckily, one of my former students is in the Republic Fleet and is stationed here in Ani. It's sad really, he's very talented and had a brilliant and cozy career in sociology ahead of him. But no, he had to play the hero and go join the military, the fool.

Well, his loss is my gain now. I heard from him that after one of the many unsuccessful Republic invasions into the contested complex in Traun, he noticed one of his fallen comrades leaving behind a Republic amplifier. With a little bit of modification, that piece of equipment would be perfect for my purposes. If you hurry you might be able to get a hold of the amplifier before someone else scoops it up. I don't know where it is exactly, but I gather from my ex-student that they were trying to force their way into the inner-most room of the complex when they beat a retreat. So have a look around that area. History waits for no man, renown sociologists or not, so to entice you into putting a step on it I'll offer you a solid BPC as a reward for a job well done.

128593:
Well, we've found out what Atek Vandano's up to, and it's not pretty. Hold on to your seat ― if you're anything like me, this is gonna piss you off something awful.

The good Mr. Vandano, it seems, is not working for the Gist on this particular occasion. Our agents have uncovered data that indicates he's helping to bring in slave labor from Amarrian colonies to the Joint Harvesting stations in this system. We think they might be here as part of the Insorum scare; our information shows that the influx of slaves to Amarrian facilities within Republic space has increased manifold in the past weeks. The holders are protecting their "investments" by bringing them to our turf under the guise of contract laborers. Vandano thinks he can do this right under our noses. We're not going to let him.

Obviously, to avoid an incident with the Amarrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, we'll have to go about this in some fairly unconventional ways, and we'll have to use operatives not officially affiliated with us. You know where I'm going with this, right?

Vandano has an associate, a lady by the name of Nanom Basskel. We have reason to believe she's one of the major architects behind this plan, and according to our intelligence she's in possession of documents detailing where they're keeping the slaves before final transport to the Joint Harvesting plants in system. She can usually be found at the contested military depot in Inder. Go out there, "remove" Miss Basskel, and bring me these documents.
128594:
Welcome, young pilot. Good to see a friend of the Empire in this foul place: If my work didn't require my being here, I would long ago have left it far behind. I do not know if your presence here shows that you possess a strong backbone or that you're merely a fool wandering around in the lion's maw. Perhaps we shall see.

It may that you can be of service to me. My task here is to monitor Minmatar activity in the constellation. The Republic trundles around like a blind dinosaur, so it's easy to track its doings. The rebels like nothing better than to boast of their heroics. But there is one group that is hard to keep tabs on, the Krusual tribe. As ever, their evasiveness makes them hard to gauge.

My superiors have finally responded to my repeated requests for assistance and have sent one of their infiltrators out here. These guys are former Minmatar slaves, correctly trained and conditioned to act as agents on our behalf within Minmatar society. The infiltrator they sent out here is sitting in one of the Joint Harvesting stations over in Hjoramold. What I want you to do is go and pick him up there, then drop him off in one of the Krusual tribe stations in Nakugard.

If you show yourself capable enough to perform this task without a glitch, I may have more tasks in line for you.

128596:
You did alright on that infiltrator job. I suppose. But I'm willing to give you another chance to impress me. The Minmatars are not the only nuisance here: The pirate infestation in the constellation is astounding. I guess it just goes to show how lousy the Republic is at keeping its territories in check.

The pirates are a constant pain the ass; sometimes it seem they have a sixth sense about where and when to be to foil my plans. If the Republic is too weak to deal with them, I guess I have to. The pirates that are proving to be the biggest pest are the ones that drop the Spy ID Slice. Kill a few of them and bring me five such insignia. You can usually find the buggers roaming in the contested complexes here in Ani.

I've even gone out on several killing sprees myself in the past. Those excursions yielded me some pretty nice Minmatar ammo that I have no use for myself. You can have it as a reward when you return with those slices.

128598:
Your performance collecting those slices was adequate. Well, anyway, adequate enough for me to trust you with an important mission. The Ani constellation is crawling with all kinds of hackers and tech-freaks. While this fact makes it that much harder to ensure that communication links remain safe, it also present us with an opportunity. These hackers like to break into databanks and steal sensitive information. Usually, their pathetic ethics keep them from exploiting the information they steal. They don't delete it, though, but store it for themselves so they can brag about their deeds to fellow hackers.

As I see it, these hackers are sitting on a gold mine, and I think few of them even realize this. If I could get my hands on some of the stuff they've collected, it could lead to my promotion and even a transfer out of this hellhole. I've discovered a small hacker community in an old ore reprocessing lab in the Tvink system. They've converted the place to become something they call Hacker Haven. I shudder even to think about what that might mean.

I want you to go over there and shoot everything to pieces. My sources inform me that inside this haven sits a little blue box that is a virtual treasure trove full of stolen data from all around the constellation. I want that box. I don't know exactly where it might lie, unfortunately, so you'll just have to keep shooting until you locate it. The blue box itself is supposedly indestructible, so don't worry about that: You should be able to pluck it from the wreckage of whatever structure it was in. This mission means a lot to me, so you'll get a fine blueprint copy as a reward if you succeed.

Oh, did I mention that the hackers are pretty well protected? Maybe you should bring some friends along.

Right now I'm looking for {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity}. These tags have been implanted into certain pirates which infest {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space, which they use to identify each other with. To acquire them you will most likely have to kill them, or buy them off someone who did exactly that. I don't really care either way, as long as they have been taken care of I'm satisfied.

This might not be the very best way to confirm deaths, but we've been quite successful in the past using this method. Forgeries are almost non-existent, as each tag costs more to manufacture than it's worth on the bounty market. Not only that but we can usually tell a fake apart from a genuine pirate tag. And they have remarkable survivability, usually found in the charred wreckage of the pirate ships despite everything else, including the pirate's corpse, having been completely vaporized.

You can find the pirates carrying the {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} in many places, but I'd first check the asteroid belts in the surrounding systems as attacking defenseless miners is their favorite past-time. Good luck, and have fun.

Forgeries are almost non-existent, as each tag costs more to manufacture than it's worth on the bounty market. Not only that but we can usually tell a fake apart from a genuine pirate tag. And they have remarkable survivability, usually found in the charred wreckage of the pirate ships despite everything else, including the pirate's corpse, having been completely vaporized.

128675: Agents from the Angel Cartel managed to infiltrate one of our stations and gather information about the station's defenses. They've planted the reports out in space near an ancient abandoned stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to be picked up. Fortunately, we managed to intercept their transmission and know the location. I want you to travel to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and pick up the stolen reports. I'll give you {[numeric]rewardQuantity} LUX as a reward. Be careful, there will definitely be guards at the pickup place which you might have to deal with.
128676: Great.  Just try to hurry over there, you never know when they might move the reports.
128677: I'll have the problem solved in no time.
128678: I'm interested in working for the Sukuuvestaa. Let me hear what you have to offer.
128679: Excellent! For your first assignment, I want you to take care of a few pesky Minmatar brigands who've decided to sabotage one of our reconnaissance missions to Nakugard VIII's moons. 128680:

128682: Find and destroy the Minmatar Brigands in one of Nakugard VIII's asteroid belts; loot their Punk ID Slices and bring them back to Mitsu Hekken. Note that you are not guaranteed to find all the ID Slices you need in one run.
128683:
Since you did so well in your previous assignment, here's another mission for you. Each of our scouts conducting reconnaissance missions keeps a digital recording of what transpires during their expedition, stored in a secret compartment within some cargo crates they're carrying on board. A few of the teams we recently sent out went missing, and we're hoping the recordings survived and are being kept by whoever attacked them (if that's in fact what happened).

I'd like you to scour the asteroid belts in the Ani constellation in search of these logs. Assuming pirates are at the root of this problem, they might still have the cargo crates on board that hold the recordings, likely quite unknown to them, of course. We've lost dozens of ships, but all I ask for you to receover five of their logs. I don't care where you find them; I just need that evidence brought to me ASAP so I have something to bring back to my superiors when they launch a formal investigation.

128686:
Hiya there. I don't know if you've visited the contested complex here in Traun. If you haven't let me warn you, it can be real tough for someone of my stature. But the Angel Cartel is operating a listening outpost there that collects all kind of interesting data from around the system. And with all the factions that are converging here in Traun, they got info on more or less every major player operating in Ani. That info can yield sizeable income, but only while it's fresh.

Me, I'm too weak to have any chance of entering the outpost and collect anything of value. But perhaps you're up to the job? As long as you have the skill and equipment to hack their databanks, of course.

Well, well, here I sit in need of a bit of help and then you come along. Must be karma, or something. I'm a long time user and abuser of every illegal substance known to man, but now I'm looking to get proactive instead of always being reactive. You follow? Ok, you look a little clueless, so let me spell it out for you. I want to manufacture the stuff myself, ok?

It all sounds sunny up to this point, right? Yeah, well, there's one snag. I haven't the faintest idea of how to go about producing anything more complex than a boiled egg. But I've got an idea. The Angel Cartel has a strong presence here in Ani and they are bound to sit on some pretty neat recipes, me thinks. So here's what I want you to do for me. Enter one of the contested complexes around the constellation, locate an Angel data fortress and hack into it. Then get back here and give me what you find. Sooner or later something of interest must turn up. I recommend the complex over in Traun, it's your best bet of finding the stuff I'm looking for.

Oh, needless to say, you have to possess some minimal knowledge of hacking to have any chance of success.

Are you proficient hacker? If you are I have need for your talents. The Sisters of EVE are conducting some very secretive research here in Ani and my master sent me out here to find out what it is. I'm already engaged in breaking into the Sister's mainframe, but it's proving to be troublesome. My master is getting restless and wants to start see some result. I know that the Angels are actively gathering information themselves, so perhaps they're sitting on something of value to me and my master. I'll pay you a bit of money if you collect some tidbits for me. The Angels operate a listening outpost in a complex over in Traun. Head over there and snoop around. 128692:
Some weeks ago I was in a sleazy space bar over in Hek when I overheard a conversation between couple of Thukkers. One of them had this really incredibly story to tell about a human civilization that once lived here in Ani long before us Minmatars arrived. One day, they invented this virtual world that people could hook into and be completely immersed. They created this beautiful virtual world, where everyone was rich and happy. Before long, they were all hooked in, their bodies suspended in stasis chambers. And thus, they faded away, into this virtual world of theirs.

That's the gist of it. Well, forgive me for finding this fascinating. I came out here as soon as I could and now I'm collecting interesting relics to find out if it's real or just a fable. I'd like you to head out to Inder and investigate an ancient wreckage in a complex there. Perhaps the key to this whole mystery lies there. But you need some basic knowledge in archaeology to be of any help.

There are great riches to be had in the contested complex here in Hjoramold. The Nefantars operated a large research facility there that gathered great amount of mysterious relics, supposedly thousands of years old. Now that the facility lies in ruins the relics are scattered around, just waiting for someone to pick them up. And that's exactly what I've been trying. But so are countless other treasure hunters and some of them really know how to shoot a gun. So I've been setting my sight on the rather more relaxed ancient wreckage site over in Inder. It doesn't yield as interesting stuff, but it's easier to get at.

The Inder site is ideal for a budding archaeologist and if you fancy yourself to be one, then by all means head over there and bring me something of interest back. There's good money to be had in this field for those bold enough to get what they want.

128696:
Hello there, you're interested in a little bit of work, yes? For many years I've been making a brisk business selling Nefantar artifacts on the black market. The buyers are all kind of people, mostly Ammatars looking for lost heirlooms or idle-rich Gallenteans looking for something unique to flaunt at the next gala showing. I long since decided to outsource the gathering of artifacts to other, more capable pilots.

Lately, the pilots working for me have been returning with more and more of some strange artifacts that I'm beginning to suspect are not of Nefantar origin. I've seen these items on occasions in the past, but now a lot more are coming in. Not that I'm complaining, mind you, for I've always had an easy time shifting them. It's getting so easy, in fact, that I'm on a constant lookout for more pilots to collect for me. It is my understanding after having talked to my other pilots that a contested complex over in Inder is the best place to find the items I want. If you do well you can always get more work from me. Might even provide a steady income for you. To locate the right items you need the right knowledge and equipment, naturally.

A clan sister of mine owns a quaint little curiosities shop back in Pator. She sells all kind of weird and wonderful items from around the known Eve universe. When she heard I was coming here to Ani, she asked me to have a look around for items for her shop. Of course, I'm happy to oblige.

I expected to pick up perhaps a few Nefantar artifacts at most, but something else has caught my eye. While digging through an old spa here in Lanngisi, I came upon a most fascinating old manuscript, written in a language I'm unfamiliar with. I sent it to my clan sister and it thrilled her. She wants me to search for more. I haven't found any more here in Lanngisi, but I've heard from reliable sources that more can be found over in an old ruin in Inder. So I'm looking for pilots such as you to help me out.

Bring me some manuscripts and I'll pay you {[item]rewardTypeID.quantityName, quantity=rewardQuantity}. Of course, you have to have some basic knowledge of archaeology before you can make head or tail of what you find.

128701:
Although I'm sure you're just itching to get into combat, I'd like to put you to a small test first ... to see if you're really sincere about helping us out. There's this minor task that needs to be done, which involves ferrying a load of medical supplies to this system. You see, Nakugard has been hit by strange viral infections of late which have devastated a few outlying settlements here and put a scare into the local populace. Not only that but it's really having a negative effect on our efforts with bringing more Krusual Tribe civilians here, a system with a viral outbreak is not exactly the first place on your list when you're thinking of relocating your family somewhere.

The Vherokior Tribe were kind enough to give us access to their Zemnar supplies on {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. Zemnar has proven to be an effective antidote against this latest outbreak, and we desperately need a large supply of the drug to prevent any more deaths and more bad publicity. I would like you to pay a visit to the Vherokior station in Teonusude and pick up the shipment and bring it to me, I'll see to it that it's distributed to all the affected settlements in Nakugard.

128703:
Since you've been so successful at kill missions, I'll give you one final assignment that involves exactly that. There is a Thukker Tribe envoy to the Angel Cartel, Vanir Makono, who's been stirring up the Cartel against us; according to our intelligence, he's currently located within the Minmatar Military Depot in Inder. I don't know what his motives are, but they're probably related to the fact the Thukker Tribe hate our guts. Heh. He's been a thorn in our side for long enough. The Gist attacks on our assets have increased tenfold since he started spreading those rumors about us.

I already sent two of my best pilots out to kill him, but I haven't heard from them since. I suggest you prepare yourself well before you attempt to infiltrate the Military Depot; it's completely overrun by Gistum thugs. You'll probably find Vanir in the headquarters of the deadspace complex. Good luck.

128705:
You've been quite a boon to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} since I first spoke to you, {[character]player.name}. You've earned your reward and then some. Unfortunately, I have nothing more for you at this time, but I'll throw you a tip: I heard some things that might interest you about the Okkelen constellation within Caldari space; apparently they're desperate for more freelance mercenaries back there. You might want to give them a shot if you aren't too busy.

Good luck!
128706:
As your second assignment, I need you to fetch a valuable Nefantar artifact from one of the Nefantar ruins through Ani. Most people consider the Nefantar ruins a lost cause when it comes to treasure hunting, as they were all looted for decades after the Rebellion, and are now either used as a hideout by pirate forces or guarded by local militia intent on saving 'valuable relics of the past' from looters. I would like to reverse this myth by proving to the people of the Republic that Ani is in fact still full of surprises, including treasures from the past. All I require is some evidence of this to present to the media, in other words our propaganda machine.

To be more specific, I'd like some kind of Nefantar relic that will raise eyebrows. They were very keen on creating portraits and sculptures of their leaders, which were unfortunately mostly destroyed by the freedom fighters during the Rebellion, and I'm certain one of them would interest all sorts of people. The Krusual Tribe are renowned treasure hunters, so finding these nefantar objects here would undoubtedly increase their interest in Ani.

Now if you're completely clueless as to where to start looking, I'll suggest one promising spot. There are some Nefantar ruins in Barkrik which have been claimed by the Maru Rebels as one of their bases. Maru is a criminal organization that is not to be taken lightly, most of it's members are wanted by the law and can be killed on sight. And other than being prepared for a fight, I suggest you bring someone along that has experience as an archaeologist, you might need someone like that to dig up the artifact for you. Good luck.

But now that you've proven yourself to be a reliable fighter pilot, you've convinced me to let you have the most difficult mission yet.  Just tell me when you're ready.
128709:
The last mission I have for you is the most difficult. The heavy pirate presence in Ani has a very negative effect on our mission, as I told you before. And the Angel Cartel are at the heart of it. Their operations in Ani must be stopped, at all costs.

As the saying goes, cut the head off the snake and you kill the snake. I'm not sure if this holds true with the Cartel, but it's worth a try. Their leader within Inder is Lagaster Malotoff, by killing him we hope to paralyze their forces for some time at least, and give the local populace a morale boost. This is the final task I have in store for you, once you have accomplished it my mission in Ani should be complete.

128712: Lagaster has been taken care of, {[character]agentID.name}.
128713: Actually I'm looking for some work.
128714:
Well why didn't you say so?! If you're good with a gun, then I have something that you'd like. If not, then get lost.

If you're still interested, I've uploaded some information into your journal. If you feel you're up to it, then let me know.
128715:
I settled here in Nakugard many years ago, lured to this place by tales of riches and glory spread by the Republic Parliament who've been desperate to populate Ani with loyal supporters of the Republic. But I've never felt at home here, and ever since I discovered I was sharing space with minions of the Amarr Empire I've felt betrayed and depressed. These people are responsible for some of the most terrible crimes in human history! And they're living under the protection of those that have sworn to protect us, the Republic government! I couldn't believe it at first ...

Apparently the late Karin Midular made a deal with Joint Harvesting a few years back to allow them to build a few stations and plantations in Ani. I don't care how much LUX they had to pay to get this deal through, or the fact they pretended to apologize for the Empire's crimes before the Rebellion. An Amarrian is an Amarrian, they'll never change, and as long as their people are located within Minmatar space I will not be at peace. And fortunately there are more within the Krusual Tribe who think the same way.

There is a growing movement within the Krusual settlements in Ani which aims at uprooting the Amarr presence in this constellation. We already have a large fleet of ships ready to strike at any moment. Our first target is a 'secret' plantation within Hjoramold, called the Jakela Plantation. We managed to discover it by using system scanners, and we've even heard rumors from there that they are using slaves to work the fields!

Our only problem is that our agents haven't found a way through their second acceleration gate. It's being guarded by an Amarrian called Rekker, and a few of his henchmen. They aren't much of a problem for our forces, but we're afraid that if we send in an entire battalion he'll simply flee at the first sight of us and take his keycard with him.

What I want you to do, {[character]player.name}, is take a small fleet of ships and launch a surprise attack against Rekker. Loot his keycard and bring it back to me, that way we'll be able to access the acceleration gate leading deeper into the plantation grounds. You'll have to do this fast, before they change the gate's security system when they figure out Rekker has been killed.

Once you're back here with the keycard I'll supply you with your reward.
128717: Find the Jakela Plantation in Hjoramold using a system scanner.  Take care to bring a Hacker Slice ID to access the first gate.  Destroy Rekker Malkun and bring his keycard back to {[character]agentID.name}.
128718:
Since you managed to accomplish my first task with aplomb, I've decided you're worthy of another highly important mission for our cause. There are a large number of civilians in Ani who have offered to join our ranks during our campaign to rid the constellation of Amarr, but we don't have the weapons to spare to arm them. One of my contacts within the Republic Security forces has promised us a large shipment of small arms which we'll use to equip our new troops with. The only catch is that this shipment is currently located in Floseswin, which is a pretty dangerous area. Which makes this job perfect for someone like you, {[character]player.name}.

Get the shipment of small arms here in one piece and I'll give you a generous reward.

128720: Great work!  This will benefit our cause immensely.  I'm sure our ground troops will now have the manpower they need to overpower the mercenary forces stationed within the plantations, so we don't have to blow up the structures which would potentially kill innocent Minmatar civilians working there.  And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
128721:
If you're still willing I have one final mission that I think you're suited for. The Joint Harvesting corporation has become aware of our presence and we believe they are preparing for a counter-attack against our forces. Finding a Mordu's mercenary in Ani confirmed our suspicions, we're certain these Mordu's goons were hired by Joint Harvesting to sabotage our operation.

Not only that, but they apparently sent a Magdesh after us. The Magdesh are a powerful family within the Mordu's Legion, highly respected bounty hunters. One of their members, Kyan, is currently hauled up in Barkrik I - Asteroid Belt 1. He's been spotted on numerous occasions snooping around near our outposts there, but never long enough for our guards to catch him. I would like you to take care of this pest, before he manages to do us any harm. Just be warned, he operates a Caldari battleship and is not to be taken lightly. You might need help on this one, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.

128723: Find Kyan Magdesh in Barkrik I - Asteroid Belt 1, destroy him and bring his DNA back to {[character]agentID.name} to confirm the deed.
128724: Well, that was the last assignment I have in store for you, {[character]player.name}.  I'm certain we can handle the rest by ourselves.  And if you want to further help our cause, I suggest sabotaging their plantations in Hjoramold and Barkrik.  We'll take all the help we can get.  Good luck on your future endeavors.
128726:
Your first assignment is to conduct a reconnaissance mission near an ice field in {[location]dungeonSolarSystemID.name}. We have reason to believe a Serpentis drug baron has set up shop there, hoarding drugs and other contraband goods in the deadspace pocket surrounding the ice field, safe from our surveillance monitors. We have also been led to believe that this particular Serpentis pirate has been smuggling arms to the Angel Cartel criminal organization, which is a serious enough crime in itself.

I want you to examine the area and report your findings back to me. If our information is correct, then I will have no choice but to launch a full scale assault into the ice field and the surrounding asteroid belt to exterminate this Serpentis pest for good. I will await your findings here in the Dream Port. Farewell.

128728: So our suspicions were confirmed ... I'll have to send one of our security teams in there to clean up what's left of the Serpentis ships.  But since you finished this task with flying colors, I'd like you to stick around for a couple other jobs that I need someone to take care of.
128729:
Now that you've proven yourself I'll fill you in on my secret assignment here in Ani. I was sent here by the Republic Fleet to prepare for a major assault that they've planned against the Angel Cartel strongholds in the constellation. The elimination of the Serpentis in the ice field was solely made to weaken the Cartel's position, as the Serpentis there were directly supplying them with arms and other equipment.

Your second task is to transport a regiment of our finest ground troops to The Sisters of Eve Bureau in Inder from the Brutor stronghold in Ivar. They will play a major role in our assault against the Cartel positions, so I need them here ASAP. I'll fill you in on your last, and most important, mission after you've completed this simple task.

128731:
Now we're entering the final stages of our preparations for the military offensive. But there is one last mission I'd like to offer you, that is critical to our objective. The Military Depot in Inder is currently under Angel Cartel control. Although the meager fleet guarding their positions there are no match for a full scale assault by the Republic armada, they have a huge advantage due to the terrain. The acceleration gate leading into the complex is not fit for large vessels, and if we take the longer route of manually flying through the deadspace area we will undoubtedly run into countless of their booby traps, potentially causing us heavy casualties.

But there is something that could turn the table in our favor, {[character]player.name}. Our agents have already infiltrated the pirate forces inside the Military Depot, and have reported a glaring weakness. They use a large scanner tower to detect any incoming ships from light years away, giving them extra time to prepare their defenses for any incoming assault. If this scanner tower is destroyed, they will lose one of their biggest advantages.

The scanner tower is located inside the Military Depot complex. Once you have destroyed it, bring me something from the wreckage as proof. I won't doubt your sincerity, {[character]player.name}, but I'm afraid my superiors are a little more skeptical and would require some sort of evidence before they launch the strike.

128733: I found this scanner data in the charred wreckage of the tower right after I destroyed it.
128734: Fantastic!  I'll send this to Manneiri Rimbrumulf immediately.  You've done your duty, {[character]player.name}, and for that I salute you.
128735: Find the Contested Minmatar Military Depot and destroy the Scanner Tower.  Return to {[character]agentID.name} in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} with the Angel Cartel Scanner Data.
128737:
I'm working toward my doctorate in Archaeology from the Science and Trade Institute. I'm already done with my thesis, but before my advisory committee allows me to submit it, they're demanding I get some more field experience. So they've sent me out here to collect some artifacts from the fabled dig sites here in Okkelen.

I've been out here for some time trying to get into these areas, but to no avail. I'm simply outclassed. The main dig site is over in Otitoh, but the excavation there is heavily infested with rogue drones, so it's very hard getting anything from there. I've heard rumors that something of interest might be found here in Otomainen, but I haven't found anything substantial yet. But I have one good lead. I understand that the artifacts the infamous Kazka bandits have pillaged or looted throughout the constellation are stored in their headquarters over in Sakkikainen.

If you're willing to help, assuming you have some basic knowledge of archaeological practices, I think that Sakkikainen is the best bet for finding something of interest that is not too dangerous to collect. My committee is mainly interested in old manuscripts, so if you could find something of that nature, I would be willing to pay you good money for it.

128739:
There are a lot of sharks swimming the dark waters of Okkelen these days. But that isn't all bad for small fish like you and me because these sharks are mainly interested in what the other sharks are doing. And wouldn't you know, they're even willing to pay good money to someone that can provide them with that information. Enter little ol' me. I've been making steady business ferreting out interesting stuff from various sources and selling them to the highest bidder.

There are a lot of places that such information can be gathered. The contested complex in Friggi is one such place, but not for those faint of heart, for it is heavily defended. But right here in Airmia is a place ideally suited for a bit of old school industrial espionage. The Guristas are operating a small spy station in the contested Lai Dai Refinery. If you possess some decent hacking skills you're bound to find something of value there. I might even be interested in buying some of the stuff you dig up.

The Chief Executive Panel may have charged only a couple of the mega-corporations with the task of settling Okkelen, but that doesn't mean the others have to sit idle by on the sidelines and watch Lai Dai and NOH hog all the glory. And all the riches, more importantly.

Ishukone wants to keep a watchful eye on the goings on here. I'm one of several covert and not-so covert operators roaming the constellation gathering intelligence. Personally, I'm particularly interested in the spy station operated by the Guristas pirates over in Airmia. Why spend a lot of time and resources to do something that others are already doing? If you are proficient hacker and have all the right equipment, you could do much worse than snoop around there and collect some choice tidbits to sell to information peddlers such as myself.

128743:
Something tells me that we're on the verge on discovering something really marvelous here in Okkelen that might change the way we look at the world forever. There are artifacts here that are thousands of years old and if we can discover who left them behind and what kind of society they lived in, it might put our own meager existence into a more enlightened perspective.

Yes, interesting times indeed, and I for one want to do what I can to advance humankind to the next rug in the evolution ladder. I'm collecting interesting relics and am on the lookout for independent pilots that have some rudimentary knowledge of archaeology to help me out in this great endeavor. Are you interested?

A better bet is heading out to the Airmia system and enter the spy station the Guristas are operating in the contested complex there. If you have some basic hacking knowledge, I'm certain you can dig up something of value to me.

Just be very careful ― a big gun is a man's best friend around here, so be prepared to face a few.
128746:
Some bright light back at headquarters got the idea that SuVee was missing out on something good here in Okkelen. So they sent poor old me out here to map the riches. Yeah, right. If I ever find out who's responsible, I'll make him dance to the tune of my AK-107. This place is a real hellhole. All I've encountered is dust and danger. I've heard plenty of stories of fabulous riches, but that's it ― just stories. My superiors are getting restless, wanting more than just hints and rumors from me, so I'm looking for prospective pilots to lend me a bit of a hand.

I'm well connected to shift these artifacts, so if you know anything about archaeology I'm interested in striking a bit of a business deal. I'll pay you good money for any {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} you manage to scavenge from the Kazka bandits.

128749:
Thanks in no small part to the documents you brought, we now have the location of the temporary facilities in this system where Vandano and his cohorts intend to keep the slaves while their forged documents are being submitted to the Republic. According to our reports, they will then be brought to the Joint Harvesting Plantation in Barkrik.

If you head out there now and destroy this outpost, our other team should be in a prime position to intercept the slave convoy when it comes in.
128750:
The colony on Inder VIII is in desperate need of some outside help, {[character]player.name}. Since no station has yet been built orbiting the planet space travel is much more infrequent than other more prominent colonies within the Republic.

The first item that I would like you to fetch for me is soil. There's an amazing lack of fresh, quality soil in the settlements that have sprung up on the planet's surface. The farmer's union has been threatening an all-out withdrawal from Inder if this issue isn't resolved. I'll pay you well if you can get the soil which I've ordered from the Vherokior Tribe to me on time.

128752: Just make sure you head out there prepared, {[character]player.name}.  The shipment you're supposed to fetch is located in a pretty dangerous area, I cannot guarantee that you won't be ambushed by pirates on the way.  Good luck.
128753:
I have three fighters on hand right now, but I need more to be able to run my show. I just received word that one of my best, Grace Tarsis, is being held by a group of Cartel thugs in a deadspace location here in Nakugard, on account of some unsettled debts. If you can find her and bring her back to me in one piece, I'll be a step closer to re-opening my arena and evading the Leisure Group's wrath.

They're keeping her in a brothel in their lair, one that's not really that heavily guarded. If you kill the guards and blow up the brothel, you should be able to get her out and bring her back. If you can do that, you will have my most heartfelt thanks.
128754:
I own and operate a portable arena of cyboerians, cybernetically augmented gladiators who fight each other for show, demonstrating a wide range of Matari martial arts. I was having problems generating revenue in my old home, so I relocated to Nakugard.

Shortly after I got here, though, a problem reared its head. Obviously I'd underestimated the extent of influence wielded by the criminal element in this area. Within weeks, most of my fighters were strung out on various illicit drugs, and I've since had to close up shop. Can't have a show if you don't have performers. And to make matters worse, my contract with the Leisure Group is still in full effect; if I'm not generating my revenue they're not going to be happy, and we most definitely do not want the Leisure Group unhappy.

There are a few things I need to be able to get my arena up and running again. Among these is oxygen; I can't very well run the place if no one can breathe, you understand. If you can go out and find me 150 units of oxygen, I'd be much obliged.
128755:
A few words of introduction are probably in order. I'm Mattheu Rochet, an investment banker and sometime independent trader. I made my fortune a while back, trading robotics after the great capsuleer influx two years ago. Since then, I've been constantly seeking ways to further the cause of the Matari, a proud people with a tragic history for which proper reparations have not been made.

I recently decided to make the Ani constellation my stomping grounds. The situation here is an intriguing one; the simmering conflict between the Ammatar and the old Republic is more evident here than in most other places I've been to, and there is much good work that can be done. In fact, I have a job for you if you feel like lending a hand.

Some associates of mine have set up shop in the Barkrik system's Joint Harvesting Food Packaging stations. They are going to install some equipment so they can keep tabs on some of the shadier elements in there. I need you to bring them a shipment of electronic parts, which they can then use to assemble their covert surveillance gear. Do this quickly and efficiently, and I'll have another job for you.
128756:
According to my sources, there are some interesting times ahead in the Nakugard system. A group of unscrupulous individuals is planning to illegally move in Matari slaves under the guise of contract workers. Some of my contacts in Nakugard are working towards fixing this problem their own way, but I want to have my people standing by in case worst comes to worst.

I have a shipment of small arms coming into the Sisters of EVE Bureau in Lanngisi. The Sisters themselves have nothing to do with it, of course, but they trust me enough to look the other way in this case. I need the weapons delivered to the Krusual Tribe bureau at Nakugard V, where my people will pick them up and put them to good use, if need be. Will you do this for me?
128757:
I've just received word from one of my Nakugard associates that the group I mentioned earlier, the ones who are bringing in the slaves, have stashed away a sizable portion of Vitoc in one of the Joint Harvesting stations in Barkrik, presumably to keep better control of their "contracted labor." Fortunately some of the station personnel in there are on my payroll, so I've managed to have the whole load of it "confiscated."

If you head over there and bring the Vitoc back to the Sisters of EVE Bureau in Lanngisi, we will be one step closer to resoundingly sending out the message. You don't try to bring Minmatar slaves into this constellation, right under everybody's nose.
128758:
I work for the Sanctuary, one of the universe's foremost research institutions. We've recently managed to unearth what we believe could be facts paving the way towards greater understanding of the EVE Gate and how it operates; why it is the way it is. For us to put this information to practical use, however, we require more research data. You seem like the competent type. If you can do a bit of leg work for me, I'll make sure you're rewarded - and you'll be able to rest knowing you did your part in moving the scientific knowledge of today that little bit further forward.

First off, we're getting in a new batch of recently discovered material from a moon in the New Eden system, but our maintenance budget has been running low and many of our tools are in a sad state of disrepair. I have a batch of repair equipment here; if you could see fit to running this over to the SOE Bureau in Lanngisi, I would be much obliged - and so would my staff.
128759:
I've just received word that our station in Lanngisi is about to receive an influx of escaped Matari slaves who have made their way from the depths of Amarr space after their colony was attacked and destroyed. I'm already pulling all the strings I can, but there's one fairly basic thing I seem to have forgotten. There's quite a number of them, and the station will need an extra supply of water.

If you can head down to our Bureau in Traun and pick up water for the newly freed, I will reward you handsomely. I am also likely to have more work for you.
128760:
The Matari refugees are safe and sound now, thanks in no small part to your efforts. The next step for us is to build them some decent living facilities in Lanngisi. To this end we will require building materials.

We've placed a large order for construction blocks at the Joint Harvesting plant in Barkrik. We quite like the idea of their materials helping to build housing for the free people their nation so callously and brutally mistreated. Do this for me, and I will see to it that you are handsomely rewarded.
128761:
The settlers on Inder VIII are becoming increasingly restless due to travel delays on the planet. Simply put, most of them can't afford vehicles which are neccessary to travel through the inhospitable terrain which covers most of the planet. So I came up with a brilliant idea, why not start a rental service where they can rent cheap but effective planetary vehicles to use when neccessary? This will not only please the inhabitants but also make me some money.

I ordered a batch of planetary vehicles from Core Complexion. They are currently waiting to be shipped from {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name}, and I'd like you to do the dirty work for me, for a nice reward of course. I hope you're up to it, I don't want to have to turn to Freedom Extension for a courier job, they're convoys are so damn expensive these days.
