128763:
Crime has run rampant on Inder VIII since it was first settled, mainly due to the extreme lack of law enforcement officers on the planet's surface. Therefore I made a formal suggestion to the Republic Security Forces to relocate some of their personnel here. They agreed to send some of their recruits, but only under the agreement that Urban Management supply them with the necessary equipment.

Most of their equipment has already arrived, but there is one last batch of small arms that hasn't made it here yet. I'd like you to fetch it for me in a jiffy, it will save me the expenses and hassle of ordering another convoy through our bureau.

128765: Well, that was the last job I have for you this time, {[character]player.name}.  I can't thank you enough, you saved me a ton of hassle dealing with those damn bureaucrats back in Abudban, it takes forever and a day to get anything done through them.  Farewell.
128766:
The trial consists of 2 tests. The first test is rather simple. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has set up some practice grounds in Otomainen where our combat pilots train every day. Inside one of these practice grounds you'll find a group of drones, similar to the rogue drones that keep harassing Caldari convoys in the outer constellations. If you manage to destroy all of these drones, you'll find some reports that you must bring back to me. These reports contain nothing of importance, they are just part of the test. Once I have the reports, you will have passed the test.

Just a word of warning though, I've already sent a few pilots on this test and none of them have returned. You might find the wreckage of their ships at the practice grounds, that is unless they fled before the drones managed to destroy them heh heh.

128769:
The final test that I need you to complete is a bit more complicated. One of the major pirate organizations in Okkelen are the Kazka Bandits. They are a constant thorn in our side, and the inadequate security forces here don't seem to have the capacity to exterminate them.

To get straight to the point, I would like you to destroy 5 of their lower-grade cruisers. Bring me the spurs from their pilot's boots, that will be proof enough of your deed. Unlike your previous mission, I don't know exactly where you'll find them. I heard that one of their hideouts is located near one of Otomainen XI's moons, but that's all I know. Return to me once you have all 5 marauder spurs.

I know this might seem like a pain in the rear-end, but I can't give you that voucher unless I know that you've got the skills to track down the prey, sometimes that's required in case we don't have a bookmark to the exact location of your targets. If you can get this done then I'm sure you have what it takes to do any of our missions.

128996:
It's time to send you into the front lines, {[character]player.name}. Yes that means flying into Audesder. It will be dangerous, there's no doubt about that. But I'm sure you're prepared for those kind of risks, considering you signed up for this job in the first place.

Your first task in Audesder is in fact to fly through Audesder, to Aedald. Our intelligence agency wants to place a spy inside their base, to gather intel on their defensive positions, plans and such. It's too risky sending him straight into the Alliance Barracks, so we're going to start with dropping him off at one of their stations in Aedald, where he'll hitch a ride on one of their ships heading to the barracks in Audesder. That's all you need to know for now, {[character]player.name}.

Drop him off at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, then hurry back here. Try not to be seen by the enemy, or you might compromise our agent's mission. Good luck.

129014:
This next mission will most likely be the hardest you've done so far. As you probably know by now, the Minmatar forces have set up a blockade at the main jump gate into Audesder, which they call the 'Minmatar Alliance Defense Brigade'. It's located not far from the stargate itself, and they are equipped with a short-range surveillance tower enabling them to detect any movement of our forces through the gate at all times. Mercenaries like you can generally get past them unhindered, but any official Amarrian strike force sent through there would have to face them or be destroyed.

To get to the point, I want to weaken the Minmatar position near the gate. The best way to do that is to take out their command post, it's destruction will hopefully send them into a disarray, giving us a hefty advantage when we launch our sneak attack. Bring me the Command Post's Bluechip as proof of your deed. Good luck.

129019:
I hope you are, {[character]player.name}, I hope you are … As I mentioned before, this last mission is critical to our campaign. It will definitely test your mettle in battle, and I am certain that you will need backup to complete the assignment. Unfortunately I won't be sending any of my own guys with you, that would most likely compromise the mission anyway, so I do hope you have some merc friends along for the ride.

Your task is to commandeer a full scale assault on the Minmatar Dreadnought Manufacturing Facility in Audesder. It's a massive installation, funded by ORE, the Gallente Federation, the Minmatar Republic and various other allies of theirs. It allows them to quickly build their dreadnought ships and deploy them immediately, with devastating effect on the battle field. If we take it out, it will seriously cripple their war effort, for some at least until they manage to build another one. This should give us the edge we need to attain victory.

You have your orders, {[character]player.name}, now make us proud. May God be with you.

The assignment is simple, and should be completed within 1 hour's time. A group of rogue drones have been activated in the Imperial Navy's testing area within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Each carries a certification result sheet which will be ejected from its interior as soon as it is destroyed. Recover 5 of these sheets and bring them back to your contact. That is all.

- Minas Iksan

129053:
Yes, and now is when it starts to get really dangerous. Again I want you to travel to Kenobanala, this time to a Khanid outpost near Fort Kumar. It was erected to accommodate a large force of Kameira soldiers, because they were not considered ‘good enough' to share living quarters with those of true Amarrian ancestry, nor even the traitorous Ammatar! As you well know, the Kameiras are Minmatar slaves of the Amarr and Khanid who are forced to serve in their military, and who's purpose is usually to be cannon fodder on the front lines in times of war.

I want these Kameiras rescued. But doing that will be tricky. The Khanid complex consists of 3 areas, not including the forward point at the entrance of the deadspace pocket. We have managed to acquire the access codes of the first two acceleration gates, but the 3rd one is unknown to us. Unfortunately the last room of the complex is where the Kameiras living quarters are.

I want you to fly to the Khanid outpost and search the rooms we have access to. Try to find something that will help us unlock the 3rd room, and bring it back here. Perhaps someone among the Khanid guards knows the code.

129065:
We managed to locate a key that should work on the 3rd acceleration gate inside the Khanid outpost where the Kameiras are being held. The Khanid commander you captured revealed its location to us. It's more reliable than an access code, since they probably already changed those after your last attack. You'll find the key in a small container not far from the stargate. It is cloaked and locked but since we know it's exact location now, your ship scanner should be able to detect it. You'll have to destroy the container to acquire the key.

Assuming that the key still works, you should be able to get into the 3rd area of the complex and save the Kameiras from captivity. I'm sure the Khanid and their allies have sent in reinforcements after your last attack, so be prepared for a difficult fight. You'll have to bring some friends along if you wish to have any chance of success.

Just a word of warning though, the Kameiras are normally extremely loyal to the Empire, being more efficiently brainwashed than normal slaves. They are raised with no education of their origins, and it usually takes some time to convince them that we speak the truth. So you'll probably have to take them by force. I'll supply you with some Eforte gas which will paralyze them instantly, allowing your crew to safely transfer them into your cargo hold. Good luck, {[character]player.name}.

It's time to send you on your last assignment, {[character]player.name}. I'm sure this will be one of the most difficult encounter you have ever faced. I'm reluctant to send you on such a suicide mission, but you're the only one qualified for the job that we have. If we sent in our fleet they would be instantly attacked by everyone in Fort Kumar. You on the other hand should be able to get by them unnoticed, if you are cautious enough.

What you need to do is destroy the assembly array of the primary Amarr dreadnought manufacturing facility in Kenobanala. It's pumping out dreadnoughts faster than we imagined, greatly boosting their military strength. If we don't take it out soon, they will be ready for a full scale assault into Audesder, and that will spell disaster for our campaign. I just don't think we're ready yet to face such a large fleet.

And I can't stress this enough, get help! You won't be able to do this alone. Good luck!

129073: Incredible!  Not even in my wildest dreams did I expect you to return alive, and successful!  You've proven to be a huge asset to the Minmatar Republic, and I thank you from the bottom of my heart.  My the light of the Minmatar Republic be with you, {[character]player.name}.
129074: This is outrageous!  I've stuck my neck out for you guys time and time again, yet I still have to prove myself!?
129075:
Ahem, I'm really sorry if I insulted you, {[character]player.name}, but there's nothing I can do about this. I was given the order to test EVERYONE before we send them out into the fray, and if I would ignore that order I risk being demoted. I hope you understand, Ison is very strict about us following her orders.

Now you'll find the details of your test assignment in the briefing which I'm about to load into your NeoCom. Complete the assignment, which I'm sure you'll do in no time, and I'll send you off to Tiadala. And don't forget to read the advice I've uploaded into your journal. Good luck.
129076:
This assignment has been created as a mandatory test to ensure all personnel are adequately equipped and ready for the tasks ahead. This is done for your safety, we have no intention of sending you needlessly to your death.

The assignment is simple, and should be completed within 1 hour's time. A few floating containers have been placed in our training grounds in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, surrounded by sentry guns and spider drones. All you have to do is retrieve the certificates from the containers. Recover 5 of these sheets to your contact. That is all.

- Ison Tiadala
129077: As I suspected, you're up for the job, {[character]player.name}.  Here's the voucher, bring it to Warlord Ison Tiadala, and she'll give you your next assignment.  Good luck out there, soldier.
129079: Do not speak with Warlord Ison unless you have powerful friends at your disposal. Although Ison will begin by sending you into fairly easy encounters, once she's satisfied with your performance you will be sent straight into fleet battles, which I doubt you will be able to face alone and survive. And as my final word of advice, take care not to enter Ammatar space when criminally flagged by their security forces. It will mean certain death.
129080:
Right now I'm looking for {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity}. These tags have been implanted into certain pirates which infest {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space, which they use to identify each other with. To acquire them you will most likely have to kill them, or buy them off someone who did exactly that. I don't really care either way, as long as they have been taken care of I'm satisfied.

This might not be the very best way to confirm deaths, but we've been quite successful in the past using this method. Forgeries are almost non-existent, as each tag costs more to manufacture than it's worth on the bounty market. Not only that but we can usually tell a fake apart from a genuine pirate tag. And they have remarkable survivability, usually found in the charred wreckage of the pirate ships despite everything else, including the pirate's corpse, having been completely vaporized.

You can find the pirates carrying the {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} in many places, but I'd first check the asteroid belts in the surrounding systems as attacking defenseless miners is their favorite past-time. Good luck, and have fun.

129102:
There are millions of minmatars living in the Joas constellation which are not ethnically Nefantar, and many of them are still loyal to the Republic. Even some of the Nefantar living in the area are sympathetic to our cause. Hence there is a strong resistance movement there, which in fact started long before the Rebellion. The strength of the resistance has varied greatly through the years, but the Audesder incident has refueled unrest in the region. And this may be a key factor in our campaign to hold Audesder.

What I'd like you to do is transfer a large arms cache to my contact in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. This contact of mine is an agent of the Joas resistance, he will see to it that the arms cache gets to the right hands. Try to avoid any contact with the Ammatar or their allies, if they find out what you're up to then you'll have one hell of a fight on your hands. Good luck.

129112:
If I have a job available! Of course I do! Do you know how hard it is to find help around here?! With FON organizing boycotts for any organization supporting us and picketing individuals we are affiliated with, I don't really blame them.

Anyway as I've already told you we have some problems with our transportation service. We're using some of our own freighters now to transport goods from Caldari space, but we're short on manpower. If you could stop by {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and bring the 50 construction blocks I had ordered to me, then I'll give you a reward. We need them for the next habitation module we're building for the workers stationed here.

129114: Back with the goods, just as promised.  Here's your reward, make good use of it!  But don't go far, I've got more jobs for you.
129116: <font color=FF0000>You will lose Gallente Federation standing for completing missions for a Caldari corporation.</font>
129117:
I have something slightly more dangerous for you this time, {[character]player.name}. We have 18 surveyors stranded on {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} after Prompt Delivery backed out on our deal to get them moved here a few days ago. Apparently they decided the risks of transporting them through Gallente space were too great. The Federation Navy has threatened to attack any corporations under the Caldari State other than Wiyrkomi, and even with our surveyors on board we fear they might hold true to their word.

If you can get the surveyors here today, I'll give you a hefty reward. Just watch out for those FON fanatics, they're everywhere these days.

129119: Good job.  But enough of these petty courier jobs, it's time to find out your true potential.  Let me know when you're ready, I have a combat mission waiting just for you!
129120:
I have a matter of urgency for you this time, {[character]player.name}. Temko, the Gallentean mercenary organization that we hired, reported to us that one of its surveillance posts in Colelie has been attacked. All of their personnel are currently unavailable, so they pleaded with us to find someone else to investigate the attack. And I think you are the man for the job.

It's been a while since the attack was reported, so we have absolutely no idea what the situation is out there. Hopefully you will be able to track down whoever is responsible and punish them. Good luck.

129122: As I guessed, it was FON which were behind the attack.  They are becoming more bold with each passing day.  I must report this to Central Command immediately.  But before you leave, there's one last task I have for you.
129123:
This time I'd like you to obtain a pass into the Azure Canyon in Colelie. The Azure Canyon is located in a pocket of deadspace which has unusually dense ion clouds, which makes it ideal for creating a massive power plant. The reason we are in Colelie is to start constructing the power station, but so far we've been stuck at square 1 due to our inability to clear the area of Serpentis pirates and FON terrorists.

To get to the point, we're sending in a few squadrons of Temko mercenaries to conduct a quick reconnaissance operation in the Azure Canyon area. But we haven't been able to get past the first acceleration gate since Serpentis agents reconfigured the lock, and it would take far too long to manually navigate through the deadspace pocket. Hence we need the keycard.

You'll find a group of FON ships blockading the gate against anyone affiliated with Wiyrkomi. We believe their leader has the keycard we need in her possession. Her name is Apte Donie, and she should be located at the forward point into the complex. Use whatever means necessary to acquire that keycard, {[character]player.name}.

You'll find him in the Central Command site in Fluekele, he's in charge of all Wiyrkomi operations in Algintal.  Take this voucher, you won't get an appointment without it.  Good luck.
129126: I'm ready for my assignment, Veko ...
129127:
Veko?? You will address me as sir, peon! I will not have some rug-rat insult me like that in public ...

Now where were we? Ah yes, your mission. Well I have a number of nuisances for you to 'take care of', and the first in line is a Gallentean called Alarus Ekire. He's the commander of the military arm of FON, the cowardly tree-huggers who've been sabotaging our operations in Federation space ever since we made that deal with the Gallente government. With him out of the picture, FON's terrorist groups will become more disorganized and less deadly, until they find a suitable replacement anyway.

You'll probably find Alarus in the Tourist area of Azure Canyon in Colelie. They've apparently made a pact with Serpentis to defend that area of deadspace against our attempts to move our own people in there. So you might have a bit of a fight on your hands, but I'm sure you'll manage.

Bring back something to prove that Alarus is no more, and I'll give you your reward.

129133: Now that you've established your worth, let's get started.
129136: Erm, on second thought I don't think I want to work for you.
129137: What?  You just wasted my time for nothing?  Get out of here punk, before I send Temko mercs on your ass.
129139:
Your second mission is to investigate the theft of a batch of drills we ordered recently. They were being shipped to our survey station in Colelie when their convoy was ambushed by unknown assailants. We have so far not retrieved any witnesses, and have not found any evidence at the crime scene linking FON or Serpentis to the attack. However gut feeling tells me it must have been FON. Serpentis would have taken the crew and held them for ransom, but we have found no evidence that they are still alive.

I'd like you to get to the bottom of this, {[character]player.name}. Fly to the FON recruitment center in Fluekele and see what you can find there. Return to me with anything that might implicate their involvement in the attack.

Dismissed.

129143:
The next job is going to be a bit more difficult than your last two assignments. This time I want you to infiltrate the Azure Canyon complex and find a place called 'The Black Market'. We have reliable information that a regiment of Temko mercenaries are being held in a prison facility there. They were sent on a reconnaissance mission into the complex a few days ago, but never returned.

I advise you to avoid a direct confrontation with the Serpentis forces at the Black Market. Just grab the mercenaries and flee, they are your number one priority in this mission. We are running out of mercenaries already, we can't afford to lose these Temko personnel.

I also recommend that you finish this assignment in a timely manner. My time is precious.

129149: Something urgent just came up. The Survey Station in Colelie was attacked by FON, probably in retaliation for our recent actions against them. 129153: I see you're back in one piece.  Maybe you're not as useless as I first thought.  In that case, I have something more you could do for me ...
129155:
Now I want you to get us some Zemnar. The Survey Station in Colelie suffered heavy casualties, and their antibiotic supplies are stretched to the limit. On top of that there has been a viral outbreak which could cause many deaths if we don't get them the Zemnar they need fast. Now a few surveyors and engineers are expendable, but this threatens the entire outpost and could compromise our operation in Colelie!

You'll find a stock of Zemnar not far from the Pend Insurance station in Fluekele, in their storage bin. They refuse to share it with us, probably as a result of pressure from the various nature lover groups which have been protesting our presence here. So we are going to have to take it by force. Do whatever it takes to get a hold of that Zemnar, and drop it off at our factory in this system. One of my lackeys will transport it to Colelie. Just don't reveal who you're working for, to anyone! Now get moving!

129159:
You've proven to be fairly reliable so far, {[character]player.name}, so I believe I can trust you for a rather sensitive assignment. We have a traitor in our ranks, or to be more precise in the ranks of the Temko mercenaries we hired. His name is Eule Vitrauze and he's apparently working for Friends of Nature on the side. We believe he's the reason the last Temko operation in the Azure Canyon complex failed.

I would ask the Temko to deal with him themselves, but Gara believes that if we make an outsider do the job and make it seem like we weren't involved in his death then our agent within FON will not be compromised. You'll probably find Eule orbiting a security outpost inside the Central Administration complex. But don't worry, the other Temko ships will not come to his aid, all you have to do is face him one-on-one, and then return to me once his ship has been turned to dust.

Dismissed.
129160:
You've proven to be fairly reliable so far, {[character]player.name}, so I believe I can trust you for a rather sensitive assignment. We have a traitor in our ranks, or to be more precise in the ranks of the Temko mercenaries we hired. His name is Eule Vitrauze and he's apparently working for Friends of Nature on the side. We believe he's the reason the last Temko operation in the Azure Canyon complex failed.

I would ask the Temko to deal with him themselves, but Gara believes that if we make an outsider do the job and make it seem like we weren't involved in his death then our agent within FON will not be compromised. You'll probably find Eule orbiting a security outpost inside the Central Administration complex. But don't worry, the other Temko ships will not come to his aid, all you have to do is face him one-on-one, and then return to me once his ship has been turned to dust.

Dismissed.
129161: Although it pains me to say it, you've managed to complete all the tasks I assigned to you on time and we owe you one.  Just don't expect any medals of honor, you're a secret agent working for us and the less our enemies know of you the better.  Now before I get all mooshy with you I suggest you turn your flabby tush around and head off to the Grand Future Information Center in Jolia, General Gara Kort has a few missions for you there.  Now be off with you.
129164:
Since you've been approved by Veko Tallaja, I guess you're suited for a few missions vital to our plans here in Algintal. To get straight to the point, we are currently on a campaign to rid the deadspace areas we purchased from Federate sources of pirates and violent protesters, namely the Friends of Nature organization which has been causing us much grief since we came to Algintal. To complete our objectives we have been forced to hire mercenaries which are permitted entrance into Federation space, considering that the government steadfastly refuses to allow any Caldari State military presence in their sovereign space. Which is understandable considering the current political climate.

Wiyrkomi sacrificed much to get this deal, and we definitely are not backing out with our tails behind our legs. Our CEO has publicly announced that we are firmly against any Caldari State incursions into Federation space, incurring the wrath of the State Chief Executive Panel which has fined us for rediculous reasons simply out of spite. And on top of that our lease on the deadspace pockets within Federation space could be annulled at any time if the Senate gives in to the protesters.

So now that you're briefed of the situation, it's time to get started. Your first target is an old abandoned Federation Navy ammunitions storage in Jolia. We have confirmed reports that the military arm of FON uses the facilities located there to store their weapons of mass destruction. Take it out and their terrorist operation in Jolia will be crippled. Over and out.

129166: With your mission a success, FON will have been dealt a serious blow.  But if I know them correctly, they'll use this as an excuse to launch a counter-attack.  Meanwhile though I'd like to start concentrating on the Serpentis.  Stick around and I'll give you more details on that.
129168: <font color=FF0000>You will lose standing with the Gallente Federation for attacking Friends of Nature.  Despite Wiyrkomi's insistence that FON are a terrorist organization, the Federation thinks of them only as a minor nuissance.  And in fact only a part of FON partake in fighting Wiyrkomi, the larger part of it is non-violent.</font>
129169: I would like to sign up for some work, if you have any.
129170: Before I let you work for me you're going to have to supply me with a voucher from Veko Tallaja, located in Central Command in Fluekele.
129171:
Before I let you work for me you're going to have to supply me with a voucher from Veko Tallaja, located in Central Command in Fluekele..

Do not accept this mission if you have not completed the pre-required mission sequence in Central Command or have acquired the neccessary voucher some other way.
129172: Now that you've established your worth, let's get started.
129173: I'd like to work for you.
129177:
Here's the deal. I'm a senior journalist for the Scope, and I'm working on an in-depth piece about the Wiyrkomi project in this constellation and the FON's (Friends of Nature's) struggle to counteract their plans. It's a big piece, and I have several reporters working on different strands in different places, so assistance from a fast-moving capsule pilot such as yourself is always needed.

As a matter of fact, I have a job for you right now if you want it. One of my reporters just completed a few interviews with Colelie project workers who are on break from the project at the Wiyrkomi Factory in Fluekele. He says he managed to get some juicy tidbits from them about the way Wiyrkomi handles its workers; grist for the cause, to mangle a metaphor.

Bring me back the interview transcripts from Fluekele, and I'll pay you as much as the agency allows me to dole out. How about it?
129178:
As I said earlier, it's time for us turn our attention to the Serpentis. The Serpentis problem should in fact be easier to deal with than our war with the Gallente environmentalists, but at the same time they are the deadlier foe. The Serpentis are not at war with us due to some fanatical idealogy, instead they are simply here to protect their financial interests. I'm quite certain that as soon as they see this 'war' becoming unprofitable in the long run, they will retreat from their positions in our territory.

So to start off we need to make them know we mean business. And to do that I want you to take out one of their drug convoys. I had the Temko mercenaries under my command conduct a massive surveillance operation, which eventually revealed one of the Serpentis's drug convoy routes. I'll supply you with a bookmark that should lead you to one such convoy. Destroy it and report back to me. And remember, the cargo should not be brought back here, I want nothing to do with their contraband.

129180: Good job.  I've sent a message to the Serpentis outpost in Azure Canyon, claiming responsibility for the attack on their convoy.  With enough pressure on them, I'm sure they will cave in.  But there's more to be done, one convoy won't affect the Serpentis much at all.  So stay tuned.
129181: The Serpentis convoy has been destroyed, as you requested General.
129182:
It seems the Wiyrkomi Corporation isn't being entirely forthcoming when it comes to their labor practices. That was some very interesting material you brought back from Fluekele. So good, in fact, that I feel a sudden, almost physical urge to follow up on it.

One of my top reporters just came in from Oursulaert. I want you to take him to the Wiyrkomi factory in Jolia, where some highly classified contacts are waiting for him. Since Wiyrkomi won't give us the straight dope, we're going to have to turn to alternative sources. I'll find out the truth yet.

Take my guy to Jolia and I'll see to it that you're rewarded handsomely.
129183:
Something fishy's going on here. Word just came in over the feednet: apparently, a FON strike squad staged an attack on a surveillance outpost in Colelie belonging to Temko, a mercenary organization contracted by Wiyrkomi to protect their holdings and help them gain a foothold in this constellation.

This doesn't feel right at all. First, FON doesn't engage in out-and-out terrorism; their battles take place on politico-ideological fronts. Second, had it been FON, why would they advertise that fact? Their tactic is the swaying of public opinion, not the destruction of their opponents' assets. This has all the hallmarks of a frame-up.

An old friend of mine who's well-connected in this area says he's managed to obtain the data core from one of the attacking ships' computers as it was brought in by salvager vessels. If we can get it into the hands of our specialists here, they might be able to extract some clues regarding the attackers' real identities and intentions. Head out to Parchanier and get me that data core. A lot may be riding on this.
129184:
Your next assignment is a pretty important one. Elere Febre is a Serpentis agent working in Fluekele, which we believe is their contact with Friends of Nature, as we've detected FON agents visiting her habitation module multiple times in the past week alone. FON are desperate to not let news of this alliance between them and Serpentis leak to the public. I'm not even sure if the majority of FON's members know of their dealings with pirates. Public opinion in favor of FON will undoubtedly plummet once people believe there is a connection between them and violent criminals.

Now killing her should be simple. The difficult part is retrieving evidence of her involvement with FON. I'm counting on her leaving some sort of evidence in her habitation module, which is located at Fluekele IV's sixth moon. Find the habitation module and destroy it, search the wreckage for anything that survived which may implicate FON's relationship with Serpentis. Return to me with your findings. Hopefully we'll be able to kill two flies in one swing with the completion of this mission.

129186: With Elere out of the picture, the Serpentis will hopefully have a more difficult time dealing with FON.  Friends of Nature are not the sort of organization to strike deals with pirates
129188: Fly to Fluekele IV's sixth moon and find Elere Febre's habitation module.  Destroy it and retrieve her data log from the wreckage.
129189:
Okay, it's about to hit the fan. We've stumbled on to something very very bad indeed. It's so bad, in fact, that I'm not even going to come close to covering it in my article. The people behind this cannot know, under any circumstances, that we know about their plans.

I can't tell you any more at this moment, but I'll tell you what I can do. I'm going to ask you for one more favor, and then I'm going to give you a contact within the FON. They have some work they need done, and since they're generally not the travelling types they could use a big strapping capsuleer to help them. But first I need to ask you one more favor.

I've collected the data I've accrued in the making of my article into one dossier, which I need brought to a safe place. Word's just reached us that Wiyrkomi have this place under wraps, so I've become compromised. I'll have to jack in and do the rest of this remotely.

Bring my dossier to my contact in Parchanier, and I'll hand over our analysis of the evidence you got for us. It's bad, friend. It's real bad.
129190:
The Serpentis have so far refused to meet any of our demands. I expected as much, a few convoys and agents are expendable in their eyes. But it's time to turn up the heat. This time I would like you to gather the best pilots you can muster and launch an offensive directly into the Azure Canyon of Colelie. Head straight towards the Black Market pocket and destroy the Serpentis Stronghold. If you can, try to recover something that will allow us to blackmail them, such as computer logs, prisoners, anything.

I suspect that Salvador Sarpati will think twice about going up against Wiyrkomi after suffering the loss of such a costly installation. If all goes as planned, the Serpentis will retreat from the Azure Canyon, giving us full access to the ion clouds.

129192:
Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. I see that you brought back a data chip containing transaction logs from within the Black Market of Azure Canyon, that will most definitely help us in our dealings with the Serpentis. I'm sure some of their customers would be less than happy to find out their involvement with a pirate organization was leaked to Federation authorities, and I'm sure the Serpentis will be desperate to keep us from uploading this data to our contacts within The Scope ...

But our work doesn't end here. We still need to deal with those fanatics in Friends of Nature ...
129193:
As your final assignment for me, {[character]player.name}, I want you obliterate the FON headquarters, located in Deltole. As you probably know, Friends of Nature mainly consists of civilians which are protected by Federation law. They claim to be a peaceful organization fighting for 'the environment', but in fact a large portion of its members are nothing but terrorist scum who are willing to sacrifice human life to protect a heap of rocks and gas clouds. I've come to realize that no matter how hard we hit them, they will always come back for more. So the only course of action I see is to exterminate the lot of them.

Unfortunately, the Federation will not look kindly upon us killing its civilians, despite them being affiliated with Friends of Nature. They don't have the same view of FON as we do. So it is vital that you do not reveal who you are working for to anyone. If you do, I'll make certain you won't live to see another day.

129195:
Awesome job, {[character]player.name}. I'm puzzled why there were no live guards at their headquarters, just drones and sentry guns, but at least their structures were destroyed. Now I just hope most of their personnel were located inside. Either way, you did what I asked you to and for that you deserve your reward.

Dismissed.
129196: The FON headquarters has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.
129198:
Welcome to the Nickel & Dime Store, {[character]player.name}. It is a humble little shop owned and operated by the Thukker tribe, catering to the needy souls in this beautiful constellation. Hm, something tells me you can be of some assistance to us ― perhaps you've worked for the Thukkers in the past?

Let's see if you've got what it takes to help our fledgling business grow. I have a small task for you: nothing complicated or risky, but it should let me gauge your talents. Deliver a few crates of goods to a nearby station for me. The rewards are modest, since this is such an easy task, but it's only the start.
129199:

129200:
Good work on your previous assignment. Despite it being a tedious one, you pulled it off without any qualms. Now for something a little more interesting.

You see, things have not been easy around here lately. The Caldari mega-corp Wiyrkomi is intent on tapping into the vast natural resources found in the constellation, much to the dismay of the many environmentalists here in the Federation. The struggle between the two sides draws unwanted attention to our little enterprise here and is making our operation difficult. Down the road, I might be tempted to have you help us with this unpleasant situation. But not just yet. First, we have to take care of another small problem that just came up.

The Serpentis drug lords are out in force here in Algintal, overseeing traffic between Federation and Republic space. We Thukkers are not into the drug scene, so we generally leave them alone. The same applies for them, for the most part. Live and let live, huh? Thing is, many of the Serpentis have grown too fond of their own goods and can get a little wild at times. One such incident occurred the other night when a gang of renegade Serpentis junkies stole some goods we were receiving from our associates in the Republic. The goods aren't all that valuable, but we must send a clear sign to the Serpentis that our goods are to be left alone.

I know that the fools who stole our goods are relaxing at the Skeleton Comet complex over in Deltole. If you're willing to go over there and teach them a lesson, a hard lesson ― a permanent lesson, get me? ― then I would be much obliged. And if you could return with some of the goods they stole, I'd be even happier.

129202:
Oh, {[character]player.name}, you've come at an opportune moment. Things are progressing as I feared they would. The continuous struggle between Wiyrkomi and the activists have cast a spotlight on the constellation. While we here are the Nickel & Dime Store are running a perfectly legal business, our associates and clients like to operate in the dark. Already, I've lost several important clients, and some employees are getting restless. So much so that I'm having difficulties making my more demanding deliveries.

Unfortunately, I do not have the means or the knowledge to do much about the situation, but my business associate Iliere Angetyn is a most resourceful Gallentean, and I'm sure he's already contemplating how to put things right. But Angetyn doesn't deal with just anyone. Only those clearly in favor with the Trust Partners company get his attention. So I have a proposal for you. Run an errand for me that one of my just-departed couriers was supposed to, and I'll give you a Trust Partners Business Card. Show this to Angetyn and he's certain to offer you something lucrative.

The errand in question is a simple delivery over the border into the Republic. It has a very small chance of getting you in trouble with the customs, but I'm sure a resourceful pilot such as yourself can pick the right route to avoid any unwanted attention.

129204: Excellent! I'm already feeling more confident about this whole thing. I think I can count on you and Angetyn together to sort this mess out.
129205: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Now, take the business card I just gave you and go talk to Iliere Angetyn.
129206: I want you to head over to the Wiyrkomi surveillance outpost here in Augnais and take out their shuttle. Make sure you locate the surveillance recordings; confiscate them and bring them back to me.
129207:
Hm. Alright. You see, Algintal was such a nice place a few years back. The traffic through its systems and the many tourists meant we could operate with minimal risk. But now that has all changed with the arrival of the Wiyrkomi corporation and their lackeys, Roden Shipyards. What were once standard border-running operations now require much more time and effort to pull off.

What is worse, the Caldari think they own the place just because they exploited a loophole in the trade agreement between the State and the Federation. They're trying to muscle us out. I want to nip that bullshit in the bud and strike back at the Wiyrkomi. That's where you come in, {[character]player.name}.

The Wiyrkomi have installed a surveillance outpost here in Augnais. The problem is, I only found out about it a few days ago, after I'd just completed an important deal with a Republic contact of mine. If the Wiyrkomi listened in on the deal, they could compromise the Thukkers' position here in Algintal. I thought it was too late to do anything about it, but the security measures of the Wiyrkomi are working against them here. The surveillance outpost operates in total radio silence and only sends out its recordings in a shuttle once a week to the Wiyrkomi headquarters over in Fluekele. The shuttle will depart tomorrow, so there is still time to take care of this ... problem. I want you to head over to the surveillance outpost and take out that shuttle. Make sure you locate the surveillance recordings and confiscate them. Bring them back to me, and we're back on track.
129208: I know how to keep my mouth shut. What kind of work do you have?
129209: Nice. Good work. But now something else has come up...
129210: Head over to the Skeletal Comet in Deltole, locate the wrecked ship, and get the drugs out.
129211:
It seems every time the Thukkers get themselves in trouble they come running to me to clean things up. I mean, I can't complain ― the Thukkers don't admit many foreigners into their ranks, so I'm in a privileged position, but still...

Anyway, as you might know, this constellation is full of activists fighting the Wiyrkomi and their plans to "spoil the natural beauty" to harvest resources. We've gotten into contact with some of the more belligerent activists, making them think we're here to support them, but of course we're just using them for our own benefit. We've provided them with some old ships and have even been providing full maintenance service for them. What they don't know is that we've used the opportunity when we service the ships to stuff their hidden cargo hatches full of contraband for them to ferry around for us. Heh. Pretty neat, eh? Yeah, well, it would be if these idiot FON guys would just shuttle peacefully around.

Thing is, one of them had to get into a fight with some Serpentis pirate over in Deltole and get blown to pieces. Of course the ship was full of drugs, and we need to clear that stuff up before anyone notices. Can you head over to the Skeletal Comet over in Deltole, locate the wrecked ship, and get the drugs out? I suspect they must be spoiled by now, what with the explosion and all, but we need to get them out anyway before the activists ― or worse, the authorities ― find them.
129212: Absolutely. What do I need to know?
129213: You got it, boss. On my way.
129214: That's what I like to hear. Git 'er done.
129215: I want you to head over to Fluekele and drop this container off at the Pend Insurance station, where a friend of mine will place it in a safe-deposit box there. I know it's a trivial thing I'm asking, but this is very sensitive material that absolutely can't get into the wrong hands ... and, besides, I need more time to prepare for your big mission.
129216:
Yes, in fact. I'm feeling very confident in your abilities, so I'm setting up a big job for you. But before that, I need you to take care of a smaller matter for me. I have acquired certain items that cast Veko Tallaja, the operation supervisor for Wiyrkomi here in Algintal, in a rather negative light. I'm not going to use this stuff just now, but I need to store it somewhere safe.

I want you to head over to Fluekele and drop it off at the Pend Insurance station there. A friend of mine will then place it in a safe-deposit box there. I know it's a trivial thing I'm asking, but this is very sensitive material that absolutely can't get into the wrong hands ... and, besides, I need more time to prepare for your big mission.
129217: Anything else come up for me?
129218: Hey, as long as there's a decent, big job coming next, I'm willing.
129219: Done, {[character]agentID.name}. Now what's this big job you mentioned?
129220: Patience, my friend. I just need to arrange one more thing. Talk to me again in a minute.
129221:
Some smugglers have built themselves a nice little hideout near here. We're not playing any games here, so killing them is the only item on the agenda. It was hell to track them down, so make sure you take them all out in one go so I don't have to repeat the process later.

If you pull this off with style, I'm sure some associates of mine would love for you to work a bit for them. When you bring me those dead smugglers' DNA, I'll give you some ship logs that my associates need to tamper with a bit to make them seem as innocent as a virgin's butt. Those logs should be ample proof to them that you're a trusted friend.
129222:
Algintal has always been a favored spot for smugglers. It's far enough out of the way so as not to attract too much attention from the authorities. Besides us at Trust Partners, the Serpentis are out here in force, as well as several independents. Usually we try to stay well clear of each other, but sometimes a group arrives that thinks it can muscle everyone else out. One such group has been making a nuisance of itself recently, and it's time to take them out. We've played Mr. Nice Guy until now, but no longer.

The smugglers in question have built themselves a nice little hideout near here. We're not playing any games here, so killing them is the only item on the agenda. It was hell to track them down, so make sure you take them all out in one go so I don't have to repeat the process later.

If you pull this off with style, I'm sure some associates of mine would love for you to work a bit for them. When you bring me those dead smugglers' DNA, I'll give you some ship logs that my associates need to tamper with a bit to make them seem as innocent as a virgin's butt. Those logs should be ample proof to them that you're a trusted friend.
129223: You kidding? I was born ready. Watchya got?
129224: Mission accomplished. Those smugglers won't be bothering you again.
129225: That's what I like to hear, {[character]player.name}. You've proven yourself to me, at least. Glad to have you onboard.
129226:
We try to keep our operation here at the Forgery under the radar, with a little bribery on the side to take care of over-zealous bureaucrats. Still, even if we're not exactly advertising our services we've established a rather formidable reputation in the underworld. We like to keep things as they are and sometimes we have to engage in some aggressive weed-killing to rid ourselves of unwanted baggage that can come back and haunt us later.

Which brings me to the job I want to offer you. A few months ago we entered an agreement with some local thugs here in Deltole. At the time we were anxious as to what the Serpentis druglords at the Skeleton Comet were up to, so we hired these guys to snoop around for us. Things went well for awhile, but now we have reason to believe the thugs have been playing both sides, offering their service to the Serpentis as well. That won't do, of course. We gave the thugs a ComLink encoder/decoder for secure communications. But what we didn't tell them was that the encoder also acts as a bug device. We only put it in their as a precaution, never intending to use it, but now we need to retrieve the encoder to confirm our believe that the thugs are two-faced bastards.

Get me that encoder so I can exact my punishment on them. I've already hatched a devious plan, if I say so myself, for framing those thugs and setting them up for the Serpentis to chew on. But first I need that encoder. The thugs have entrenched themselves deep inside the Skeleton Comet complex, acting as any other small time smuggling cartel. The encoder should be located in their Relay Station, so target that.

129228:
I'm glad you came along, {[character]player.name}. As you probably already know the arrival of the Wiyrkomi corporation in the constellation has stirred things up a bit. Tourism is way down and the authorities are unfairly blaming us smugglers. It's getting harder and harder to conduct any decent smuggle run and we have to be twice as careful. Not that it harms us here at the Forgery much, if anything it only makes our services even more sought after.

A Minmatar associate of mine needs to get a large quantity of high quality X-Instinct into Gallente space, but he's not willing to risk the Federation customs at times like these. That's were we come into the picture. I need a small favor from you. I ordered a large quantity of dolls, but they're sitting in a TranStellar Shipping warehouse over in Adiere. Are you willing to fetch them for me? It's a trivial assignment, I know, but I'm positively swamped at the moment, as you can well understand.

129230:
You've come through for me big time in the past, {[character]player.name}. So I have an important task for you now. First, I'll let you in on a little secret. You've probably already encountered some of the activists here in Algintal, fighting to get Wiyrkomi out. Well, we Thukkers are in the same boat. We also want Wiyrkomi out. Not because we care for the environment, but because Wiyrkomi's presence here is hitting our business hard. But the problem is we can't draw attention to ourselves. If Wiyrkomi or the Federation start perceiving the Thukker tribe as a real threat in the constellation they will come down on our heads real hard. And we don't want that to happen, now do we?

So we've been trying to manipulate things as much as we can behind the scenes. By discreetly supporting the more militant elements of FON we hope the activists can be of enough nuisance to the Wiyrkomi that the Caldari will flee with their tail between their legs. We've used every method we can come up with for this, including stirring some of the Serpentis druglords into action.

A few weeks ago a powerful druglord associated with the Angel Cartel, known as Don Rico, agreed to help out. At the time we didn't think that FON would amount to much, so we invested pretty heavily in getting Don Rico involved. The results were immediate and at first his diligence thrilled us. But recently it has started to get out of hand, with Don Rico getting ever more outrageous fighting Wiyrkomi and their cronies. Our sources close to the druglord tell us that Don Rico has grown much too fond of his own product and is completely out of control.

We need to restrain Don Rico before his actions jeopardize the whole operation. I know that the Federation Navy and CONCORD are starting to take notice and the last thing we need is for him to fall into their hands. He knows too much. So we need to take him out quickly. And you're just the pilot for the job. Unfortunately, I don't know the exact whereabouts of Don Rico. He likes to cruise around in his pleasure yacht and he could be lurking anywhere in the constellation. We need to flush him out and I know just the thing to stir him into showing his face. He owns a drug factory not far from here and I want you to raid it. Kill a few of his henchmen. Don Rico's greatest weakness is his vanity and vengefulness. A direct attack on his possessions will certainly make him come screaming in revenge. And that's our chance to take him out. But first, the raid. All Don Rico's henchmen have a smuggler signet. Collect a few of these signets and bring them to me. Let's see what happens then.

129232:
Just as I predicted the raid on the drug factory got just the results we wanted. Don Rico is screaming fury on all the underworld channels trying to find the culprit. Don't worry, we'll keep you identity hidden long enough for you take him out for good. It's a dangerous assignment, but if you don't do it you'll have Don Rico's revenge hanging over your head for the rest of your life. Sorry to put you in this position, but look at it from my point of view, it was a win-win situation. Anyway, you're getting handsomely rewarded for all of this, so don't sulk too much.

When you accept this mission I'll give you the coordinates to the place where Don Rico is hiding out at the moment. Like all druglords he's even more paranoid than I am, so rest assured he's got artillery and plenty of it. Perhaps bringing a few friends along would be a good idea.

129234: Very well done, {[character]player.name}! I have an urgent message for you to deliver to Drusk Amakkit over in Parchanier. He will explain matters to you. Please hurry!
129235:
You probably know already that we've been subtly manipulating FON and Serpentis into working together against Wiyrkomi. While this is not without risk we feel it's the best chance of driving the Caldari megalomaniacs out of Algintal so we can get back to some serious smuggling.

But things are now rapidly progressing out of control and we have to get more directly involved to get things under control again. There's this Serpentis agent by the name of Elere Febre that we linked up with a FON contact. Febre is the main liaison between the two sides and has worked wonders in the short time she's been involved. But according to this message you brought me her cover is blown. Wiyrkomi is on to her and is probably planning to take her out as we speak. Or worse, take her into custody and interrogate her. We cannot let that happen as she could then reveal the Thukkers involvement.

Time is of the essence here, so the first thing we need to do is distract the Wiyrkomi until we come up with a real plan. I don't have time to assemble squad of my own so some improvisation is the order of the day. You're the only one here, so I guess I must rely on you. We must instigate a fake attack on the Wiyrkomi by FON. To do that we need an authentic FON banner. I know that FON has an operation station inside the Skeletal Comet complex over in Deltole. It's overlooking the huge rogue drone hive in there. What do you say about raiding the place and steal me a FON banner? Return with it here and we're half way home in throwing Wiyrkomi off the scent.

129237:
I must congratulate you on being so quick in bringing me the banner. I wasn't feeling all that optimistic about our chances in thwarting Wiyrkomi as they were already on the move, but now things look different. I've already put in motion a fake sabotage attack on one of the Wiyrkomi stations in the system. All my agents there need is the banner to leave behind after the raid.

The Caldari are a suspicious lot, so any member of the Thukkers entering one of their stations is bound to attract attention. But you're presence there will not. To complete your recent success in getting the banner all you need to do now is getting the banner into the Wiyrkomi station and we'll take care of the rest.

129239:
The sabotage attack on the Wiyrkomi station in Jolia was only a limited success, but it was enough to divert their attention long enough for Elere Febre to cover her tracks. She's abandoned her habitation module and gone into hiding for the time being. Wiyrkomi is bound to raid her place soon, but she was careful in leaving no traces of her own DNA there, though she left a fake one that hopefully will have them running in circles.

But there is still one loose end we need to tie up. Febre's contact within the FON is making a nuisance of himself and before he does something rash we must take him out. Before Febre went into hiding she set up a meeting with the guy to discuss the future. She gave me the coordinates for that meeting and I want you to go over there and kill the guy. Just remember, even if he's a pansy activists doesn't mean he's a walkover and he may very well have some backup with him. So take care. And perhaps take some backup with you. The situation is intense and you never know what might be lying ahead.

But good job, nevertheless. We can now breath easier knowing that all loose ends have been tied up. Wiyrkomi will get nowhere with their enquiry.
129243:
Great to hear that. Now the first task I have for you is pretty dangerous. We were expecting a large group of tourists here from Du Annes today but unfortunately their cruiser's warp-drive broke down in Deltole. On top of that they stumbled into a deadspace pocket filled with rogue drones. The last we heard of them was their distress signal indicating they were under attack. I can only hope that they managed to escape, but at this time it's impossible to tell.

I would like you to fly into the deadspace pocket where they were last seen and search for them. Destroy every rogue drone ship that you find. If they are still alive they might need some help repairing their warp-drive, if not then they at least would need help fighting off the drones. Good luck.

129246: Try talking to some in the vicinity and get back to me once you have a Trust Partners Business Card.
129247: Before I even contemplate working with you, I must be certain you are a true friend of the Trust Partners. For me to be sure, you need to give me a Trust Partners Business Card. You can get one by doing well for other agents of our firm. Try talking to some in the vicinity and get back to me once you have an appropriate business card.
129248: I will return with a Trust Partners Business Card.
129249: Yeah, I'll get right on it, loser.
129252: Very good, I can see you are to be trusted with sensitive Thukker matters. I think we can begin to do business.
129253: I'm not sure what you mean. How can I prove that?
129254:
The next mission in line is rather simple. A Federal Intelligence officer is scheduled to inspect our outpost this week. He was supposed to arrive later today but his ship was delayed. The Federal Intelligence Office demanded that we provide him with a quick transport so that he is able to complete his assignment on time. My take on this entire situation is that they did this on purpose just to see how far we're willing to go to please Federation authorities.

Now, considering that you completed your last assignment with flying colors I assume this will be a piece of cake for someone of your caliber. Just pick up the FIO officer at {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and get him back here as quickly as possible.

129256: Nicely done.  But don't leave yet, there's one more task I have in store for you.
129257: Do you have anything from a member of the Trust Partners to show me? I'm sorry if I come across as a bit paranoid, but in my line of work it's vital to know who you're dealing with. If you don't have any documents from another Trust Partner agent, I suggest you go talk to someone else.
129258: Ok, let's see those documents you have, then.
129259: Don't worry, you can trust me. I have with me ship logs from another agent of the Trust Partners.
129260: Sorry, I don't have any documents for you.
129261: No sweat, just come and talk to me when you have the right documents for me.
129262: You have some ship logs, eh? Could you hand them over, please?
129263: You have some ship logs, eh? Could you hand them over, please?
129264: Ah, they're from Angetyn. Excellent! Yes, I can doctor them for him. Not that I haven't done so many times in the past, mind you. But what to do with you? Angetyn only sends me pilots he thinks highly of, so let's see if you're as talented as he thinks.
129265: I have no time to deal with just anyone. Do you have some business with me? I'm waiting for an urgent message from an agent friend of mine. If you don't have the message then you can be of no help to me. So don't bother trying to talk to me any further unless you have that message with you.
129266: I have an urgent message from Krester Rupptofs to you. He told me you would tell me what the big hurry is.
129267: A message from Krester? I was expecting as much. Here, let's see what it says.
129268: I do not have any message for you, sorry. I will come back later when I have one.
129269: Ah! This is urgent indeed! It seems the Wiyrkomi bastards are more clever than I gave them credit for.
129270: I hope to see you later when you have something of interest for me.
129271: Give Drusk the message from Krester Rupptofs.
129272:
Now that you've finished the most pressing tasks I have, it's time to send my report to Miloise Roden in the Roden Shipyard headquarters. It contains some pretty sensitive information, so I want it kept safe and secure until it's in the hangar of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Don't mess this up!

Dismissed.
129273: Now that you've finished the most pressing tasks I have, it's time to send my report to Miloise Roden in the Roden Shipyard headquarters.  It contains some pretty sensitive information, so I want it kept safe and secure until it's in the hangar of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Don't mess this up!
129274: You've done all I've asked you to, with style.  I suggest you take a look at the Wiyrkomi Survey Station in Colelie or the Command Center in Fluekele if you're in need of some more work.  Good luck!
129275: Tell me what kind of business we're talking about and I'll think about it.
129276:
Ok, I'm here on official business from {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. I was sent here to inspect the Central Command station of Wiyrkomi in Algintal, and as a side project keep an eye out on Roden Shipyards, who've been Wiyrkomi's primary allies in Federation space.

Now my first objective is to make sure there isn't any illegal trade going on here. I haven't been able to discover any contraband during my stay here, but I'd like to test something before I fill my first report. I'd like to see how well prepared the Temko mercenaries guarding this installation are concerning illegal goods. So I want somebody inconspicuous to try to infiltrate the compound with drugs inside of his cargo hold. You look like just the person for that assignment.

You'll find the drugs on {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}, simply grab them and bring them to me. Federation customs officials won't touch you, they know it's my crash. Temko don't however, hence the test. If you get attacked by Temko, then flee and come back later, I'll explain everything to them once the test is complete.

129278: So the guards didn't lift a finger to stop you?  Intriguing.  I'll have to mention this in my report!  But don't go far, I have some more work for you.
129279:
For your second assignment I'd like you to investigate a Wiyrkomi storage facility in Jolia. I stumbled upon some documents revealing it's location while inside the Central Command control tower. They were a bit startled when I informed them of what I had discovered, so I'm thinking something fishy might be afloat there.

I will upload a bookmark into your journal which sends you to a deadspace pocket. Inside you'll find this storage facility. Take a look inside, and tell me what you find. Thanks.

129281: So they replaced the sign on the acceleration gate leading to the storage facility with one leading to a drone hive?  This will go straight into my report.  I'll also take a look at this data chip you found in the storage facility itself, but I'm sure there's nothing of interest inside it.  If they knew you were coming and managed to replace the sign on the acceleration gates, they probably had enough time to empty the storage containers as well.  But good work anyway.
129282: First of all, do you have something for me...? If you know what I'm talking about, then hand it over, please. If you don't, then I'm sorry, but I don't have anything for you.
129283: First of all, do you have something for me...? If you know what I'm talking about, then hand it over, please. If you don't, then I'm sorry, but I don't have anything for you.
129285: I'm sorry, I have no idea what you're talking about.  Ta.
129286: I'm sorry, I must have misunderstood.  I don't have what you're looking for.
129287: Bring the top-secret information into Preaux Gallot's possession.
129289: Very well, then, let's see it.
129290: Excellent, thank you. I'm going to take a look at this; get back to me in a minute or two.
129291:
First, a proper introduction. I'm Preaux Gallot, one of FON's chief coordinators in this area. As you may know, the Wiyrkomi corporation is trying to move into this area, corrupting the vast tracts of natural beauty found here with their horrible industry. Moreover, the piece of evidence you just brought me seems to indicate there are things at play here far worse than we originally suspected.

It appears the Wiyrkomi corporation has been hiring mercenaries to stage attacks on their own outposts in the area, attacks which they then frame us for in order to lessen our stature in the public eye. We need to put a stop to this as soon as possible. If we lose our lobbyist support, the Federation is likely to succumb to the deals being proffered by the corrupt Caldari business machine, and this entire area will be turned into just another locale for these corporate bigwigs to ravage.

An operative of ours, Suho Tatanal, has just returned from a protest on Parchanier II. He's a canny investigator with an eye for details; I want you to bring him the aggregated evidence we've gathered on the case so far, then report back to me. I'll have another assignment for you very soon.
129292:
It's now time to turn our eyes towards Roden Shipyards. They have always been a shady corporation, and their alliance with Wiyrkomi certainly raised a few eyebrows. I was specifically told to find out exactly what part they play in all of this.

Yesterday I stumbled upon something that may be of vital importance to my investigation. My ship's sensors picked up an encoded transmission from a Roden Shipyards outpost located in Fluekele. I haven't been able to make much of it yet, but with the proper data decoder I will be able to tell what the contents of this transmission are. So my assignment to you is to find such a decoder and bring it to me. My suggestion is to scour the asteroid belts of Jolia, there is a Serpentis agent there called Pourpas Aunten who is renowned for decoding CONCORD and Federation Navy signals. If there's anyone in the galaxy which has the decoder I need, it's him.
129293:
It's now time to turn our eyes towards Roden Shipyards. They have always been a shady corporation, and their alliance with Wiyrkomi certainly raised a few eyebrows. I was specifically told to find out exactly what part they play in all of this.

Yesterday I stumbled upon something that may be of vital importance to my investigation. My ship's sensors picked up an encoded transmission from a Roden Shipyards outpost located in Fluekele. I haven't been able to make much of it yet, but with the proper data decoder I will be able to tell what the contents of this transmission are. So my assignment to you is to find such a decoder and bring it to me. My suggestion is to scour the asteroid belts of Jolia, there is a Serpentis agent there called Pourpas Aunten who is renowned for decoding CONCORD and Federation Navy signals. If there's anyone in the galaxy which has the decoder I need, it's him.
129294: Nice job.  I hope you gave Pourpas Aunten my regards, heh heh.  Now just give me a moment to analyze the transmission ...
129296:
I've managed to decode the transmission but I can't make much of it. The interesting part though is that it originates from Maqeri Camcen's ship within the Contested Gallente Roden Shipyard Outpost. I checked my database and Maqeri is in fact rumored to be part of the Angel Cartel. What the Cartel would be doing in a Roden Shipyard Outpost in Fluekele is beyond me, unless there are Serpentis there. My best guess is that there are Serpentis operating inside the same deadspace are as Roden Shipyard, and this Maqeri is some sort of envoy from the Cartel.

Anyway I must get to the bottom of this. Meet with this Maqeri fellow and see if you can convince him to have a chat with me in person. If he's hostile and refuses to speak with you then you have my full authority to eliminate him. If you choose the gun rather than your wit, then at least bring evidence of his demise to me.

129301: Congratulations on a job well done.  I have no more tasks for you, so I suggest talking to someone else if you're still in need of work.  Just stay away from those Wiyrkomi agents, I think they're up to no good ...
129302: {[character]player.name}!  Please help me.  My friend, Isone Flosin, has gone missing.  We were just cruising around on our shuttles within the inner areas of this complex when we were attacked by rogue drones!  I managed to escape, but in my haste I didn't notice that Isone had stopped following me.  I need to know what happened to her, and my ship is in no shape to venture back in there. How horrible! I never thought something like this could happen here. I don't know how I will be able to face her parents, they told us never to venture any further into the complex than the first area but we just couldn't resist. I'm so ashamed ...

Could you at least talk to Isone's father, in the Central Administration complex in Fluekele. Tell him I sent you, Isone's DNA will prove that. Please tell him the whole story, I'm just too traumatized at the moment to meet him myself. Thank you.
129305: Please hurry, I'm certain she's in grave danger!
129307: Find Isone Flosin inside the Contested Gallente Roden Shipyard Outpost, dead or alive, and bring her back to Nilla Elermare.
129308: As a matter of fact, I found her.  I am sorry to give you these sad tidings but ...
129309: Arg! I can't believe those two! I told them never to venture deep into the Roden Shipyard outpost. How could they betray me like this! Please, wait a moment for me to gather my senses ...
129311: Isone must be avenged.  The Serpentis must be responsible for her death.  We've catered to their needs for far too long.  I couldn't believe my ears when they told me we were supposed to treat the Serpentis living in the outpost as comrades!  But enough of this rambling, back to the mission at hand.  I want you to infiltrate the Corelum Drughouse again and look for clues which might lead to whoever is behind her death.  I know of one person who might know, he serves as a guard at the Serpentis storage facility inside that deadspace area.  His name is Jark something.  Good luck.

129315: You brought back Jark himself?  Well, hopefully he will be able to reveal who's behind the tragedy when I interrogate him.  Stay tuned, as soon as he talks I might have another job for you.
129316:
While I interrogate the prisoner, I would like you to bring Isone's things to her mother on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} as well as a note from me describing the situation. 129319:
I've managed to extract the information I needed out of poor Jark. It seems that my Isone was accidentally killed by 'rogue' drone ships guarding the Serpentis drug storage area. Now I cannot really blame a computer for her death, but I can blame it's creators. In fact these drones are not 'rogue' at all, they are just programmed to act like them. An ingenious gallente scientist working for the Serpentis actually managed to reprogram these rogue drones to serve Salvador Sarpati and his wild schemes. The Federation Navy also tends to ignore areas infested with rogue drones, which is beneficial to the Serpentis.

Fortunately Jark knew of a Serpentis science lab in Colelie which is behind all of the drones in the Roden Shipyard complex. I want this science lab destroyed. Whoever resides in there is undoubtedly responsible for Isone's death, and must pay the ultimate price.

129322: Excellent news.  Although I do not feel better.  Killing those Serpentis will not bring my Isone back, nothing will.  Even if I have her cloned it will not be the same ...  Now leave me, I would like to be alone for a while.
129323: Ok first of all I'll need a large batch of dense veldspar, around 14 portions should do, with each portion size being 333 units. You will probably find veldspar in one of the asteroid fields in Colelie, if not then try a neighboring system. If you're fast, I'll even get a bonus and of course I'll split it with you.
129324: I was sent here by {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} to help gather ore for Wiyrkomi's construction workers in the Survey Station. They're hoarding up minerals and ore for the eventual construction of the power plant in Azure Canyon. The only problem is I'm not much of a combat pilot and I didn't expect there to be such an abundance of pirates festering the asteroid belts in Colelie. So I was thinking, maybe you could help me out a little? I'll split the earnings I would have received for doing the same job with you. What do you say, {[character]player.name}?
129325:
Your second job is to get me 4 portions of Omber, or 2000 units to be exact. You might find it a bit difficult to find that type or ore around these parts, but you're in luck. I know of a great spot to mine some. You see I was in Fluekele a few days ago scouting for some ore, this is before I decided the job was too dangerous for me, and I managed to stumble upon a small cluttering of asteroids in the middle of nowhere. And lo and behold, there was an asteroid brimming with minerals, which on closer inspection was Omber! Unfortunately as soon as I had discovered this magnificent find, a group of Serpentis who had been following me attacked. I believe they were being led by that scoundrel Ansedon Blat, I could be wrong though. I met him while I was at the Roden Shipyards Outpost in Fluekele, and he must have decided to follow me when I left on my expedition. That backstabber and his goons must pay.

On second thought, I'm not satisfied with just getting the omber. You'll have to kill those Serpentis bastards too, if you find them. Return to me with the omber when you're done.

I'm perfectly safe in the Survey Station ... so if you wouldn't mind I'd like you to make the run for me.  If you do, just wait a sec and let me grab my report.
129328: Ok, my boss is located in our warehouse in Ane.  Just drop this report at his desk and he'll wire the payment to my account.  I'll give you something in return for your efforts as well.  Just some items that I think you might find useful, and frankly I have no need of.  Take it or leave it.

129330: FON?  That some kind of fertilizer company?  Seriously, I'm just here for some work ...
129331:
You don't know what FON stands for?! Friends of Nature of course! We ... errr they stand for everything that's good about the Federation. Originating from a group battling to save rare animal species from extinction, it has grown somewhat after space travel became more common. Now it fights for the preservation of the natural phenomena which decorate our night sky.

Now you said you were looking for some work. As a matter of fact there is something that you could do for me which would really make my day. Temko are evil corporate peons who care nothing for our heritage, the Azure Canyon. They work for a no-good money-grubbing Caldari corporation which intends to destroy our natural reserves for its own gain. It so happens that one of Temko's commanders, Maschteri Markan, had the audacity to try and blackmail us when we sabotaged one of Wiyrkomi's construction sites, where they were building a survey station. He recorded the event and threatened to release it to The Scope and the Federation authorities if we wouldn't give in to his demands.

Find these records and bring them to me, or somehow convince him to hand them over himself, and I will reward you generously.
129332: I didn't tell you to kill him!  I'm ready to die for my beliefs, but I won't take part in cold blooded murder!  I guess I owe you your reward, but this is the last time I'll ever do business with you, {[character]player.name}.  You're a bad, bad man.
