130005: Find TakmahlLore 3 in Takmahl Digital Mezzotint containers
130007:
This is the Museum Arcana, where you'll find the finest collection of rare and beautiful items from all over. But what we are most famous for is our collection of Takmahl artefacts. The Takmahls were once part of the great Amarr Empire, but were exiled from the empire a long time ago, only shortly after us Amarrians took to space again. The Takmahls were heretics of the worst sort, some call them the predecessors of the Blood Raider cult.

For centuries nothing was heard from them, but not long ago relics were found here in Araz that show that the Takmahls had a thriving culture for many centuries after their departure from the glorious Amarr Empire. Yet at some point they died out, for what reasons I do not know. Archaeologists and treasure seekers from all over have since convened here in Araz, dreaming of uncovering the secrets of the Takmahls, or more precisely, their fabled treasures.

Yet my job here is not just overseeing the museum, but more importantly I am here as a member of the Theology Council. It is our job to make sure the despicable scriptures and rituals of the Takmahls are kept well under wrap. The last thing the Empire needs right now is another religious schism.

Your presence here means that you are an archaeologist of some merits. I have use of someone with your talents, rooting out those seeking false enlightenment or harbingers of discord. Help me out a bit and I will give you the key to the hidden treasures of the Takmahls. But only if you first prove yourself to be a champion of the Amarr faith.

There is a certain item to be find among the relics you see here scattered around. I want you to use your archaeological skills to unearth for me a Centrifugal Primer. It's advanced theoretical texts that I hope will give us rare insights into the rise and fall of the Takmahls. Bring me one of them, from past experience I know that your best bet of finding one is in a Digital Mezzotint. It's a rare item, so don't be too discouraged if you don't find it right away. If you haven't realised already this is a test of your mettle. If you manage to find me one I'll reward you well later down the line, but even if you fail I still have some use for you. Talk to me again when you have the Primer, or when you have given up the search.

130034:
We're doing a good job protecting the Empire from the foul influences that the Takmahl theology might impose. But more is needed and I want you to show me one more time your dedication in rooting out these blaspehmous religious artefacts of the Takmahl. Once you've done that then you truly are an honorable pilot worthy to learn where the true treasures of the Takmahls lie.

The Arcana Patrons seek the potentially most dangerous items of the Takmahls, their holy scriptures. But we must tolerate them for they are important clients of the museum, vital for its survival. Yet you are not bound by the same restrictions I am, so you can move against them without putting the future wellbeing of the museum in jeopardy. Hunt down the Arcana Patrons and bring me back the ritual texts they are collecting. Those texts could cause severe disturbance in the Empire if revealed and the Theology Council is not about to let some uncouth art collectors hoard them.

You were not born yesterday, so I shouldn't have to urge caution, but yet I feel I must do so as the Arcana Patrons are a dangerous lot. Do not lose faith if you don't find the texts right away, in this assignment as so many others patience is a virtue worth practicing. But if you do manage to get the texts quickly, say within the next 3 hours or so, I will be a happy man and will reward you accordingly. And as promised, the moment you bring me those texts the key to the Labyrinth, wherein the hidden treasures of the Takmahls await, will be yours.

130046:
Nice of you to drop by, {[character]player.name}. And what an uncanny coincidence...

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a slight problem on its hands. One of our agents sent a certain mercenary on a very important courier mission to deliver an item of great value to our headquarters. This was a few weeks ago, and this mercenary never showed up at his destination. At first we thought he had simply run off with the goods, but upon further investigation that proved not to be the case. His ship had been destroyed, though, we received no transmissions from him, and we found clues at the site linking the crime to a certain pirate who also happens to work as a bounty hunter. I have no doubt that some pirate organization put him up to it, but that is of little importance compared to retrieving the item that was stolen.

Now we looked up this bounty hunter and we discovered something that will interest you, no doubt. What we found was that he is currently on an assignment to kill none other than you, {[character]player.name}. Who hired him we do not know, but considering your past I'm sure you have a few suspects in mind who might pull something like this off. Now that we have a mutual target, I thought, "Why not ask {[character]player.name} to take care of the job?" And then suddenly here you are.

By doing this assignment, you'll not only rid yourself of a rat who's on your tail, but you will retrieve the item that we're after. I'm sure you're willing to get the job done, eh? I'll upload the pirate scumbag's current location into your NeoCom; he's out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} hanging around a casino. He's a pretty tough nut to crack, I hear, so you may want to bring backup with you just in case.

130097:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} recently sacked one of its employees after a routine inspection revealed a large amount of indecent pictures stored in his personal database.  Sadly, this ex-employee wasn't all too pleased with our 
decision, and has resorted to camping outside of our headquarters and harassing our customers.  Fortunately though, we dug up some old offenses this guy made and revealed them to the authorities, who promptly lowered his security rating quite a bit.  In effect, he's fair game.  Please warp over to the location on the bookmark I'm about to give you and squash this little pest.  I doubt he will survive for long, as some of our customers are 
heavily armed.  So hurry up and take him out if you want your reward.
130098:
I knew you were up to it. Now, the story behind this mission is actually rather complicated, but you just need to know the basics. The reason I'm telling you this at all is because I don't want you finding about this later and getting it into your head that I betrayed you, because I'd never do that *smile*. Anyway, two years ago one of the new recruits within our marketing department started to show an incredible amount of promise, making decisions that generated an enormous amount of revenue for us. Needless to say, he quickly rose up the ranks within our corporation as well as earning a place within the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} government, and we owe our recent successes largely to his 'efforts'.

However quickly some of us became suspicious, especially those within our ranks which were jealous of his success. After a lot of research and investigation, we came to the conclusion that he had a contact within the Guristas Pirates which was supplying him with sensitive information which they had acquired through illegal means. As you might know, these pirates are infamous within the Caldari territories, and have even spread to neighboring regions. For this reason we must not allow this to reach the ears of ANYONE affiliated with the authorities, or it will have dire consequences. I hope I have made myself perfectly clear on that matter. I expect your full discretion. I'll download more information into your mission journal once you get started. Good luck.
130099:
I have a job for you this time which I would not have given to just anybody. I know that I can trust you, your faithful service to me in the past has proven that. Now to cut the story short, what I need is a ship destroyed. But there is a 'slight' problem, which I'll get to. You see, this ship isn't just any old pirate ship, it contains a high ranking official within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, who also happens to be a member within the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} government. This isn't a rescue mission, this is a destroy mission. But don't worry, this mission is completely confidential. If you're interested, then I'll give you more details, otherwise this conversation never happened. Just take note of the fact your target is very powerful, do not attempt this unless you have a powerful warship at your disposal, or friends.

The ship you are supposed to destroy is actually a Guristas Emissary vessel, which is used as a secret meeting place between the person which must be killed, and his Guristas contacts. You will probably also notice his own ship nearby, which may or may not be unmanned at the time. You must also destroy this vessel, whether your target is inside it or not, to make it look like he was ambushed by pirates. And take care of anyone else nearby, noone may escape. I hope I have made myself clear.

Oh and please note, you can keep whatever you find in the wreckage of these ships, it is of no concern to us. We will of course reward you as well when you have finished the task. The bookmark I gave you will show the exact location of the meeting place so getting there shouldn't be a problem.
130100: I'm up to the job, and don't worry, you can trust me with keeping this under the table.

130103: Marvelous.  You really did good out there, and I am absolutely certain I can trust you with keeping quiet about this.  However, let this be an educated warning to you:  don't mess with the system, because in the end you WILL regret it!

130201:
Recently, we started noticing an increased presence of Amarr military drones in the area. Our fears were just confirmed a few hours ago when one of our members stumbled upon a transport ship with an Amarr logo on its hull parked in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. A ship scan revealed a hoard of construction blocks in its cargo hold. This means they must be constructing something in the proximity, which is of course unacceptable. Their project must be stopped in its infancy at all costs. I want you to warp to a remote stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} which we believe the latest transport ship we spotted was intending to use. Wait for a few minutes until it arrives. But hurry before it's too late!

And remember, do not reveal your identity to anyone nearby, as we want to keep a lid on this operation. We do not want to ignite the spark of a full fledged war with the Empire.

We currently have a rogue slave trader on our hands, {[character]player.name}. The Blood Raiders have apparently dispatched a group of their own to {[location]agentConstellationID.name} to look for potential victims. They've been raiding outlying settlements, which have weak security systems in place.

Our primary objective right now is to get back the people they've taken captive. We think we've located their slave pen in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it's your job to make sure. Destroy the structure and rescue the slaves if you can, then report back to me. We'll deal with these slave traders later.

130246: I was sent to speak with you, Aviekko, and I have this certificate to prove it.
130247: Ah, so you're a qualified pilot eh.  I have some work for you after all.  Just give me a minute to go over my files, I'll have something for you to do in a jiffy ...
130248: Ok, show me the certificate.  You better not be pulling my leg ...
130250:
Before you begin I should get you acquainted with my current assignment. I am Aviekko Ta, agent of Atoa Issa. I am one of many agents which were dispatched by Atoa to search for leads of the missing relics, which were stolen from the 13 Achur temples. So far I've had little luck, but I believe my venture in hiring graduates from the prominent aerospace aviation schools, like yourself, will pay off in the long run.

Your first task is to retrieve a few starmaps of mine from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. I just ordered them from our archives on our home-planet Achura in Saisio. They should lead us Kikko Roisen, who I've suspected for quite some time to have been involved with the infamous heist.

Anyway, get going. I need those starmaps asap.

So far I've had little luck, but I believe my venture in hiring graduates from the prominent aerospace aviation schools, like yourself, will pay off in the long run.

Your first task is to retrieve a few starmaps of mine from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name}. I just ordered them from our archives on our home-planet Achura in Saisio. They should lead us Kikko Roisen, who I've suspected for quite some time to have been involved with the infamous heist.

Anyway, get going. I need those starmaps asap.
130252: Excellent.  I'll have a look at these starmaps immediately and compare them to the data I already have about Kikko.  I'll let you know when I've found something ...
130255:
The sacred pieces believed to be from the Rod of the Creator were stolen from under the watchful gaze of the Achur religious order. This any true Achur would know. The State has pledged enormous resources to tracking down the thieves. But even so the Elder Visionaries of Achura are not satisfied. They do not trust the State government, and they cannot sit idly by as their religion is ridiculed for its failure to protect the icons of its faith.

And so the Celestial Imperative was devised. Atoa Issa, a proud Achur himself, took leave of his prominent position within the Caldari Navy to oversee the search for the scoundrels who dared insult the Achur religion and people of Achura. By his side stands Seer Chakai Potan, representative of the temples of Achura. Together they control the enormous wealth the Achur government and the temples have supplied to fund this investigation. And to quote Atoa, 'no stone shall remain unturned, no world shall elude our probing gaze. I vow to you, people of Achura, that I will spend every fiber of my existance from here after to track down these vile, wretched thieves and restore the honor of our people!'

Visionary Atahari has had him tracked ever since his bungled burglary attempt at the temple a few years ago, so that should come as no surprise. But I've managed to narrow down these locations to 3 settlements, where he has been spotted very frequently. These are the most likely locations where we will find him.

I truly hope he hasn't left the system, but at this stage we can only cross our fingers. The mercenary tracking Kikko on Atahari's command disappeared when he tried to confront Kikko on my behalf, and that may have triggered him to think about relocating himself. Fortunately rumor still has it that he hasn't left Autama, but you never can be too sure.

130299: Since you are so eager to work for me, {[character]player.name}, I would like to start off our relationship by explaining a few critical details.
130300:
I am Avrue Auz, agent of Beizan Picholen. I came to Chandeille (Lirsautton V) eight years ago, during the height of the Picholen-Auboure family feud. Deni Picholen hired me as Beizan's secretary and financial manager. The Picholen family is quite wealthy, having long owned a number of franchises connected with Kaalakiota and their wares.

Anyway, the feud was quite draining on the Picholens, especially their wallet. But the biggest disaster the family had ever faced came only a few years ago. It was a dreadfully cold afternoon during the height of the Chabash winter on Chandeille when I received the news that a Picholen industrial had been caught by planetary security forces, trying to smuggle a troop of slaves and illegal combat boosters into Namin City. Speculation had it that the slaves were to be used as cheap manpower in a secret military operation directed against Auboure, named after its ancient ruling family.

To me, this siezure of assets was bad enough, but to make matters far worse, my employer, Beizan, was directly implicated in the deal, for the industrial smuggling the contraband had been rented in his name. It was a debacle. Kaalakiota canceled their multi-million LUX deal with Picholen, and the Governor of Chandeille placed a huge fine on the family that has basically crippled its financial status. In other words, the Picholens lost everything other than their name and sovereignty over Namin City. Most of their lands were confiscated, as well as their overseas bank accounts. I'm a bit surprised you haven't heard this story, in fact; it was all over the Federation media at the time.

But anyway, to cut the story short, Beizan was imprisoned in Pinmouth, an infamous Federation prison facility in Lirsautton, and resides there still. It is my firm belief, however, that Beizan is really innocent, and that is why I sent for someone like you.
130302:
Your first task is to raid a merchant operating a small trading hub in Meves. He is known to have dealings with the Auboure family; he was in fact their first contact when they started expanding their trade relations outside of Lirsautton to compete with the Picholens. It is my firm belief that the Auboures have something to do with the smuggling incident that resulted in Beizan's arrest ― yes, I believe he was framed.

The merchant's name is Kelmiler Delbone. Interrogate him for me, find a way to make him reveal what he knows about the incident. Once you have something, report back to me.

Not yet proven, of course, but the interesting part is that Govarde has been sighted there frequently by civilians staying at the resort. I want you to snoop around and search for any clues that might lead us to him.
130335: So, what did you find out?
130336: Pay a visit to {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and pick up a package for me from an acquaintance of mine who's Navy data technician there.
130337:
The results of the autopsy scan show that Eilard was killed by a blaster at close range, most likely by the Serpentis goons who were waiting for you when you arrived. However, I did find an interesting bit of data in his ComPlant. The Serpentis probably hadn't gotten to extracting it when you showed up, so I was able to recover his datajournal entries.

Most of the information was useless (if mildly entertaining...), but one very recent bit of mem-script reads, "Meet Govarde at 1800h." Now, I might be reaching a little here, but perhaps this "Govarde" was one of the Serpentis you killed earlier? Maybe he was the person Eilard was due to meet? Certainly a difficult theory to prove, but I have an idea.

I want you to pay a visit to {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} and pick up a package from a Navy data technician there. The records are off limits to non-Navy personnel, for they contain extensive data on the Serpentis, but I have a contact working there who should be able to do the research for me. He owes me one, and this is as good a time as any to pay up.
130338: Excellent.  One minute while I take a look at this data ...
130339: What's the word from the medical lab?
130341:
The Khanid Insurgency are rebels who want to topple the Khanid government and install one that'd be more inclined to start a war with the Amarr. They are led by an old, crazed hag going by the name of Deza Yobili. She claims to have been 'wronged' by the Khanid Monarchy, because as part of an exchange deal we handed her husband to the Amarr authorities in return for a group of Khanid citizens that had been illegally held in Amarr prisons. Her husband was nothing more than a murderer, and yet some misguided souls within the Kingdom view him as a martyr. It's a rather sad ordeal, all in all.

We are doing everything we can to stop Deza and her cronies, but she keeps eluding our grasp. And their numbers refuse to drop, which is why we have started taking extra measures to quell this uprising attempt before it gets out of hand.

Now here is where you come in. One of my servants, Ziona Koon, went missing while she was posing as a student for the Royal Amarr Institute in Emrayur. The last I heard of her she was on to something. She left a report in her quarters in Emrayur, and I would like to retrieve that report to figure out what happened to her. Please retrieve this report for me.

130347:
The Khanid zealot, Deza Yobili, nicknamed ‘the black widow', runs a guerilla army whose aim is to enact a coup against the current regime. She has captured the hearts of many hardline Khanids due to her heart-wrenching story. Her husband, Jabil Yobili and 3 of her sons were executed by Amarr Imperial forces after they had been handed over by the Khanid Navy as a part of an exchange deal for Khanid POWs. Jabil and his sons had been accused by the Empire of slaughtering many Amarrian citizens during an insurgency in Gousoviba.

Deza's youngest son, Abarak Yobili, was imprisoned by the Khanid government for ‘causing civil unrest', when he led a demonstration against the newly rejuvenated Khanid – Amarr alliance.

Deza is the figurehead in a persistent movement to oust the current monarch of the Khanid Kingdom, and to sever their ties with the Empire once more. They are still greatly outnumbered and opposed by the majority of the Khanid nobility, but even so they are considered a threat and the Khanid monarch is eager to eradicate this thorn from his side.

I think I've found our lead. According to the prisoner, the man we're after is Mamin Choonka. He runs a diner in Ashab, somewhere near the moon of Ashab II. It offers a hefty discount to students of the academy, hence it's quite popular among their ranks.

I want you to pay him a visit. But don't go in with guns flaring, I want you to get to know him. Tell him you just graduated from the academy, and let's hope he tries to convert you to his cause. If all goes well, he will offer you a place within the Khanid insurgency. Perhaps that will lead us to one of their bases, or even better Deza Yobili.

It's hard to pin Choonka down, so I won't give you a bookmark. Instead, I want you to fly to his base at the moon of Ashab II and find him on your own. I'm sure you won't have any trouble.

130357: Amazing!  This operation has gone more smoothly than I had expected, even in my wildest dreams.  I will report back to the Royal Family immediately, but before I leave I have one more task to give you.
130359: Find Mamin Choonka at his diner in Ashab, near the warp-in point of Ashab II's moon.  See if you can acquire the coordinates to the Khanid insurgency from him.
130360: I heard you had work available.  Was my source correct?
130361: Now that depends entirely upon the source, {[character]player.name}. But yes, I might have something available. It depends on whether you're willing to risk your neck or not. My assignments involve fighting ... lots of it. If you're looking for something more on the lines of dung-hauling, I suggest you look elsewhere.
130362: Then I am definitely what you're looking for. I am well prepared for combat.
130363: Ah, I was hoping you had something safe and easy. I'll have to decline.
130364: Your first job involves taking on a group of rogue drones that have for some god-forsaken reason decided to infest my storage facility in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Destroy all of them, and then report back to me.
130365: Your first job involves taking on a group of rogue drones that have for some god-forsaken reason decided to infest my storage facility in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. Destroy all of them, and then report back to me.
130366: A job well done, {[character]player.name}.  Take your reward, but don't leave yet.  I have more tasks in store for you.
130367:
You did well against artificial intelligence, I'll give you that. But can you cut it against living opponents? Your next assignment is to destroy a pirate convoy carrying illegal goods into {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. You might ask, "how did you find out about this convoy?" The answer is that I ordered the goods myself. Through a contact, of course ― I would never reveal my true identity to those bastards.

Destroy the convoy, and bring the database from one of the ships to me if you manage to find one intact. I need to present it to the authorities so that we might trace their travel route to its origin and eliminate their drug factory for good.

130378: Anything else you need me to do, {[character]agentID.name}?
130379:
I've had a sinking suspicion for quite some time now that I'm being followed. I kept seeing the same mysterious man behind the corner whenever I turned my head. It was getting quite antagonizing. I work for the Khanid secret-service, so I notice these things quite well ...

Anyway I had the man's ship bugged, and we tracked him down to guess where ... Mamin Choonka's diner. Obviously Choonka has somehow gotten a hold of my identity, and probably wants me killed. I suspect they will strike after I leave the station. Which leaves me in a sort of a dilemma, as I have to meet with my superiors soon for a meeting in Khanid space.

To make things easier for me, I would like you to take care of these pests. That should clear the way for me to leave the station for a while. I will give you the exact coordinates for their ships, as we still have one of them bugged.

Ok, you're now all set to speak with Pinala Adala. You'll probably find her at her desk in the Eram IX - Moon 4 - Sebiestor tribe Bureau. And don't forget to bring your graduation certificate when you pay her a visit!

If you forget the location of this agent, you can always look it up by opening the 'show info' window for the graduation certificate.
130400: I have an important job for you, {[character]player.name}.  Because of your good standing and the fact you have successfully completed a number of missions for {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} we have decided you are worth the trust of a very important courier job. It entails bringing a large cargo of transaction and salary logs to this station from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} where they have been stored for the last few weeks for a routine inspection by the authorities.  This data holds information of sensitive nature on our recent business dealings, earnings and expenses and wages that we pay our staff members.  Under no circumstances may any of these reports be lost, or worse yet fall into the wrong hands.  Pirates have a tendency to want this information so they can sell it to our rivals.  They used to have easy access to this information by hacking our transmission calls, but now that we send these reports via freight this is no longer as serious of a problem.  I trust you on this, {[character]player.name}, don't let me down.

130434:
We need you for a very important assassination mission, {[character]player.name}. The Caldari State military has set up a base in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, intent on flushing out pirate activity here. We cannot afford to launch a full scale attack on it at the moment, so we have been forced to resort to scare tactics to drive them away. We planned to assassinate their commander, who is their highest-ranking official at the military outpost, but so fair all of our attempts have been foiled. You are our last hope, {[character]player.name}.

Now is the perfect time to undertake this mission. We know that the Commander is traveling through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} at this very moment, and we can supply you a bookmark to his approximate location. Should you strike immediately, then you may catch them by surprise. He is traveling with a small troop from his armada occupying the military base, so the fight may be difficult for you if you go in alone.

130440: Now that I know you have the skills to pull through, it's time to test your loyalty.  So I'll get straight to the point.  I work for a Matar citizen, who wishes to remain anonymous, who was wronged by a certain Vherokior shaman.  My client wants revenge, and this requires the capture of this Vherokior individual.  If you don't have the guts to take part in this endeavor, then I suggest you leave now.
130441: So, what do you need me for?
130442: I'm up for the job, as long as it doesn't involve breaking the law.
130443:
Oh don't worry about that, you won't be breaking any laws. Or in other words, no one will know that you are breaking any laws. We dug up some dirt on the shaman in question, and soon he will be a wanted man in the Republic. We won't reveal it to the authorities until we have him though, just to make sure we get there before the police do. We need him alive, he's of no use to us dead.

Once our allegations of him are proven, he will be executed. It will matter little to the authorities if we do the honors for them. Therefore you have nothing to fear.

Now for your task, I want you to apprehend a member of the Angel Cartel. The Cartel is the biggest criminal organization in the known universe, so finding a few of their members shouldn't be very difficult. I'll even upload a bookmark to one of their hideouts for you, into your journal.
130444: Warp to the coordinates that Pinala gave you, recorded inside your mission journal.  Destroy the Angel Cartel ships at their hideout and capture one of their pilots from the ejected container (if one survives).  Bring this person back to your agent, as long as the captive is still alive.
130445: Here is the prisoner you asked for.
130446: Excellent!  He will do nicely.  But there's more to be done, so stick around.
130448:
The Brutor, Hnarlir Afer, has been an outcast from his home-world, Matar, ever since his Voluval ritual. The mark it left behind was so shameful even his loving father disowned him. He moved to the Gallente Federation, where hardly anyone recognized the mark or paid it any attention. There he began a life of a mercenary, having been bred as a space pilot by his military veteran father.

He quickly made a name for himself, before becoming a freelancer. Using the wealth he garnered from that profession, he started up his own corporation, The Markoni Dragons. It has been quite successful, earning Hnarlir a small fortune.

But even with his change of fortune, Hnarlir greatly misses his homeworld. He desperately wants to return and reclaim a position within his nation of birth. But he dares not return with the mark on his cheek as visible as ever. His family has suffered enough shame on his behalf already.

Yet Hnarlir still has hope. Hope that his ‘condition' can finally be modified. Even though it goes against everything the Minmatar consider holy, Hnarlir is just desperate, and wealthy, enough to pull it off. He wants to learn the method which the Vheriokor shamans use to perform the Voluval ritual and modify the mark so that it no longer resembles the symbol of the Ammatar Mandate.
130449: Now I would like you to drop off these reports I have to the Vherokior Bureau in Gelfiven.  An associate of mine will retrieve it from the hangar there.  These reports and the Angel Cartel prisoner you brought me will be enough to convince any jury of the Vherokior shaman's guilt.  That should set us up nicely for capturing him.

130457:

He is currently meditating somewhere in Eram, but I haven't been able to track him down. If you didn't know, this meditation process of the Vherokior shamans can take months or even years, and frankly I'd rather not wait that long.

There is one link to Logut that I haven't pursued ... yet. His name is Matique Karani, and he's an associate of Loguts. I want you to pay Matique a visit and force him to reveal the whereabouts of Logut. Use any means necessary.

Oh and you'll probably have to deal with a few guards Matique hired. If it weren't for them, I'd have done the dirty work myself a long time ago.

130476:
No, this cannot be! Touch a strand of hair on Dari's head and we'll have the Republic Fleet so far up your ass they'll hear your screams on Amarr Prime. But I will speak to Logut, as long as Dari is unharmed.

*long pause*

Logut has agreed to your terms, he will cooperate as long as Dari remains safe with me. He would do anything for his daughter, even surrender to treasonous scoundrels like yourself. But be warned, if he is not returned safe and sound within the month, we will contact the Minmatar secret service and they will hunt you down like the dog you are. Be-gone!¨
130479: The key to the gateway is hidden inside the blasted neon sign near Logut's Abode, so bring along a Data Analyzer.
130480: Actually, I was sent here by a person named Pinala Adala.  I was supposed to kidnap Logut, but I've had a change of heart.

130483: Sorry but I don't have time to wait for you, I have business elsewhere.
130484:
I have spoken with Logut. He says that he will come with you under the pretense that you have 'kidnapped' him for Pinala. He will be wearing a bug attached to his garments, which will send his exact coordinates to me. I will then inform the government of his kidnapper's location, and hopefully they'll be taken care of by the Republic Fleet.

However before he can commit himself to such a dangerous task, he wants you to do him a favor. His daughter, Dari Akell, lost her husband to the Angel Cartel. He was a miner, working as a contractor in Elgoi for Core Complexion inc, when a gang of Cartel thugs struck. They had threatened to 'cause grievous harm' to the mining operation if the foreman would neglect to pay them tribute, but he had refused. So they made an example of some of his subordinates, including Dari's husband. The Cartel got what they wanted, and Logut's son-in-law is now dead.

Needless to say, Logut wants revenge. I will supply you with a bookmark to the mining operation where Dari's husband was stationed, a few Angel goons should be located nearby. Destroy them. Do not return until this task has been accomplished.

130654: I'm looking for some work, as long as it's for the greater good of the State ...
130655:
Ah then I have something for you. I'm in charge of security for the Minedrill expedition forces stationed here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. As you probably know this is risky space, but even so we've been harassed by the same pirate far too many times for it to be coincidence. Also upon investigating the matter further, I discovered that this pirate is in fact called 'Black Jack', a notorious felon who terrorized Molden Heath not too long ago. There was a documentary about him released by The Scope ...

Anyway, if you find him then kill him for me, please. He's been the bane of too many of my colleagues and has been making quite a fool out of my security division in fact. There are many stories floating around which tell of his greatly exaggerated 'victories' over my men and those of the Navy guarding the civilian excavators, which are often completely false and unjustified. Now if you could bring me something to prove he's dead, his DNA would probably do, then I'll be able to vindicate the reputation of the security division here in Kois City.

Is it that obvious? Well, since you had the guts to fly out here into no-mans land you might be of some use to me.

I was sent here along with the rest of my division to set up a blockade around the O-LR1H gate, to prevent the Guristas from continuing to flood this system with their fighters. Unfortunately we're simply outnumbered and outgunned, there's no way for us to hold that position and the admiral was very clear when I left that he could not spare any reinforcements for quite some time.

So we've been forced to do nothing more than monitor the gate, alerting our forces of any possible threat. It's rather embarrassing to say the least, but here's where you come in ...
130677:
During my research of the Guristas movements through {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, I discovered that most of the Guristas squadrons flying through {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} originate from a certain outpost within O-LR1H. I believe that's where their command post in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} is located. Not only that but local rumor has it that many of the Guristas ships currently stationed in {[location]agentConstellationID.name} have only recently arrived to the constellation.

So my conclusion naturally is that a large portion of the Guristas forces that have been harassing us here lately are part of an assembly of fighters recently allocated here by the Guristas central command in 6NJ8-V. With this in mind I would also assume they are acting on specific orders and not randomly attacking us when the opportunity arrives, like is often the case with pirates in these parts.

Now if I could only get a hold of their plans, I would have some good news finally to present to Admiral Aurobe Kois. Knowledge of their next move would give us a huge advantage. Acquiring this knowledge is of course easier said than done.

This is where you come in. Your job, obviously, is to acquire this data. And I know of two ways to do it. Your first option is to befriend one of their leaders within the Iacta Space Plain in O-LR1H and somehow acquire the information through him. This is of course highly difficult and only possible if you are in good standing with the Guristas organization. Your second option is to rescue the last agent I sent on the very same task, Otsalen Mano. He found something, but before he could return to me his identity was discovered. He's currently being held in one of their prison facilities near the Iacta Space Plain in O-LR1H. And there's nothing I can do about it until I get more firepower ...

Anyway, don't return until you have the Guristas war plans!

130744:
Quite right, {[character]player.name}. I think it's time for you to know the objective of my mission here in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. We were to infiltrate Kois City, the central administrative complex in G5ED-Y, from where the Caldari send all of their expeditions, and answer the question that has been nagging my superiors back home, "Why are they here?".

Now getting into Kois City will be no easy task. It's heavily fortified. But on the bright side I think I know exactly what we're looking for. My sources tell me that the expeditionary forces store most of the data they have collected in a computer within the city's science labs. Backup data is also stored in data chips within their storage facility in the civilian sector of the city. Therefore your task is to somehow get into the civilian quarter and acquire at least one of those data chips. From this data we will hopefully be able to piece together their objective, and find out if it's worth our time to get involved.

This used to be Black Jack's task, but I assume he discovered something that convinced him to cut ties with us and go solo. But I will tell you this, it is in your best interest to complete this task at any cost. Should you fail, or decide to 'keep' the data for yourself, the Syndicate will hunt you down like a dog and force you to watch your own family executed in the cruelest of ways. Is that clear?

I've had the DED squadron tracked for some time now. I'll upload a bookmark to their current location into your journal. Find them and take out their leader ― that should be enough to send them crawling back to their homeland with their tails between their collective legs.

130766:
Yes, your next assignment is a little more personal in nature. You see, I was born and raised in the Venal system, and during my teens I joined the Guristas militia. I never knew my parents, but I assume they were loyal to the Guristas. I did have a few comrades that I could call friends, and my life was relatively stable. But then came the assignment that would change everything.

I was sent to E-8CSQ to find and apprehend a traitor, Akkeshu Karuan. My orders were specific, to bring him back dead or alive to Jirai Laitanen at the Guristas headquarters. I was not to return, not ever, until and unless this task was accomplished. I never questioned my orders, and frankly I don't give a damn what Akkeshu was accused of. For my entire life, I have known nothing other than the Guristas, the organization that fed and clothed me during my darkest of times, and I owe them my life.

But unfortunately the mission did not go as planned. I fought Akkeshu and his men inside what is now known as "Cadaver Reef." I was victorious in that battle, but Akkeshu still slipped through my grasp. He and what remained of his gang fled deeper into the deadspace pocket, and of course I followed with the fleet under my command. That action turned out to be a terrible mistake. Akkeshu knew the area like the back of his hand, and he managed to use that knowledge to his advantage. Once he warped away from our targeting systems, all we could find was an acceleration gate. When we activated it, it propelled us deeper into the rock-filled deadspace complex. But somehow Akkeshu had managed to reconfigure the gate, and instead of finding him on the other side, we were sent straight into a massive drone hive. We put up a brave fight and managed to destroy the hive, but at enormous cost. The fleet was shattered, and I was left with a force so small we could not hope to face Akkeshu again.

So here I am, all these years later, rotting in a town filled with hopelessness and depression. I so yearn to return to my roots, but I know that if I do so, I will be promptly executed for my failure.

I am now too old and out of practice to attempt to find Akkeshu again. But considering how well you dealt with your last mission, I have hope that perhaps you can succeed where I failed. All I ask for is evidence of Akkeshu's death; with that, I can return to my homeland and hopefully redeem myself, dying in peace among my own people. I do not have many years left, and you cannot imagine how much I wish to spend them in the land of my birth instead of a place like Makeinu Town.

Find Cadaver Reef. Use scan probes. Bring me proof of Akkeshu's demise, and I will give you my most prized possessions.
130767:
Yes, your next assignment is a little more personal in nature. You see, I was born and raised in the Venal system, and during my teens I joined the Guristas militia. I never knew my parents, but I assume they were loyal to the Guristas. I did have a few comrades that I could call friends, and my life was relatively stable. But then came the assignment that would change everything.

I was sent to E-8CSQ to find and apprehend a traitor, Akkeshu Karuan. My orders were specific, to bring him back dead or alive to Jirai Laitanen at the Guristas headquarters. I was not to return, not ever, until and unless this task was accomplished. I never questioned my orders, and frankly I don't give a damn what Akkeshu was accused of. For my entire life, I have known nothing other than the Guristas, the organization that fed and clothed me during my darkest of times, and I owe them my life.

But unfortunately the mission did not go as planned. I fought Akkeshu and his men inside what is now known as "Cadaver Reef." I was victorious in that battle, but Akkeshu still slipped through my grasp. He and what remained of his gang fled deeper into the deadspace pocket, and of course I followed with the fleet under my command. That action turned out to be a terrible mistake. Akkeshu knew the area like the back of his hand, and he managed to use that knowledge to his advantage. Once he warped away from our targeting systems, all we could find was an acceleration gate. When we activated it, it propelled us deeper into the rock-filled deadspace complex. But somehow Akkeshu had managed to reconfigure the gate, and instead of finding him on the other side, we were sent straight into a massive drone hive. We put up a brave fight and managed to destroy the hive, but at enormous cost. The fleet was shattered, and I was left with a force so small we could not hope to face Akkeshu again.

So here I am, all these years later, rotting in a town filled with hopelessness and depression. I so yearn to return to my roots, but I know that if I do so, I will be promptly executed for my failure.

I am now too old and out of practice to attempt to find Akkeshu again. But considering how well you dealt with your last mission, I have hope that perhaps you can succeed where I failed. All I ask for is evidence of Akkeshu's death; with that, I can return to my homeland and hopefully redeem myself, dying in peace among my own people. I do not have many years left, and you cannot imagine how much I wish to spend them in the land of my birth instead of a place like Makeinu Town.

Find Cadaver Reef. Use scan probes. Bring me proof of Akkeshu's demise, and I will give you my most prized possessions.
130769: I can ask for nothing more.
130771: Incredible! I simply could not bring myself to believe you would succeed, {[character]player.name}, but here you are. I owe you more than I can ever repay, but I hope this meager reward will have made it worth your time. Take care.
130773: To finish this mission, you must first find Cadaver Reef via system scanning. It lies somewhere in this constellation. Akkeshu might be located inside; destroy his ship and return with his DNA for your reward.
130774: So what brought you all the way out here, {[character]agentID.name}?
130775:
I came here to investigate Constellation 09-4XW, which has been reported to contain massive gas clouds full of material used in booster manufacturing. There have been a lot of rumors about it within {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, and I thought I'd take a look for myself. Unfortunately, the number of rogue drones and outlaws here has me quite worried, so I dare not go looking for the clouds myself. Hence, I might have a job for you...

However, I suggest you refrain from accepting my task unless you have access to a gas cloud harvester module. Without that, you will just be wasting my time.
130776: I'll take anything you got as long as it's worth my time.
130777:
Okay, what I need you to do for me is find one of the famed 09-4XW gas clouds. Now of course I'm referring specifically to those gas clouds containing the materials I need for booster manufacturing. You must tell me where the cloud is and get me a sample from it. If you do this for me, I'll give you a booster blueprint copy, plus a little extra cash if you're fast. And you'll learn something in the process. Sounds useful, huh?

You will find information on how to find and access the clouds in the message I uploaded into your journal.
130778: I found one of the gas clouds you've been looking for, {[character]agentID.name}, and it's at these coordinates ...

130835:
Alright, I'll tell you a little story. My expedition had discovered an area filled with gas clouds thicker than I had ever witnessed in my life, and we were ecstatic. For days we harvested the gas fields, with no end in sight. At that time I was already starting to daydream about where I would retire when I finished this job. It was probably the greatest moment of my life. Unfortunately, followed by the worst.

Once we had filled our cargo holds, we started to align our ships for warp. It was then that they hit us. They came from nowhere and warp scrambled our industrials and jammed the two merc ships escorting us. They demanded over half of our cargo. We debated. But before we could give an answer, they attacked. Half the expedition was wiped out, including some of my closest friends. The ones who survived were told to go back to camp and relay our story to the rest of the miners and harvesters, so that the next time one of our expeditions runs into the Guristas we follow their orders immediately.

Now I just want to leave this dreadful place, I knew I took a huge risk by coming here but now that I've seen the face of death ... I just don't think I have it in me anymore.
130836: I'm sorry for your loss.  Perhaps I can help.
130837:
I know some of the families of my colleagues who perished on that fateful day, and I would like their bodies returned to me so that I can bring them back to Caldari space for proper burial. If you're up for the job, I'll give you a bookmark to the deadspace area where they lost their lives. You should be able to find the wreckage of their ships there.

You'll probably have to navigate through at least two pockets though to find all of them, once the Guristas attacked we tried to flee via the acceleration gates there, some of us only made it past one gate before being mowed down.

130845: You're observation is correct, I AM frustrated!  And it's rather embarrassing to tell you the truth ... but if you're a merc for hire then I'll spill the beans, as long as you promise to help me.
130847:
Ok, just promise you won't laugh. You see, before I came here I was a computer programmer. I specialized in creating and maintaining artificial intelligence for Kaalakiota, probes and drones and that sort of stuff. Well after I got here, I realized I needed some heavy duty protection considering the relative lawlessness of this place, and the mercs here were just way too expensive.

So I used my expertise to set up a self-maintaining drone facility, which provided me with enough backup to safely harvest the gas fields around here. It worked like a charm to begin with ... until hardware failure wiped out the secret password I've been using to access the mother-drone computer's mainframe.

Now I can't even get into my own home! I've been sitting around here for days but none of these good-for-nothing mercs have the guts to face my drones. Maybe you've got it in you?

Anyway first I want my stash of extracted gas chemicals. You'll find a few containers full of it in my storage facility. I'll give you the coordinates, all you have to do is warp there, take out the drones guarding the stash, loot it, and bring it back here.
130848: I brought back the stash.  Some advice though, carry a backup of that damn password!
130849:
Hey! Don't tell me what to do! If I didn't have another job for you, I'd keep the reward for myself. Learn some manners!

Besides, you have no idea how much CPU a complex password like that takes. Hacker-proof passwords are no laughing matter these days.

130858:
Have I got any? Are you mad? I've been sitting here all day looking for contractors with some combat experience. Now I need someone I can rely on for this job, and I have to say I'm impressed with the way you've dealt with some of your previous assignments for Caldari agents. So maybe you're cut out for this ...

Inside sources tell me that they are not working for the core Guristas leadership in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, so they won't be as deadly and organized as I first feared. But they're still a major threat, and as such I need someone to take care of 'em. If you can do the job, in other words take 'em out before they reach Pioneer's Sanctuary, then I'll reward you generously.

It so happens that I know where one of their stopping points will be, I will give you the coordinates of course.

Now I have a mission that would require you to be extremely meticulous and discreet. From looking at your accomplishments here in Fatimar Outpost you probably have what it takes to get it done. And oddly enough I trust you to keep a lid on this more than Kushan Horeat and his men.

If you're still interested, let me know.

130946:
I'll start from the beginning. I joined Frolo's crew many years ago, when I was a young lad, and served under him right up to his death. Those were some good times, and we made a fortune from harvesting gas clouds in this area and neighboring constellations. Dorim, Frolo's second son, also served under his father and we became the best of friends.

Now life here was simple, until Frolo died. He was a great man, a remarkable leader. The pioneers out here all looked up to him and followed the rules while he was around. But soon after his death that was about to change.

A few months after Frolo passed away, his firstborn, Jamur Fatimar, arrived in Fatimar Outpost. He had lived all his life with his mother in Amarr space, far away from the grueling life we have here in no-man's-land. Basically he was fed with a silver spoon his entire life, and that rubbed off on him.

As soon as he arrived he claimed ownership of the Outpost. We decided to play along with his little game, as neither I nor Dorim had any real ambition to take on the leadership role. But people quickly started to despise him. He was much harsher than Frolo ever was, and was very detached from the local miners and harvesters here who Frolo used to work along-side. He was a strict, traditional Amarrian ruler who had zero tolerance for any difference of opinion from his own. He implemented a hefty tax which was largely used to pay for his extravagant lifestyle. Needless to say, things got hairy around here. Some of pioneers split away from Fatimar Outpost and founded their own colonies elsewhere, and there were rumors of a rebellion.

When I saw everything that we had built virtually crumbling beneath us, I was forced to intervene. I claimed leadership over Fatimar Outpost. A power struggle ensued, which I eventually won. As you might expect, Jamur was not very fond of losing his title and decided to split away from us, forming his own colony elsewhere in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}. But I've always had the impression that he was out for revenge, and therefore I've had his little colony under surveillance for quite some time. And that's what alerted me to an extremely worrying turn of events. Jamur had been in contact with someone from outside {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, who my sources tell me has promised to help him in 'his war with Fatimar Outpost'. I can't imagine what a bitter, power hungry man like Jamur would do to reclaim his title. I want you to find out for me. I will upload the coordinates of the meeting point into your NeoCom, all you have to do is warp there and disrupt the meeting. Bring this 'agent' to me for questioning.

I've been looking for someone of your talents. It has come to our attention that an armada of Amarr crusaders has arrived in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}. According to our sources, their primary objective is to destroy the Pagera Manton, which they view as being a sacrilegious icon of the Blood Raider faith. They believe the Blood Raider organization is defiling the graveyard of their ancestors, and their aim is to 'give them rest'.

These sorts of incursions are nothing new, but this time they mean business. I've never seen such a huge armada threaten our beloved holy site, and to top it off it's being led by one of the Amarrian High Priests, Heftah Nekmar, which is of some concern to us. He has recently led a campaign of propaganda against the Blood Raider religion from inside the Amarrian territories, and the destruction of the Pagera Manton would certainly be viewed as a mighty victory by his people.

131117:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM, called the Pagera Manton. The Pagera Manton was a giant space-ship that was at the head of a massive Amarrian exploration team that had ventured into unknown lands hundreds of years ago. A malfunction in its warp-drive stranded the ship, far away from the rest of the fleet. During that time space-communication was not as sophisticated as today, and it had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition. Years passed and the crew had finally lost all hope of survival. Food supply was running dangerously low, and it seemed that starvation was inevitable. It was then that one of the officers, an Ammatar by the name of Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands. He staged a successful coup against the commanding officer of the ship and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents inside a secure chamber under his control. These unfortunate souls became the crews new food supply, unbeknownst to most of the crewmembers. For over a year this plan worked, although Kalorr did have to turn to his own followers eventually to replenish his stock of human meat.

Over a century later the ship was discovered by Blood Raider pioneers scouring the distant solar-systems of OK-FEM. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few dozen gigantic tanks encasing millions of liters of blood. Unbeknownst to them the blood had been collected by Kalorr who dried the human meat before consumption. The blood had been meant as a final foodsource after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed as the machine responsible for recycling the air supply malfunctioned which caused the remaining crew to slowly suffocate. Fortunately the blood containers were kept in sub-freezing temperature, which despite over a centry of decay were still up and working when the Pagera was found. And not only that, Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own container, along with his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread through the Blood Raider territories, and their revered High Priest at the time declared it a 'gift from God'. The blood was stripped from the tanks and brought back to the Blood Raider headquarters for examination and ritualistic purposes. Kalorr was cloned, using genetic material retrieved from his body taken from the Pagera, and he was immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Years later he was even made into a saint.

And to this day the Pagera is closely guarded by Kalorr and his small army of clones, extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning and a terrible history has rendered the former Amarrian expeditioner completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups. Kalorr is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals, no matter to which religion or organization they belong to.

131149:
One of the most revered holy sites of the Blood Raiders is located in the constellation OK-FEM. The original Pagera Manton was a gigantic battleship, flagship of a massive Amarrian exploration team seeking unknown systems roughly 200 years ago. However, a malfunction of the then newly built jumpgate into OK-FEM caused an explosion in the Pagera Manton's tachyonometry, resulting in the destruction of its subwarp drives. The ship was stranded in a distant and uninhabited system, and space communication not being as sophisticated as it is today, the Manton had no way of contacting other vessels of the expedition.

Years passed and the crew eventually lost all hope of survival. The food supply running dangerously low, starvation was imminent. Then, one of the senior officers, an Amarr Holder (and secretly a Sani Sabik adherent) by the name of Lieutenant-Commander Kalorr Makur, took matters into his own hands: He staged a successful coup against the ship's commanding officer and had his most loyal followers bind and gag the dissidents within a secure chamber. These unfortunate souls became the new leadership's food supply, although Makur apparently managed to keep this fact secret from most of his followers. According to the ship's logs, maintained by Makur, this plan worked for several years... although there is evidence that Makur did occasionally turn to his own followers to replenish his "stock," hiding his motives behind the guise of executions for crimes supposedly committed against the commander. Eventually, the ship's air supply malfunctioned, and the sixty or so remaining crewmembers slowly suffocated.

Over a century later, some time before the Amarr invasion of the Minmatar homeworlds, the ship was discovered by Amarr outlaws. They found the remains of the crew, and more importantly a few enormous tanks holding thousands of liters of human blood; it seems Makur had dried his human meat before consumption. The blood had been intended as a final food source after the meat supply had run out, but was never actually consumed before Makur and his crew died. Fortunately the containers were kept in cryo-vaults, which despite over a century of decay were still up and working when the Manton was found. And Kalorr Makur's body was discovered in its very own cryo-tank, along with those of his closest allies.

News of the find quickly spread throughout the pirates in the region and thence into the territories of the nascent Blood Raiders, whose revered High Priest declared the Manton a "gift from God." The blood was brought back to the Raider headquarters. Kalorr Makur was cloned using genetic material retrieved from his body, and immediately instated as an officer of the Blood Raiders. Several years later, he was beatified and sainted.

To this day, the floating wreck of the Pagera Manton is closely guarded by Makur and his small army of clones, all extremely loyal to the Blood Raiders. Drugs, many generations of cloning, and a terrible personal history have rendered the former Amarrian capsuleer completely insane. And despite the Pagera being a popular point of pilgrimage for the members of the Blood Raider organization, few even of that cult venture there outside of large, heavily armed groups, for Makur is known to pick off stragglers for his sinister rituals no matter to what religion or organization they belong.

Welcome to Yakura Harvesting Depot, {[character]player.name}. I have use for someone like you. You see, I'm not the typical Serpentis member, in fact I never took up the stereotypical practice of piracy. Instead I've devoted my life to creating a business which specializes in harvesting gas and rock from the Pegasus constellation. I still work for the Serpentis of course, but I've more interest in finding lucrative roid and gas fields than bullying the passersby.

Anyway, I have a small job for you. Our scanners have indicated that there is a large quantity of gas clouds in a certain area in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We think the source is pretty close to a certain asteroid belt, which has been claimed by an Astral Mining Inc. expedition. I want you to warp over to this asteroid belt and take a sample from one of the asteroids there, bring it back to me for inspection. We're hoping to find gas residue on the rock which would indicate the presence of gas clouds nearby.

Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I have a task I want you to complete. If you do it right, I might have a small reward for you.

The next Legends Trial battle starts at midnight tonight, and as head of security around here, my job is to make sure it goes as smoothly as possible. However, there is a small problem. The documents detailing the fighters and their ships were scheduled to be delivered to me from {[location]objectiveLocationID.name} this morning. However, the courier assigned to the task has obviously failed us, and as such I need you to step up and fill his place. Go get the documents and bring them to me. Do it quickly and I will have a little something extra waiting for you.

Fly safe.
131166:
Precisely one week from today, the Gallente Gaming Commission will have another Legends Trial tournament. The famed contestant, Kuroki Tselmi, will be going up against his long-time rival, Hadni Riiuto. Now, everybody loves to see two fighters face each other when they also have a personal dislike for each other. It makes the entire fight that much more intense. Of course, given the nature of mankind, everybody and their pet has placed some money on the outcome of this fight.

Acquaintances of mine also placed money on this fight and we are all hoping that Kuroki Tselmi will win. He usually does, but it probably won't hurt if we try to give fate a little nudge, here. This is where you come in.

I need you to go to Riiuto's agent. When you meet him, have a word with him about this whole business. He'll know what to do next, and we'll all be able to sleep a little easier at night knowing important people won't lose a lot of money on the match.

Now, I have spoken to Riiuto's agent and he sounds fine with it, but keep your wits about you; don't go thinking this is going to be a walk in the bio-dome. This needs to go precisely as planned with no screw-ups, otherwise the Betting Commission will be on top of this like a Gallente escort, and they'll ride this thing for all it's worth if they find out.. I suggest you bring some friends to make sure the agent doesn't feel like telling anyone about this. What do you say, do we have a deal?

131170:
As it turns out, you did your job a little too well. We seem to have scared Riiuto into seeking protection from the Gaming Commission. Perhaps we should have stuck to bribery. Oh well, we'll remember that for next time. We still need Tselmi to win this match against Riiuto and one way of accomplishing that is having Riiuto pull out of the match prematurely due to “unforeseen circumstances,” or whatever the Commission will choose to call it when you blow him out of the sky.

Because of our previous attempt of nudging fate into the right and profitable direction for my friends, our boy Riiuto is a little more concerned about his safety. He is flying with a heavy escort, but luckily for you I have a plan that cannot fail if you follow the instructions to the letter. It's not that complicated; just go to the location and hide behind an asteroid. After some time you'll see Riiuto and his escort meet up with a fuel tanker to refuel their ships. This will be the time to come out of hiding and attack them. If you attack before this moment, Riiuto and his escort will know something is up.

I trust you will perform as well as you did before. Don't let me down now, because I took the liberty of placing a little more money on this, using another friend of mine. If you're good to me, I might add you to the payroll during the next Legends Trial, or get you better seats if you want to play it safe. You do want to Tselmi to win, right? I mean, you're a sports fan, right?

131174:
We had a team of people doing mining work for us in one of our harvester outposts. It's a thankless and hazardous job, eons away from the safe mining you ship pilots get to engage in. The harvesting equipment they have to use is incredibly dangerous in untrained hands and requires both physical strength and endurance, particularly for the length of time these people have to work. I daren't even think of the accidents that might have occurred had the Minecore harvesters not taken it on themselves to ease their working days a bit with some innocent entertainment. It breaks up the monotony somewhat, so that one's focus on the mining laser won't accidentally slip, leaving some poor soul plastered all over the nearby asteroids.

The Minecore harvesters aren't allowed to have any signals in their suits apart from the ones required to run their equipment. All they have is closed communication channels. So a few began telling jokes, and some of them shared stories from past work, and eventually it turned out that one or two of them, embarrassed though they were at first, could even carry a tune. There is now a core troupe of harvesters who have dedicated themselves to keeping up their coworkers' spirits, maintaining a steady stream of radio talk all through the day. These are men whose only thoughts were how long it was until the end of their shift and how much they were going to drink when they got back to their quarters, and now for the first time they all have something to look forward to.

Except that their workplace is now under siege by rogue drones, and the company apparently refuses to waste manpower rescuing 'expendable resources'. If these people die, the tradition dies with them, and the entire workforce slides back into old, ugly habits. I cannot let that happen, no matter what the company thinks. I want you to go in there and get them.
131175:
Thank you for your task. I know not everyone cares about company morale, but with these poor people, distraction and boredom can kill. I'm sure the whole mess will give them plenty to talk about when they feel up to returning to work.

Unfortunately, we have a new problem. Not everyone feels so philanthropical toward their fellow man, even under circumstances where you'd think that people would stick together and help one another out. Now that you've cleared the last of the Minecore harvesters out of the area, the scavengers arrive. I have reason to believe that these rogue harvesters, unaffiliated with Minecore, have moved in and are proceeding to rob us of our equipment. These people undoubtedly intend to set up a business of their own, and plan to use our property as a starting point. The next step will certainly be attempts to headhunt our own employees, with extravagant offers of better working conditions, higher pay, more benefits and time off. Total and utter lies, all of it. Rogue operators pay even less, and if you desert the company to go work for them, you might as well have placed yourself in indentured servitude. I am not letting that happen to my people, especially now that they've built so much camaraderie and trust. I want you to return to the outpost, find these cowardly harvesters and destroy them, and retrieve our mining equipment.

Now, most of our mobile research facilities are expendable, but this one is a bit special. Get in there and retrieve the imprisoned chemist, Achove Oullen.
131177: No worries. I´ll be back with him as soon as possible. And no boy bands. Got it.
131178: Excellent. Now we just have to hope our dear friend recovers from his trauma and can get back to work A.S.A.P. But we still have to deal with thouse CTF Forces before the inflict more damage to our operation, so talk to me again in a minute, after I take this Com-call.
131179:
One of our labs a few systems out is under a DED blockade, and all our "material" there is being confiscated. Our guards are being hit with serious firepower even as we speak. Now, most of our mobile research facilities are expendable, but this one is a bit special. Our lead chemist there, Achove Oullen, was recruited after his rather embarrassing fall from grace at Poteque Pharmaceuticals. The man was an incredibly hard worker, often spending entire nights in his laboratory, and had been doing sterling work for the company.

Unbeknownst to his superiors, though, he had a tendency to use the lab for certain pet projects outside office hours. Most of these were completely illegal, of course, and poor Achove was found out when he attempted to synthesize a new drug that would allow the user to experience synesthetic highs, in which you see smells, taste sounds, and so on. His first test of the drug held him in rapt fascination all night.

All seemed to be going well until his radio alarm rang. Bit of a funny story, actually. Due to his frequent overnight stays at the lab, he had set the alarm to wake him at a preset hour in the morning so that he could take a quick shower and shave before his associates poured in, and had unwisely tuned it to a station that played almost nothing except the top 20 hits in the region. The songs apparently smelled and tasted so vile that he vomited, splattering equipment and furniture with chunky bile. He was still retching when his coworkers arrived on the scene, and to this day he still screams at the very mention of pop music.

All that aside, we felt he showed promise, so after he had been dismissed from Poteque, we snapped him up and set him back to work in earnest on his synesthetic drug, a booster called Sikes-8. The drug will be a key factor in our operation for the next year, but all this work will be for naught if poor Achove is taken into custody. Heh. No doubt they'll play an endless sequence of boy bands until he just cracks and tells them everything! Ha! But seriously, it would only be a matter of time before the Cartel got their hands on the information and used it to strengthen their hold on the drug market.

You have to intervene; retrieve the imprisoned Achove for us. Just be careful what you play on your ship's loudspeakers when you're on your way back....
131180:
While on a routine courier job, one of my pilots recently ran into CTF forces that nearly destroyed his ship. Fortunately, his systems were intact enough that he could track their heading. Our covert ops ships later scanned the area and eventually discovered what is likely a DED communications and supply station.

I want you to scope out the location, and if you find any hint of a CTF depot there, I want you to conduct a surgical strike on them before they know what's happening. If you come across any shipyards or supply facilities, I want them blown to pieces so they can't fuel and repair their ships, and if anyone stands in your way, hull their ships. Show no mercy.
131181:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! Thanks again for saving Achove. I hope you remembered to place him a sound-proofed cabin on your way here.

The DED activities have begun to trouble us. There have been far too many sightings of their ships, including ones that would not be here unless they had a safe-house of some kind nearby. While on a routine courier job, one of my pilots recently ran into CTF forces that seemed entirely blasé about their ammo supplies ... at least judging by the prodigious amount they fired into his shield, armor, and structure. He barely escaped the onslaught; his ship was taking direct hits to its hull, and the barrage of munitions was such that it nearly roasted him in his pod. Despite being wounded and needing medical attention, he reported to me directly after he'd docked. Stout fellow.

He told me that after the CTF forces had fragged his ship for a while, they'd casually and inexplicably taken off, and fortunately his systems were intact enough that he could track their heading. He gave me as much information as he could, then headed off to the med labs to have new eyebrows tattooed on.

The information he gave me wasn't much to go on, but it was enough. Our covert ops ships scanned the area and eventually discovered a location that is extremely likely to hold a DED communications and supply station. As much as I'd like to avenge my brave pilot and his scorched eyebrows, we don't dare risk a full-scale attack on the depot for fear that they will pick up the fleet's signal on their scanner post. Instead, we need to send in a single ship, or maybe a small squad of pilots if you have some willing allies, hoping that they can sneak in without triggering a full-scale reaction.

I'm putting you in command of this operation. I want you to scope out the location, and if you find any hint of a CTF depot there, I want you to conduct a surgical strike on them before they know what's happening. If you come across any shipyards or supply facilities, I want them blown to pieces so they can't fuel and repair their ships, and if anyone stands in your way, hull their ships. Show no mercy.
131182: Excellent work! Hopefully CTF will finally give up their efforts in our region ― or at least they won't be able to re-supply their ships in our space anymore ― and we can finally start mass-production of our new drugs. Oh, and by the way, Achove Oullen is doing well and extends his thanks. For what it's worth, he's taken up listening to Amarrian choral chanting, of all things...
131183: Good on you, {[character]player.name}! Destroy every one of those shipyards and make sure all the defending forces are destroyed. No prisoners, and no survivors.
131184:
For quite some time now, we have been aware of a security leak within our organization. Federal operatives have always been willing to pay a lot of money for inside information, and it has become abundantly clear to us in recent days that one of our commanders has fallen prey to the temptation of working for both sides.

We have no proof as to who the leak might be, but recently some of our people retrieved an encoded computer chip from the wreckage of a scout outpost. The chip contained documents which we think provide clues to the mole's identity. The chip is slightly damaged, so some parts are unencrypted and other parts missing entirely.

I want you to take the chip and bring it to our best code decryptor. He currently resides deep within the A8-XBW system, and you might have to go through some rogue drones to reach him there. Don't annoy him too much: He values his privacy and doesn't like being disturbed. There is a data terminal at his docking bay, so dock there and then bring me back the news.

131188:
Our decryption expert just got back to us with the results. Fortunately, the chip was not too damaged. We have some very trustworthy indications that the snitch is a well known commander within the organization. It came as quite a surprise to me personally that he would start playing for the other team, though in retrospect it does make sense that only someone in his position would have been able to feed the enemy the information they've apparently been receiving.

The commander is on vacation right now at his residence and doesn't go on active duty for three days, so now is the time to strike. His residence is in the A8-XBW system. Gear up and fly there as fast as you can. Make the bastard suffer for betraying us ― let's hope it will be sufficient warning for others not to do the same.

Return to me when you have completed your task.

Great work. 
But somthing tells me they aren't done yet. So be ready if i need you in short notice.
131194:
Something even bigger has come up, and I'm putting my best pilot, you, on the job. We've just learned that the group of Fed ships you took out wasn't just there for retaliation. It appears that through an informant within our ranks, the Federation have caught wind of our next-gen booster project. The platoons in question were reportedly dispatched for one purpose: to locate and terminate our star scientist, the one who masterminded the project and who currently holds the prototype formulas. The Federate officers you took care of were getting awfully close to him and managed to relay their information back to Fed Central before you took them out, so now we have an even larger Fed group attacking our primary research facilities in 4-EP12. 

The facility itself is not as important as the scientist himself, and the plans he holds. Should these designs fall into the wrong hands, years of research will be lost and those responsible, myself included, would probably find ourselves swiftly exiled from existence. Load up your guns and put an end to this siege. Save our scientist, and return to me when your task is complete.

Some of our advertisers have a real problem with this, so they need the operation brought to a halt.

Naturally, I'd do it myself, but I figure since you are such an eager puppy you would just love to do it for me, wouldn't you?

Those blasted Serps just keep bouncing back. They seem determined to profit from the proceedings in some way. After we took out their tournament site, they appear to have immediately put their backup plan into action, namely to put up a brothel for tournament visitors in need of some after-hours entertainment. 

Their hiring practices leave a lot to be desired. They've abducted some of the finest exotic dancers this system has to offer. My immediate superior, bless his heart, has a particular affinity for one of these dancers, a girl who goes by the name of Layla. I need you to head out to the brothel, blow the living you-know-what out of it and bring the girl back. The Scope will be in your debt, friend.
