131202:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! It is good to see there are freelancers who still maintain some loyalty to the Federation. It pleases me greatly that capsuleers like yourself still prove willing to help us out at need. Anyway, if you are looking for something to do, I know a little job that might just mix profit with pleasure.

The Serpentis are setting up a little shop in this area where they are training their fighters, intending to bring them into the tournament. Now, we aren't afraid of a little competition, but these fighters aren't all-natural, if you know what I mean. We're going to need them kidnapped and brought back here. Chances are you're going to find the substance the Serps have been feeding their fighters as well, and I know some people who are very interested to see it recovered. Purely for research, of course. I wouldn't dream of touching the stuff myself....

OK, OK, so maybe years ago when I was younger I might have tried some, but you know how it is — everyone experiments a little. No harm in that. Right? Just don't let me find out that you've kept a little for yourself. I need ... I mean, I want it all. To give to our researchers, of course. Ahem. Yes.

So, well, before you go ... listen, I would appreciate it if you could keep this matter to yourself. I´m sure you´ll agree that not everybody needs to know about this, hm?
131203:
Good day. Looking for a job, are you? I have just the thing for a strapping capsuleer such as yourself. 

We're helping with putting on the Legends Trial, that great and massive confrontation. We've hit a snag, though; we had a shipment of supplies that were supposed to get here this morning, but the convoy ran into some technical difficulties and it appears they won't get here in time.

We've had wind of a Serpentis outpost in the vicinity, though, so we're thinking we might just outsource and play them at their own game. How about it? You up for a little hit-snatch-and-run?

I have another mission for you. Just another small supply run, one for which I'll reward you handsomely, to show our appreciation for... hold on.  Give me a second, here. I have something coming in over the wire.

...

Oh, lord. Oh, sweet sister of mercy. Looks like we made the Serpentis mighty mad. In retaliation for our little loan of goods, they've gone all-out and attacked a Gallente station in XG-D1L

131211:
Welcome back, and congratulations on your task. Not that I had anything to do with it in any way whatsoever, but I'm very happy with your efforts. Which I know nothing about. But good job nonetheless. Whatever you did.

While you were away, we received orders that I've been praying for. We've located the booster manufacturing facility itself, and it's time to strike at the source. There are some that claim this recent attack by an unnamed pilot on a smuggling convoy was badly timed, and that we now have only a few days before the Cartel decides to move its operation to a new secret location. But then, I don't recall those same people giving any good reason why we should allow even one parcel of drugs to pass into the hands of our citizens.

Nevertheless, fingers have been pointed, and people are quite annoyed at having to rush in. While I don't have the slightest doubts that I made the right decision in sending you to destroy that convoy - NOT sending you to destroy that convoy, I should say, because of course I had nothing to do with it - it may nonetheless be a wise decision on our part to get there first and destroy that manufacturing facility all by ourselves. It will give us a little added glory, just in case someone decides to get clever about that convoy business.
131212: One can never have too much loot- ... glory, I mean.
131213: I've had my fill of glory for the time being. Thanks, but no thanks.
131214:
You've heard, I hope, of the Angel Cartel drug smuggling into Minmatar space. No one will ever know how many lives have been destroyed by this ugly scourge, but while we cannot help those poor souls who have already fallen prey to booster abuse, I'm not going to sit by and let the drugs continue spreading to new victims. 

I am aware that not everyone around here shares my sentiments. My superiors feel that it's useless to strike at the dealers and the couriers, that the only way to uproot this problem is to stop it at its source. They say that to do otherwise is a waste of time and money.

And they're right, I'm sure. Of course they're right. So what I am absolutely not going to do is send out a single rogue pilot and tell him to cut off a supply convoy carrying drugs to Minmatar children. Let's be crystal clear on that. I am certainly not asking you to help me out on a secret task to rid us of one clandestine shipment, just one, even if nobody would notice its disappearance anyway. We understand one another, I trust.
131215: We certainly do. I'll be back after I've not destroyed the convoy that's not flying through space nearby.
131216: I'm not doing this. And when I say "not", I mean "not". At all. You understand that, I trust.
131217: The thing you asked me not to do has been ... not done.
131218: Excellent! I'll see you back here after you've done whatever it is you were going to do that I had nothing to do with in any way whatsoever.
131219: I'm sorry to hear that. I had hoped you would see things my way.
131220: Splendid! You've saved lives, you know.
131222: I'll help out. It's for the girl's own good.
131223: Thank you. I'm sure the young woman will learn her lesson from this.
131224: I can't take part in this. Something stinks.
131225: That's a shame. Her uncle will have to make an extra effort to teach her the error of her ways, then.
131227: Excellent. The girl's uncle assures me that he will take good care of her from now on. Very good care indeed.
131228:
Okelle Alash has not yet broken under questioning. However, now that his fleet failed to save him, we have reason to believe that his brother Martokar is going to try it. This is the big break we were hoping for. Martokar is the very man we've been after, a brutal criminal who arrived here on the run, having been implicated in kidnappings, slave trade and the murder of CONCORD officers. He hasn't been here long and has already established himself a big player in the booster smuggling business. We need this man taken down.

Martokar is amassing an attack fleet at the moment, and one of the people he tried to recruit has been spotted by our agents in a nearby establishment, ranting about the lousy offer he got. This man is the only chance we'll get at discovering Martokar's precise location, so we need you to retrieve him right away. If we screw this up, Martokar may strike at any time while we're completely unprepared, and good people will die. Obviously, Martokar is going to want to silence this poor fellow before he can reveal anything, so we need to get there first.

However, we mustn't let Martokar think that we've got sensitive information on him, since that'll only make him change his plans and will ruin any advantage we had. We therefore need you to lay waste to the entire location, making it look like our informant perished in the process. Once you've destroyed the place and anyone snooping around, bring the guy back to us.
131229:
It's time to end the reign of Martokar Alash. The informant you brought in gave us all the information we needed, and we now know where the warlord is.

I cannot emphasize enough how important it is that you wipe out not only this man but the entire force you see there and anything else in the vicinity. Before Martokar came here, he was on the verge of being a target for a Republic invasion fleet. Duliner Nerhoger, the chief of intelligence in the Republic Justice Department, has personally contacted my superiors to notify them that if we fail, we can expect repercussions.

That's not to mention the scourge of organized crime, which we know is always trying to get a toehold. Unless we show Martokar and everyone else that we mean business, someone else will simply move in to fill the gap he left. We have to ensure that the only thing remaining in that place are the burnt and wrecked remains of the last criminal who dared oppose us. But at the same time we don't dare bring in a massive fleet, for fear that Martokar get wind of it and take off. We've trusted you this far, and I have complete faith in your abilities to take care of the matter.
131230: Once I'm done, there will be nothing left but dust.
131231: I'm scared! I don't wanna do it!
131232: Excellent. I'll let Duliner Nerhoger know we've got our best pilot on the case.
131233: ... did you fall into the cloning vat or something?
131235: Great, great, great. Thank you for your services.
131236:
As you may know, Minecore has been launching expeditions into BLC-X0 in order to find more gas cloud sites. We've been pretty successful so far, if I do say so myself. But success breeds the need for more success, and also breeds a certain type of man who expects that success. My superior, Akrada Ubje, is that type of man.

Akrada is one of the few people in Minecore who can deal with the pirates on their own terms. The Angel Cartel have us in a stranglehold, but Akrada is so defiant of everything and everyone that the Angels respect him, and even if it's the grudging respect a predator may show its prey, it's one of the things that has kept them from completely devouring our operations here. Problem is, Akrada expects everyone else to be defiant, showing constant bravery and strength so that the pirates won't think us weak. This means he occasionally demands too much, and the rest of us have to ensure he doesn't push us into something dangerous.

We've recently received word of quite a promising gas cloud. However, we have also heard that Sansha's Nation plans to establish a base there, intending to beat us to the punch. They have put up a scanning sentry there which will call for backup the instant an enemy force approaches. I want you to destroy this sentry, and do it quickly. No matter what Akrada says, we cannot deal with this on our own.

Unfortunately, the Sansha's Nation isn't so easily deterred. They received backup right after you left, and have now set up a full base in the area. The place is crawling with Sansha's pirates and we desperately need your services again. I can't let this get to Akrada, since he'll go berserk and demand we all fly in there, guns blazing. Anyone who refuses will find themselves out of a job at the very least, which in this part of space is tantamount to death by starvation.

131254: Find someone else to do your grunt work.
131255: I don't like the look of those Sansha's. I'm leaving.
131256:
The concept of 'miner's justice' is new to some freelancers here. Have you heard of it? No? It's rather simple, really. Space can be dangerous, and we at the Angel Cartel are charged with keeping the peace, ensuring that people don't step out of line. We don't have the luxury of courts and lawyers, nor the option to hold long and protracted trials, so justice tends to be meted out in swift, decisive doses. It's quite a convenient arrangement for the most part, and the mining harvesters only need to defray the slight cost involved.

Sadly, though, not everyone sees it this way. There are some who feel themselves to be beyond the reach of justice, and who apparently believe they won't have to face the consequences of their rebellious actions. I've received word of a group of harvesters who have been misreporting their earnings and paying only a fraction of what they should, thus swindling the Cartel out of our rightly-earned tribute. Needless to say, this kind of behavior is absolutely unacceptable.

You are to head out, destroy their equipment and ships along with anything else you find, but return the harvesting personnel to us intact. While normally I wouldn't hesitate in demanding their bodies be splattered all over deep space, we need them alive to extract information about any other rogue operations.

131266:
We've finished with the harvesters you brought in, and it turns out they weren't just skimming the profits. There is a gas cloud there, a very valuable gas cloud, which they had discovered and were hoping to keep all for themselves.

This isn't some minor act of subterfuge, it's outright betrayal! I cannot express how angry I am at this. Here we are, working day and night to ensure the safety of these people, and for very little pay, I might add, and this is how they treat us. Rest assured, we will make a memorable example of these traitors. Their bodies will be flayed open and their skin will flap in the wind like the bloodied flags of a failed uprising.

As for the gas cloud, since you were the one who brought these miscreants to justice, you're the only one I trust to inspect the cloud and verify whether it's as valuable as they claimed. Head out there, give it a look, and tell me what you saw. I suppose it's possible that the Minmatars will get a little cranky at the fact that you were responsible for the mutilation and death of their kind, but I'm sure they won't do anything drastic about it. Still, I'd appreciate if you also made sure that the area was clear of enemies.

131276:
You are talking to the last survivor of a vicious, dishonorable assault. I used to soar through this area with the rest of my gang, taking care of business, talking to people who needed a good talking to, maybe knocking them around a bit, keeping things tight and running. I loved my job, and I was good at it.

But then we ran into a bunch of Sansha's, and things went very wrong. They snuck up on us while we were minding our own business, and they murdered every single one of my gangmates. I still have nightmares about those last few seconds, when each one of my communication channels to them was filled with screams, then static. Then nothing at all. The Sansha's left me alive only so that I could crawl back to home and tell the tale, a message that they were coming to push us out of the territory.

We're going to send them a message in return. We don't dare risk total war, though, so we need a freelancer. You are going to head out, find a bunch of Sansha's puppets, and kill them. Bring me back their tags so that I can hang them over my bed like a set of wind chimes; that ought to stop then nightmares for good.

131286:
After you left, I got to thinking. Killing some random gang of Sansha's is good, but it's not enough. All we did was send the message that someone had wanted to kill their grunts. We need more.

As luck would have it, the person reputed to be Sansha's provincial leader in this area, a man named Abufyr Joek, is situated not far from us. If we take him out, along with all his staff and guards, we will be sending a clear message to those brainless drones. They won't dare declare war on us, since they'll have nothing to officially tie the attack to our forces, but they'll know exactly who was responsible. Abufyr probably gave permission for his troops to roam around and viciously murder anyone they met, and even if he didn't he's still the nominal figurehead for them, so his death will be a statement. 

Kill everyone you see at that place, then bring me back Abufyr's head, and we'll show Sansha's Nation what happens when you get the stupid, stupid idea to attack the Angel Cartel. Don't worry about special storage, either, just put it in your cargo hold like everything else. We want it to be good and ripe before we vacuum-seal it to send off to the Sansha.

131304:
This one is personal. I haven't usually bothered too much about Sansha's Nation; they're here, and we're going to kick them out eventually, but until now they haven't been worth the effort. That's all changed. They have taken my sister.

Understand, this is one of very few people in the world who means anything to me. We grew up together, and since I was older by a few years, I was the protector. She isn't too clever, dear Nokana, but she always meant well, and all the times I had to pull her out of trouble were paid for a thousand times over by the times she stood by me when no one else would. When I got this job as an Angel Cartel agent, she demanded that she be employed here as well so that she could keep an eye on me. It's risky business sometimes, being an agent for the pirates, and Nokana wouldn't let me do it alone.

But now it's all gone wrong. Nokana apparently heard of a group of Sansha's who had it in for me, and went to try and negotiate with them. She's wonderful, my sister, but she's no diplomat, and they ended up kidnapping her. If my bosses find out about her meddling they'll fire both of us, so I need you to go in, get her, and return her to me before anyone else finds out. I hear they're keeping her in a slave pen, the barbarians!

131309: Don't worry. I'll take good care of her.

131314:
Now that Nokana is safe, I've decided it's too much of a risk to let her stay here. Wanting to protect me is good and fine, and exactly what I'd expect from her, but she's going to end up getting both of us into serious trouble, and if anything happened to her I would never forgive myself. Not to mention that I'd have to tell our parents, and they'd have my hide.

I would like you to take her back to my parents' place in Cartel space. I know this is a little outside the realm of your usual work, to be escorting someone home like a chaperon, but I'd really appreciate it. You did a good job in bringing Nokana back, and I'm sure you're as eager as I am to ensure that she doesn't cost us any more time and effort.

I'll arrange matters here, talk to her superiors and give them some reasonable explanation. A friend of mine will meet Nokana at the landing point, so once you've docked safe and sound, let me know and we'll take care of the rest.

Just don't let her convince you to turn around or do anything silly. Head straight home with her. And for heaven's sake, don't tell her anything about this conversation. I'll take care of that as well.

131316:
We've run into a little trouble. Word has spread that Okelle Alash is being held captive, and his legion is going absolutely insane. Apparently it's all right for them to terrorize innocent citizens, but not for us to start hitting back. They're tearing through the constellation, firing at everything in sight and demanding that Okelle be returned to them in one piece.

This, unfortunately, is no longer an option, not unless they have a surgeon on their team who specializes in reattaching fingers. We will have to fight them. Their fleet is disorganized as you'd expect pirates to be, but nonetheless they have a small scouting party that flies ahead and coordinates the primary fleet. You have to take out the scouting party first, so that the primary fleet will be left blinded and confused. Once you're done with that, report to me and we'll see if we can use you in taking care of the remnants of Okelle's fleet.
131317:
Right now I'm looking for {[item]objectiveTypeID.quantityName, quantity=objectiveQuantity}. These tags have been implanted into certain pirates which infest {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space, which they use to identify each other with. To acquire them you will most likely have to kill them, or buy them off someone who did exactly that. I don't really care either way, as long as they have been taken care of I'm satisfied.

This might not be the very best way to confirm deaths, but we've been quite successful in the past using this method. Forgeries are almost non-existent, as each tag costs more to manufacture than it's worth on the bounty market. Not only that but we can usually tell a fake apart from a genuine pirate tag. And they have remarkable survivability, usually found in the charred wreckage of the pirate ships despite everything else, including the pirate's corpse, having been completely vaporized.

You can find the pirates carrying the {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} in many places, but I'd first check the asteroid belts in the surrounding systems as attacking defenseless miners is their favorite past-time. Good luck, and have fun.

131497:
We ran Okelle's hard drive through disinfection and decryption, and we got lucky! Sometimes these things are set to self-destruct after unauthorized access, or they've been planted and are full of things that attempt to infect our reader programs the instant we start picking them apart. I'd have thought that our data extraction people would be professional enough not to hook the darn things right up to our systems, but sometimes they get a little overzealous. It took us a month to clear out the last infection we got.

At any rate, we now know Okelle's whereabouts. Remember that he's undoubtedly aware that we're after him, and that we intend to use him as a bartering chip to lure his brother out of hiding, so he's not going to come quietly. Try not to hang around, either, or he'll just escape. Go in there, kill any backup forces you see, and bring Okelle back to us alive.

131749: I'm glad to see you. Things are heating up. You may be aware that we've been hunting the infamous Thukker warlord named Martokar Alash. He's proved quite difficult to provoke out of hiding, but we've finally been given a good lead. Unfortunately it's not to him, but to his brother, Okelle Alash. I don't know if our capturing Okelle will drive Martokar out of hiding, but at the very least it will give him one more thing to worry about. Okelle is a bit of a wild one. He's reportedly done just about every drug in existence, goes through a girlfriend a month and ends up leaving them at that harem of his, has built up a reputation for being near-suicidal in battle, and all in all lives the definite pirate lifestyle. You should be aware that once you start hunting him, though, he may be a little more cautious. He's only foolhardy when he's the one who chooses the battlefield, and this time we're aiming to catch him with his pants down. He'll probably manage to escape before you reach his harem, so if you don't find him there, I want you to bring back something he left that'll allow us to determine his whereabouts. It's a fairly well hidden place, so you'll have to search hard.
131750: So long as it doesn't have to be organic, I'm your man.
131751: Very good. Don't dally there, mind.
131753: Thanks. I hope you didn't pick up anything else at that place.
131754: I'd much rather pay the place an unofficial visit. Thanks, but no thanks.
131755: I do wish you people wouldn't put your own needs first all the time.
131756:
The container you delivered to me was completely empty! Those damned Serpentis must have snatched the documents as you were loading the container aboard your ship.

I'm putting the blame for this mess squarely on your back. You need to solve this, {[character]player.name}! If my superiors find out the documents have been lost, we can expect some heads to roll ... your head, to be precise. Find the documents and bring them to me straight away. They cannot have gotten very far; I'm actually pretty sure they're in this very system.
131757:
While the royal family does not officially condone the fighting between Methros and Arachnan, they do not see it as any major threat to their claim to power in this region. To that end they are willing to let it continue as the infighting is bringing a much needed economic boost to the region.

With this in mind, it is our duty to monitor the conflict and inform the Emperor and his council should either of the parties engage in business detrimental to the empire.

We have a mission suited to your talents my friend. Lord Methros and Arachnan have secret outposts inside their sphere of influence in Araz, from where they conduct various operations. We are of course aware of these outposts, as the Emperor Family has ears and eyes in all corners of the Empire, figuratively speaking of course. I want you to make an unannounced visit to these outposts and retrieve an encrypted data burst located inside them.

I want you to start with Lord Methros' outpost. I'll give you a bookmark to it's exact location, of course. I will inform his guards of your visit as soon as you arrive, since doing it any earlier would compromise your mission.

I'd like you to do some reconnaissance for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, my friend. Our operatives in an outpost within {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} have requested a convoy of goods, through some pretty hostile territory. There are a few routes we could take to reach the destination, and you're going to help us find the safest route.

All I need you to do is scout ahead and see if there are any pirates, rogue drones or dangerous terrain. Report your findings to me. I'll upload a bookmark to the first area into your NeoCom.
131815: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.
131816: So the first area was filled with pirates?  I expected as much.  Looks like we'll be looking some more, get ready for your next mission.

131819:
Why, yes, you heard correctly. I've been contracted by {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} to hunt down their enemies, and I am currently on the lookout for certain tags that would prove their demise. These tags can be acquired only by removing them from their dead bodies, of course. By the way, I'm an expert on appraising tags, so don't bother to try to trick me with forgeries. If you have the genuine stuff, then I'll pay for it. And you'll earn some good will with {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} at the same time. A win-win situation if you ask me.

132102: I want you to escort a convoy of trade goods heading out to our headquarters. It's just a formality, but a necessary one nonetheless. You'll find a bookmark to their current location in your NeoCom.
132103: Rogue drones looting trade convoys? Might be that there's a new hive nearby, I suppose, or maybe it's someone sinister pulling their strings. Who knows? Regardless, you did good ― can't blame you for the convoy's destruction. It was probably destroyed before you set out from the station. Take your reward, you've earned it.
132104:
We've discovered a small repair station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. By itself, this station is no issue, but when our patrols scanned the site they detected pirates in the area. This particular repair station is owned by a local mercenary gang that allows felonious individuals to dock there, and they are therefore aiding and abetting known criminals.

I would like you to do us all a favor and remove this repair station from existence. It's not registered in the government's official database and it's being used to break the law ― that is all the information I need to authorize decisive action against it. It may be guarded, so be careful.
132105: Excellent! That repair station will aid pirates and outlaws no more.
132106: Hm. Guess I was wrong about you.
132108: In this mission you must find and destroy a structure in space, the repair station.  It will not appear in your overview unless you have 'Large Collidable Structure' selected in your overview settings.  Make sure that your settings are correctly configured, finding structures without using the overview is not always easy.

132216:
I'll get right down to it then. I am {[character]agentID.name}, an operative of C.E.R.N., a corporation with strong ties with CONCORD. We oversee a part of their technological research and development, that's all I can tell you. My role within the corporation is confidential, but I am here on official business.

The problem we currently face is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We set up a number of particle accelerators there, for various testing and research purposes, which we abandoned a few years ago. We stripped them of everything we needed, but apparently one of them was still in a condition to continue functioning.

A few weeks ago we were informed that someone, or rather something, had managed to override the system lock we placed on one of the particle accelerators and turn it back on. The problem is whoever did this doesn't seem to have a clue of the dangers involved in running these things, the type of particle accelerator involved has instruments inside which can in theory create energy in enormous quantities. The catch is that once the energy level reaches a certain point, the operation becomes extremely unstable and liable to cause a chain reaction resulting in an explosion of catastrophic proportion, and cause conditions to arise which may result in the formation of a miniature black hole. The latest reports indicate that the particle accelerator has become so unstable it could blow at any minute.

We've already sent a team to shut down the accelerator, but we lost contact with them days ago. The last transmissions we heard from their leader indicated that they had found a strange object which was draining energy from the accelerator. It appears that this object is causing the dangerous energy bursts which we are afraid may cause the conditions necessary for the formation of the black hole. If you were to remove this object, then we expect the particle accelerator to quickly defuse as its capacitor has already drained and relies on external energy output managed by this object.

Now I won't say this isn't dangerous, we've already lost one team on this job. But if you have the guts then the mission is yours. I would however advise you to bring along some friends, the gate leading to the site in question is only configured to work with small frigates which may be poorly equipped to deal with the situation by themselves. A squadron of them however ...

132251:
To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as an available cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably 6,000 m3).

I recently learned that a manufacturer for the Imperial Navy has taken over a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, where they build components for their slave transports. I want you to defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course.

I understand that the Amarr, fearing an action just such as the one I'm proposing, have booby-trapping these cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.
132252:
Yes, my friend, you have. I have a proposal that could make us both a great deal of LUX, as well as inconvenience the Imperial Navy. How does that sound?

I recently learned that a manufacturer for the Imperial Navy has taken over a complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} ― yes, the sheer audacity, I know! ― where they build components for Bestowers, which as you know are their favored slave transports. By going in there and destroying the outpost, we can set their production well back and reduce the efficacy of their entire imperial slave transport apparatus; further, by taking their finished ship's components and modifying them for our own use, we can gain valuable help in advancing our own interests.

I want you to go into that complex, defeat whatever guards or defenses they've put in place, and bring back the freight containers they've got stored there. This isn't as simple as it sounds, of course, and that's why I need someone with your skills and resources: The whole deadspace complex will be heavily guarded, without a doubt … and it gets more complicated than that.

I understand that the Amarr, fearing an action just such as the one I'm proposing, have booby-trapping these cargo containers: You'll need to hack the floating containers to get the secure containers inside, and the outer containers will no doubt detonate if you fail to hack them properly. There may be other decoy containers in the compound, too ― you'll need to find the ones with the secure containers inside.

To complete this mission, you will require a ship with a hacking module online, as well as a cargo capacity of at least 2,000 m3 volume (and preferably one with a capacity of 6,000 m3).

Like the Caldari, the Intaki were once subjugated by the Gallenteans; some remain part of the Federation, but others long ago departed en masse to form the Intaki Syndicate, an independent state on the borders of the Gallente Federation. This “Syndicate” is not overtly political in any real sense ― each member station enjoys complete autonomy ― but the Intaki share economic information and generally help each other, for instance banding together when necessary in their common defense.

In reality, the Syndicate is a haven for various undesirable elements of society, yet without being too rough and tough. It has long fostered the role of mediator between merchants from the empires and the outer regions, which makes trading with Syndicate space quite brisk, and the Intaki are generally known as a highly individualistic, spiritual people.

The Nefantar have left behind their tribal heritage and taken up many (but not all) aspects of the Amarrian religion, a movement that has resulted in a unique blend of cultures.

The Ammatar Mandate and the Minmatar Republic have been locked in a state of cold war for a few years now; since the Vindication Wars, there hasn't been a large-scale battle between them, mainly due to former Prime Minister Karin Midular's diplomatic efforts. However, after Midular's passing, the animosity between the two peoples cannot be denied. The Ammatar aristocracy see themselves as the rightful rulers of all the Matar tribes; for their part, most Minmatar hold little more than bitter animosity toward the tribe that long ago betrayed its cousins, and a widespread hatred of the Ammatar is still common among them.

The oligarchic Caldari State stands for corporate capitalism in its purest form. There are eight great "mega-corporations" that together own more than 90 percentage of all property within the State. Each corporation is made up of thousands of companies of various sizes, each with any number of specific market interests, ranging from simple mining companies to powerful security companies. There is no single, unified government as such; each megacorp rules its territories like a kingdom with little or no interference from the others.

In State matters such as foreign policy, the all-powerful Board of Directors, which consists of the CEOs of the eight megacorps, determines the behavior of the State (the tiebreaker vote in deadlock situations belongs to the CEO of Modern Finances). The Board also makes sure that the social infrastructure of the State remains intact and settles all major quarrels between the corporations.

The eight major corporations are Kaalakiota, Sukuuvestaa, Nugoeihuvi, Ishukone, Wiyrkomi, Hyasyoda, CBD, and Lai Dai.

My friend, whose name I'm afraid I'm not at liberty to reveal, has a small but lucrative mining concern in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Until now, he‘s been subcontracting NMA to do the work there for him, but recently some claimjumpers came in and started throwing their weight around, waving datacards around saying they had just bought the rights to mine there. They came in a couple of transports, sporting some pretty advanced small arms and carrying themselves like they knew how to use them, so the NMA guys played it safe and pulled out; they weren‘t armed to resist a hostile takeover of that magnitude.

Since then, a few well-spent kredits from a couple of his agents uncovered the fact that the guys who moved in are actually working for Core Complexion Inc. ― some Minmatar mining conglomerate that's in bed with the Sebiestor tribe ― and that they apparently got access to mining rights there through some loophole in some treaty. I don't know the details, and it's obviously not legit, but you've got to be careful when lawyers get involved, eh? Anyway, one of these ruffians got drunk one night and let it slip that they were sent in to get their hands on whatever valuable ore they could … I guess for building new ships. I don't know what that means, but it can't be good.

Anyway, here's the thing: Until the legal crap gets dealt with, these guys are untouchable by the authorities. Not to mention the fact that they've been working away to put up some pretty hefty defense towers around the place. But you ... you could roll on in there and just waste them, and we could pretend some pirates or freebooters had taken it on themselves to deal with the Minmatar scum. Nobody'd be the wiser. Whaddya think? The LUX is good.

Religion is of great importance to every Amarrian ― at least in public, if not in private. This fervor has at various times been the cause of both great good and great evil, as has religion in every age of humankind.

Shortly after recovering from the closure of EVE, millennia ago, the Amarrians began to expand their realm and colonize other planets and, eventually, constellations. The worlds they conquered were enslaved, a practice justified by the Amarr Scriptures. Ever since, the Amarrians have attempted to enslave every nation and race they have encountered, and slavery remains an essential part of Amarr society. This practice has, of course, tainted their relations with other races.

Well, things there in the past 24 hours have very quickly gone downhill. Knowing the jig is up, the Amarrians behind the whole thing sent in a task force of ships and supplies, and they've set up a bunch of powerful sentry towers, turning the place into a labor camp so they can strip the place and flee before the military can be called in to deal with them. No doubt taking all the laborers with them at gunpoint to be made into slaves when they return. Cunning bastards.

Since the navy likely won't be able to rally a response soon enough, we desperately need someone like you, who knows starship combat. We need you to go in there and destroy the Amarrian forces so we can send in some personnel transports to get those workers out!

Now, it's possible, though unlikely, that there were some survivors aboard one of those wrecked ships and that they've just recently been able to repair their communications systems enough to send out distress signals. I say it's possible.

What's more likely, though, is that some explorers or salvage workers got trapped out there, or maybe even that some pirates have set up this phony distress call to lure unsuspecting rescuers out to their doom. In any case, I want it checked out, just in case there are actually some of our people still out there. Because of the potential danger, though, I'm only willing to send one of our best, most capable pilots out there. And that means you.

Go on out there and see what's causing this signal. You'll be well rewarded, as always.

I've just received word that the Amarr have actually had the gall to build one of their temple complexes in our space! Well, they're claiming it's their space. And since it's in low-security, we'd be declaring an open act of war by sending in the Republic Navy to remove them. Some day, I think, we'll be ready to do that, but not today.

So what I need you for is this: You know the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system? We cannot allow this humiliating action of theirs to go unpunished. The beauty of sending you in there, as a privateer, is that we can claim complete ignorance. Go there and kill every Amarr you find. Once you've dealt with the defenses, I can send in our people to take care of the rest of the cleanup.

So here's what I've been able to find out: The Minmatar have moved, within the past few days, against a number of our free agents such as yourself; unfortunately, not all of the capsuleers they targeted proved as resilient as you. Four of them were podded, may God rest their souls. I don't like this kind of concerted effort on the part of the Minmatar, {[character]player.name}. God knows what it all means.

Now, my spies report, it seems they are growing even more daring, moving against a number of our civilian colonies. With four of our top pilots gone, and even with the Navy pulling its weight, we're going to be hard pressed to protect all of those people. We all need to do our part. I need you to go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to the civilian outpost there and evacuate those people. Destroy any preliminary Minmatar forces you encounter, get those civilians out of the citizen quarters, and bring them all safely back to me here at {[location]agentStationID.name}.

This mission is extremely dangerous. You should not undertake it without at least a handful of gang-mates all in powerful, combat-ready ships.

While you were out saving those civilians, the Minmatar, as we suspected they were going to, hit several other habitations; in total, the loss of life is staggering. Casualty reports are still coming in, but already it's numbering in the thousands, and likely it will be tens of thousands by the time we have confirmed intelligence. Thank God you were able to rescue some of our people, at least.

But now it is time to meet these Minmatar in battle. Our scouts report a squad of enemy ships, including carriers, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Desperate times call for … ah, you know how it goes: I want you to get out there and stop those ships. I'll be honest, {[character]player.name}. I think the likelihood of your returning to me in a new clone is high, but we have no choice ― we must stop them from slaughtering our people. This, like it or not, is war.

Some years ago, the great Emperor Doriam, in the spirit of co-operation and generosity, allowed some Minmatar refugees to set up home in a former Ammatar station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They were not enslaved, but have been allowed to live free folk, as long as they maintained an excise quota on all of their trade. We have allowed them to continue thus in order to honor the reforms undertaken by Emperor Doriam, but recently one of their number took it upon himself to resist an Imperial customs inspection of their homes, killing the officer in question.

The Minmatar attempted to cover it all up, of course, but we soon got to the bottom of the matter. As they have thrown aside our goodwill and struck down one of the Chosen, the Navy has been ordered to dispense God's judgment upon the heathens. The Admiralty, however, feels that this job is best undertaken by a loyal but independent pilot, rather than official Navy forces, and we have chosen you to dispense with our punishment.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any resistance, so that I can send transports in there to bring back the entire population of the habitats, women, children, and all. After that, destroy all the colony structures, and we will then, in our divine mercy, place any survivors into slavery ― if any are innocent ― and begin them on their path to glorious enlightenment through proper service to the Empire.

Now, we have had reports of Minmatar Republic ships in the area, likely attempting to evacuate the inhabitants: If you are fired upon, you have all authority to defend yourself by any means necessary … and by that, I mean kill them all. God's will be done.

132955: Good. But I must repeat: The Caldari ships in the area are reportedly numerous and powerful. Be careful.
132956: Are you saying you can't do it? Alright, alright, fine. I'll get someone else.
132957:
Well, we seem to have a bit of a situation here, and I'm hoping you can help me out. You see, some civilian living in a colony complex out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} brought some creature home from a nearby planet ― I guess he was part of a work detail there or something ― and apparently it was a carrier for some weird disease that quickly spread through the colony. We quarantined the colony and sent some scientists in there to contain and study the disease, and they've determined that it's a virus that mutates too quickly to be safely controlled.

The trouble is, some Caldari corporation ― we haven't found out who exactly ― caught wind of this and has figured out that it can make a profit by getting samples and selling the virus to their military as a weapon. However, our scientists assure us that the risk is too high without a great deal more research and testing. But we sure as hell don't want the Caldari getting their hands on this stuff.

Trouble is, this Caldari corporation has already moved on the civilian complex, no doubt bribing some government official to get permission to send in mercenary ships and thus secure the area. We can't send in our military for fear of political repercussions, so I need someone like you to deal with this matter for me.

Fly to the coordinates provided and destroy any Caldari ships there, and then destroy all the colony structures so no one else gets any ideas about collecting samples of this biological weapon. We'll cove the whole thing up as an act of piracy, and it'll soon be forgotten. Especially by you and me. Right? Okay.

Now, we've had reports of some tough ships in their fleet: Be careful out there, but be sure to kill them all, and leave no colony structures intact. We don't want anyone escaping with this virus.
132958:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. {[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!
132959:
This type of breeding facility produces Minmatar children ready to assume their place as servants to the Amarr; rumors abound that the slaves in these places hail from other races as well, including even fallen Amarr who are sent here rather than to penal colonies. 
Brood slaves are held within breeder colonies for years for the sole purpose of increasing a slaver's stock. Discarded when they have outlived their usefulness, these poor people have a terribly short life expectancy, although that fact might be a blessing when one considers the misery of their existence. Slavers who use such methods tend to be secretive about it, anchoring their breeding centers in low-security space; these facilities, however profitable, are looked down upon even in Amarrian society (especially since the Doriam reforms).
132961:
I recently sent a capsuleer out to investigate disturbing reports from the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system: The number of missing persons cases on some outlying planets there has risen sharply and there have even been reports of lost ships. The locals are a superstitious lot, so they blame it on angering some spirit or other, but I have no such beliefs ― I suspect foul play. My capsuleer returned, unfortunately in his pod, but my suspicions were confirmed. What he reported is very disturbing, and we need someone with resources such as you possess to deal with it.

It appears an unprincipled Amarrian Holder has set up a heavily guarded slave breeding facility there. You cannot know the sheer horror of these places, our people penned and bred like cattle; the men sold or sent to work camps, the women used mercilessly. The owner no doubt felt that the place would remain undetected in unregulated space, so close here to a ready supply of … well, what I'm sure they would refer to as “livestock.”

{[character]player.name}, go to this facility, rescue as many of my people as you can, and then reduce the place to cinders! Kill every Amarrian there ― make them pay for what they have done. Leave nothing intact, nothing ― the facilities least of all, lest some other Amarrian come in and occupy them!
132962: That's truly unfortunate. Now what am I supposed to do?!
132963: See to it. Get those poor people out of that hellhole!
132964: Ah, wonderful. I knew you wouldn't fail. Justice has been done.
132965: Well, I see where your priorities lie…. Good day.
132967: I feel bad about those poor people, but the defenses at that compound are beyond me. I give up.
132968: I sympathize with the plight of those people, of course, but take on an entire slaver complex by myself? That's suicide. Clones are too expensive for that.
132969: I've rescued the slaves and destroyed the facility.
132970: Don't worry, I'll make every one of them pay in blood.
132974:
{[character]player.name},

Scouts inform me that the station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has been evacuated and disassembled. No doubt the Holder who owned the place caught wind of our efforts, and your tardiness has allowed him time to remove his operation to another system.

May the fates of those slaves weigh on your soul.

{[character]agentID.name}
132975:
A couple of years ago, the Serpentis Corporation built a station out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and everyone in the constellation has been worried about it since. At first, as always with the Serpentis, things were fine ― they kept up a clean front and acted like a legitimate corporation. More recently, though, they've been pirating nearby gates and causing all kinds of problems for the local police forces. CONCORD intervention is minimal, of course, in low-sec, and they're always careful to make things seem like some other pirate group is responsible.

These raids must be stopped. And here's an interesting thing: Interstellar law states that an unoccupied station can be freely commandeered. And that Serpentis station apparently has some state-of-the-art tech that we'd like to get our hands on. So that's why I need you: {[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and destroy every damned Serpentis you find there so we can go in and claim the station for our own.
132976: Many thanks. I came as soon as I got your message. Is there something I can help you with?
132977: I've reconsidered your offer, and I've found it wanting. Sorry, I‘m out.
132978: A Serpentis battle station, and you want me to go in there? Are you mad?! Uh... no! As if...!!
132979: The Serpentis station is defenseless. Good fight, that was.
132980: Oh, yeah, take out some Serpentis? For sure! I hate those guys!
132985: Wow, take it easy. I just asked. No harm in asking, is there?
132986: Ha! Well done! I knew you wouldn't let me down, {[character]player.name}.
132987: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}. Do be careful, though. It won't be an easy job.
132988: {[character]player.name}, this was our first real opportunity to strike back at those bloody pirates. I can't believe this!

132991:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

133043:
Some of the top cybernetics experts in the region were recently here at {[location]agentStationID.name} for a conference, and they made me a proposal that I found quite intriguing. These scientists theorize that the Sansha mindslave technology is leaps ahead of anything we currently have in the realm of cerebro-emission communications. You might call what they've got a sort of limited telepathy, I suppose. Anyway, these scientists were having heated arguments about the risks and benefits of toying with Sansha tech. And that's where it gets interesting.

A handful of them approached me after the conference and spoke of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that they had learned of. They asked if I knew any ships' captains who might be interested in “acquiring” a few Sansha mindslaves for them to experiment on. Now, a friend in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this station very soon, so our window of opportunity is narrow. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and getting a little something on the side.

Destroy a Sansha tower and pick up some prisoners. What could be easier?
133044: Thank you, {[character]agentID.name}. I trust you are well. You have some work for me?
133045: I think I'd rather not finish this mission. Sorry, second thoughts: Sansha are too creepy.
133046: I don't think I care to bring Sansha aboard my ship, thanks very much. No, find someone else.
133047: The Sansha Battletower is no more, {[character]agentID.name}, and the prisoners are here in station.
133048: Sansha prisoners, eh? Well, I can set my cargo bay to keep them in cryo-containment, I suppose. Sure, I'm in.
133053: I understand your reticence, but think of the LUX! Ah, well, your loss.
133054: Well done. I'll send the reward directly to your Interstellar account.
133055: Excellent. I'll await your return with bated breath … and a heap of LUX.
133056: Blast it! Oh, fine. I'm sure I can find someone else to share the reward with me.

{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Solen Sagul, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Sagul's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Sagul has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

133087:
I do, yes. It's quite sensitive, actually, so I'd appreciate it if this matter remained between us. It seems some cybernetics experts among the Caldari and the god-fearing Amarr have recently made efforts to acquire Sansha mindslave technology. Now, we don't know what they're after, specifically, but we can't afford to let them jump ahead of us. We have a couple of sympathizers among them who we think we can convince to defect, so maybe they can keep us up to date on what has transpired with this Sansha research.

Anyway, we know of a Sansha base in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and a friend of mine in the Admiralty tells me the Navy is apparently planning to move against this base very soon, so I've devised a plan. Our window of opportunity is narrow, so you'd need to be ready to move fast. We'd be doing the authorities a favor, and allowing our people to remain abreast of the most current scientific theory.

You seem a little confused. Oh, I guess I haven't really filled you in on my little brainstorm… Heh. Ok, here it is: Go out there, destroy the Sansha tower, and pick up some prisoners to bring back here. Easy enough, right?
133088:
Solen Sagul found a way to sneak back into the research facility here in {[location]agentStationID.name}; he got the help of some old friends in the corporation who had no idea he is ... changed. The problem is that he managed to slip out with copies of some preliminary design documents for a prototype battleship that's going to be built here in the station next year. I take it I don't have to tell you how valuable these documents are, nor what would happen if they fall into the wrong hands.

Now, we managed to get a tracking beacon painted onto Sagul's ship as he blasted out of here, and one of our scanning engineers was then able to track him to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We sent a recon pilot out there, and she was able to pick up some heavy drone activity. We need those copies of the design documents destroyed, {[character]player.name}, along with Sagul and all of his “friends.” If you get out there and he isn't around, don't worry: He's bound to show his face out there eventually.

133178:
{[character]player.name}, an employee of ours, Dimitri Ulanus, has been acting a little odd lately; he comes and goes at strange hours and doesn't say where he is going or where he's been, but he often takes company ships and disappears for days at a time. We are lucky if he shows up for meetings, and when he does appear he utters the strangest things, completely inappropriate and ... well, just unsettling. We could deal with it if we thought he was just insane, but we are afraid it's more than that.

You've heard those stories about people taken alive into rogue drone hives? Well, one of Ulanus's co-workers claims he heard the man muttering something about “the hive mother” and “the song of the drones.” We need to be sure that Ulanus has not been ... taken by the drones. We had security look around in his logs and they found this location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that he's visited several times in the past months. It's a dark, nasty part of space, though, and I can't send just anyone: Maybe you can take a look and tell us what you find.

Oh, and if you do find anything remarkable there, I need you to get in close and have a good look before you report back to me.

Recent advances in station design among the Minmatar, particularly the Sebiestor tribe, have resulted in frighteningly powerful battle stations capable of withstanding tremendous punishment. They are not to be underestimated.

{[character]player.name}, these Minmatar rebels, as you know, are always causing problems, so their raids in outlying systems don't normally draw too much notice. Not normally. Recently, though, we've been hearing rumors about some kind of “super” battle station they're building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, supposedly with a full capital ship maintenance array. I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, but just to be safe, maybe I could pay you to check things out for me?

So, could you fly out there and investigate these rumors for me? I'll pay you handsomely. And if you do encounter any Minmatar, or any kind of enemy station, just take care of it for me, won't you? We can't afford that kind of trouble around here. As is standard these days, do it quickly and I'll throw in a substantial bonus. What do you think?

133302:
The oligarchic Caldari State stands for corporate capitalism in its purest form. There are eight great “mega-corporations” that together own more than 90 percentage of all property within the State. Each corporation is made up of thousands of companies of various sizes, each with any number of specific market interests, ranging from simple mining companies to powerful security companies. There is no single, unified government as such; each megacorp rules its territories like a kingdom with little or no interference from the others. 
The eight major corporations are Kaalakiota, Sukuuvestaa, Nugoeihuvi, Ishukone, Wiyrkomi, Hyasyoda, CBD, and Lai Dai.
133303:
Recent advances in station design among the Caldari, who have shared their designs through treaty with their Amarrian allies, have resulted in frighteningly powerful battle stations capable of withstanding tremendous punishment. They are not to be underestimated.

{[character]player.name}, our scouts have just discovered an extremely powerful battle station the Amarrians are building, combining their efforts with top Caldari military designers, out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The truly frightening part, though, is that the damned thing is apparently pretty much fully operational ― who the hell knows how they've managed to keep the entire project hidden for the months it must have taken to build! ― and worse yet, it's tricked out with a massive capital ship maintenance array.

Now, I don‘t really have the resources at hand to investigate these rumors, and I‘m afraid that it‘s going to take the Navy too long to get out here to deal with the thing. So I imagine you can see where this is all going by now: I need someone to head in there and take that station apart, and it has to happen right now. You think you can handle this one? Needless to say, we can't afford any Amarr capital ships being built or serviced so close to our territory.
133304: Thanks, {[character]agentID.name}. Been a while... I think. I get to so many stations, see, that it's hard to remember where all I've been sometimes.
133305: I can't finish the job, {[character]agentID.name}. I‘m sorry.
133306: A simple recon mission? No, thank you. I had expected something a little more ... meaningful.
133307: By all the hells, that was a tough fight. If the Amarr are putting these things together elsewhere, we should be concerned. Very concerned.
133308: Damn. This is serious. Okay, I'm on it.
133313: I'm sorry you find things too dull for your liking here, {[character]player.name}.
133314: I don't like to think about it, {[character]player.name}. But it bears thinking about.
133315: That's why I called you in on this one, {[character]player.name}. I knew you'd jump on it.
133316: Not as sorry as I am! What the hell's going to happen now??

133408:
A few months ago, a relative of one of the executive officers of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} disappeared for a while. I won't name any names, because we want to avoid tarnishing any valuable reputations. You get me? Okay. We now know that she was involved with some shady fellows, one guy in particular who's known for his close ties to people in the Blood Raiders. I understand he's a pilot who's trying to get accepted into the Raiders' organization, actually.

Now, the girl doesn't want to talk about what happened, but she was pretty messed up and she's now with child. I think she had a crush on this guy for some time, or at least that's what her friends told me. Poor kid. This guy needs to be brought to justice. Terminal justice, if you take my meaning. The beauty of it is, we know he's currently hiding out at a Raider recruitment station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so if we take out that whole station, then we make points with the authorities and we clear up this personal issue at the same time.

So here it is: I want you to go out there and take out that recruitment station ― I mean reduce it to scrap ― along with any Blood Raiders you might find guarding it. Sound good? The reward, as always, will be commensurate with the risk.

133412:
The Amarr Empire has had its share of religious cults and fanatics in the past, but few have been as successful, or as much feared, as the Blood Raiders. The Raiders are a corrupted sect of an ancient cult called Sani Sabik, which historically used human blood in its rituals. The Blood Raiders believe that cloned bodies have “purer” blood than other bodies, and this explains their penchant for operating mainly in space, attacking unwary spacefarers and draining their bodies of blood.

The Blood Raiders are led by the fearsome Omir Sarikusa, who has remained on top of the DED most wanted list for many years now. Under his leadership, the Raiders have become more organized, and they have firmly established several bases in the Bleak Lands region.
133413: Are you serious?! I mean, I'd heard you were unstoppable.
133414: That is good news. Very good news. Well done.
133415: Too bad, {[character]player.name}. You could have made some serious points with the powers-that-be on this one.
133416: Glad to be here. So I assume there's something I can help you out with?
133417: I'm gonna have to call it quits on this mission, {[character]agentID.name}. Sorry.
133418: Man, I've tangled with the Blood Raiders before. But take out a fully guarded station?! No, I don't think I'm interested.
133419: It is done. The Raider station is destroyed, and the creep who assaulted that young girl is no more.
133422:
{[character]player.name}, The cretin who assaulted my boss‘s relative is now a member of the Raiders, and he‘s long gone from the recruitment station. The military has been called in to deal with the station itself, so our opportunity is lost. Damn shame, too. I had high hopes for a promotion once this was dealt with.

Guess maybe I should look for someone else next time, maybe, eh?

Formed by two former members of the Caldari Navy who go by the names “Fatal” and “The Rabbit,” the Guristas are a constant thorn in the side of the Caldari State. The Guristas are traditional pirates in the sense that their operation is not based around some creed or ideology, but rather a plain and simple motivation: greed.

133445:
The Serpentis Corporation was founded a few decades ago by V. Salvador Sarpati. At first a legitimate corporation, it was engaged in hi-tech research, but with time its ties to organized crime grew and the Serpentis research stations, scattered around in remote areas, became infamous pirate havens. Sarpati made a deal with the Angel Cartel early on to gain protection for his stations, and the duty was taken on by the Guardian Angels. Both sides have prospered enormously from this deal ― Serpentis can operate in peace, and the Angel Cartel gets access to the illegal research efforts of the Serpentis.

It is strongly believed that Serpentis is the largest developer and manufacturer of illegal neural boosters, especially since Sarpati's father was a renowned specialist in that field. The home of the Serpentis criminal organization is the Phoenix constellation in the Fountain region.

133475:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We have since received intelligence confirming that the Legion has been hired to assassinate one of our high-ranking officials. We can't let this happen, of course, so we need someone of your caliber to destroy them all. Make sure no one survives.

Of course, we ourselves have used the Legion in the past for … well, for various things. So we don't want to make a big political scene out of this if we ever have to hire them in the future. That's why we mustn't send one of our own ships out to confront them. No, you're the right one for this job. Leave no trace behind; I don't want this biting us in the ass later on.

Oh, and one other thing: Our spies inform us that Taisu Magdesh might actually be part of the Mordu strike force, so be extra careful if he appears ― his reputation is hard won.
133476:
The origin of Mordu's Legion is an indirect result of the Gallente-Caldari War, during which a group of Intaki military personnel sided with the Caldari. The Intakis were placed into a separate unit commanded by a Caldari officer named Mordu. After the war, the Intakis settled in Caldari space, but unwillingly became embroiled in a battle against Caldari locals in what is now known as the Waschi Uprising. Mordu's Legion formed at that time as a mercenary fighting force, and after the uprising it stayed active, working for the highest bidder ― but, it is said, acting always with integrity and honor.

Mordu's Legion is loosely associated with the Caldari Navy, but remains independent. The Legion is commonly hired by companies to protect valuable assets in low-security space, most often near the Caldari State; for instance, Outer Ring Excavations pays the Legion handsomely to patrol the Outer Ring region.

The Angels have a “research station” out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. That‘s bad enough. Now, last week, a friend told me that a couple of scientists who work for his pharmaceutical corporation were kidnapped by the Angels and taken to their glorified floating drug lab. Their ruffians have been showing up in stations all through the system, and in nearby systems too, pushing some new, experimental drug they're making by the shipload in this station of theirs. “Wrath,” they're calling it. Well, that's the last straw.

I want something done about this, and the Navy doesn't seem to care about what's going on. So I've arranged for a nice little reward for the first captain who's willing to go out there and take out that station. I'm serious. Destroy the whole place, and take out all the pirates you see flying around there. And if you can, bring those scientists back here, too; they have families to feed, for god's sake!

Piracy ramped up in local shipping lanes. And now this: We find out that the Serpentis have moved on and pretty much left the place in the hands of the Angels.

Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, an Amarrian named Galin Famis, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

Now, the Amarr government has spoken out against this act of corporate terrorism, but so far they haven't taken any overt actions to deal with it. We could make big points if we could find Famis. We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I'll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

We're not expecting you to go to war for this, but you should be prepared to meet some rough customers.

But before we wiped their minds, they gave us clues to the location of their leader.

And what emerged was the Fellowship of the Flame of Peace.

Let me make it clear: I want you to go in there and wipe them out. You knocked them off balance with your previous attack. Now you must finish them off. I've uploaded the location of their hideout into your databank. Now, get going, and don't come back until you've destroyed them.

Go there, destroy their habitat, and crush all resistance. Capture some of them alive and bring them back for interrogation.

We know that the cultist have members from all walks of life, civilians and otherwise. Some of them are likely to be experienced combat pilots, though. Don't go out there without fitting your ship for a fight.

The frigate Sunhammer was recently attacked by Angel Cartel pirates; the captain called for reinforcements and managed to warp away, but the Angels scanned him down and pursued him, and the ship was lost... yet not before the fast-thinking captain jettisoned his cargo to avoid the risk of its being destroyed in the firefight. The captain's pod made it back in one piece, and the cargo's mostly expendible, but for one thing: Among the junk they had to ditch was a Brutor Tribe roster with all the history and lineage of tribal members in this sector from over a century ago.

Oh, of course there's a good chance the Angels will still be lingering in the vicinity of the cargo, so be prepared for a fight.

I wish I could say Amarr sympathizers were uncommon. We like to tell ourselves that we cleaned house when we expelled the Nefantar tribe – the Ammatar – from the Republic. But of course life is not so simple. For every ten Minmatar we have fighting to free our brethren from Amarrian captivity or to restore some bit of our displaced old ways, there is one who will sell out his brother for a few LUX. And it only takes one dissenter, one cowardly traitor, to undermine the efforts of hundreds. This is why it is always a top priority for the Republic to ferret out the weak or the corrupt from positions of power. And why the corrupt must be instantly and decisively exterminated.

The prisoner who was rescued is one such figure, formerly a local politician of some influence. He had everyone fooled with his historical conservation initiatives, until an anonymous tip led to his arrest. He was on his way to the Tribunal when the Amarr spy took him ― bastard probably had a deal worked out with the Amarr the whole time.

Somehow Delainen subverted Calus's research. They inserted the nanites, programmed by Prof. Delainen, into a battlecruiser's systems, but the things immediately began to malfunction. Everyone in the lab was killed, including Calus.

We believe that the nanites somehow merged Delainen into the ship they had created, making it some sort of bizarre biomechanical symbiote. We want you to go out there and confront it; we've tracked its location, and it's still in this system. I've sent the coordinates to your NeoCom. Destroy it if you must, and then sift through the wreckage to find its central AI core. Bring that back for further study.

Well, that thing is gone, so the station is safe for now. The breached districts have been sealed off until repair crews can get in there. But I suppose you're wondering what happened. Let me back up for a moment.

Dr. Calus's original goal was to create a ship energy system that used advanced nanites to harvest the energy that binds subatomic particles together. The amount of energy that could be produced would be staggering. Think of it. The offensive potential of our ships and weapons systems could be increased a hundred-fold at least, maybe a thousand-fold.

But somehow Delainen subverted Calus's research. He spent years living in close proximity to a nest of rogue drones; he even claimed to have struck up a beneficial relationship with them. Who knows what that does to a person?

They inserted the nanites, programmed by Prof. Delainen, into the battlecruiser's systems, but the things immediately began to malfunction. In less than ten minutes, they had changed the structure of the ship to ... something else. The security 'reels show a flash of light, almost like a jump gate activation, and then Delainen just disappears. Then, immediately, the metallic beast begins to move. We have heard of massive rogue drones, but this is different.

The ship actually spoke to Calus, who was injured during the ship's violent transformation. It said its name was "ROM." Then it blew a hole through the wall of the station into open space and blasted out of there. Everyone in the lab was killed, including Calus.

We believe that the nanites somehow merged Delainen into the ship they had created, making it some sort of bizarre biomechanical symbiote. But we need to know what happened for certain, and this ― well, this Delainen-ROM symbiote, I guess, for lack of a better name ― is the only thing that can give us the answers.

We want you to go out there and confront it; we've tracked its location, and it's still in this system. I'll send the coordinates to your NeoCom. Destroy it if you must, and then sift through the wreckage to find its central AI core. Bring that back for further study.

134116:
I've got some confidential mining survey reports here I need hand-delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I suspect that there are some fairly valuable mineral deposits nearby and they may need help mining them. Deliver this and I'll see to it that you're suitably rewarded... and put in a good word for you with the station manager. I've entered the station location into your Neocom.

134117:

I need it hand-delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Deliver this and I'll see to it that you're suitably rewarded... and put in a good word for you with the station manager.

What do you say?
134118: Ha. Good. Contact me as soon as you get there, alright?
134119: Thanks for the assist. Come back soon and we'll have more work for you.
134120: I say… I'm on my way.
134122: Thanks, {[character]agentID.name}. What sort of work did you have in mind?
134123: Excellent. You had better move. We cannot afford to lose her.
134124: What would you have me do?
134125:
A slave named Jaliti has escaped from the house of the one of the five Heirs to the Imperial Throne. We don't know why or how, but she has commandeered a luxury transport and is still on the run. The Heir in question, who will of course remain anonymous, demands her return, for he greatly enjoys her beauty and company. She is also privy to a great number of personal secrets that could cause great embarrassment to the Heir, and perhaps even to the Imperial Council.

We intercepted a transmission indicating that she intends to meet a contact in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We don't know whom she will meet, but you must stop her and bring her back, any way you can. Alive if possible, but dead if necessary. I'm sure if you're successful, the rewards will be substantial. We are dealing with an Heir, after all.

The ship Jaliti commandeered is known to be well-armed. You might need a battle-ready frigate to bring her back.
134126: I have the slave in custody and her Minmatar lover is floating ash.
134127: Splendid! In custody. Splendid! The Heir will be pleased.
134128: I didn't think you were up to this challenge. Perhaps you should go do something less meaningful.
134129: Most of the difficult labor in the Empire is performed by legions of uneducated slaves, who serve at the beck and call of those who are both clearly and naturally above their station. From conquered races to hereditary servants, Amarrian slaves are diverse and numerous, and they spend their entire lives working toward enlightenment under the guidance of their rightful masters.
134131:
I'm not entirely sure you're ready for an important task like this, but time is of the essence. This may well be the most important mission you have ever undertaken.

A slave named Jaliti has escaped from the house of the one of the five Heirs to the Imperial Throne. We don't know why or how, but she has commandeered a luxury transport and is still on the run.
