134135: You were not paid to think, fool! Your rashness will not sit well with those in power, and certainly does not bode well for your future.
134136: Alas, Jalita has surely escaped by now and is lost to us forever. Your failure will not sit well with those in power, and certainly does not bode well for your future.
134138: The Vitoc Method is fundamental to the Amarr slave market. The Method has two key components: a deadly, highly toxic drug with a seemingly viral ability to mutate, and its carefully-guarded antidote: Vitoc. The subject infected with the chemically engineered virus will suffer an agonizing death without regular doses of Vitoc; his daily dose, however, will react with the toxin to bring him several hours of euphoria in addition to keeping the virus inert for a short time.
134139: Go pick up the Vitoc shipment in its warded container and bring it back to {[location]agentStationID.name}.
134141:
Well, some good, some… Heh. Just kidding. No, folks are saying good things about you.

Anyway, listen, I have a lead on a Vitoc shipment not far from here. I've arranged a buy, but I need someone to make the pick-up under the radar. We've arranged for special packaging that will keep the authorities from being able to scan the stuff in your hold, since the stuff is normally highly illegal around here, so you don't need to worry about that.

{[character]player.name}, this could provide the breakthrough our researchers need. Can I trust you to handle it?
134142: I'm sorry I entrusted you with something so sensitive.
134143: Work fast. We're counting on you.
134144: So my source was right about you. Nice. Listen, I should have more work for you soon. I've arranged for a Civilian Relic Analyzer to be placed in your hangar in station; come and see me once you have it fitted on your ship.
134145: I understand. Please excuse me; I've no time to waste.
134146: Someone bought the Vitoc out from under us. When you're working with smugglers, you work fast, and you don't take anything for granted.
134147: I have to find someone who can get this done before our contact sells that Vitoc to someone else. Don't contact me again unless you have the time to do the job.
134153: I'm not dealing with drug-runners. I quit.
134154: Oh, yeah? All good, I hope. So what's going on?
134155:
Hack the wrecked Amarrian science vessel's computers and bring whatever you find back to your agent. Be sure to have some weaponry fitted as well: There's a good chance some pirates have already caught wind of this wrecked vessel as well.

Make sure you fit out the Civilian Relic Analyzer that your agent gave you before you leave the station. You may have to run it for a few cycles before you find anything on the wrecked ship.
134156:
Well, I've got a job you can do to prove it. We're always looking for information. After the last job you ran, I think I can trust you with something a little more sensitive.

I just got a tip that there's a wrecked Amarrian science vessel nearby that is likely to contain something useful; apparently it was here on some kind of "goodwill incentive program" devised by some clown in CONCORD, but the ship was jumped by Brutor Tribe radicals before it landed in station. Heh. Stupid CONCORD, and pathetic Amarrians ― no doubt they were using this program to scout for slave-ship raids anyway.

Point is, though, that I need you to get in there and hack it; take whatever data you can from it before the pirates rip the whole thing to pieces for salvage. This is more important to us than you can understand right now. Matari lives may well be at stake here.
134157: My source was wrong about you.
134158: Your loyalty is in the right place.
134159: So my source was right about you. I'll pass your name along. Come back and talk to me again in a while, will you?
134160: I see. Don't come back until you're ready to prove yourself worthy of my trust.
134161: The pirates beat you to it. There's nothing left of that science vessel.
134162: The pirates beat you to it. There's nothing left of that science vessel.
134164: I have the information you asked for.
134165: This is all a little too dull for me. I'm more of a straightforward, shoot-em-up kind of capsuleer. Good luck finding someone else.
134166: Guess I can't be trusted after all. I quit.
134167: I can. And I'm glad you feel that way.
134168:
The Nefantar go by many names, but Ammatar is the most common ― though their former Minmatar brethren sometimes refer to them as “the Lost Tribe” in pity, but more often “the Fawning” or “the Yoked” in scorn. The Nefantar have left behind their tribal heritage and taken up many (but not all) aspects of the Amarrian religion, a movement that has resulted in a unique blend of cultures.

The Ammatar Mandate and the Minmatar Republic have been locked in a state of cold war for years now; since the Vindication Wars, there hasn't been a large-scale battle between them, mainly due to former Prime Minister Karin Midular's diplomatic efforts. However, after Midular's passing, the animosity between the two peoples cannot be denied.

The old, traditionally aristocratic bloodlines of the Nefantar see themselves as the rightful rulers of all the Matar tribes; for their part, most Minmatar hold little more than bitter animosity toward the tribe that long ago betrayed its cousins, and a widespread hatred of the Ammatar is still common among all other Matari.
134169:
One of our research stations has been compromised, and we believe that the Amarr and their allies, the traitorous, mongrel Nefantar, will attempt to destroy it. We need you to get in there and defend the station, for I can't be sure I can mobilize local military forces in time.

The Amarrians will go to any lengths to prevent us from reverse-engineering a treatment that could invalidate the Vitoc Method. If we can make it costly enough for them, though, they may just be forced to give up on this station, with it being so deep in our sovereignty.
134171:
One of our research stations ― the very one where I sent the information from that science vessel you hacked for us ― has been compromised, and we believe that the Amarr and their allies, the traitorous, mongrel Nefantar, will attempt to destroy it. As you know, we Minmatar have many small research stations scattered throughout space to better avoid Amarr detection, but as a result, our resources are necessarily splintered.

The loss of this research station would be a tremendous setback to us. We need you to get in there and defend the station, for I can't be sure I can mobilize local military forces in time. The Amarrians will go to any lengths to prevent us from reverse-engineering a treatment that could invalidate the Vitoc Method. If we can make it costly enough for them, though, they may just be forced to give up on this station, with it being so deep in our sovereignty.
134172: We will not take this betrayal lightly.
134173: You will do what you must.
134174: Though this battle was small, it is still a great victory. And already it bears unexpected fruit. Return to me when you are ready to take on a great labor.
134175: I hope, for your sake, that you do not come to regret this choice.
134176: The station has been destroyed by Nafantar raiders. The Matari lives lost are on your head.
134177: We are sending someone who understands the importance of speed. Stand down.
134181: The station is safe, and the Ammatar have learned a painful lesson.
134182: I don't think I can do that.
134183: I can't fight a war by myself! I'm outta here.
134185:
This type of breeding facility produces Minmatar children ready to assume their place as servants to the Amarr; rumors abound that the slaves in these places hail from other races as well, including even fallen Amarr who are sent here rather than to penal colonies.

Brood slaves are held within breeder colonies for the sole purpose of increasing a slaver's stock. Discarded when they have outlived their usefulness, these poor souls have a terribly short life expectancy, although that fact might be a blessing when one considers the misery of their existence.

Slavers who use such methods tend to be secretive about it, often anchoring their breeding centers in low-sec or unclaimed space; however profitable, these facilities are generally looked down upon even in polite Amarrian society (especially since the Doriam reforms).
134186: Destroy the Amarr Breeding Facility, kill any enemy ships there, and return any enslaved Matari you find to {[location]agentStationID.name}.
134187: Amarr Breeding Facilities – Even Death Is Better
134188:
We have tracked down an Amarr "breeding facility." {[character]player.name}, I was held in one of these places once, when I was young, and it is only thanks to the efforts of one such as yourself that I find myself a free person today. They're hellholes.

You will find only women and children there; the boys are shipped elsewhere before they turn nine. Most of these facilities don't even bother with Vitoc; they prefer cheaper, more primitive methods of control. After all, the work is hardly complicated: Where humane restraints don't work, brute force and fear often will.

Destroy this place. Rescue as many Matari as you can, but be certain that even those who die are better off.

134190: Steel yourself, and do what must be done.

134193: The Amarr have swift counter-intelligence. They have moved their operations, and we don't know where.
134194: I pray there is still time to rescue those unfortunates. Clearly, that rescue will fall to someone else.
134196: You are released from your obligation
134197: I understand. I'll do what you ask of me.
134198: I've brought back as many as I could.
134199: I can't condemn innocent victims to death, even in the face of such an atrocity.
134200: I'm not doing this. I'm done here.
134202:
When mining for specific minerals, use the Overview to help. Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Now, if you plan to mine this type of ore regularly, you can click the Overview arrow again and select “Save current type selection as…” and put in whatever name seems appropriate. Now you can return to this setting anytime you want to simply by using the Overview arrow to select “Load [type].”
134203: Scouts we hired from Minmatar Mining found that there are some significant amounts of Augumene nearby. That's not normally a very valuable substance, but we're using a fabrication process here that utilizes Augumene as a catalyst, so we'll take all we can get. We need 400 units.

134206: Well, get to work then! We'll see you on your return.
134207: That's a great help to us, friend. Come back and see me, okay?
134208: Doesn't sound too exciting, but I'll do it.

Once you've reprocessed enough, return with it to your agent to complete the mission.
134212: Our production here is going into high gear and we're experiencing shortages of just about everything. We expect everyone to pitch in. I need you to obtain 750 units of Tritanium and deliver them here. You've been reliable so far: care to help out again? 134216: Thanks a million, {[character]player.name}. We'll be needing some help on another matter, so come back soon.
134219: Sounds good to me. What do you need?
134220: If you take too much damage in battle, be sure to warp out to a nearby station for repairs; also be sure to replenish your ammunition if you're running low. Pirates can be pretty tough, so you'll need to be on your toes to deal with them.
134221:
It seems that our activity in this system has attracted unwanted attention. Mercenaries and pirates of a variety of allegiances have been preying on our unarmed miners and transports. This can't go on! The industrial production of this sector is vital to our military effort.

Hunt these bastards down. I've uploaded their current location to your NeoCom.
134223:
It seems that our activity in this system has attracted unwanted attention. Mercenaries and pirates of a variety of allegiances have been preying on our unarmed miners and transports. This can't go on! The industrial production of this sector is vital to our military effort.

Are you willing to hunt these bastards down? We have lots of pilots who are good mining operators, but only the rare few are also capsuleers capable of taking on pirates and raiders like you can. There's a generous reward in it if you're in, not to mention the bounties and loot on the enemies themselves.
134225: I knew we could count on you, {[character]player.name}. We're planning to finish those raiders off once and for all, so stick around, huh?
134226: I won't leave one pirate vessel intact.
134229:
It looks as if there was some organization behind all the recent pirate activity. We've just learned that they maintain communications in adjacent systems via a communications tower network in this very system! We need someone to take out the pirates' tower array. That someone is you.

I'll enter the locations into your bookmarks. If you leave now, there's every chance you'll catch 'em napping. We'll offer a decent reward plus a bonus if you hit them fast.
134230:

We've just learned that they maintain communications in adjacent systems via a communications tower network in this very system! If one of their scouts is forced to flee, the others maintain contact with him via FTL communications made possible by this com network.

We need someone to take out the pirates' tower array. There's been a lot of subspace chatter over the past few days, and we have a pretty good idea that they're planning something big. We need to hit them hard before that happens, throw a wrench in their plans.

So, would you like to be the one who goes in there and finishes them off? I'll enter the locations into your bookmarks. If you leave now, there's every chance you'll catch 'em napping. We'll offer a decent reward plus a bonus if you hit them fast.
134232: Happily, I I consider it well spent. You've proven yourself admirably. This system is a safer place because of you.
134233: I'll head out there right away. They don't stand a chance.
134234: Those tower arrays are history. Now, about that reward?
134235: Hey, {[character]agentID.name}. Alright, tell me about this idea of yours.
134236: When you reach your destination system, right-click in open space, and you will find a submenu for this mission. One of the options there is to dock at the desired station: This menu makes it easy for you to go straight there without having to search through the overview list for the destination station.
134237: I have a fresh shipment of slaves here that need to be vaccinated, prepped, and properly indoctrinated. Please take them to our facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
134239:
Well said, well said.

{[character]player.name}, I have a fresh shipment of slaves here that need to be vaccinated, prepped, and properly indoctrinated. Please take them to our facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Let us not make their keepers wait.
134240: You cannot complete a simple mission like this? Hm. That does not bode well for your future in the Empire.
134241: That is precisely what I wanted to hear.
134242: Well done, {[character]player.name}! But there is indeed something else: You won't believe what has happened! Give me just a moment to finish reading this report and then come speak to me again.
134243: That is unfortunate. I'm sure I can find someone else for this lucrative opportunity.
134244: I found someone else to take care of this. No need to bother. I should add that your lack of spirit disturbs me…
134245: I found someone else to take care of this. No need to bother. I should add that your lack of spirit disturbs me…
134250: Thank you. The Empire deserves no less of us.
134251: You can usually find the items your agent requires by sifting through the wreckage of destroyed ships or structures, or by looking inside floating cargo containers.
134252: A woman named Zira started an uprising among those new slaves almost the moment they arrived at the indoctrination facility. It was a bloody affair, and several guards and innocent citizens were killed or wounded. You are to hunt down Zira, terminate her with extreme prejudice as a lesson to them all, and recapture the other escaped slaves.
134254:
Oh, they have their uses, I assure you. Just rule them with an iron hand, my friend.

Anyway, it seems a woman named Zira started an uprising among those new slaves almost the moment they arrived at the indoctrination facility. It was a bloody affair, and several guards and innocent citizens were killed or wounded. This insubordination cannot be tolerated. You are to hunt down Zira, terminate her with extreme prejudice as a lesson to them all, and recapture the other escaped slaves.

Don't waste any time. We've tracked them to a deadspace location, but they may be planning to jump out of the system even as we speak. I've uploaded their location to your NeoCom.
134255: What, scared away by the thought of facing a few miserable sub-humans? This does not look good on you. Not good at all.
134257: Nice work. These escapees will be severely punished. Now, don't go far; I'm sure I can find something else for you.
134258:
Who's paid you to think?! Your job is to do!! Ach!

I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.
134259: You allowed those filthy, disease-ridden slaves to escape. Now they will carry their pestilence to the rest of the galaxy!
134260: You allowed those filthy, disease-ridden slaves to escape. Now they will carry their pestilence to the rest of the galaxy!
134264: Slaves in custody. Zira is dead.
134265: Let them go. They're not worth the trouble.
134266: On second thought, I think we should just let these slaves go. They're just not worth the trouble.
134267: More trouble than they're worth, slaves. Alright, what can I do?
134268:
You can make multiple consecutive jumps through stargates much more quickly manually than you can relying on Autopilot (because the Autopilot brings your ship out of warp 15 km from the stargate each time you warp, forcing you to then fly at sub-warp speed to within 2,500 m of the gate before jumping).

First, set your destination by right-clicking on the location in the journal entry or in your bookmarks. The correct stargate icon will now be highlighted in yellow, both in your overview and in space.

Now, right-click on the stargate (either in space or in the overview) and use the "Warp to within 0 km" option… and then turn on Autopilot; you will drop out of warp directly beside the stargate and, because Autopilot is on, jump immediately. As soon as you begin to jump, turn your Autopilot back off; once you've jumped, simply repeat the whole "Warp to 0 km" process with each stargate along the route until you arrive at your destination system.
134270: You cannot complete a simple mission like this? Oh, dear. Oh dear, oh dear, oh dear. This does not bode well for your future in the Empire.
134271: It didn't take them long. We were right about this Zira Cobalus. Return immediately so we can discuss the next step.
134272: That is unfortunate. I'm sure I can find someone else whose loyalty is not so plainly in question. Keep one eye over your shoulder, my friend.
134273: You waited too long. Someone erased all the data we had on this "Zira." Now we will never know the truth.
134275: I'll get this over there right away.
134277: Oh, I've had enough of this business, I think. Not interested. Sorry.
134278: I think I'm going to pack it in after all. I'm tired of being your errand-runner.
134280: If your ship is badly damaged and in danger of destruction, you should consider warping away from an encounter. You can repair your ship at most stations, for a cost dependent upon the amount of damage, or you can use Hull Repairers and Armor Repairers to fix the damage yourself while you are in space. But before you try to fit those items to your ship, you should make sure you have the correct skills.
134281:
We did intercept an encrypted transmission from Zira's contact. (We sent a recovery team to pick up Zira's remains, and we discovered that she had a cybernetic transceiver implanted in her brain.) Her contact identified himself only as "Helter."

We don't know who he is, but we think, from examinations of his speech patterns, that he is Amarrian. The coordinates of the rendezvous were included in the transmission, and I've uploaded them into your data bank. Go out there and see who we're dealing with. But be careful.
134283:
I think you can, yes. Are you ready for another mission, a truly important one? Good.

We did intercept an encrypted transmission from Zira's contact. How could a naked slave with no possessions receive a transmission, you ask? We sent a recovery team to pick up Zira's remains, and we discovered that she had a cybernetic transceiver implanted in her brain. Not a simple cybernetic implant, but something bio-electrical, beyond our current technology, deep in her cerebral cortex.

Her contact identified himself only as "Helter." We don't know who he is, but we think, from examinations of his speech patterns, that he is Amarrian. The coordinates of the rendezvous were included in the transmission, and I've uploaded them into your data bank.

Go out there and see who we're dealing with. But be careful.
134284: I was afraid this was too much for you. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy elsewhere... maybe hauling trash or something.
134286: Excellent! So, a double agent working with the Minmatar... No surprise, really. Those mindless sub-humans will do anything to stick a thorn in the side of the Empire, and true loyalty is at a premium these days. Now, we do have a chance to finish this before it goes any further: Come see me as soon as you can.
134287: I was afraid this was too much for you. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.
134288: You waited too long. We have missed an opportunity to thwart the rendezvous and discover the identity of the Amarrian double agent. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.
134289: You waited too long. We have missed an opportunity to thwart the rendezvous and discover the identity of the Amarrian double agent. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.
134292: Sounds more like my kind of work. Sure, I'm in.
134293: The contact is an Amarrian, and his name is Garmasi Jowai. He is definitely working with the Minmatar.
134294: This sounds too dangerous to me. I don't want to be a spy; just give me some pirates to fight or something.
134295: This is too dangerous. Bring in the Navy or something, okay?
134296: That's frustrating. Is there some way I can help?
134297:
Some deadspace acceleration gates are locked so that you cannot use them until all the enemy ships in the area have been destroyed. If you warp into a deadspace area and you become surrounded by enemies, consider warping out again to repair or to try a different tactic rather than running for the next acceleration gate.

When you warp to an encounter area that you expect might be swarming with enemies, do not use the "Warp to 0 km" option if you can avoid it. Instead, warp to 50 km or so, and force your enemies to come to you. This is a useful option particularly if you are outgunned or seriously outnumbered, especially if you use long-range weapons. (Unfortunately, this tactic isn't available in many deadspace locations, but it should be used whenever possible.)
134298:
Now is our chance to apprehend Garmasi Jowai. Intel has determined that he is meeting his Minmatar handlers in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Get out there and catch him, and bring him in to face the Emperor's justice.

The strength of the Minmatar force is unknown, but you can bet they'll be heavily armed. You should not attempt this mission without a well-armed ship, and you should be prepared to warp out for repairs if necessary.
134300:
Excellent. This is our chance to apprehend Jowai and make him pay — as well as getting some useful intelligence from him. Intel has determined that he is meeting his Minmatar handlers in a remote pocket of deadspace in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Our ships are too far away, and you've shown great courage and resourcefulness up till now.

Get out there and catch him, {[character]player.name}, and bring him in to face Imperial Justice. Our interrogators are quite... skilled. And you will be well rewarded, of course.
134301: It seems the Minmatar frightened you off after all. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.
134302: Excellent. Glad to have you working on this one.
134303: You have done the Empire a great service, {[character]player.name}. You will be handsomely rewarded.
134304: It seems the Minmatar frightened you off after all. From now on, we'll have to keep you busy hauling garbage or something.
134305: You waited too long. Garmasi Jowai escaped from the rendezvous point with his Minmatar handlers. Your lack of initiative puts your loyalty in question, {[character]player.name}.

134314:
The Empire has been studying the ships flown by the Minmatar for some time. Though they mostly fly variants of standard Minmatar ships, the Thukkers usually have specific load outs: They favor Explosive and Thermal weapons, and their ships have a low heat tolerance, making Thermal weapons the best to use against them. If you are using laser weapons, X-Ray or Gamma lenses could be good to equip. If you feel like bringing the fight in closer, Multifrequency lenses do even more Thermal damage, but at the cost of range.

Remember, whatever weapon you use to destroy their ships, Thukkers decompress explosively, just like any other Minmatar...

Head out to their hiding spot. Wipe the savages out. All of Creation will be a safer place for their deaths. And remain wary. I smell the Minmatar "government" behind all this.

The big concern is that filming for the holo Tears of the Sky is taking place in the same area. Smart money would bet that the Caldari mega-corps are funding these guys; the State is desperate to keep this holo from coming out.

134493:
The easiest way to travel to a destination system quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group; once you have selected "Stargate" there, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in your mission journal and choose "Set destination." You will notice that the next stargate along your route, both in space and in your Overview, is now yellow.

Next, right-click on the yellow stargate (in space or in the Overview) and select "Warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot, then sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

After you have completed the mission, if you have problems finding your way back to the agent, simply open the "People and Places" window from your NeoCom and check the Agents tab; the agent you are working for should be displayed there. Right-click on the appropriate agent and select "Set destination," then turn on your Autopilot to make your way back to the agent's system.

So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while. It should be easy, even for a pup like you, but it will show me that you're serious.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

134503:
Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it into their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in your mission's Journal entry and select "Add to Overview." 

Also, to complete the mission objectives, the Banidine should be located in your Item Hangar and not in your Ore Hold.

Click the small white arrow beside the word “Overview”; from there, select “Load default,” and then “Mining.” Then, you can right-click any type of asteroid in your overview and select “Remove from Overview”; keep doing this until only the type you want is left in your overview.

Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks — you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in your mission journal and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the slaves are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.

It seems that the construction works at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are experiencing an unfortunate labor shortage, possibly brought on by their overly harsh personnel management methods. It is important to the Empire that we get them a shipment of elite slaves so that they do not fall any further behind schedule. Are you a loyal enough citizen to do this task and do it quickly?

I will upload a bookmark to your People & Places databank; use it to locate and reach your destination.

134922: I am a loyal citizen. I will deliver the cargo.
134923: The slaves have been successfully delivered, {[character]agentID.name}.

134925:
The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in your mission journal and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the slaves are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.
134926:
It just so happens that we're opening some new clubs over in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The problem is that the talent has gotten stranded here, and has to be over to the station for the grand opening. You probably know the rest. It's important that this be taken care of soon, so we're offering a substantial reward to anyone who wants to take the job.

Remember to move the dancers to your cargo hold before departure.

Hey, I'm glad you asked!

Here at Nugoeihuvi Corporation, we're all about pleasure. I'm sure you've seen our adverts — "If it's fun, it must be from Nugoeihuvi." And it just so happens that we're opening some new clubs over in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The problem is that the talent has gotten stranded here, and has to be over to the station for the grand opening. What talent you ask? Well, I mean the dancers, {[character]player.name}... Exotic dancing is an art form, you know, appreciated on the highest intellectual level. And we've got a bunch of dancers just standing around waiting for a ship to take 'em to their new home.

You probably know the rest. We need a fast, reliable pilot and a ship without any major mechanical problems. That brave and resourceful pilot needs to take these dancers to their destination so that they can get bringing in the high-rollers and thus earning their wages. It's important that this be taken care of soon, so we're offering a substantial reward to anyone who wants to take the job. You up to it, kid?
134929: Good going. Now deliver those dancers, tiger! And try not to make too many stops along the way to… enjoy the merchandise, m'okay? Heh.
134930: Thanks! We're counting the money already.
134931: Okay, I guess I'll do it.

Remember to move the marines to your cargo hold before departure.

We believe that the cursed Amarrians are planning a major invasion, and we need to equip our warriors to repel their attacks on planetary environs. On the loading dock is a shipment of weapons for our 412th Regiment, currently garrisoned at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Can you get it there for them?

134952:
To purchase Tritanium from the market, open the Market button from your NeoCom on the left. When the Market window is open, click on the Search tab and search for "Tritanium." Doing so will open a list containing the buyers and sellers in the region.

To purchase 15 units of Tritanium from a particular seller, right-click an item from the listing and select "Buy this"; in the "Quantity" field on the window that pops up, change the value to "15." Be sure to note the location of the order, as you will have to pick up the Tritanium from that station. (If you're not sure what station you've bought something from, you can always find all of your possessions, in any station, using the "Assets" window in your NeoCom.) Click "Buy."

Do NOT click "Place a Buy Order" unless there is a seller at your station that can fill the order immediately or you are willing to depend upon someone filling your order before this mission times out.

A number of weeks ago I ordered a case of long-limb roe from a respectable supplier who was docked at this very station. The delivery staff was atrocious. Many of the packages were damaged, and most of the roes were half rancid. I made sure everyone on that staff was fired, but I am not so quickly inclined to trust these new hires. We're going to have a little test. And I need someone of your caliber, a graduate and a capsuleer, to help.

Acquire for me just 15 units of Tritanium. You can purchase them from the market or mine ore to reprocess it yourself — how you get it is up to you. Keep the Tritanium in your cargo hold and then talk to me again. I will send someone from among the new staff to pick up the mineral.

If you need further instructions on purchasing items, I shall provide them in the mission briefing I'll upload to your Journal.

134988: You disappoint me. I thought you could handle a simple courier mission, but apparently I was wrong. I suppose I'll have to limit your work to garbage runs. I've found someone else to take care of this.

Interesting, yes. Also disgusting.

One of the seeds had thoughts of its own on whom or what might be its host. Unbeknownst to us, a botanist here named Horei Falcosis took one of the seeds for examination before you shipped the package; a short time ago, as he worked with it, it shot out a tendril and sank it into his flesh. It was several minutes before he was discovered, and by that time, the seed's tendrils had penetrated his body in several locations. Falcosis was unconscious by this time, and the seed had pulled itself close to his body and started to secrete a protective resin.

Brings new meaning to giving one's body to science, don't you think?

In any case, this station does not have the proper facilities to care for him. And since this tree has now been designated noxious and dangerous — the other seeds were all incinerated safely, I understand — Falcosis has been placed in cryogenic stasis for transport. One of the functions of my job is to ensure things operate smoothly in this region. I have a number of informants that keep me in the loop of the less visible happenings. They tend to be skittish by nature, but recently one of my informants was noticeably shaken. He won't send the information, and he won't meet me in person. He's insisted that I send a third party to pick up the data.

Normally I'd just find another informant, but this one was on the trail of a particularly virulent heretic. The man can't be anything but mad—he calls himself The Crackpot, for one thing—but it's damned hard to track a madman. He's been attracting attention, even followers from among the weak-minded, and it's long past time to put a stop to his nonsense.

If you'll go and pick up that data, it could help us track this menace down.

His determination and his powers of persuasion have compelled his own people and others to sacrifice many things they thought sacred to ensure that tranquility will prevail, now and forever."

Still, that leaves us with a pile of gilded filth on our hands.

I want you to go pick up the copies that are being held and bring them back here. We're having the Pax Amarria covers stripped off before we send them along for the ceremonial burning.

We are working closely with several bathhouses through Nugoeihuvi to acquire the large number of companions required for SPLET. We are close to completing the contracts. All that is required to finalize is a final inspection, to be performed by the SPLET organizer.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

We found the best cost-effective solution by working with NOH's bathhouses. Traveling with SPLET will be a "companion army." We are close to completing the contracts. All that is left is a final round of...negotiation by the SPLET chairman.

Pick up the NOH prostitute-- I'll upload the station address to your NeoCom-- and return her here. After this last mission, I believe the program will be ready to launch.

135162: Excellent.  Thanks to your help, SPLET will soon be making its way through the Caldari ranks.

135180: Since their invention sometime around the Gallente-Caldari War, drones have become commonplace in nearly all facets of life. Drones vary in size from that of a human eye up to those that rival the largest frigates, and they have been built to fill the roles of fighters, miners, and repair vehicles, as well as household cleaning units and tiny children's toys — not to mention their various military uses in space stations and on planetary surfaces alike. New uses for drone technology are being developed constantly.
135182:
You ever try mining with drones? Useful little guys, huh? Yeah, well, to a point…

Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines. But of course the genius didn't test the things properly before sending them out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to mine Mercium. And of course now he's made himself scarce.

You can probably guess what happened. Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want — our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.

I've just discovered a sizable deposit of Pithix out by an old mining station. The station's been abandoned for a while now, but there are still working sensors in the area; that's how we picked up on the Pithix. Problem is, the transmission's hardly secure. I need you to get out there and bring me back that rock before someone else cleans the place out.

Oh, there might also be some rogue drone activity in the area. Fair warning.

In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother giving it a unique listing in their mining packages when they produce standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the Pithix at the mission location, simply right-click the "Pithix" icon in your mission's Journal entry and select "Add to Overview."

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with it. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. See you then.

War is one of the biggest boons to business you could hope for. It's a hungry giant that will eat anything you can throw at it. And the thing is, if you don't feed it, it will just eat you…. But if you feed it well? Oh, the rewards. Public recognition, sure, but the contracts, the contracts, {[character]player.name}! That's where the real LUX is. And we're going to get those contracts. Oh, yes. But first we need minerals.

Right now, it seems the giant on our doorstep wants Oeryl, and we're going to give it to him. There's a deposit out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Bring back all 5,600 units of the stuff and I'll make sure you get your share of the reward.

135381:

135382:
I have a friend in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I'd better go lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?

Your agent's datapad has given you the coordinates to one of the competitors of your agent's "friend" in the Gallente Navy. Your "mission" once you arrive there should be abundantly clear.

135391: It's good to see you so well rested, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm afraid I have some bad news: I've lost your datapad, the one with the coordinates on it? Oh, and I fear that a certain Gallente lieutenant may have run into some trouble as well.
135392: What the hell are you yammering on about?! I 'm going to go wash down a few Starsi and leave you to your rest. You apparently need it.

135394: I'm ready to serve in any way I can.
135395:
Gallente Navy ships are not often allowed inside State borders – at least not officially. Conditions determined in the Iyen-Oursta Treaty at the end of the war place strict conditions on the manner in which each nation's fleets enter the other's sovereign space.

One of the current laws allows such deployments, though, if they are hired by a third party as part of usual trade business. Additionally, they must meet stringent size and composition requirements that greatly limit any damage they could potentially cause. Since official search and rescue missions are, by treaty, conducted exclusively by the nation that owns the space, further "hostile" forces cannot legally be sent to recover hired navy forces that go missing.
135396:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. Worse, they've offered Navy vessels as security for these companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. A local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Get out there and deal with them. This is a standard office complex; an outer layer of security with the offices behind them. Take out all of the guards, then go for their headquarters.
135398:
There has been an ongoing situation in the entertainment industry, the gambling sector in particular. We've started to see Gallente companies buying out the smaller ones here and reaping profits from our own citizens. This isn't entirely new, of course — they've been trying to do it for decades — but it's actually seeing widespread success now.

What concerns us is that the Federation is officially starting to play an active role in all of this. They've offered Navy vessels as security for the companies' spacebound offices, many of which are located here in our own regions. Since these security forces come at a greatly subsidized cost, we're starting to see a few troubling things. First off, the companies obviously have more LUX to fund further acquisitions. More important, however, is this slow build-up inside our space of Gallente military units. They may be relatively inexperienced and poorly equipped, for the most part, but it's the quantity that concerns us, not the quality.

Make no mistake, {[character]player.name}: This is in all likelihood just their first step. Soon the Federation will forge these various companies into a more unified and organized conglomerate, and then we'll see them pushing to allow larger military escorts with better equipment. Their intentions are nothing short of an economic war with us over one of our key industries, followed by a direct assault in our own backyard once we're sufficiently weakened.

So, we're getting loyal pod pilots like you together and sending them off to as many of these "company sites" as we can find. They were supposed to have registered their offices with our officials, but a combination of lazy State bureaucrats and Gallente scheming means there are currently numerous sites out there that we don't have exact coordinates for. Our mistake in part, yes, but we're fixing it now. It's easy enough to disclaim any official involvement in this little removal operation too, since we have your kind doing the work for us.

Anyway, a local recon force recently found such a Gallente Navy headquarters nearby in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you ready to act?
135399: You disappoint me, {[character]player.name}. Next time you take up a mission, understand that we will expect you to see it through — no matter the cost.
135400: Excellent, I'm sure you will, {[character]player.name}. I'm sending the location now.
135401: You did? Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. On behalf of the countless Caldari whose jobs you have saved, I thank you.
135402: The State does not ask much of its people. Your lack of loyalty will not be tolerated for very long around these parts, {[character]player.name}.
135403: You promised to deal with that company I needed removed, remember? Well, now too much time has passed and they've relocated their headquarters after noticing our scouts. You have let me down, {[character]player.name}, and countless other Caldari as well.
135404: My offer of work is withdrawn. I can't wait for you to consider the mission forever, {[character]player.name}. I've given the task to another pilot who can act more speedily.
135407: I can't believe this is allowed to happen! Give me the coordinates. I'll show them the fast route back to Gallente space: via clone replacement.
135408: My work is done. You won't be seeing any new acquisition bids from that company.
135409: I don't think I care enough about your economic concerns to risk my ship over it.
135410: You know, upon reflection, I'm less sure about this mission now. They're not breaking any laws, so if you want them gone you'll have to find someone else.
135412:
Over the years, the Caldari have seen various citizens desert their posts in search of better futures elsewhere. The Guristas have always recruited disgruntled ex-State pilots into their ranks, while Mordu's Legion has taken in those who were unhappy with their place in the State, but who remained patriotic or were otherwise obligated to maintain good relations.

Recently, however, there has been an increase in defections to various Gallente corporations, usually in the research and security sectors, and even to the Federation Navy. While such a thing was virtually unheard of in the past, the Federation is increasingly becoming the home to a certain class of Caldari: those skilled pilots and technicians who have come to disagree violently with the State, but who, for various reasons, do not want to enter the seedy underworld of galactic piracy. Such people have found the Federation most sympathetic and welcoming.
135413:
One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. I need this situation sorted. We have to send a message that any treacherous behavior against the State will have truly dire consequences.

We have been able to locate the traitor's temporary living quarters, which are still in State space and therefore under our jurisdiction. Can you head over there and deal with this, {[character]player.name}? I don't want this fool making it to Gallente space alive. Oh, and bring what's left of him back to me, just for certainty's sake.
135415:
We have a serious matter to deal with, {[character]player.name}. Very serious. One of our people has betrayed us and is planning to defect to the Gallente.

It's not as if he knows anything particularly important. Nor does he pose much of a threat. It's the principle of the thing. And the example this sets for others. This particular traitor is fairly high-profile, you see, which makes it difficult for us to act more openly. We've already lost enough people to the Guristas and the Legion, and if we start losing people to the Federation, who knows where it will end.

135417: Good to hear. One less leech, we can do without.
135418: Ha! Impressive work, {[character]player.name}. I heard you made a real mess of those traitors. Here is your reward — take it with my thanks.
135419: Excuse me? You want to encourage this behavior?! Your lack of loyalty is disconcerting, {[character]player.name}. Not to mention the lack of foresight....
135420: I made it explicitly clear to you that there was only a small amount of time to stop that traitor from defecting to the Federation. The opportunity has passed. Mend your ways, {[character]player.name}, or you will find yourself without friends very quickly.
135421: I cannot keep waiting for an answer, {[character]player.name}. If we cannot deal with this traitor quickly, he will vanish into Federation space. Since you seem unable to help me battle this problem, I will find another pilot with the courage and the initiative to do so.
135424: Yes, it's a distressing trend, I agree. I'll see to it he never makes it to Federation space.
135425: It's done: Add one more traitor to the body count... and some LUX to my account, please.
135426: What a pointless job! I want to make a difference, maybe get rich along the way... not chase down people who just happen to like Intaki wine. Get back to me with some real work, ok?
135427: You know what? I've changed my mind. If this guy wants to run to Gallente so bad, let him.
135428: I might be. What did you have in mind?

The Gallente have somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

Fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

135511: Ha! Yes… yes indeed. You're a source of inspiration for us all, I assure you. I'll have the transport fleet on standby; report back to me immediately after the area is secure.
135512: You truly are an asset to the State, {[character]player.name}. I honestly don't know what we would have done without your help. Be proud of the work you have done today.
135513: Suicide missions!? You have a clone, do you not, {[character]player.name}?! Unlike the many important Caldari whose clones are in peril…! A true Caldari would give anything to serve the State in such an important matter. Clearly you are no such thing.

I suggest you fix your attitude.

135629:
Amarrian society, a religious oligarchy, relies on slaves to do nearly all of its manual labor and servant work. Of course, Gallenteans despise this practice. Honest workers should be given an honest wage, not kept in bondage.

Amarr's slaves are often taken wherever they can be found. Citizens of the Gallente Federation, as any other nation, sometimes find themselves locked in Amarrian slave collars. Most of the time, there is little to be done about it, especially if the slaves were kidnapped in low-security or otherwise lightly policed areas of space.
135630:
An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.

You will need a well-armed frigate to accomplish this mission. The slave ship is probably armed, and might have escorts as well.
135632:
Alright, then. An Amarrian Holder we've suspected for some time of black market slave trading has overstepped his bounds and nabbed a few loyal Gallente citizens for his slave pens. You must stop him. He thinks he's getting away unnoticed, but I want you to prove him wrong.

Destroy this scumbag's ship and bring those slaves back to me, {[character]player.name}. We'll make sure they are returned to their homes. After they pay back their transport fees, that is.
135633: Good, good. I like your spirit. That's why I asked you to do this job.
135634: Excellent. I'm sure those poor, unwashed people would shower you with gratitude. But first, let's see that they have showers of their own, eh?
135639: I'll bring back those citizens, don't you worry.
135640: Alright, I'm back. One less slaver to worry about, assuming he didn't have a clone, and a bunch of Gallenteans happy to be home.
135642:
Pisharpar Corilian is one of the most renowned Amarrian poets of all time. He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor.
135643:
This, {[character]player.name}: All the great nations in the galaxy have long allowed each other to travel freely in pursuit of commerce, but I've just heard a story that makes me think this time of freedom is near its end.

Pisharpar Corilian is one of Amarr's most renowned poets of all time. He is gifted, but a typical example of a poet. He's effete, arrogant, and overly sensitive — always with his head in the clouds and his feet floating half a meter off the floor. In Corilian's case, this is literal: So obese that his legs can no longer support his weight, he uses a hoverchair to get around.

He is also a spy. He has been on a "book tour" of Gallente space for several months now, and our suspicions were confirmed when we tracked a coded transmission coming from his pleasure yacht. We believe he has had secret data chips implanted within his massive rolls of flesh, where he can hide all sorts of sensitive information.

We cannot tolerate this blatant abuse of the arts! We want him terminated immediately… but it must look like piracy. That's where you come in. He is currently traveling to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Warp in, blast him and his entourage to smithereens, and warp out. Simple.

Now, it's likely that a man this respected in Amarrian society has a clone, but at least we'll have destroyed whatever information he's gathered into his data-ridden body. Take care of him, and you'll be doing us all a great favor — both politically and artistically... (If you've never read his work, you'll have to take my word for it.)
135644: You can't handle one pitiful, overweight poet? What kind of capsuleer are you?
135646: Nice work. When news gets out, of course, it will be a "terrible act of piracy"… but in the meantime I think we can drink a toast to that whining bastard's bloated, frozen corpse.
135647: Wow, I would never have thought…. Well, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.
135652: Very well. It ain't over till... well, er, till the fat man is dead.
135653: Chalk up one large, whiny poet. Clone or no, that was a surprising pleasure, I must admit.
135654: But I myself am a great patron of the arts! I love his work!! I can't kill him!
135655: Find somebody else to do this. I have better things to do than hunt down some stupid poet, even if he is a spy.
135656: Uh, okay. Fair enough. Care to explain what's on your mind, though?
135657:
The toxic chemical known as Vitoc is the preferred method Amarrians use to control their slaves. The drug is injected into the slaves, and the slaves must work to retrieve a periodic dose of antidote to the poison. Gallente scientists, among others, have been chasing the formula for Vitoc for years, but without success. The drug behaves in many ways like a virus.

If one could find the cure, the entire Amarrian economy might be crippled… assuming that cure could somehow be supplied to a sufficient number of their slaves.
135658:
An informant within the Amarrian Empire has given us a break in our long quest to find the cure for the slave drug, Vitoc. A sample of their most recent version of the drug has been ... diverted to be transported on an industrial ship passing near Gallente space. If we move quickly, we can intercept the industrial ship, steal its top secret cargo, and it will all be blamed on pirates.

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me.

Amarrian convoys are well guarded when they pass near Gallente space. Be prepared for a fight.
135660:

Destroy the industrial ship and bring the Vitoc to me. Can you do it?
135661: This was a golden opportunity to strike a serious blow against Amarr slavery! Have you no guts at all?
135662: I'm uploading you the coordinates as we speak. Your target will not be in this area for long, though, so don't dally.
135663: Excellent work. I'm glad we can depend on you. Our scientists will want to see this stuff as soon as possible.
135664: I see. Showing your true colors, eh? Well, I just hope I can find a pilot with a sense of moral propriety for this job.
135669: I'm the capsuleer for this job. Just tell me where to find that ship.
135670: Alright – those Amarr creeps never knew what hit them, and I've got the Vitoc samples right here.
135671: I don't care all that much about any Amarrian slaves. I mean, sure, slavery's bad… but risk my ship over it? No, thanks.
135672: I just don't have time for this Vitoc mission. You'll have to find someone else.
135673: Wow, great news! How can I help?
135689: Sometimes a mission might not turn out the way you anticipated. You might have incomplete information from your agent, and conditions can change during the mission. Such changes are generally communicated to you directly, either through a direct pop-up window when using an acceleration gate or by means of a text message appearing in your local chat channel.
135690:
We have a research scientist currently in a small, secret outpost near here; he's originally Caldari, but he recognized the error of his upbringing and came over to our side after the war. More importantly, though, he's on the verge of a breakthrough in a high-priority weapons technology project. And likely as a direct result of that research, we think someone's trying to kill him. He has requested secure transport out of there, and we can't risk losing him.

Head over to the location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back here to me, will you? This mission requires the utmost secrecy, so don't tell anyone where you're going or say anything about your passenger. Got it? He's an important man, and there will be a decent bonus if you get him here discreetly and quickly.

135702: Looks like your scientist has had, er, a… bit of a setback. Too bad about that.  Hope he had a good clone ready.
135703: Let him find his own ride. My time is too valuable to spend it ferrying around some egghead.
135704: You know, on second thought, let this lapdog scientist of yours find his own ride.
135705: Okay, sounds good. What is it?
135707: That's precisely what I wanted to hear. I'm glad we understand one another. Don't waste any time.
135708: Ha! Nice work, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward — you've earned it.
135709: You would allow a madman to harm our beloved monument? What kind of patriot are you? Gods, I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.
135710:
{[character]player.name},

Your lack of initiative has allowed that insane Amarrian terrorist to detonate a bomb on the Crystal Boulevard! Where the hell were you?! Thousands are dead, and the repair costs will be astronomical. But you capsuleers never seem to think in such terms. Sickening, really.

I pray, for all our sakes, that you will learn to let your conscience guide you in the future.

{[character]agentID.name}
135712: This madman will never plant his bomb. Or see another sunrise, for that matter.
135713: The terrorist is now a grease smear on his battlecruiser's smoking wreck.
135714: What do I care about the Crystal Boulevard? I never shop there.
135715: Okay, I'm officially intrigued. What's up?
135716:
There's been an increase in Caldari activity in surrounding systems. We think those self-righteous bastards might be up to something. Of course, that's nothing new.

We've placed passive reconnaissance units in several nearby locations, but we don't want any direct transmissions from them for fear of attracting Caldari attention. So we've decided to dispatch "unofficial" vessels like yours to pick up the data chips from their base and bring them back here. The Caldari are less likely to suspect — or at least less likely to interfere with — a capsuleer, so they should leave you alone.

If you do get jumped, however, remember that the recon unit is the top priority. Get it out of there if you can. Do it fast and there'll be a substantial bonus.
135717: I knew you were good for it, {[character]player.name}.
135718: Good job, capsuleer. You show some promise, I must admit.
135719: I can't say I'm too surprised, {[character]player.name}.
135721: Here are the data chips from your recon base, {[character]agentID.name}.
135722: Sorry. I don't want to get involved.
135723: Yeah, I'm interested in helping out.
135724: Acceleration gates are one of the main means of intrastellar travel. They can propel space craft great distances without the need for a large gravitational body as an end point.  If the enemy has found a way to quickly and properly configure an acceleration gate to be used as a weapon, the consequences could be dire indeed.
135725:
We've found what appears to be a large collection of acceleration gates surrounded by Minmatar ships. These gates have apparently been modified to act as "simple" mass drivers. Theoretically, they could propel asteroids or similar celestial bodies at Amarrian targets. The combination of mass and velocity produced by such a gate could easily destroy a station; I don't even want to think what the results would be for a planetary impact.

We need you to stop the Minmatar before they get a chance to use these devices. Destroy any enemy ships you find. But do not destroy the gates: We do not know how dangerous that would be… and in any case, our scientists want to take a closer look.

135792: Ah, {[character]player.name}, good to see you. To business. We've just detected a hidden Amarrian reconaissance outpost nearby. I don't need to explain the threat to you, do I? We must wipe them out before they are able to expand their operations further into our territory. If you can take care of this problem for me, you will be well rewarded.
135793: Good job. We should be receiving the tracking data shortly -- be sure to check back in soon.
135794:
We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've added it to your bookmarks.

It's vital that we figure out just exactly what the Caldari are up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing; access the structure and bring me whatever Communications Logs you find inside.
135795:
We did, yes. This is big, really big. We've decrypted the data and analyzed the telemetry, and the Caldari are definitely amassing near this sector for some reason. Worse still, we suspect that our communication problems aren't the result of excessive ionization after all: We think the Caldari are jamming our transmissions. We sent out some scouts to track down the source of the interference, and they've traced the jamming signals to a location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

Here's the report with all pertinent information; I've added it to your bookmarks. It's vital that we figure out just exactly what they're up to as soon as possible. Enemy scouts may be interdicting any traffic in that system as well, so be on the lookout for enemy vessels. Avoid or destroy them, as you see fit.

There's bound to be a structure of some kind out there that's causing the signal interference, and I need you to see what exactly it's doing. Get a report on whatever you find out there back to me as soon as possible.
135796:
Even with the best of equipment and space superiority, any long-term military engagement has to rely on ground and station personnel. And personnel are only as reliable as their morale. I won't lie to you, the morale of our soldiers could be better.

To fix this, a number of the mega-corporations have joined together to produce SPLET—the State Personnel Life Enrichment Tour. This program will tour to various parts of the State, providing entertainment and other morale services for our soldiers.

The first thing we need is food, and there are crates of frozen food waiting not too far from here. Bring the food here so our chefs can start to figure out how to stretch it into an appropriately festive-- but still economical-- dish.
135797:
The courier ship Swiftsure had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. Eventually they managed to make it back in one piece; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.
135798:
So it would seem.

Listen, the courier ship Swiftsure has just had a warp drive mishap in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and was forced to jettison its cargo lest it be damaged or lost if the core blew. They're crawling back to their home station as we speak; however, the cargo they had to ditch was a set of important Federation court records. We don't have backups available, so those records are irreplaceable, and they can't get another courier out there until tomorrow sometime. Bloody couriers. Can't get good help these days.

{[character]player.name}, we need someone to head out there and find those records right away. There's a healthy reward in it for you if you succeed. I've uploaded the location of the Swiftsure's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and get it back to me here.
135799:
My suppliers can't keep up with all this demand for their excellent moonshine. So I've taken the liberty of modifying the booze a little bit. Yes, yes, I admit it, I'm adding water to it. To make certain the drunkards I deal with won't notice, I've come up with a devilish little scheme.

An old schoolmate of mine is a janitor on the School of Applied Knowledge over in Sakkikainen. Some graduation students there have come up with a strange little mixture they call Rotgut. I don't know the scientific mumbo-jumbo for how it works, all I know is that it increases the intoxication effects of alcohol many times. That's exactly what I need for my watered-down wares. I need someone discreet to pop over there and get me a bit of this Rotgut. Then, once the new concoction is ready, all I have to do is lay back and watch the dimes roll in.

135801:
Good day to you. I was sent out here to this constellation to compile a comprehensive dossier about the political situation. The recipient of the dossier is none of your business. I must admit I underestimated the difficulty of this mission. After all, how much can be going on in a remote, unimportant constellation such as this? But the political situation here is in a constant motion. It seems lot of people are taking a sudden interest in this place.

Fortunately, I have found a solution to my problems here. The Angel Cartel has a strong presence here in Ani and they are even more anxious than I am to keep a tab on the goings on here. What I need to do is get my hands on some of the information they've collected. Then, finishing my report should be a breeze. Or that's what I hope, at least. The constant fluctuations in the political climate makes me fear my task here will be endless. Just remember to fit your Relic Analyzer into your ship before you head out.

135803:
The Crystal Boulevard is indeed one of the great monuments of the Gallente Federation. It is perhaps the most stunning sight in the galaxy, a sea of gleaming crystal spires and sparkling lights, teeming with inhabitants and tourists. As such, it is a symbol of pride for the Gallente, a symbol of wealth, a symbol of freedom.

That makes it a wonderful target for enemies of the Federation as well.
135804: Excellent. Now get to it, before that bastard gets away.
135805: Good job! We'll analyze the data right away. Come back in a few hours and we may have some more work for you.
135807: I've eliminated the traitor and obtained his log book.
135809:
Turns out the traitor was on his way to meet up with his contact, a Caldari spy, in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Head out there and take him down.
135810:
We've analyzed the data you brought back from the traitor's ship. He was on his way to meet up with his contact, some Caldari spy, in the asteroid fields of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. With luck, the contact is still out there waiting for the traitor's arrival.

Can you head on out to that system and take him down? His ship is likely to be pretty powerful, but if you can capture him alive we'll provide you with a substantial bounty.
135812: Excellent job! You've helped deal a major blow to the Caldari spy network.
135813: I'll get him and bring him back.
135814: The contact has been dealt with, {[character]agentID.name}.

135817: See you when you return, my friend.

135834:
Egonics, Inc. is unique in the Gallente music industry. Extremely popular among young citizens of virtually every star nation, Egonics produces the only entertainment headset that transmits music directly into the user's brain. The company's contracted musical artists tailor the music to the individual tastes of every listener.

The technology's growing popularity has caused it spread across the galaxy, except in the Amarr Empire, where possession of Egonics tech is outlawed.
135836:
What's wrong? Listen to this. Egonics headsets: They're the fashion, right? All the kids have to have them. But some people, including me, have always been afraid that something like this could happen.

Apparently some Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people — all of them wearing Egonics devices — simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. This strange exodus went unnoticed because, other than their destination, the people seemed to be behaving normally. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss.

Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station. Of course, they thought their network security was iron-clad, but now I can assure you they're rethinking their assumptions. This is a catastrophe of the highest order, {[character]player.name}!

Just imagine what a tragedy this would be if it wasn't Federation policy to put a tracking beacon on every Bestower that docks in our sovereignty!

If you can get all of those Gallente citizens back, there's a big reward for you. And if you can keep the Egonics corporate name out of it, so much the better… If you see any Scope reporters nosing around as you leave, pray, ignore them.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.

The slaver ship likely has escorts, as well.
135837:
{[character]player.name},

Fortunately, the Navy was able to catch that Amarrian monster as he tried to leave Federation space with those kids. No thanks to you, of course. I can't believe you just sat on this mission! Over a thousand young lives were at stake!

I think maybe you need to take a deep look at what really matters to you in this life, friend. Obviously, something's not quite right in your head.

{[character]agentID.name}
135839: Forget it. I've changed my mind. Let the Navy deal with this.
135840: You're just going to let that slaver get away with a thousand kids? What kind of person are you? Perhaps you should work out of Amarr space from now on!
135843:
These pirates in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders. In fact, we believe the Gallente government has sanctioned these "pirates" as privateers.

Go out there and wipe them out. Yes, this is a “terminate with extreme prejudice” matter. The bounty on the pirate commander is sizeable, but you'll need proof of his death to collect it: Bring back his head and you'll be well-rewarded for your efforts.

You're going to face a sizable force of pirates. You'll likely need at least a battlecruiser, and maybe even a few allies.

And they've been using their base in that system as a launching point to strike out into neighboring systems as well. Of course, pirates are to be expected these days, but these pirates are different. They are well funded, well equipped, and commanded by some canny ship commanders.

135858: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll find someone else, I suppose.
