135865:
Now that I have your attention, I'll tell you my story. I am a prominent salesman sent to Otitoh on a special assignment from Expert Distribution. Well… I was.

I was born and raised in New Caldari, and I wasn't prepared for the harsh life of this run-down system. My first few months here were quite difficult, and I often thought about abandoning my work here and running back to my family.

In my depressed and lonely state, I needed a companion: someone to ease the tension of everyday life here. My wife refused to leave our home in New Caldari, so I had no one. So, I was completely helpless when I stumbled upon a beautiful young woman who seemed to be caught up in the same situation that I was. There was no one around who gave a damn.

I found her in a bar in the Lai Dai station in Otitoh. She actually started the conversation— considering how I was brought up, I'm not used to a woman taking the initiative in such matters. Anyway, next thing I knew, I was waking up the next morning in her bedroom with a terrible hangover. Before I had time to fully clothe myself, I discovered my mistake: the door to the apartment opened and a short, gnarled old man came in. As soon as I saw him, I knew I was in trouble.

That man was Eteri Tazaki, an officer of the Lai Dai Protection Services. He was furious, but— fortunately for me—unarmed. He chased me out of the apartment, calling for the guards. I managed to escape into a nearby alley, and, with my heart about to explode, I ran as fast as I could to the hangar bay.

I've been running ever since. The fact is, every law enforcement officer in this system seems to be corrupt, and by the virtue of his position alone, Tazaki has managed to convince the authorities that I raped his wife. I'm now a wanted man, hunted by those I once trusted with my life. I'm still trying to come to terms with what has happened, but it's hard. I just hope my family doesn't hear about this until I have time to explain everything in person.

What I need from you, {[character]player.name}, is help to escape this constellation. I can't risk trying to make the jump out of here without adequate preparation; if I'm caught, I could end up in prison for the rest of my life. That's something I want to avoid at all costs, especially in these parts.

Your first task will be a difficult one. The sheriff of Otitoh, Togany, has been snooping around the area looking for me. I think he must have been tipped off by one of the locals, because he's currently scouring the asteroid belts near here, where I usually run at the first sight of law enforcement officers. You must take him out— destroy his ship or whatever; just prevent him from finding me. I fear that if he's not taken care of soon, I will be caught. If he catches me, he'll call in back-up, and there'll be no stopping them. He's currently located near one of the moons of Otitoh VII. Bring me proof of his demise and you will be rewarded.
135866:
Amazing stuff, {[character]player.name}. I didn't expect you to bring him here alive, but I'm quite pleased; this won't go over as badly with the authorities as killing him would've. I'll keep him prisoner on my ship until I've managed to get away from Okkelen, then I'll release him. Now we have to move fast: once the authorities figure out their sheriff is missing, they'll send out search teams, and then I'll be in serious trouble.

Get ready for your next assignment.

The most powerful of these beacons are located in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; go there and destroy them quickly. There will be ships guarding the beacons, and they'll no doubt put up a very strong resistance.

135891: Fair enough. I can't order you.
135892: Things are going badly. Because you were slow to act, the Sansha station we found launched a raid against one of our facilities. Now I have to pull people off the line to handle the mess.  Next time, make sure you can do what needs to be done.

Excellent. Now, first off, I must stress that this is all strictly confidential. If any word of this matter were to get out, it could tarnish our appearance in the public eye, not to mention damage Federation morale.

It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier. We need to stop them, destroy that ship, and get back the computer with the... public confidence procedures.

Keep it on the sly, {[character]player.name}, and you'll be well rewarded. What do you think?

A few hours ago, an Amarrian strike force hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone now, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

Warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; you'll need to move quickly. And if it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves.
135927:
You may already know that Amarr is preparing for war. It seems that they want to take back what they feel was once rightfully theirs and make us all slaves in the process. It will be the Day of Darkness all over again, if they have their way.

But they will not. We Minmatar will not kneel to that sociopathic, god-mongering cult run by feeble cybernetic monstrosities. The Amarrians will either perish or slay us to the last — either way, they will never again make us their slaves.

We've not come to open warfare yet, but the Imperials have been raiding along the frontier, trying to provoke us into a fight. A few hours ago they hit a refugee convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have gone, but we've picked up a distress transmission that claims there are survivors. It could be a trap, or the Amarrians may be planning to return and capture the survivors for sale as slaves in the Empire.

So, we need a good, capable captain who's willing to warp over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and investigate. If there really are any survivors, get them before the Amarrians do; survivors may not last long out there, so you'll need to move quickly.

If it proves an ambush, then take out any Amarrian bastards who show themselves. Will you do it?
135928: On your way, captain. Death to Amarr!
135929: Thank god! We'll see to the refugees' comfort. Take your reward and my personal gratitude.
135930: I'm… shocked. My reports have you a fearless, dedicated veteran. I am supremely disappointed, both in you and in my intelligence.
135931: I will help you to the best of my ability. The Republic!
135932: The refugees are safe and the Amarrian ships are destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.
135933: I know it's important, but the danger sounds too great. I can't risk my ship over a few civilians.
135934: I'll serve the Republic any way I can, {[character]agentID.name}. What is needed of me?
135935:
We've been having problems with a Sansha outpost for a while now. I've finally received clearance to sponsor a raid on the facility. I guess someone got tired of paying for new haulers.

So how about it? Get some of your capsuleer buddies together and destroy every Sansha you find. You'll be a hero; and since the Sansha are all unholy mockeries of all that is human, you don't even have to feel bad about killing them!
135936: Sansha's Nation is just this side of rogue drones-- in some ways the Nation is worse. At least drones are machines acting like they're alive. Sansha were people; now they act like machines. Best thing about both is that you can blow the hell out of them and still maintain a clear moral high ground.

To prove yourself to me, bring me a piece of the extremely valuable mineral, neophite. I hear Akira Helkelen has a little neophite in stock; you might want to pay him a visit at the Rush Town Ruins if you don't have any neophite yourself.

136062:
Now that you've neutralized the sheriff, it's time to prepare my getaway ship. I will need a cloaking device to keep myself from being detected, just in case CONCORD or Customs have been notified about me. Being cloaked doesn't make my plan foolproof, but it will increase my chance of escape significantly.

You should be able to find a Prototype Cloaking Device on the market; I'd buy it myself if I wasn't trying to lie low. If you don't think you'll be able to get ahold of one, don't screw me around-- just don't bother taking this job.

136064:
I'm almost ready to set off for the outer regions, where I can hide until my lawyer clears my name, but there's one final obstacle. I was scanning the stargate to Ihakana from a great distance to avoid detection, when I noticed a few Caldari bandits led by Bai Tarziiki camping nearby. I remember seeing Bai's face in a news bulletin a while back; he's reputed to be a member of the Kazka Bandits, a notorious gang of outlaw mercenaries in these parts. They are also rumored to have close ties with the corrupt security forces in Otitoh, which Eteri is a part of.

I'm not sure what Bai is up to, but I have a sinking feeling that he was sent by Eteri to block my exit. He probably knows that Ihakana is the first place I would go to. Outlaws like Bai are experts at sniffing out people in hiding, so there's no doubt that he has an anti-cloaking device and multiple scanners on his ship. I can't afford to take this kind of chance: if they catch me I'll be tortured and killed.

Your last task is simple. Take out Bai, and bring me proof that he won't bother me anymore. His corpse will do.

Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you.

Although Sansha's Nation usually has a firm grip over the criminal strata in our system, the Angel Cartel has been poking its ugly nose in here of late-- which is perfectly fine with us. In fact, watching the two outlawed organizations duke it out is one of my favorite pastimes. If we're lucky, it will give both sides a good bruising, which will only work in our favor.

Of course, there's also bad news. An InterBus ship traveling to {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} got caught in the middle of one of the pirate warzones. The ship was damaged beyond repair and can neither warp out nor navigate away from the crossfire. Your task is to rescue the ship's crew. Please retrieve them before any more harm is done; they're already scared out of their minds. The faster you get this done, the better.

Good luck.

136097:
Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you. Although the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} have traditionally had a firm grip over this system, Sansha's Nation has been poking its ugly nose in here of late. We were about to assemble a strike force to take care of their latest infiltration when we noticed something interesting. The Sansha fleet that we had stumbled upon is fighting for their lives against a sizable Gallente armada!

We aren't sure where the Gallente came from or what they're doing here, but I suspect it's one of those blasted entrepreneurs, scouring space outside of Federation borders for possible business opportunities. Either way, we're always happy when our enemies fight each other. When they're done, it's that much easier for us to clean up the pieces.

Now, what I need you to do is fairly simple: retrieve some of our valuable drug stash that's lying in the middle of their little warzone. You'll have to navigate through the contested deadspace area to get to it, but I'm sure someone of your caliber can handle that. Just stay clear of their main fleet and you'll make it.

Good luck.

136102: I thought you had a bit more fortitude. It's people like you that allow the Federation to get away with committing this kind of treachery.
136103: Here's the coordinates for where the deal is going down. Good hunting, kirjuun.
136104: Good work, {[character]player.name}. You've done a great job for the State and this corporation.
136105: Most disappointing, pilot. How can you sit idly by while the Federation poisons our bodies and our minds? Hopefully someone else will have the courage to stand up to them.
136106: You failed to stop the drug deal, and likely Federation penetration of our borders as well. 136107: Due to your lack of action, {[character]player.name}, I was forced to find another pilot to carry out this mission. Hopefully, in the future, you will be more punctual, pilot.
136110: I'll take care of the problem, {[character]agentID.name}. This intrusion must be stopped.
136111: The drug runners' ships have been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}, and I managed to bring back a few of them alive for interrogation.
136112: I don't think I feel like dealing with this mess right now.
136113: How can I be of service to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} and the State, kirjuun?
136114:
It looks as if one of our public confidence operatives has turned. What's a public confidence operative? A person whose job it is to spread good news and make sure the general public doesn't lose faith in the government. Yes, I guess you could call it "propaganda management"… but hell, what's a government without propaganda?

Anyway, it seems those fascists in the Caldari State have managed to turn the guy, and he's heading for enemy space with a computer full of our public confidence procedures. He's met up with some Caldari warships, and they're escorting him to the frontier.

Stop them, destroy their ships, and bring back the data chip containing the public confidence procedures.
136115:
Good work. I'm glad I found you.

Take this data chip. On it, you will find evidence that the Wiyrkomi corporation have been engaging in terrorism against themselves in order to shift the public's opinion regarding both them and FON. It's not absolutely 100 percent reliable, but what there is seems solid enough. Bring this chip to Preaux Gallot in the Natura Seminary in Audaerne. There is more to be done yet, and I have a feeling this is all just beginning.

Thank you for all your help. You've done us a great service.
136116:
A traditional Caldari privateer's song

Oh, poor old man, your bunny will die.
And we say so, and we know so.
Oh, poor old man, your bunny gonna die
Oh, poor old man!

We'll drag it down to the State line,
We'll drop it down inside the border,
We'll drop it off into the void, hey.

We'll drop it off into the void, now,
Sing it down with a long, long roll.
The peggies can have its body,
And the devil can have its soul.
136117:
This is a pre-recorded message: Why are you lookin' here? You forget somethin'? Are you stupid, 's that it? We're barely done talkin' and it all already slipped outta your head? GO KILL THE DAMN TRAITOR.

Damn rookies.
136119:
You heard me, {[character]player.name}. Animal problems. And stop lookin' at me like I'm crazy or I'll be tempted to do somthin' we'll both regret. Just shut up and listen.

This is what happens: You scour the land, lookin' hard and far and wide and all that. After much of that business, you find yourself a good bunny. Real proper, no poser crap – the real deal. Least that's what you think. You give this bunny everything of yourself. All your knowledge, all your expertise, all your damn money. Hell… all your love, even. I said stop lookin' at me like that!

What was I–? Oh… right.

So, for a while that works well – with a real big emphasis on the "for a while" bit. This little bunny looks after itself proper, looks after you real good in turn too. As it damn well should, little bugger. Then one day, outta the blue, it seems to think it's had enough. Thinks it will just hop on over to the Mordus Legion and work for them instead. After everything you've done for it. "Better money," it says. "Doing what's right," it says. Dumb bunny. Real damn stupid.

You know what you do next, right? Go on, tell me what you do and prove you're not as green as you look.
136120: Eh… useless after all. I knew it. I could smell the fear on you, ya damn rookie! Howsabout you forget about that next time, eh? You got a damn pod, what more could ya want?
136121: Huh. That's right. Guess you might be useful after all. Alright, then, my young protégé: Stage two – here's the coordinates. I'm not giving you a damn thing. Go show me you're more than just talk!
136122: Good work, Rookie! Now go and have yourself a party on me. Oh, and remember: this is what happens to bad bunnies. Don't get any funny ideas under those long, furry ears of yours.
136123: Wrong answer, Rookie. Howsabout you take that tub of yours and paddle back to State space before you figure out you can't swim with the big fish.
136124: You take it out back, have one last look at it, then put a bullet in its furry little head.
136125: Hop, hop, bang. "Crap, I'm dead." I think it's payday.
136126: Uhm… what I do is… or what someone needs to do, at least, is stop gobbling the ol' Blue Pill. I think you need to get some rest… and maybe some rehab. Sheesh.
136127: I forgot what I was supposed to do, so I figure I'll just do nothing instead. Seeya.
136128: Uh… wha-?! Like, vermin in your apartment or something? You know I'm a capsuleer, right?
136129: I'm not sure you're thinking this through: the Brothers of Freedom are more of a threat than you realize. Perhaps you'll learn before it's too late.
136131: Good work, {[character]player.name}. Perhaps Torvil will restrict himself to overpaid speaking engagements for bleeding-heart, over-privileged Gallente from now on, instead of trying to spit in our faces.
136132: Don't tell me you actually sympathize with these morons? For your sake, I hope you don't.
136133: I never heard back from you, {[character]player.name}, so I'm going to assume you don't have the stomach to take care of this Brothers of Freedom tyuui. That's unfortunate, but thankfully there are plenty of other loyal Caldari pilots out there looking for work.
136137: The transmitter has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm just disappointed I didn't catch Torvil there himself.
136138: I don't think I want to mess with it if it's inside the Republic. I hear they eat their prisoners.
136139: I've decided it's not worth risking my hide just to shut up someone who's making fun of you. Do your own dirty work.
136140: Oh? What sort of mission is that?
136141:
Sometimes calling itself "The Scions of Athra," the Athran Brotherhood is a group of Khanid secessionists with headquarters located on the Khanid homeworld of Amarr Prime (called Athra in the Old Khanid tongue). This group tends to rise perhaps every other generation or so, seemingly from its own ashes, making trouble for local government and interstellar trade alike.

Given the many large pirate organizations and other independent "freebooters" of New Eden, not to mention the constant weight of intergalactic politics and the ongoing "Minmatar Problem," Amarr rulers cannot generally spare a large-scale military effort to deal with these relatively minor troublemakers. Perhaps this is the reason the Brotherhood seems never to die, but always reappears just when authorities start to think they've rid themselves of the nuisance.
136142:
You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here: It used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. And I suspect it may have become the hideout for a chapter of the Athran Brotherhood. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

All you need to do is fly close to the structure and see if you pick up any short-range radio transmissions or see any other signs of activity. Then get back here and let me know what you found.
136144:
You don't say! Well, yes, in fact, I do have something I could use you for.

You've heard of the "Athran Brotherhood"? No? Well, that's no surprise, really. They're little more than a nuisance, and few in number. But they can be a pain at times. And we're pretty sure there's a chapter of them hereabouts. But we don't know where they're hiding out. That's what I want you to find out for me, actually.

There's a small station built into an old asteroid near here. Used to be a mining outpost till they hollowed the thing out. It's been abandoned for a few years now, but some rumors of activity in that area have been surfacing. I need you to go check those rumors out and let me know what you find.

Seem like something you'd be interested in?
136145: It's possible, but not generally, no. If they do engage, don't feel obliged to mess with them, unless you feel you're in no danger.
136146: Yeah, I got your ship's logs once you docked. Stick around and talk to me again in a bit, would you? We need to get to the bottom of this.
136147: Seems straightforward enough. Are these Athrans hostile?
136148: Alright, I went out there, and I definitely picked up some Athran radio transmissions. I also picked up some carbon scoring when they opened fire on me...
136149: Sounds pretty dull, actually. I think I'll pass.
136150: I've given it some more thought, and actually I'm not sure I'm up to tracking down these Athrans for you. Sorry.
136151: Well, thanks. I'm just wondering if you might have some work for a recent graduate. I'm a decent combat pilot.
136153: The Athrans seem pretty dangerous. I think I'm throwing in the towel. Sorry.
136154: What if it's a trap? I mean, they seemed to know I was coming last time, right? Sorry, but I just can't risk my ship....
136155: You bet. I'll be back before you can say, "Hey, where'd you go?"
136156: Suit yourself. I was giving you a chance to be of service to your nation, but if you want to hide behind your degree, well… I can't stop you.
136157: That's what I like to hear. Be careful out there, eh? These Athrans seem more... volatile than most.
136158: I had doubts about you all along, to be honest. Just goes to show I'm still a good judge of character.
136159:
Yes. We put a covert ops ship out there around the same time you left for your last mission, and the pilot corroborated your story. He also reports that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left. Fortunately, he was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, I want you to head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.
136161:
Always be ready to warp out if you start taking heavy damage, whether in a mission or in lawless space. Sometimes it's a good idea to have a jump route selected before going into a mission so you can simply click your autopilot to get out quickly; this is a valid approach only with relatively small ships, though. Eventually, once you get into something like a Battleship, aligning to warp can take so long — especially if you begin once you're already taking heavy damage — that your ship might be destroyed by the time you actually start your warp.

Remember too that if you take damage in battle, you can always return to a nearby station for repairs; also be sure to replenish your ammunition while you're there if you're running low. Combat in EVE can be deadly and costly, so do what you can to cut your losses.

"It's better to warp away and fight again another day."
136162: I certainly am. Have you been able to discover what the Athrans were after?
136163: Uh, I've decided this mission isn't for me. Sorry, but you'll have to find someone else.
136164: Hm, I don't know. Their munitions depot is bound to be heavily guarded. Maybe you should get someone more experienced to handle this one. Too risky.
136165: Woo! That was one big explosion. That's my kind of mission.
136166: Finally, we're taking the fight to them. I'll be there in moments.
136167: You can't always take the safe way out, you know. Sometimes a warrior has to bleed a little to serve his nation... or hers. Point is, danger is part of the job.
136168: Glad you enjoyed it. Listen, this all may not be over yet, so don't wander too far off, okay?
136169: Good show. But be careful out there: They may know you're coming.
136170: The Athran Brotherhood has an ammunitions depot located in this very system. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking there shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself. They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them.
136171: I found those Athrans, alright. And they're in league with the Minmatar, it would seem. They made pretty short work of a chapel structure out there.
136172: I wonder what was so important about that chapel… Hm. Give me a while to look into this, then come back and see me, will you? Thanks.
136173: Attacking Couriers or Haulers in Hi-sec
136174: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. I assume then that you did not intercept the shipment, else I would have a shiny new set of tools.
136175: I see that my competitors have just put up a new selection of construction tools on the market. You missed the window of opportunity. I need timely and punctual help, not indecisive help.
136178: A chance to take out one of those spineless couriers without risking CONCORD? Consider it done!
136179: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.
136180: I'm not going to take out a lowly courier, risk or no risk.
136181: Nothing like a little healthy competition, right?
136182: That's what I like to hear!
136183: It's done. Here are the construction tools.
136184: Hah! Let's see how they do without their exclusive stock! Don't go anywhere. There's more to be done.
136185: Come on, this is a professional hauler. He almost doesn't even count as a person.
136186:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.
136187:
There's a small family-run corporation operating in the neighboring system. A real pain, you know? They've got a corner on just about every small commodity in the region. I can't even get any of their suppliers to sell to me, and it's pissing me off.

I've got a plan, though. They keep getting exclusive contracts because they keep their shipments secret and secure. But I've figured out where they go. I know when and where one of their supply shipments are going to be. And even better, it's in a dead space pocket that CONCORD doesn't monitor.

Intercept the ship, blow it up, and bring the supplies--construction tools, I think-- back to me.
136188: You know, our security personnel just barely stopped an attempt on my life. We are still in danger, and you just walk away? This isn't over yet. I'll never understand you capsuleers, I swear.
136189: Of course, yes. One does not ask a favor of a capsuleer otherwise, you know...
136190:
You're not alone in being attacked. Our security personnel barely stopped an attempt on my life just a few minutes after you left for that last mission. My life flashed before my eyes, I swear!

Listen, we need to end this. Let me look into this a bit further; come back and talk to me soon, though, okay? I'm not going to be able to sleep until we finish this thing.
136191: I guess my LUX and my friendship aren't incentive enough, huh? I see where we stand. Hmph. Thanks. For nothing.
136192: Sure, I can take it over there for you. I mean, you're paying me, right?
136193: Not really interested in playing delivery-stooge, no. Thanks anyway.
136194: I've had enough of this. Sorry, but I can't finish this mission. Keep your reward.
136195: Of course, {[character]agentID.name}. What do you need?
136196: Not going to-but it's just a courier! They were made to be popped!
136197: Truth be told, nowhere in the universe is safe for the humble courier. Even though CONCORD patrols the so-called "hi-sec" areas of space (security rating 0.5-1.0), that doesn't ensure your protection one hundred percent. It is possible for a capsuleer of sufficient skill or equipment to take out another capsuleer before CONCORD fully retaliates. Usually the certainty of losing a ship to CONCORD is enough to dissuade hi-sec attacks, but if the payout or cargo is worth enough, an attacker might think it worth the trouble.
136198: Head out to the deadspace location they Athrans are using as a hideout. Deal with those creeps and take out their leader, Cosensin Thrand.
136199:
We know who their leader is, {[character]player.name}: some woman called Cosensin Thrand. And it seems she's hiding out in this very star system. Now we can take these nut-jobs out once and for all.

I'll upload the coordinates of the deadspace location they're using as a hideout. Get on out there and deal with these creeps, and you'll be well rewarded. Good luck!
136200:
I see. Well, I must assume you have good reason.

Until next time.
136201: I thought you might, {[character]player.name}. I thought you might.
136202: Excellent news! I knew you would conclude this matter admirably. I shall speak on your behalf to my associates. God speed. And thank you.
136203: There is no room for cowardice in a capsuleer. I mean, you're virtually immortal! It's shameful.
136204: My pleasure. I'm going to enjoy this mission.
136205: Cosensin Thrand and her henchmen are no longer… well, they're just no longer. If you take my meaning.
136206:
Hm. These guys are pretty dangerous. And you want me to take out their leader? I don't know…

Nah, sounds too risky.
136207: This might be a problem for you, but I can't finish this mission. Sorry. I just can't.
136208: How so? What did you find?
136209:
Well, it seems they're simply trying to disrupt the local infrastructure. What they seek to gain by doing so, I don't know... but that's the terrorist mentality for you.

But what's more interesting is that I've discovered they have an ammunitions depot not far from here. If we can take it out, we'll seriously disrupt their plans, whatever they might be. In fact, they have a Bestower full of explosives docking shortly: Get over there and take out that ship, then deal with the depot itself. They're sure to have some guards, but you've proven yourself capable of dealing with them. God speed.
136210: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
136211: Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and mine 333 units of Augumene ore.
136213:
Well, I need someone who can handle a ship, but who also knows how to rip ore. If you can do that, then we might be able to come to an agreement.

You've heard of Augumene ore before? It's not too common because it's too costly to refine safely. Thing is, though, a team of scientists working for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} think they've figured out a way to do it cheaply. We need someone to procure some of the ore, though, so they can run some tests.

Interested?
136214: Excellent. We'll make it worth your while.
136215: Well, that's up to our scientists, not me. But you did good work. In fact, I may have another job for you shortly, so come back in a bit, will you?
136216: But you won't be building any cred with {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} while you mine that way. Ah, well — your choice, not mine.
136217: Yeah, I'm a decent 'roid miner. I'll have this Augumene back to you in a jiffy.
136218: I've got your Augumene here. Good luck making any use of it.
136219: Not really interested in mining for someone else's profit, no. I can hit the belts on my own if I want to mine, and that way I cut out the middle man.
136220: I've changed my mind. Sorry. I can't be bothered mining for someone else, though. Just doesn't make sense.
136221: Capsuleer, in fact. You need a starship pilot? I might be available….
136222:
The Athrans seem to have vanished, so either we dealt with the last of them, or the remaining few have gone deep into hiding. Either way, it looks like we've seen the end of their plotting.

All that remains is for you to give a report to the Assistant Chief Security Officer for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So how about it? Do you mind flying over there and letting him know what's been happening? You'll be generously reimbursed for your time, of course.
136223: Prepare an oral report regarding your actions in the Athran Uprising for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s Assistant Chief Security Officer. He's currently at a meeting at our office in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.
136224: Well, looks like the Minmatar were trying pretty hard to cover their tracks. Sorry I couldn't deliver the report — and, er... it looks like {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has some cleanup to do over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Not much left of your offices there.
136225: While academies and universities can provide a good foundation, successful capsuleers know that education continues forever. Skill books are the quickest and most reliable way for a capsuleer to learn to use new equipment or systems.
136226:
I have this crazy idea about owning my own outpost. I just need to put my plans into action.

First thing I need is an instructional book on running a corporation. I've found the perfect book for me. I'll pay you to go and pick it up for me.
136228:
I have this crazy idea about owning my own outpost. I've heard it's just like printing LUX. I'm in strong enough favor with the local powers, and I've secured a number of interested investors. Now I just need to put my plans into action.

First thing I need is an instructional book on running a corporation. The books you capsuleers use are a bit over my head. Luckily, I've found the perfect book for me. I'll pay you to go and pick it up for me.
136229: Bootleg? Are you kidding? The skill book makers track that stuff more than CONCORD. Their lawyers are more vicious, too.
136230: Show no fear! Show no mercy! Get the book!
136231: Thanks! I'll start reading this immediately. While I'm studying this, I have something else you can do for me.
136232: You're going to have a tough time of this universe if you can't be bothered to get a book.
136233: I could have spacewalked to the damn station, picked up my book, read it, and spacewalked back by now. Get with the program, huh?
136234: Why are you so indecisive about books? Do they frighten you? Are you afraid you might catch "the literacy"?
136237: I ain't afraid of no book. I'll get it.
136240: I'm not going to finish this book delivery. Just bootleg it or something.
136241: Oh yeah? What do you want?
136242:
Oh, it's nothing complicated or difficult, frankly. But it's not something I'd trust to a common courier service or even an encrypted FTL transmission.

Can you go pick up the formula our scientists have been working on and bring it back to me here? They've stored a copy in some encrypted data crystals. I need to have my personal team review the process before I can let the experiment go ahead.
136243: Of course, of course. Payment on delivery, as usual.
136244: Good job. And thanks again. Talk to me whenever you have time and we'll see if I can't dig up some more work for you.
136245: Well, if that's how you see it, then fine. But you do realize I would have paid you…?
136246: Sure. As long as I'm paid according to my station, then I'm all for it.
136247: Formula delivered, safe and sound. Glad to do business with you.
136248: You know, I didn't graduate from the best university in the universe just so I could pick up packages for people. So, no. Thanks, but no.
136249: I changed my mind. Sorry. I've got better things to do than fetch your formula for you.
136251:
Pick up the encrypted data crystals -- I've uploaded the destination into your NeoCom -- and bring it back to your agent.

Once you collect it, remember to put the data crystals in your cargohold before you leave the station.
136252:
I've recently hired a number of highly trained... I can't say that with a straight face.

Bums. I hired bums.

Go pick up my bums.
136253: You capsuleers are lucky. A couple of you get together, any of you can start a corporation. There are a bunch of you out in 0.0 controlling territory that rivals the empires. But even you guys have to work together to do it.
136255:
I hate people, personally. But it's damn hard to get anything done in this universe by yourself. With that in mind, I've recently hired a number of highly trained...I can't say that with a straight face.

Bums. I hired bums.

Go pick up my bums.
136256: I pick hating the homeless. It upsets me less.
136257: I pick hating the homeless. It upsets me less.
136258: Desperate is the best kind of work force.
136259: Good job. I'll have them broken and dehumanized within a week. You're turning into quite the helper.
136260: Never mind about the bums. I just filled all my positions with some of the local children. If you got the bums already, you can just go ahead and space them or something.
136261: I just received word that the homeless have been moved to another station. Apparently some bureaucratic know-nothing decided to have another capsuleer ship them off to improve appearances.
136266: I don't want to support your exploitation of the homeless, I hate the homeless and wish them to remain in abject poverty, or I am simply lazy. Take your pick.
136267: I don't want to support your exploitation of the homeless, I hate the homeless and wish them to remain in abject poverty, or I am simply lazy. Take your pick.
136269: The Augumene ore reprocessed using the new formula, for some reason, produces a deadly allergic reaction in most people of the Matari racial type. There are only a handful of survivors at that reprocessing station. Evacuate the surviving scientists from the quarantine station next to their outpost/lab.
136270:
Listen, things were going fine. Just fine. My team had approved the procedure and tested the results. But here's the thing. None of the science team was of Matari heritage. They were all Caldari or mixed-blood. So what we didn't realize until way too late is that the Augumene ore reprocessed using this new formula, for god knows what reason, produces a severe and deadly allergic reaction in most people of the Matari racial type.

{[character]player.name}, almost the entire population of that reprocessing lab was Matari. There are only a handful of survivors. It's a disaster, a huge disaster. First thing, we need to evacuate the surviving scientists from the quarantine station next to their lab. That's your first job. Come back when that's done, and we'll have more to do, I imagine.
136271: Oh, thank you. This is horrible. Horrible.
136272: So many things to do. Listen, thanks for getting them. Just give me a minute to figure out the next step and then come back, will you?
136273: It's not a disease, it's an allergic reaction. And these are the survivors, and they're in quarantine. But, hey, suit yourself. I've got enough problems already; I don't need you adding to them.
136274: Alright, calm down. It's a tragedy, but we'll manage. I'll go get the survivors, okay?
136275: Alright, I've picked up the survivors and brought them back. What's next?
136276: Uh, I'm not sure I want any people who might be infected with some weird disease on my ship. Er, no thanks.
136277: We do? We? Really? What in the world is it?
136278: What do you mean? What's happened now?
136279: I've decided to back out of this mission, actually. I'm just not up to it. Sorry.
136280: Um, I'm really not a combat pilot, if you take my meaning. Maybe this is more of a job for the navy? Sorry.
136281:
The lab is no more, and neither are the Amarr agents they sent in. Any more, that is. Uh, neither are they any more. "Anymore"? Ehh… either way, that doesn't make much sense, does it? I mean, they're all dead. And so is the lab. Or, well, it's not so much dead as…

Mission complete. All done. Thanks — sorry! Thanks.
136282: You got it. I've been looking forward to testing my new ship's fittings against Amarr scum. Perfect timing.
136283: Alright, fair enough. But good god, I hope they can get there in time. Imagine the death toll…
136284: Good, good. Be careful out there. Who knows what kind of force they'll have waiting.
136285:
The damned Amarr, that's what! What else?! God, I need a break.

Alright, it seems the Amarrians somehow caught wind of our, er, difficulties here, and they're eager as all hell to get their hands on the Augumene reprocessing formula. I mean, what better than a biological weapon for use against the Minmatar that was developed by the Minmatar and their allies, right?

Anyway, they may already have a team in that lab. I need you to head right back out there and destroy that lab before they get their hands on the formula. If you manage to blow up some Amarrian marines while you're at it, so much the better. And if they offer up any resistance, don't hesitate to take them out. We can cover up the destruction of a few ships, but we simply cannot afford to let them get the formula. Understand?
136286: The Amarrians somehow caught wind of our difficulties here, and they're eager to get their hands on the Augumene reprocessing formula. They may already have a team in that lab. Get out there and destroy that lab before they get their hands on the formula. And if they offer up any resistance, don't hesitate to take them out.
136287: Oh, thank you. I think. This may not be over yet, so don't go too far. Oh, and hold onto that blueprint I just gave you; we're going to need to produce an antidote for this allergen.
136288: Sounds good. What do you need me to do?
136289: I just can't be bothered to finish making the antidote. Sorry. Maybe someone can do it.
136290: Sorry, I'm not flying out to that place again. Twice is more than enough, thanks.
136291: Here's your antidote, {[character]agentID.name}. I pray we won't need to use it.
136292: Sounds pretty simple. Get DNA, make antidote. Sure, I can do that.
136293: Very well. I see how it is. Well, I'm sure I can find someone willing to do this job for me.
136294: I share your sentiment, my friend. Let us hope this whole incident is now far behind us.
136295: Excellent. You're doing us a great service, {[character]player.name}.
136296: You come this far and then quit?! Acts speak far more loudly than words, you know. And your inaction here has spoken to your character more clearly than you know.
136297:
Well, I gave you the blueprint we'd been working on for the antidote after your last mission. In theory, we don't need to worry about the reprocessed Augumene being produced anymore, but just in case, we want to have the antidote on hand in case the Amarr somehow did get a copy, despite your efforts. Or, for that matter, if their scientists were to rediscover the process on their own.

However, to make the antidote, we need a DNA sample from a Matari subject who was affected by the reprocessed Augumene — which means I need you to head back out to the lab site and sift through the debris out there. Once you have the DNA sample, find a station where you can manufacture the antidote, then bring the finished product back to me.
136299:
To make the antidote, we need a DNA sample from a Matari subject who was affected by the reprocessed Augumene — which means I need you to head back out to the lab site and sift through the debris out there. Once you have the DNA sample, find a station where you can manufacture the antidote, then bring the finished product back to me.

Use the blueprint copy I gave you at the end of your last mission; if you're unsure what to do, review Aura's "Industry" tutorial, which you can access from your NeoCom.
136300: To finish this mission, you first need to acquire the Minmatar DNA from the laboratory site (where you destroyed the lab in your last mission). Once you have the DNA, use it and the blueprint you received at the end of your last mission to manufacture the Modified Augumene Antidote. With the antidote in your hangar, talk to your agent again to complete the mission.
136301: Capsuleers can have their own structures (POS). These can be used for tasks such as mining, storage, or research. One of the ways capsuleers in 0.0 wage war is by attacking POSes. Though such an attack can be difficult to mount, the loss of a structure is a huge one.
136302:
That blasted family corp sent mercenaries after my new outpost. Can you believe that? Who do they think they are?!

Get to my outpost. Kill every mercenary you can. Maybe it's not too late to save it.
136304:
It's that blasted family corp! They've sent mercenaries after my new outpost. Can you believe that? I mean, yeah, I may have messed with their supply route a bit, but-- Who do they think they are?!

Get to my outpost. Kill every mercenary you can. Maybe it's not too late to save it.

The first wave of these new Suntendi Virtu-Real Implants has already hit market, but there's been a bit of a snag in production. Has to do with expected sales figures from the previous generation of implants or something… I don't know, corporate jargon, you know. Not my thing.

The technology's growing popularity has caused it spread across the galaxy, except in the higher-security regions of the Amarr Empire, where possession of Egonics tech is outlawed.

The lower the security level of the system, the higher the likelihood of your encountering pirates — whether NPC ships or other players, either of whom are most likely more than willing to blow you to smithereens.

Always, in EVE, being aware of the chatter in the local chat channel can mean the difference between life and death… or at least between surviving in your current clone and having to buy a new one.

136384:
The damned Caldari, that's who! Messing around with our technology, scrambling the implant signals so they emit harmful EM pulses.

This is all-out, goddamned war! I mean it! I want to tear those bastards a new—

Listen, long and short: We found out that some covert operations from the Caldari State have been sabotaging this whole project. While we were building the implants, they had spies putting in receptors that would allow a transmission station — which they were building nearby at the same time — to mess with the implants. That's what caused all the shorts and explosions.

Well, now we know where the station is. And, since you're a capsuleer, we've got the right person for the job right here among us. Go out there and blow that scrambling beacon to bits. And take any bloody Caldari you see out with it. You have full authority. Make them pay.

Destroying structures can be a difficult undertaking. Most structures have very high hit points, at least relative to small ships like frigates, and they take a lot of punishment before being destroyed. And like ships, the bigger they are, the more shields and structure they generally have.

In a mission such as this, where you're asked to destroy a structure, it's generally a good idea to fit as much firepower on your ship as you're able: Otherwise, you simply might never be able to overcome your target's shield recharge rate, let alone rip apart its structure.

Anyway, we could use someone to go and check these rumors out. Supposedly there was a sighting very recently out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you're ready, head on out there and see what you can find. And don't worry — you'll be well paid for your time.

Others include the mysterious Sleepers, who some say are the ancestors of the enigmatic Jovians.

Those who wish to learn more of these ancient peoples are well-advised to develop their Science and Archaeology skills.

136409:
Given the FTL (faster-than-light) communications capabilities of contemporary starships, it would seem that transporting data or communications physically, by means data crystals or datapad, would be a thing of the distant past. However, for every data transfer via subspace or interstellar transmission, there is a risk of interception. Idea theft and espionage are par for the course in the competitive universe of EVE.

When governments and powerful corporations need to transfer information without risk of interference, they often rely on capsuleers. Common courier ships may be used for less sensitive yet vital data, but only capsuleers offer the combination of piloting ability and inherent security desired by the rich and powerful; of course, one must always take the risk that a capsuleer is trustworthy, but such employers can generally afford to pay their "couriers" well enough to buy their loyalty.

We've got another set of coordinates here for a deadspace complex where sightings have been fairly common. Head out there and see if you can't approach one of these ships, assuming you find one, and then come back and tell me whatever you can about it.

Now, we have no idea if these things are hostile, if they really exist. But if what you told me is true, that you saw one take out a couple of Gallente ships, then we need to be careful. You need to be careful, that is. If you're under attack, get the hell out of there. And if not, well, just find out what you can. Don't take any unnecessary risks.

It's a cult of some kind, comprised of traitors and murderers who are working to bring about the downfall of all we hold dear. 136448:
It easy to think of the Amarr Empire as a cold, cruel, hegemonic state endorsing terrible repression and subjugation. Anyone making such an argument would have a strong case. But of course life is never so simple: For every Amarrian "true believer" in the Empire, there is another who doubts not only his or her faith, but also the government that reifies religious doctrine.

That isn't to say that half of the Amarrians in the Empire are traitors and rebels — far from it. But to assume that every free Amarrian citizen condones slavery and colonization is to make a grievous error. There are many sympathizers to the Minmatar cause in Amarr.

One such group is the coalition of the "Secret Starway" (called by some the "Secret Stairway"), a loose network of liberal idealists who work actively, but always covertly, to assist escaped slaves slip out of the Empire's sovereignty. One of the chief ironies of this group is that most of its members are fervent believers in the State religion; they simply have alternate, "heretical" views of those passages from the Scriptures that tend to be used in support of slavery.
136449: That's what I was hoping to hear, {[character]agentID.name}. What is it?
136450: I've tired of this mission. Sorry, but I quit.
136451: God, I'm tired of doing courier runs for you. No, I've had enough, thanks.
136452: As long as they're all well-caged, then yeah — sure. I have a cousin who was mauled by those things, so I won't take any chances.
136453: It's not as if you aren't being well paid for your efforts, {[character]player.name}. But have it your way.
136454: Damn it! These "Starway" murderers must be stopped. Let me do a bit of digging and see what our intelligence has rooted out. Come back in a bit.
136455: Of course. They're entirely secure. No worries. Feel free to inspect them before they're loaded to your ship, if that'll make you feel better.
136456: Why take the mission in the first place only to quit now?! Fine, fine, have it your way.
136457: One of the tactics we've come up with in terms of dealing with this "Secret Starway" group is to use slaver hounds to sniff them out. So I've arranged for a large shipment of the beasts. Could you go and pick them up for me? It's a private deadspace compound, but I'll upload the coordinates for you and arrange for you to be allowed in with no hassles.
136459:
The sinuous slaver hound, mammalian yet rather serpentine in form, is commonly referred to as a "slaver." A native of Syrikos V, it has been bred by the Amarrians from the time they first settled that planet more than a millennium ago. The favorable use of the slaver as guard animal and hunting beast alike has led to its being exported from Syrikos V to virtually every other Amarrian agricultural planet, and to many industrial and mining colonies as well.

Over the centuries, the slaver has become fashionable among wealthy Amarrians as a pet for those willing to risk its often murderous nature; these hounds can become extremely loyal and devoted to their owners if disciplined well and handled with great care. As well, breeders and handlers have produced several subspecies of "toy slavers," smaller breeds more suitable for keeping as pets.
136460: How do you mean? What kind of progress?
136461: I may not be a fan of your courier missions, but I'm not an assassin either. This woman is a citizen of the Empire. At worst, she deserves a fair trial.
136463: I'm on it. She will suffer the fate of all traitors — long live the Empire!
136464: I had no idea you were in a position to judge the decrees of the Heirs themselves. Forgive me: I was not informed that you had been coronated the next emperor….
136465: Well done. You have served the Empire admirably. I foresee a grand future for you, my young friend.

I'll give you the coordinates: Get over there and make sure she doesn't escape. In fact, make sure she never has the opportunity to escape again, if you take my meaning. You've just been given free license.

Often frigate pilots exploit this, ganging up in groups called "wolf packs" to take down larger ships. The long targeting time and slower tracking of the larger ships makes taking down these wolf packs difficult. Often the best counter to wolf packs are other frigates, resulting in battles-within-battles.

It's time for you to get your knuckles bruised.

They have a scout scoping the place ahead of them. Only he's not going to get to the final area. He's going to be jumped by some other pirate. You will be that pirate.

The short version is this: The Gallente have set up a drone control tower not far from here that, combined with the chip our saboteur was putting into the robots, made them behave erratically. In fact, they started self-modifying as a result, effectively making themselves into rogue drones with limited AI.

But now we know where the control transmitter array is, and I've already sent in ships to destroy the "contaminated" outpost. Now all we need is for you to gear up and go take out the transmitter, and we'll be back in business. So how about it?

136644:

136653:
Given the FTL (faster-than-light) communications capabilities of contemporary starships, it would seem that transporting data or communications physically, by means data crystals or datapad, would be a thing of the distant past. However, for every data transfer via subspace or interstellar transmission, there is a risk of interception. Idea theft and espionage are par for the course in the competitive universe of EVE.

When governments and powerful corporations need to transfer information without risk of interference, they often rely on capsuleers. Common courier ships may be used for less sensitive yet vital data, but only capsuleers offer the combination of piloting ability and inherent security desired by the rich and powerful; of course, one must always take the risk that a capsuleer is trustworthy, but such employers can generally afford to pay their "couriers" well enough to buy their loyalty.

136662: Go on back out there and take out that Caldari research outpost. We have full license to destroy any Caldari we see in the vicinity, as well.

It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. We've had some run-ins with Angel Cartel recently in these parts, so watch your back.
136825:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.

136832: A gang of Serpentis cartel thugs is being used by Federation intelligence to slip assets into the State during drugs runs. You are to intercept one of these runs in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system, destroy the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners you can find. Bring them back to your agent so that they can be remanded to Tribunal custody.
136833:
Some critics might argue that the State has a complicated relationship with organized crime. While the various criminal enterprises in the State (including the Guristas) do cut into the bottom line of the megacorporations, these enterprises are also used by said corporations as a means of arm's-length corporate espionage. Or so the pundits say.

Therefore, these cynical observers aver, while corporate security generally tries to keep a firm hand against the criminal syndicates, their upper management simultaneously ensures that the symbiotic relationship between the corporations and the syndicates is preserved, often to the frustration of the security forces and the Navy.
136834:
We've recently received intelligence that a deal is going down in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system between a Caldari buyer and a minor, local branch of the Serpentis drug cartel. While this is a bit of a concern in and of itself, the bigger problem is that we believe the cartel is being paid by elements within the Federation intelligence community; their goal, apparently, is to use this particular drug route as a way to insert intelligence assets into the State. That is of considerably greater concern to us.

We would like you to fly to the coordinates of this rendezvous, eliminate the Serpentis vessels there, and recover any prisoners that you can find. We'll turn them over to the Tribunal for further questioning.
136835: I... I've decided that I don't want to go after these Serpentis guys. You did hear what they did to the last guy who tried, right?
136836: Even when on the brink of war, sometimes the people need a reminder just what all of their taxes are paying for. Air shows have long been a reliable PR program that gets the people excited about military tech in a slightly friendlier venue than a state-funded parade. There are accidents every so often, and the introduction of the vacuum of space has certainly not made them any safer, but damn if they are not still popular.

Your thief is dead, here's your cargo. I taught your friend a lesson, all right — don't mess with me. Too bad he's dead, because I'd like to teach him that one again.

Now pay up.
136901: Sure, I don't mind teaching scum like that a lesson or two. Count me in.
136904: {[character]player.name}, I really could have used you on this job. It's unfortunate things didn't work out… but I'm sure the fault is all yours.
136905: Because of your failure to deal with the small matter of bringing justice to the Gallente thief at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, my business is now facing bankruptcy. Sooner or later, {[character]player.name}, you're going to have realize we're all in this together, and start acting accordingly.

136907: Superbly done, {[character]player.name} ! If only I could have been there, to see him mewl as his ship crumbled around him — oh, the hilarity! Enjoy your reward, friend. You've earned it.
136908: This pleases me more than you know, {[character]player.name}. We'll show this crooked wretch how we do things downstation.
136909: You disappoint me, {[character]player.name}. If I can't count on you, then who can I count on? This universe grows darker every day...

I wish everyone was as straightforward as you, {[character]player.name}. Then I wouldn't be in this situation.

I supplied this Gallente leech with certain items he requested, and then he warps away before paying me. Some people, I tell you. So, I need to teach him some manners. Well, okay… I need you to teach him some manners.

My sources tell me he can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. {[character]player.name}, I'd like you to do that — teach him his manners — by flying out there, blasting his ship to so much dust, then returning my stolen cargo to me. If that doesn't teach him, nothing will.
136912:
It's simple, really: I supplied this ungrateful Gallente leech with items he requested, and then he warps away before paying me. I'd like you teach him some manners — by blasting his ship to stardust, then returning my stolen cargo to me.

My sources tell me he can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.
136913:
Remember to keep an eye on your shields and armor during battle. But if you do forget and you happen to lose a ship, well… hey, that's the life of a capsuleer. Just get a new one, even if you've got to beg, borrow, or steal, and just get right back to work.

Get used to the idea: Ships — not to mention your current clone — won't last forever.
136914: Sure, but... how about something with a little action?

136916: I don't want any part of royal family machinations. I hate politics.
136917: The Tash-Murkon traitor is in the hold — a little the worse for wear, but he's alive.
136918: He won't know what hit him.
136923: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.
136924: You have done well; the Tash-Murkon family will certainly appreciate your efforts. I shudder to think of the horrors that await Geeral when he is returned to his family.
136925: Don't waste any time! And don't worry: House Tash-Murkon has formally disowned Geeral already, so you'll face no repercussions from them.
136926: I must question your loyalty to the Emperor, or else your bravery. You are not the ship captain I thought you were.
136927:
I have just the thing, never fear.

As you may know, members of the royal families can be... er, marginally eccentric. However, rarely do they prove disloyal to the Empire. The Tash-Murkon family is one of the richest in the galaxy. The kind of wealth they can bring to bear is mind-boggling. One of their scions, an otherwise respectable man named Geeral — he is, in fact, one-hundred and seventy-eighth in line for the throne — has turned traitor.

He has stolen the access codes for some of the family's secret bank accounts and fled toward Gallente space. If he reaches it, the Gallente would be only too willing to drain those funds dry in an effort to throw the entire Amarrian government into chaos. Naturally, we cannot allow this to happen.

We have tracked Geeral Tash-Murkon to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We suspect he is going to meet his Gallentean allies, who will escort him back to Gallente space. Go out there and capture Geeral. Bring him back to me; destroy his allies.

Our naval units managed to ambush an Amarrian strike force and forced them to jump into Republic space. Now, just between you and me, our action was a ploy to pin the incident on the Empire and gain support for our war efforts... but I never told you that, right?

Well, I was against the plan from the beginning, since those blasted religious fanatics always have some kind of trick up their sleeves. In this case, it turns out that their force was simply stronger than our intelligence led us to believe, and we took some serious damage. And now they're loose inside Republic territory.

Personally, I think they were expecting it all along and just used our attack as an excuse to get a raiding force inside our borders. Now we've got a wolf by the ears — a number of enemy ships escorting the carrier Lupus Nivius. They took some losses in the initial battle, but our ships are even worse off and we simply don't have the resources in this sector to stop them.

We're looking for resourceful pilots to fly to the Lupus's last known location and hit it hard before the crew can effect repairs and start raiding. There's a squadron guarding her, so you'll have to take them down too. I'll upload the enemy's location to your Neocom.

I suggest you find some help for this one — they're going to be pretty tough to take down on your own. Can you do it?

137047:
One of the most infamous of Amarrian vessels, the Lupus Nivius is nearly 80 years old, and has participated in many different engagements during its long and varied career. The Lupus has been extensively refitted with advanced technology and high-end weaponry. It has served as a raider par exellence, often leading flotillas of battleships and cruisers on missions deep inside Minmatar and Gallente territory.

The Lupus participated in the bombardment of several planets during the Empire's attempts to reconquer the Khanid Kingdom, and its name is spoken of with hatred and fear in Minmatar space — it is widely believed that the Lupus was responsible for the massacre of several refugee convoys as they attempted to escape from Ammatar space three decades ago.

I'd intended to make a gift of them-- my own new design, very strong-- when I accepted my rightful prize. It seems fitting to use them as the agent of destruction for those too blind to see the brilliance right before their eyes.
