137162: While Caldari society is not what most people would call democratic, the shareholder meeting is one of the few places in the State where a certain type of democracy still exists. Anyone who is a corporate shareholder is welcome to attend a shareholder meeting either in person or virtually and voice their concerns to the corporation's board of directors, whether they own one share or millions. While most small shareholders do not bother to attend and simply proxy their shares to one of the large voting blocs within the corporation (the largest of which is usually the board of directors itself), this has been used on occasion to embarrass corporate officers; those who do so, however, do not generally have long to revel in their triumph.
137164:
So what you're going to be doing is an old fashioned tower-buzz. It's rather simple. I'll give you a series of nine start and end points. Fly between these points. This will take you past the onlookers, giving them a good buzz.

If you have the skills and equipment, you can use a Micro-Warp Drive (MWD) for this. It's not required, but you'll go crazy fast.

Note: You will have to add Large Collidable Objects to your Overview to see these mission specific beacons. The first one will be called Beacon 1.
137165:
So what you're going to be doing is an old fashioned tower-buzz. It's rather simple. I'll give you a series of nine start and end points. Fly between these points. This will take you past the onlookers, giving them a good buzz.

Of course there is no air in space, so the buzz will be simulated with massive subwoofers we've hidden around their seating, but they'll love it.

If you have the skills and equipment, you can use a Micro-Warp Drive (MWD) for this. It's not required, but you'll go crazy fast.

Note: You will have to add Large Collidable Objects to your Overview to see these mission specific beacons. The first one will be called Beacon 1.
137166: The CCA is a division of the Caldari Business Tribunal, which is the only nationwide law enforcement agency in the Caldari State. The CCA is in charge of policing trade at the borders of Caldari space and enforcing any customs duties or tariffs, though the State generally has few of those with both the Liberal and Practical factions both being free trade advocates. However, the CCA tends to be short-staffed, despite being adequately funded, and as a result they often outsource customs duties to the Navy or corporate security forces, who will in turn sometimes subcontract to individual pod-pilots. In general, customs duties are a low priority (and sometimes an obstruction) for many of the Caldari megacorporations' operations, so they tend to be pushed upon pilots and officers towards the low end of the totem pole.
137167: We need you to intercept a possible group of smugglers trying to get out of the State with some military-grade sensor components in secure storage containers. You'll need to fly to the intercept point and wait for our signal. If it's the right ship, we want you to disable the vessel and take possession of the cargo and crew. Bring them back to your agent, and he'll turn them over to the proper authorities.
137169: I've been asked to help the Customs Authority apprehend a group of smugglers trying to get some military-grade sensor components out of the State where they can sell them to the highest bidder. They've sent us a list of possible targets and we've been tracking them; one of the suspect vessels has just entered our jurisdiction. I'd like you to intercept this ship; once you're there, we'll let you know if that's the one we're looking for. If it is, you'll need to disable the vessel, apprehend the crew, and confiscate the sensor components, which are being carried in small secure containers. Can you handle that for me?
137170: Unfortunate. Those smugglers will be selling those sensor components on the black market soon enough, I'm sure. We'll have to find some other way to deal with this.
137171: Excellent. Good hunting out there, {[character]player.name}. Keep an eye out for anyone that might come to their aid; you don't want to be caught in an ambush.
137172: Good work, {[character]player.name}. You handled that admirably; I've got another mission for you, if you're interested. Just let me know when you're ready.
137173: Well, sorry it's not your cup of tea, but someone's got to do it, after all. I'll see if I can't find something more your speed for next time.
137174: I couldn't hold this mission for you any longer, {[character]player.name}; those smugglers were going to get away if we didn't do something and fast. Next time, please let me know if you're going to be able to help or not; we managed to catch them this time, but it won't always work out that way.
137176: Just leave it to me, {[character]agentID.name}. I'll catch those smugglers.
137177: I managed to catch the smugglers and capture their cargo. Had to deal with a few miscreants along the way, though.
137178: I don't really feel like playing the State's meter maid today.
137179: I'm not going to have time to take care of this penny-ante business, {[character]agentID.name}.
137180: I might be. What's the job?
137181: The Cult of the Lash is a splinter sect of the Blood Raiders. The center of their belief is that the amount of pain and suffering in the universe is a constant, and that therefore they must inflict as much pain on others to reduce the amount of suffering visited upon the rest of humanity, especially themselves. Their most frequent victims are captured crews and slaves from their raids upon Amarr colonies, due to their special contempt for the Amarr faith, but they have been expanding their raids into other areas of the cluster. Like the main Blood Raider cult, the Cult of Lash actually has small groups of adherents secreted away in almost every region of the cluster, practicing in secret on kidnapped members of dispossessed classes.
137182: We've been asked by the Customs Authority to intercept a transport ship that has been tracked coming from the Amarr Empire that they believe is carrying a cargo of slaves, which is of course illegal here in the State. They have intelligence that this ship may be linked to a splinter sect of the Blood Raider cults, so you'll need to keep a lookout for trouble when you're trying to apprehend them.
137184: We've been asked by the Customs Authority to intercept a transport ship that has been tracked coming from the Amarr Empire that they believe is carrying a cargo of slaves, which is of course illegal here in the State. They have intelligence that this ship may be linked to a splinter sect of the Blood Raider cults, so you'll need to keep a lookout for trouble when you're trying to apprehend them. Think you can handle this for me?
137185: Great things come from many small deeds. Hopefully someday you'll realize that.
137186: Glad to hear it. I'll see you when you return.
137187: Excellent work. You've helped us smash a dangerous cult of Blood Raiders; against such a dangerous menace, every small victory helps.
137188: Someone has to do it, and not every mission is an easy one. In the future, I hope you'll realize the obligation that we all have to do our small part for the State.
137189: If you aren't going to get back to me, pilot, you give me no choice but to turn to other pilots to take care of my jobs. Thankfully, the pilot I selected for this mission managed to take care of the job with aplomb-- she broke up the Blood Raider cult behind this smuggling operation. Next time, please let me know if you won't be able to take care of the job promptly, instead of letting me hang.
137191: I'll take care of it, no problem.
137192: I've recovered the slave cargo, {[character]agentID.name}, and it looks like the ship did belong to the Blood Raiders. They've been dealt with.
137193: Blood Raiders? I don't think this is really my line of work. I'll pass.
137194: On second thought, I've decided I'm not interested in being the Customs Authority's errand boy.
137196: Despite the death of Dr. Ullia Hnolku at the hands of Caldari paramilitary forces and the capture of all remaining insorum samples by enemies of the State, Zainou Biotech continues to research the process for creating the material at various locations in the Caldari State. Speculation continues as to what their intentions are if they ever manage to replicate the process; some within the Amarr Empire fear the Caldari will use it as a weapon should they have reason to fight the Empire, while the Federation's halls echo with concerns that the Caldari will use it as a counterweight to break the Republic from the grasp of the Gallente. The only sure bet is that the Republic would pay almost any price, in money or blood, to have the secret of insorum creation in its hands.
137197:
A convoy belonging to the Zainou Biotech corporation has broadcast a distress call to all nearby stations, saying they are under attack by unknown hostiles and going down fast. Because the convoy's cargo, chemical components of an insorum prototype, is such a valuable and dangerous one, the CEP itself has given orders for all nearby agents to find ships capable of rescuing the cargo, even if the ships in the convoy are otherwise unsalvageable.

You will need to fly to the last reported location of the convoy, eliminate the attacking vessels, and either escort the convoy to safety or recover the insorum components from the wreckage if it is already too late. It is imperative that this be taken care of as soon as possible; we cannot allow this cargo to fall into the wrong hands.

You will need a Salvager to complete this task.
137199:
We've just received a distress call from a Zainou Biotech transport ship nearby, saying that she was under attack by unknown hostiles and her escort force was failing fast. Unfortunately, most of the nearby vessels are unable to assist and as a result the CEP has ordered everyone in the general vicinity to try and find pod pilots willing to assist the transport before it is too late.

It is critical that they receive that assistance, because that convoy is carrying a large quantity of chemical components for a new synthesis of insorum. No doubt you're aware of how valuable such a thing would be, and how dangerous it would be if it were to fall into the wrong hands. Zainou, and the State, cannot allow such a compound to fall into the hands of terrorists or foreign powers. We need you to fly to the last reported location of this convoy and destroy any attackers; if the convoy is still in serviceable shape, escort it to the nearest safe station, otherwise, recover whatever you can of the insorum synthesis components and bring them back to me immediately. Are you up to it?

You will need a Salvager to complete this task.
137200: Do you understand what you're doing? You're handing over a doomsday weapon to people who have no compunctions against its use! I sincerely hope that you never have cause to look back at this day and realize what a mistake you made, but I fear that time will come all too soon.
137201: Good hunting, pilot. For the sake of the State and its citizens, I hope you do not fail.
137202: Minmatar terrorists, eh? We should have known. You have performed a great service for the Caldari State. You've earned your reward ten times over today. Enjoy it while you can.
137203: Perhaps it's for the best. After all, it would be better to place something of such import in the hands of someone more responsible.
137204: You've failed both me and the Caldari State. Your failure to recover the insorum prototype components has as good as handed them over to Minmatar extremists, and who knows what those primitives will do? I hope you can sleep at night with that resting on your conscience, pilot.
137205: I'm afraid this mission was far too important to let sit any longer. Thankfully, you're not the only pod pilot in the service of the State, and one of them was able to take care of the problem, keeping this valuable cargo from falling into the hands of Minmatar extremists. Next time, I hope you will heed the call and come to the aid of the State promptly, instead of neglecting your obligations.
137207: Insorum convoy rescued by loyalist pilot
137208: I won't let something so dangerous fall into enemy hands, I swear.
137209: The convoy was destroyed by Minmatar terrorists, {[character]agentID.name}, but I was able to recover the insorum components.
137210: I don't have time to take on this sort of responsibility right now, {[character]agentID.name}.
137211: I can't take care of this right now; you'll have to find someone else. Or not; I don't really care.
137212: I'll certainly try, kirjuun. What can I do to serve the State today?
137213:
There are a number of treaties that regulate the way in which the various nations of the cluster are supposed to relate to each other and what behaviors are and are not acceptable for them to take against one another. In reality, every nation subverts these same treaties by engaging in a number of questionable practices, perpetuating a state of cold war where men and women on both sides fight and die while the two sides pretend to make nice with one another.

Perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than between the Caldari State and the Gallente Federation. While Caldari megacorporations have made a science of public relations and marketing, and the Federation has carefully cultivated a sympathetic image since the end of the Yulai Convention, beneath the polite veneer of both nations, knives flash in the dark. For the State, this shadow war is not about dominance or revenge, but fear. For all their seeming arrogance, the Caldari are deathly afraid that the Federation is only waiting for a moment of vulnerability before they can begin the process of re-assimilating the State into their nation, something which many Caldari already see them doing to the Republic. Often, this war gets the most bloody when the Gallente make what look like altruistic gestures, as the Caldari tend to interpret this as an attempt to get them to drop their guard in preparation for some sort of attack.
137214: In order to prevent a number of Gallente corporations from appropriately countering a move by Sukuuvesta, we need to eliminate a Gallente listening post which is providing intelligence to those corporations. You and any pilots accompanying you are to fly to the listening post in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and destroy it. There will very likely be a strong Federation defense fleet stationed there, but the destruction of that fleet is not required. The listening post is your top priority.
137216:
Recently, the Sukuuvesta corporation has been planning a major operation in a number of systems along the Gallente border, an operation which would be, shall we say, detrimental to the market share of a number of Gallente corporations. Unfortunately, these corporations are also politically well-connected, and we know that they have extensive connections within the Federation intelligence community. They've used these connections to get a Federation listening post to focus its attention on the very systems Sukuuvesta is planning their operation in, and as a result if Sukuuvesta makes a move, they will have enough forewarning to counter it, costing the megacorporation and the State billions.

The listening post attached to this particular region of space is in a rather precarious position; technically, according to the Gallente government, it is actually a civilian data archive and not at all related to the Federation intelligence apparatus. Furthermore, acting on behalf of the Gallente corporations, unlike in the State, is actually a violation of Gallente law. This means that were it to suffer an “accident” at the hands of someone not specifically affiliated with the State, there would be little the Federation could do in response. Hopefully, you can be that someone for us.
137217: I hope you know what you're doing. It isn't wise to anger one of the megacorps, and you've just endangered billions of Sukuuvesta investment dollars. I'd watch my back if I were you.
137218: Excellent. I'll send word that you're on the case; let me know as soon as you've finished taking care of the listening post.
137219: Perfect; I'll inform Sukuuvesta at once. They'll be indebted to us – and you – for a long time to come.
137220: Very well, I suppose this sort of job isn't for everyone. I'll have to find something more suited to your talents.
137221: You waited far too long to get this done, and Sukuuvesta was forced to go ahead with their plans. Unfortunately, exactly what we expected happened, and their acquisition was blocked-- thanks to some rather “prescient” financial maneuvering. You've cost them a great deal. I'd watch my back if I were you.
137222: I never heard back from you, so I was forced to find someone else to take care of this problem. Time, tide, and megacorps wait for no man. Next time, do us both a favor and give me an answer so that we don't waste this time again.
137223: Sukuuvesta acquistion blocked by Gallente coalition
137225: A chance to collect interest on a debt they've owed us for a century? I'll gladly help any way I can, kirjuun.
137226: The Gallente listening post has been destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}.
137227: I don't particularly feel like wading into the middle of an international incident right now.
137228: This is crazy-- what were you thinking? I can't possibly fight all those ships!
137229: I am ready to do my duty, kirjuun. How can I serve the State today?
137230:
An enemy cruiser squadron has been causing some serious trouble for our forces in this area. Unfortunately, we're also trying to deal with an Amarr offensive in this sector, and that means that regular naval forces are stretched thin. In order to take some pressure off, we need you to take out the tactical relay that they are using to coordinate their activities. Hopefully, that will buy our fleet some time to deal with the offensive.

Fly to the given coordinates, find and eliminate the tactical relay, and return to your agent.
137231: Bla Bla Ambush the enemy convoy
137232:
Those damn Amarr have managed to discover an asteroid belt in one of the contested systems nearby! Head over there and destroy them as soon as possible. Once you do, we can exploit the resources ourselves.

Just make sure you're ready to fight. Capsuleers loyal to the Empire might be out in force.
137233: We've been watching Imperial Navy units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Matari; most of them non-combatants I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.
137234: I hear you might have some work for me...
137235:
I don't know how to tell you this. Here goes: I quit your mission.

Heh, I guess I do know how to tell you.
137236: I don't know if I'll be able to take this mission. Find someone else.
137237: I've brought in your snitch. The Serpentis shouldn't suspect a thing.
137238: Don't worry. I can handle this.
137241: Waiting is not an option. Because of this, I've had to assign the job to another pilot. Come back when you're ready to actually work.
137242: The informant grew nervous waiting around for you to come extract him. Because of that, it looks like we've lost an opportunity to gain valuable information about our enemies. I am disappointed in your failure.
137243: You should not refuse missions so lightly.
137244: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}! Without your help, we may never have been able to extract the informant from the Serpentis. They do not like traitors and, if they found out, he'd have met an ugly death.
137245: I knew I could count on you. Just be sure you make the fight look real. If not, Serpentis will suspect something. And his associates will be trying to kill you for real anyway.
137246: You can't even beat someone who wants to lose? Hmph, what are we going to do with you?
137247:
As you well know, the Serpentis are notorious pirates across the galaxy. They are particularly troublesome here, pushing their drugs and committing all sorts of crimes against the Federation. Every so often, though, one of them finds a conscience and decides to change his criminal ways.

It just so happens that a Serpentis captain is ready to turn himself in. Of course, he can't just dock in one of our stations and surrender: He'd be dead before he exited warp. Now, that wouldn't be a big deal, normally, but this one has information that can help bring down several higher ranking Serpentis members.

We've agreed to send someone over there for a show for this captain's friends, someone to fight with him and destroy his ship. He'll have already ejected of course and made his way to your cargo hold. Are you up to it?
137248: A Serpentis captain wants to surrender to us and help right his wrongs. He's currently hiding out in a small deadspace pocket with some other Serpentis watching him. Get over there, make a show of wiping him and his followers out, and then bring him back to us unharmed.
137250: I've decided I had enough of this. I quit.
137251: Come back to me when you've got something interesting.
137252: I've picked up the parts, as you asked.
137253: That sounds simple enough. Sure, I can do it.
137256: Yes or no, that's all we needed. Instead, you made us wait. I can't stand indecision.
137257: The Mannar are nothing if not patient! But they can't wait for those parts to be repaired any longer. I've had to send someone else in with new equipment.
137258: Your lack of willingness is disheartening.
137259: I hope those rogue drones weren't too much trouble? I doubted they'd be much of a match for you.
137260: I knew you'd be up for it. Careful out there.
137261: I was hoping I wouldn't have to waste our resources to deliver new parts, but I guess I will now.
137262:
This one should be pretty simple. Near here is a mining colony owned and run by some Mannar workers. Usually, they keep things pretty solid. We even have a deal with them where we protect them and supply them with parts in exchange for a cheap supply of minerals. It all works out fine.

Recently, though, they've had some problems with rogue drones, and some of their equipment was damaged. Trouble is, we're in the middle of arming to protect against the Caldari threat, so we can't wait for them to fix their machines. Instead, I've been authorized to have their tools repaired.

You'll have to fly out to their base and pick up the tools. It shouldn't be much of a problem, though you might encounter some rogue drones or a few pirates, maybe. So you'd better go in armed.
137263:
A Mannar mining colony has recently been attacked by rogue drones. Unfortunately, this mining colony supplies us with a good deal of cheap minerals we use for our defense initiatives. We can't wait for them to repair the damage done by the drones, so we've decided to fix their equipment for them, free of charge. The sooner we can get them back to work, the better.

All you need to do is pick up the parts from their mining colony and bring them back here. Good luck!
137264: Oh, sorry 'bout that. Listen – I'm just here for some work. I hear you might have something?
137265: Sorry to disappoint, {[character]player.name}, but I don't see this job working out for me the way I'd prefer — you know, like me surviving it. Find yourself another hero. One with less foresight.
137266: So you've already lost two teams of your employees to some mysterious fate… and you want me to join them?! Do I have "IDIOT" written on my forehead? No thanks, {[character]agentID.name}.
137267: Your mining crew ran into a slave-raiding party. Those scum won't be slave raiding anymore, though — or breathing, for that matter. Here's your crew; now hand over the LUX!
137268: I do love the ominous, dangerous-sounding jobs. I'll do it, {[character]agentID.name}.
137271: {[character]player.name} — since replying to potential employers is so low on your priority list, I've gone and hired someone else for the job we discussed. I hope you find the time in your busy schedule to read this message.
137272: Not that you probably care, {[character]player.name}, but thanks to your inability to do the job, those miners are probably dead now. Or worse. Have a nice night!
137273: Well, I'm sorry the job sounds too dangerous for you, {[character]player.name}. If I get any jobs that involve ice cream and lollipops, should I give you a call?
137274: Oh, wonderfully done, {[character]player.name}! Those miner implants are safe and sound! You've done {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} a great service, one we probably won't forget.
137275: Oh, thank you. You know, if you can bring back those miners in a hurry, I could maybe slap a bonus on your fee. So get moving!
137276: I'm not disappointed, {[character]player.name}. I actually had a bet going that you would quit. Thanks for letting me win!
137277:
Yes, that's true. You're {[character]player.name}, right? So many new capsuleers these days – hard to keep them all straight. My apologies.

Anyway, listen: We recently lost contact with a small group of miners at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Outside of the miners' distress beacon being activated, we've heard nothing from them for two days. Just... silence.

Normally, we'd just hire new crews. But we spent a fortune on implants for those miners, and we're not ready to write those off. So would you please go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and see what's what?

Whatever the case, you'll need to bring those miners back here for examination and questioning.
137279: Investigate the distress beacon at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and rescue the lost miners.
137280:
It never fails to amuse the more cynical in New Eden that the Amarr — with all their holier than thou piety — see nothing wrong with their use of slaves. Still, this darker side of the Amarrian faith, while upsetting to many, never fails to generate the gleam of potential profits for those willing to provide such slaves.

The Angel Cartel — arguably the strongest criminal organization plaguing the star lanes today — has not let this business opportunity go amiss. Yet it is a matter even the Cartel handles delicately, since it has no wish to openly provoke the Minmatar Empire or its Gallente allies. Still, if a few Minmatar ships go missing, who would notice? The blackness of space promises many dangers to the unwary, and much LUX to those who happen to be in the right place at the right time (with the right weapons...).
137281: Mission accomplished. The communications platform is so much space dust.
137282: I hope I can find someone else to handle this on such short notice.
137283: Excellent. The Emperor will be pleased. Fear not, only the Amarrian government will know of your involvement in this enterprise.
137285: I guess I'll have to find someone with a little stronger loyalty to the Empire.
137289: We've learned that an Amarrian agent has infiltrated our ranks and has been actively working against us ever since. Maybe we spooked him, or perhaps the timing is just a coincidence, but he's been spotted in a nearby contested sector organizing a small squadron of troops to undoubtedly strike at our weakest points. Whether he knows we're on to him or not is irrelevant now; dead spies pose no threat, understood?
137290:
The Amarr are resupplying one of their relay stations in a nearby contested system-- it's due to run out soon and the convoy dispatched to resupply it hasn't arrived yet. Your job is to intercept the convoy and destroy the industrials before they have a chance to complete their mission.

The mission shouldn't be too difficult, as long as you don't encounter any pod pilots fighting for the Amarr. You should fit your ship to defend itself from other pod pilots just in case.
137291:
I'm glad you're here, pilot. It's come to my attention that the Amarr have a relay station in a nearby contested system. The station is being used to send monitor classified Republic transmissions and then transmit them back to Amarr space, where their code-breakers can get to work figuring out what we mean. So far, we haven't had an opportunity to strike at it, and it's unlikely we'll get one soon.

However, we've received intelligence that the Amarr have dispatched a convoy to refuel the station. If we can destroy that convoy, we'll hamper their spying operations for at least a little while.
137292: That relay station is causing serious problems for us. I'll have to get someone else to stop them.
137293: I knew you would be up for it, pilot. The convoy is lightly guarded and the only important targets are their industrials. Once you destroy them, you can get out of there or mop up as needed. Just remember, because the system is contested, pod pilots working for the Amarr may try to stop you. Be sure that your ship is set up to counter them as well.
137294: Good work. I knew I could count on you. With that relay station out of commission, our local transmissions will be harder for the Amarr to intercept, at least until they manage to sneak another convoy in there.
137295: Is destroying a few industrials really that difficult? I suppose I'll have to find someone else to complete this mission for me.
137296: Blowing up some supply industrials? Sounds easy enough.
137297: That station won't be seeing new supplies any time soon.
137299: I have to abandon your mission.

The mission shouldn't be too difficult, as long as you don't encounter any pod pilots fighting for the Caldari. You should fit your ship to defend itself from other pod pilots just in case.

I'm glad you're here, pilot. It's come to my attention that the Caldari have a relay station in a nearby contested system. So far, we haven't had an opportunity to strike at it directly, and it's unlikely we'll get one soon.

However, we've received intelligence that the Caldari have dispatched a convoy to resupply the station. If we can destroy that convoy, we'll hamper their spying operations for at least a short period of time.

137333:
Amarr forces in this sector have been taking heavy losses from enemy hit and run attacks on our fleets, damaging morale and stalling our offensives. Naval Intelligence believes that these attacks are being masterminded by the local Minmatar sector commander, and has determined that our best option for ending these attacks is to eliminate him.

We have located a staging point that the sector commander is using for his attacks. You need to fly to these coordinates and wait for the commander and his escort to arrive, then eliminate him. Be aware that you may need to engage multiple groups of enemy forces while waiting, so be prepared for a protracted battle. Return to your agent when the sector commander has been destroyed.
137334:
We've been taking some heavy losses in the last few weeks along this area of the front. An enemy frigate squadron has been hitting our ships hard, taking out stragglers and scouts and then fading into space before we can counterattack, and it's starting to take its toll not only on our physical resources but an even heavier one on our morale. Our captains are getting too cautious, too unwilling to push for gains, and our general staff is getting concerned that the front will be stalled because of this. This is unacceptable.

Naval Intelligence believes that the person behind these attacks is the local Minmatar sector commander. Eliminating him will hopefully end these attacks, give our forces a morale boost, and shift the momentum in this sector back to our side. Because of our problems with morale, we aren't sure that regular naval forces can handle this job; we'd like you to deal with this problem for us.

We've located a rendezvous point that this commander is going to be using for staging his next series of raids. You will need to fly there, eliminate his ship, and then report in. There will likely be a significant enemy presence there aside from the sector commander and his direct escort, so be prepared for a protracted battle.
137335: Excellent. I'll be looking forward to hearing from you. Remember, this commander is an expert at surprise attacks, so don't let him sneak up on you.
137336: Great work, pilot. We'll make sure that word of your victory is spread to the rest of our forces; that will help morale more than you can realize.

The Gallente Federation is trying to set up a starbase inside one of the contested systems. If they manage to get it up and running, they'll have a staging point from which to launch further attacks against us. Luckily, it is not yet fully operational and has a highly explosive reactor that is just waiting to be destroyed.

I've uploaded the location of the starbase to your NeoCom. Head over there and destroy the reactor. Just watch out for the pod pilots working for the Federation. They will try to stop you if they can.
137610:
Those damn Gallente. Always up to something sneaky. Thankfully we've enough spies in their midst to keep them from pulling off anything too big. One of those spies just reported that the Federation is trying to construct a starbase inside a nearby contested system.

A fully functioning starbase can cause us a huge headache. They're tough and require a lot of manpower to destroy. Because of our spies we have a first strike advantage. The starbase hasn't been completed yet, and the idiot Gallente have filled their main reactor full of fuel.

If you head over there and destroy the reactor, the entire starbase will blow. Do you think you can do this for me?

137614: Don't you think you can handle this?

137687: An old smuggler's gate connects a system deep inside Republic territory with one of the contested systems nearby. It's been offline for years, but the Republic is trying to get it running again. Destroy the repair ships trying to repair the gate.
137688:
Our contested territory is riddled with old, inoperable gates. Some of them were put up by our enemies, others by common smugglers hoping to get past customs. Well, it turns out that the Republic has discovered one of these derelict gates. Normally, this wouldn't be an issue, but the gate connects to a system deep in Republic space.

I don't need to tell you what could happen if those Minmatar slave dogs get that gate online. We can't spare the manpower to destroy the gate itself, but the ships working to repair it aren't nearly so sturdy.

I want you to fly over there and take them out. Are you up for it?
137689: Grr. I wish I'd known you couldn't handle it from the start!

Optimally, we'd like to get a better idea of Minmatar positions, communications codes, fleet readiness and their own intelligence estimates of our disposition, but they've been working hard to keep us from getting our hands on anything more than a vague picture.

We've decided to try a bit of an end-run around their counterintelligence screen. We know where they have a secure datastore in an area of deadspace. We don't know where they are headed or what they're up to, but we definitely want to find out. I request that you intercept the transport and capture the men on board. Bring them back to us for questioning.

We believe the escort team is split up into a few groups. If you strike fast and hard, you'll probably avoid getting swarmed by them all at once. Just keep a look out for any stray ships; we don't want them escaping back to their home base to report the incident.
138896:
Because of the importance placed on "saving face" in Caldari culture, mid- and high-level executives often remain employed despite failures in leadership or performance, simply because firing them publicly would damage the corporation's reputation. In extreme cases, it is not altogether unknown for superiors within the corporation to arrange "accidents" for executives who fail to meet objectives and threaten their employer's bottom line. This eliminates the drain on corporate resources and allows them to save face.

While such methods of dealing with "problem employees" are simply not discussed openly (doing so would be in horribly poor taste, after all), it is something that lurks in the back of every corporate executive's mind.
138897:
Boosters are made by processing chemicals extracted from special gas clouds that can be found in certain deadspace areas in many regions. Some constellations, such as E-8CSQ, 09-4XW, 9HXQ-G, OK-FEM, Pegasus, Assilot, I-3ODK, and 760-9C, however, are rumored to have massive clouds of a scale not seen anywhere else. Finding these clouds requires the ability to conduct long-range scanning, for example via scan probes. Finding them is not always an easy task, though; it sometimes requires quite a bit of exploration.

The downside of searching for these clouds is the fact that they are generally located in dangerous pirate-infested space. Few if any of these clouds exist in civilized space, having been depleted long ago by the mega-corporations. Hence, searching for them can be quite risky and is not recommended for any but the most experienced combat pilots.

To extract the chemicals from the gas clouds, you need a gas cloud harvester module. You also need to find the correct type of gas cloud. Not all clouds have chemicals that the gas cloud harvester can extract, and therefore you might have to go through some trial and error at first before you get the hang of gas cloud harvesting.

Today, most boosters are very much illegal in civilized space, due to the horrible side-effects experienced by users during the Great Booster Craze many decades ago. Manufacturing them must therefore be done in lawless space, outside the spheres of power of the major civilized factions. Similarly, anyone caught smuggling illegal boosters into civilized space can face very steep penalties.

Manufacturing boosters can broken into a few phases. Phase 1 involves extracting the material from the gas cloud. Phase 2 requires a refinery structure with the appropriate service module to process the chemicals and create reactions. Phase 3 also requires a structure or station with the equipment for booster manufacturing to process the reaction and create the booster. This simple 3-step process will result in the creation of a fairly common booster. With additional work, the right blueprint, and a combination of several low-quality boosters, one can create higher-quality versions.
138898: The advent of the Starbase has seen vast changes in the nature of entrenched, long-term warfare. The tactics of battlefield logistics had to be almost entirely reinvented when forces suddenly had the capability to restock and reship inside hostile space. This process is ongoing even today, as empires discover new ways to utilize the potent abilities afforded by these structures.
138899: We've recently had to deal with some rather resilient Caldari forces in a nearby contested sector. It seemed like every hard-earned victory counted for nothing; they would simply retreat, regroup and repair. We knew they had to have a Starbase somewhere to do this as effectively as they were. That Starbase has now been found. You simply need to destroy the Main Reactor powering the shields. From there we can send in a team to clear the rest out.

138937: We've been watching Federation Navy units piling into a contested sector nearby. We were moments away from moving on them until we noticed one of their more highly-ranked Field Commanders arriving on the scene. This woman has killed countless Caldari; most of them non-combatants I no longer give a damn about anything except that Commander and her guards. Kill them and you'll get your pay, maybe even some respect.
138938:
I knew you would be up for it. The convoy guards should not pose a significant challenge to you. And besides, the only real targets are the industrials carrying the ground troops. Destroy them and you can avoid fighting the other ships, unless you want to.

The main threat to your mission will be capsuleers supporting the Federation.
138939: Excellent. Without supplies, the Caldari forces in the area will lose morale and fight at less than 100 percent! It'll allow us to make inroads into the system.
138940:
The Minmatar Republic has located numerous hidden asteroid belts that our miners use to provide resources for the war effort. Usually, they don't get touched by anyone except us and the people we send out there... even if they're not technically in Republic space. However, it seems the Amarr Empire has sent some miners into one of our fields in an area of space they consider theirs; while we've been busy with other things, they've been sneaking in and mining our ore!

This is unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners and show them that we're always watching. Just prepare yourself for any pod pilots working for the Amarr. They're sure to be in the area.
138941:
Amarr has located numerous hidden asteroid belts that we mine for the betterment of the Empire. Usually, these locations are known only to us... even if they're not technically in our sovereign space. However, it seems the Minmatar have sent some miners into one of our fields in an area of space they consider "theirs"; while we've been busy with other things, they've been sneaking in and mining our ore!

This situation is unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners and show them that the Empire is always watching. Just prepare yourself for any pod pilots working for the Matari scum: They're sure to be in the area.
138942:
The State has numerous asteroid belts secreted away, from which our miners provide resources for the war effort. Usually, these sites don't get touched by anyone except us and the companies we contract out to mine them. However, it seems the Gallente have recently sent some miners in to steal our asteroids. This is unacceptable.

I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom. I want you to go out there and destroy those miners; show them that we're always vigilant. Just be ready for any Federation-sponsored pod pilots: They've been reported in the area.
138943:
The Federation has located numerous asteroid belts hidden away all over charted space. Usually, these sites are so out of the way that they're rarely found, let alone touched by anyone except us. But it seems the Caldari State has found one of them and sent some miners in to steal those asteroids: Those capitalist pigs have been sneaking in and mining our ore!

As you can see, this situation is entirely unacceptable. I've uploaded the location of the belt to your NeoCom -- I want you to go out there and destroy those miners. Show them that the Federation will not tolerate such acts. Just be wary of any pod pilots working for the State. They'll almost certainly attack you on sight.
138944:
Uncountable numbers of hidden asteroid belts dot all of known space; some of them are quite valuable -- so much that both we and our enemies would risk going into contested space to find and exploit them. The Minmatar have recently sent miners into a rich field we discovered some time ago -- in a region of "contested space" -- and we certainly can't have them taking our ore.

If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves. Can you do it?
138945:
Our scanners haven't revealed any combat ships escorting the miners. That could be simple hubris on the part of the Gallente, or it could mean they've reinforcements a short way away. The miners are the only important targets, so focus on them.

Just be careful, as I said earlier -- capsuleers loyal to the Federation are in the area.
138946:
It's no secret that many hidden asteroid belts dot all of known space. Some of them are so valuable that our people would risk going into contested space to find and exploit them. Well, we've recently done just that -- we discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt. In Gallente-contested space...

Trouble is, the Gallente seem to have noticed. But we simply can't let them take it: If you can drive them out of there, we'll send in a special ops mining force and have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves. Can you do it?
138947:
Our scanners haven't revealed any combat ships escorting the miners. That could be simple hubris on the part of the Caldari, or it could mean they've reinforcements a short way away. The miners are the only important targets, so focus on them.

138948:
Those damn Caldari have managed to discover an asteroid belt we had claimed in one of the contested systems nearby! Head over there and destroy them as soon as possible. Once you do, we can exploit the resources ourselves.

Just make sure you're ready to fight. Capsuleers loyal to the State might be out in force.
138949:
As you know, there are a large number of hidden asteroid belts all throughout space. Some of them are quite valuable, so much that both we and our enemies would risk going into contested space to find them. Well, we've recently done just that... but the Caldari have apparently spotted our ships in the vicinity.

We discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt that had managed to elude our scanners for some time. Now that the Caldari have also pinpointed it, though, we need to get in there fast. We simply can't let them strip it of all value. We want to be the ones to do that. If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious mineral resources all to ourselves -- and keep their war-mongering fingers away from it. Can you do it?
138950:

Just be careful out there, like I said.
138951:
It's no secret that a large number of hidden asteroid belts dot all parts of space, including the Republic -- and Amarr. Some of them are quite valuable, so much that we would most certainly risk going into Amarr space to procure them. Well, our scouts recently found just such a field in Amarr-contested space.

They've discovered a fairly sizable asteroid belt. Now that we've pinpointed it, though, the Amarr seem to have noticed our activities there... and we simply can't let them strip the site of all those resources. If you can drive them out of there, we'll have those precious minerals all to ourselves. Can you do it?
138953: Miners in a combat zone? Don't they know what could happen to them? They should see it coming!
138954: It looks like the State likes to send its citizens into dangerous territory to mine. Well, their stupidity is to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, capsuleers loyal to the State are in the area; they might prove difficult.
138955: I can just imagine those miners cursing the commander who sent them into hostile territory for some ore. Just before you sent them to a fiery demise, of course.
138956:
Good news, follower! We've just discovered the State doing something incredibly foolish! It turns out they've been sending miners into a contested system for ore. The impudence! Did they think they could do this with impunity!? I hope they're ready to pay for their folly.

I want you to be the one to make them pay. Our normal forces are occupied with other objectives. I'd like you to head over there and take out those miners. It will deny the Caldari a large amount of precious mineral resources. What do you say?
138957: Miners in a combat zone? How can they be so stupid?!
138958: It seems the Federation likes to send its citizens into hostile territory to mine. Ah, well. Their mistake. And to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, capsuleers loyal to the Federation are likely to be in the area, and they might prove more difficult.
138959: The Empire has made a mistake. A really dumb one: They've sent miners out into hostile territory for ore. What's their stupidity is to our benefit. Just head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you. However, some Amarrian capsuleers have been spotted in the area, so be ready for a firefight.
138960:
Good news, follower! We've just discovered the Empire doing something incredibly foolish! It turns out they've been sending in miners to a contested system near their sovereign space. I hope they're ready to pay for their folly.

I want you to be the one to make them pay. Our normal forces are occupied with other objectives: I'd like you to head over there and take out those miners. Not only will it deny Amarr a large amount of precious mineral resources, it will also sting their sickening pride. What do you say?
138961: The Republic has sent workers into hostile territory to mine asteroids. Well, their foolish overconfidence is to our benefit. All you have to do is head over there and blow up the mining vessels, then report back to us. The miners and any escort they have should pose no problem to you; however, the Republic capsuleers in the area might prove difficult. Be ready.
138963: I hope it wasn't too much trouble for you. With that repair crew out of the way, we can take our time and send a demolition crew to destroy it when we get the chance. You have done the State proud.
138964:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} surveillance spotted a small team of Thukker mercenaries in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, probably up to no good. They're wanted men, and need to be taken care of. I would ask you to bring them in for trial but that really isn't necessary, the exception being their captain. I want him taken alive and brought to me. We'd like to figure out exactly what they've been up to.

Your objectives in this mission are not as simple as they sound, however. We haven't been able to locate their captain's hideout yet. but we expect him to show up if you warp to some of his minions who are holed up in a small asteroid belt in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. So I suggest you destroy the first group of mercenaries you encounter as fast as you can, before more reinforcements arrive, or you'll have a heck of a battle on your hands.

138968:
Moments ago we launched an offensive against a Caldari compound inside a hostile sector where they have strong numbers and superior logistics support.

Initial reconnaissance has suggested they may have the capability to field more vessels than we had originally anticipated. Naturally, we're not turning around in the face of this news, we've come too far and a retreat will only encourage them. We're not going to risk getting slaughtered however, and this is where you come in.

I want you to fly over there and ensure the success of this operation. I'll personally relay further information to you once you've made it onto the field. Don't worry about any orders or cohesion with our own forces there, you'll be answering directly to me and following only my orders.

Briefing over. Get going.
138969:
We've learned that the remaining Athrans pulled out as soon as you left your last mission. Fortunately, one of our recon pilots was able to trail them to another location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

{[character]player.name}, head out there and find out what's going on. See what these Athrans are up to, and report any suspicious activity back to me. And if they open fire on you again, you're fully authorized to shoot back. Don't take any chances.
138970:
Today is a day of mourning, {[character]player.name}. One of our most esteemed officers was brutally murdered by Sansha scum. He had been in the forefront of our campaign to rid {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} space of those filthy pirate dogs, and now he is dead. We will miss his services to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} greatly, and I hope to see you at his funeral, {[character]player.name}.

Now to the point. This great injustice demands retribution, and you will be the deliverer of our wrath. We know of a Sansha Outpost lurking in the fringes of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and you are to find it and destroy it. I'll supply you with a bookmark that should take you to an acceleration gate leading to it. Once there, your task is to completely obliterate their base. However be warned, their outpost is heavily guarded, I suggest you clear the guards before attempting to destroy the Outpost structure itself. Good luck.

The easiest way to travel to a destination station quickly is to use the Overview. Stargates are marked in the Overview settings panel under the "Celestial" group. Once you have selected "stargate" in the Overview settings, right-click on the hyperlinked destination system in your mission journal and choose "set destination." You will notice that the applicable stargate in your Overview is now yellow, as well as the one in space that leads to the next system along your route.

Next, simply right-click on the yellow stargate in the Overview (or in space) and hit "warp to within 0m"; turn on your Autopilot and simply sit back and relax until you are in the destination system.

Once you have arrived in the correct star system, simply right-click anywhere in space. In the drop-down window that appears, your current mission information appears at the bottom. From there, select the "dock" option and your Autopilot will bring you into the station momentarily.

Once the weapons are delivered, return to your agent's home station (also available via the drop-down simply by right-clicking anywhere in space) to collect your reward.
138981:
Quafe has been secretly developing a new soft drink called Quafe Unleashed that they say will revolutionize the entire soft drink industry. But only hours ago, the formula was stolen. Security records show that a Quafe employee, a guy called Quince Nemirda, has just left the station with the top-secret formula in his possession. Quafe representatives believe that he might be on his way to try to sell or deliver the formula to one of Quafe's competitors, and have offered a reward for the recovery of the formula.

We were able to track him for a while, and we've just heard that he's now in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. I‘ll upload the coordinates to your NeoCom. Stop him before he meets his contact, and bring back the formula.

We're not expecting you to go to war for this, but you should be prepared to meet some rough customers.

138987: The Darkonnen is an organization that sprung up from rogue elements within the Khanid Kingdom, starting off as a small band of smugglers operating between lawless space and Khanid-controlled territory. They were renowned for their ruthlessness in dealing with their competitors, eliminating a good deal of small-time criminals within the Kingdom, as well as cleverly eluding the local authorities most of the time. A few years ago, their founder and leader, Michelin Adonnis, was captured by Khanid secret police and sentenced to life in prison for various offenses. His arrest caused a slight setback for the outlawed organization, but in the end it turned out to be not enough to halt their inevitable expansion. Today they are a well known pirate/smuggler network who base their operations in numerous systems in Amarr and Khanid space.
138988:
The freighter Bright Prospect struck an asteroid when emerging from warp in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The jump drive was badly damaged and they thought it might blow, but they managed to make it back in one piece. However, among the cargo, which was mostly expendable, was a set of important Ishukone corporate records; they were forced to jettison the records lest they be lost if the ship's warp core blew. We don't have backups, so the records are irreplaceable.

We need someone to get out there and recover those records. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, as well as my gratitude.

I've uploaded the location of the Bright Prospect's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and bring them back to me here.

We need someone to get out there and recover those records. I've uploaded the location of the Bright Prospect's cargo dump into your onboard computer. It should appear in your bookmarks. Once you've located the records, place them in your cargo hold and bring them back to me here. There's a reward in it for you if you succeed, of course, as well as my gratitude.

The Caldari State is building up its ground troops in a nearby contested system with plans to launch an attack on our fortified positions.

We've discovered a troop transport moving toward their command outpost. You need merely destroy the industrials and don't need to bother with the convoy guards.
138997:
In a nearby contested system, the Caldari State has long held illusions of claiming it entirely for themselves. Now, we've always been able to stop them, but lately they've started moving ground troops into their command outpost there.

We cannot attack the command outpost directly. It's too well guarded and our forces are kept occupied in other areas. However, if they manage to get enough ground troops there, they can launch an attack on our planetary holdings.

Our scanners have picked up a lightly guarded convoy filled with troops heading toward the command outpost. You can take them out, no sweat, right?
138998:
What I am about to ask you is strictly confidential, understood?

We've come across a civilian facility inside a nearby sector where the State's presence is strong. This compound has become a home away from home for thousands of their citizens, the majority of whom are families of the soldiers and commanders serving abroad – that is, who are killing our own Gallente people.

Their arrogance is astounding, no? They seem to think we will allow them to exist in peace simply because they bear no weapons. Their weak security presence suggests as much. Understand pilot; these people are as significant a threat as any other. What they provide may not be firepower or logistics but it is crucial to their war effort nonetheless. These people are here to boost the morale of their forces; this is something that cannot be allowed to continue.

We've found they have one major weakness: their supply line. The colony is completely dependent on regular shipments from Industrials. If you can intercept and destroy these Industrials, we can starve the enemy out.

I have terrible news, {[character]player.name}. A major personnel convoy carrying countless {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} members was completely obliterated by Guristas ships, led by that damned commander of theirs, Rachen Mysuna. His reputation as a brutal Guristas military leader has traveled far and wide these past few years, and it's time to put an end to his miserable existence.

I want you to be the bringer of our vengeance, {[character]player.name}. Strike him down like the dog he is. When his battleship has been turned to dust, then you shall receive your reward.
139011: Some of our explorers have just located a hidden asteroid belt that is apparently full of rare ore — here in local space. That's more than a little suspicious. The signature the belt is giving off is obvious enough that it seems nearly impossible it hasn't been found and mined out before now. We're afraid it might be a trap of some sort. We want you to warp over there and check it out, then report back.
139012:
Yes, I certainly do have something for you. Recently, some explorers employed by {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} discovered an extremely strong gravimetric signature. Their scanners indicated the hidden belt was full of rare ore. Now, while this news would normally be cause for joy, I'm suspicious.

I'd like you to fly over to the belt and check it out. If it really is full of ore-- wonderful. If not, get back to me with the news as quickly as possible.
139013: I should have known better than to trust you.
139014: Excellent. Remember, we have no idea who might be there waiting for you. So be ready for anything.
139015: I've never heard of them setting ambushes before. That is disturbing news.
139016: I can understand your nervousness, I suppose. I'll have to find someone else.
139017: Is the prospect of springing a trap really that unnerving? I'm afraid I can't wait for your courage to show up.
139018: You still haven't answered me about the mission. I'm assuming that means "no", so I'll find someone else.
139022: Looks like rogue drones staged this ambush.
139023: You want me to walk into a trap on purpose? No, thanks-- find some other patsy.
139024: The prospect of walking into a trap doesn't appeal to me. I'm quitting your mission.
139025: I know, I'm awesome. Anyway, you got anything to do?
139026:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets a number of years ago -- some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by then-President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.
139027: Good. Here are the coordinates for the transmitter; remember, you must destroy it and any vessels that would defend it, but it isn't necessary to engage the Republic Navy ships. Get out if you have to.
139028: Because you couldn't take out the Brothers of Freedom transmitter, some soft-headed fools at one of our border mining colonies seem to have taken their “sermons” to heart and, in the wake of Heth's recent successes, have begun a wildcat strike, setting back production and causing a number of injuries and even a few deaths. I hope you realize what your failure here cost us, {[character]player.name}.
139029: You said I should come back, remember?
139030: Well, I must say — you are not the fearless captain I had thought you were.
139031: Nice work.  I'll keep you in mind when something else comes up.
139032: I hope I can find someone else to handle this.
139033: I'll raze the outpost until nothing is left but fiery debris.
139034: I destroyed it all. Those Gallente won't be getting any more of that Arkonor anytime soon.
139035: Listen, I've got enough to worry about without getting the Gallente pissed at me. And there's already plenty of Caldari to mess with out there.
139036: There's a lot of Gallente out there: You might need to call in some big guns on this one. Sorry, I'm done.
139037: Good stuff. That's why I'm here.
139038: A high-ranking Gallente officer has experienced a religious conversion and wants to defect to Amarr. This man, Admiral Meledier, has apparently arranged to lead a reconnaissance foray into our space and is holed up in an old outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Get out there and extract him from the rendezvous point.
139039:
A Gallente admiral has seen the light of true faith and experienced a religious conversion. A hand-written, hand-delivered letter — on actual paper! — arrived in the office this morning, expressing Admiral Meledier's desire to defect. Having a high-ranking Gallente officer suddenly join our side could cause tremendous damage to the ability of their capsuleers to wage war against us: His knowledge of their systems and tactics would be staggering.

We want you to go collect him from the rendezvous point in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. You game?
139040: Fantastic. Alright, you might as well move out: A chance like this won't come again anytime soon.
139041: Excellent work. You have done well. Glory to Amarr!
139042: How very disappointing, {[character]player.name}. The Empire will not look with pleasure upon your lack of courage.
139043: Yes, of course. What is it, {[character]agentID.name}?
139044: Are you kidding? I'm not going up against an entire squadron of the Gallente Navy!
139045: Mission accomplished. Admiral Meledier is on board.
139046: I'll bring him in safe and sound.
139051: Several of our brethren were slain by a group of infidel miners encroaching on our territory in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. These outsiders are stealing our precious resources. Go out there and kill them all; bring their cargo back to me.
139052:

Recently, several of our brethren were slain by a group of infidel miners encroaching on our territory in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. 139076:
Many bars have their fair share of tall tales, but one recurring favorite is that of the fabled “lost Jovian gate.” This tale always follows a similar narrative: the friend-of-a-friend was traveling in one of the outer regions, when, suddenly, his ship dropped out of warp. The crew found themselves in the middle of nowhere, with an inactive jump gate of strange design just in front of them.

As they approached the gate, it suddenly activated, propelling the crew into Jovian space, which was either some sort of utopia or a place of blackest horror. Before the crew could gather any evidence, some sort of danger-- usually a Jovian warship of marvelous design-- immediately appeared to force the pilot back through the gate, undertaking an emergency warp as back on the other side. Invariably, the ship's log was somehow erased. The gate, of course, cannot be rediscovered, and is once more lost to time.
139077:
Our spies have intercepted a leaked transmission from a mining survey crew who reported the discovery of an abandoned jump gate. Now, that may not sound exciting, but based on what the mining crew's description of the gate's position and general design, we think it could be a lost Jovian jump gate, able to access their space.

I want you to travel to the gate coordinates and secure that location until the elite forces arrive. Sounds easy, but it's going to be anything but.
139078: Tales of the Lost Jovian Gate

139081: Make sure you take plenty of ammo-- this gate is the sort of thing our competition will sacrifice almost anything to secure.
139082: You've given us the opportunity to study the gate, which could lead to some considerable technological advances. Good work.
139083: You must've come to the wrong office. Missions for those lacking guts are down the hall, to the right.
139084: Do you understand how important this mission was to the Cartel? We're now forced into a major military action to take the gate from the forces established there. Don't think we'll forget your incompetence any time soon.
139085: What are you doing? Securing the asset before any of the other factions arrived was a matter of timing as well as firepower! I'll find someone else, as you're obviously not up to the task.
139088: I'll secure the gate for you, piece of cake.
139089: That space is a graveyard now. But it's a secure, Cartel-owned graveyard.
139090: Is this a “take it or leave it” option?  If so, I'll leave it.
139091: It's hell out there! I'm not losing my stuff over some antique jump gate – I quit!
139092: It usually is. Please, go on.
139093:
Certain unofficial militia groups in several Caldari systems are very interested in acquiring themselves some serious firepower. They must also have some well-connected financial backers, as they want to pay top LUX to get their hands on these weapons, and in large quantities, ASAP.

You've got a solid reputation with us, so I want you to broker the deal on my behalf. Meet my man at the rendezvous point provided. He'll have the weapons cache. Everything goes well; the Caldari will show up, you'll trade the stuff, the end. But if the deal goes south, I want you to take out every last one of them and bring the weapons back here.

139096: Get going, champ; they'll be waiting.
139097: Really? I never thought such shady, anonymous characters would even consider betrayal. How about that?
139098: Easy there, I'm not gonna make you do it. I'll just find another pilot to represent me at the deal.
139099: Because of you, the deal has fallen through. If you weren't one of those “elite” pilots, you'd be out of an airlock by now. Sleep lightly, friend.

139104: Well, the "deal" proved to be a straight setup, but I showed them what it means to mess with the Cartel.
139105: So, the odds of something going wrong are high enough that you want me to go instead of you? I'll pass, thanks.
139106: I had a bad feeling about this when I took the mission, and now things are just bad all around. I quit.

139108: Good work. I knew I could count on you. With that relay station out of commission, our local transmissions will be harder for the Caldari to intercept, at least until they manage to sneak another convoy in there.
139109:
In the last few weeks, we've become aware of an FTL transmitter in the area which has been broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State. Usually, the Federation isn't quite this bold in its slander of our state, so a number of corporate intelligence offices looked into the matter and found to our surprise that this transmitter is actually being run by someone we are all too familiar with: Melarius Torvil and his so-called “Brothers of Freedom.”

Obviously, we cannot allow this situation to continue. Torvil's persistent ability to elude capture by Caldari authorities is frustrating enough, but we cannot simply stand by while he rubs it in our faces. Frankly, the fact that the Republic is allowing this kind of dangerous nonsense makes me thankful our militia capsuleers are giving them a hard time.

Anyway, we would like you to fly to the transmitter in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}: Destroy it and any Minmatar vessels in the area. If the Republic Navy sends any ships to assist, feel free to eliminate them as well, but it isn't necessary; I don't think they'll be willing to stick their necks out over what is a rather diplomatically shady activity anyway.

What do you say? Can you handle this for me?
139110: The "Brothers of Freedom" have set up an FTL transmitter in the area of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and are broadcasting anti-corporate propaganda into the State, with the help of some Minmatar sympathizers. This situation is completely unacceptable; the transmitter must be destroyed, and we want you take care of it. Eliminate the transmitter and any hostile ships nearby. If the Minmatar Navy interferes, you can take out their vessels as well, but it's not strictly necessary.
139111: Engage the hostile fleet.  Watch out for reinforcements.  Kill as many as you can and then get out.
139113: We have reports of a strange Angel fleet massing in a nearby system.  The reports say they're all small ships, but I'm not sure if I'd trust that.  I need a pilot to round up some mates and go take them out.  You game?
139114: Funny, I thought you were a combat pilot.
139117: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?
139118: Or were you just too busy watching vids?
139119: Had to send someone else. Sorry, chump.
139123: Man, that was a lot of little ships.  What the heck was that all about?
139124: Sounds risky. I think I'll pass.
139125: This is too much work. Find some other chump.
139126: That depends. You got something interesting for me?
139127: I just might be, yes. What have you got?
139128: I'm taking more damage than I expected. I need to bail out of this mission, {[character]agentID.name}. Sorry.
139130: Base and enemy vessels destroyed, {[character]agentID.name}. It looks as if the Angel Cartel took some interest in things as well.
139131: I'll take care of the Amarrians for you, happily.
139132: Too bad. Soon we're all going to have to help out whether we want to or not.
139133: Good work. I guess the Angels really are interested in this sector.
139135: This isn't going to look good to my superiors, {[character]player.name}, but I accept your decision.
139136:
Oh, we have a number of possibilities, but only a few really choice assignments for especially trustworthy capsuleers like yourself.

These are definitely dangerous times, {[character]player.name}. The corsairs are getting bolder, crime is rampant, and the empires are pretty much at war, which will plunge us all into chaos and cost millions of lives. Unfortunately for people like me, there's not much we can do to change the inevitable; all we can do is try to make sure that what comes costs us as little as possible — in lives, worlds, and materials. To that end, I'm overseeing a lot of war prep in this region, and I'm in need of good pilots who know their stuff and aren't afraid to take some risks now and again.

This has been a hot sector lately. The Angel Cartel is especially active, but fortunately for us they're equal opportunity raiders, and have been as hard on the Caldari and the Amarr as they have on us. Amarr, for their part, have been sending in reconnaissance craft, which suggests either that they have designs on this region or they think we'll be using it as a staging area.

In fact, we think Imperial forces are rebuilding an abandoned CONCORD station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and will be using it to service their vessels, so they may be planning a more long-term presence in the region. These are just the opening moves in the great game, I assure you, but we can't let ourselves be outmaneuvered.

We're short-handed right now, so we're not above hiring independents; we'd like you to take out this station. There may be some Amarrian ships in the area, but we don't anticipate anything like a full-scale defense. Get in, destroy the base, and get out, and you'll have earned yourself a nice reward... and helped to keep the Empire out of this sector.
139137:
