139138: If you're paying well, then you're right — I am perfect for it.
139139: Shouldn't this really be something the police could take care of?
139140: You were right: the customs official was letting slaves into the Federation. But he won't be doing so any longer.
139141: I will do anything necessary to ensure that the Federation remains a bastion of freedom!
139146: I am surprised. I wouldn't have taken you for someone who'd allow such an injustice to continue.
139147: Good work. The Federation does its utmost to make sure our enemies cannot undermine our way of life, and you've struck a great blow today in that pursuit.
139148: Excellent. Now, get out there and catch this scumbag. And vaporize the smugglers as well. They're not our main targets, but eliminating a few of them should help you let off some steam.
139149: Great. Unless something is done, this problem will just continue to grow. I never thought you would be so selfish.
139150:
A customs officer has long been suspected of taking bribes from the Amarr. There is an old smuggler's gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that is supposed to have been deactivated, but lately ships have been registered coming through it. We believe it is the customs officer, allowing illegal slavers to bypass our normal checkpoints and bring slaves through the Federation.

We want you to fly out to the stargate and catch him in the act. Once you do, you're free to eliminate him with extreme prejudice.
139151:
It is a sad day when you cannot trust your own citizens, don't you agree? Well, today is a sad day. You see, one of our customs agents may be accepting bribes. What's worse, he may actually be helping those Amarr slaver scum smuggle slaves through the Federation.

We have long suspected the officer, but never had any concrete proof. He has been incredibly careful in covering his tracks. But finally, we think we've got him. There's an old smuggler's stargate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that's supposed to be inactive. It seems the transmission logger isn't inactive, though, and it recently sent us a traffic report… and several industrial ships belonging to "Imperial Human Resources," a well-known Amarrian slave company, were recorded passing through the gate.

We believe the customs official is the one opening the gate for the smugglers, and he just left the station a short time ago. We planted a bug on his ship, so we have his current location. I want you to fly out there, catch the customs official in the act of opening the gate, and destroy him.
139152: I thought you were a warrior of the Republic. I must've been thinking of somebody else.
139154: Unbelievable. You destroyed the shipyard and their fleet. And you came back, which is a bonus.
139155: Oh, so I suppose you want to do something a little less dangerous?
139157: I'll just get someone who has some balls, then.
139160: I'll need to round up my wingmen, but consider that shipyard dust.
139163: Okay, this is a bit much. I'm gonna have to quit.
139165:
You know what they say about assumptions, right? …something about, uh, sums and options… I think.

Why am I here again?
139166: Hey, I didn't sign up for this when I accepted your mission!
139167: Wow, you know, I have something more important to do. Like... uh... yeah — no thanks.
139168: I've destroyed the satellite, but I think there's something more going on here than meets the eye.
139169: You really must not like people who grew up planetside. Anyway, I'll take care of it.
139174: You're really turning me down? If I have to deal directly with those dust-snufflers, I'll scream.
139175: What? Caldari forces protecting that satellite? Great. Just great. Now we'll have to launch a whole investigation into the matter. I might even get sent planetside. I do hate this job sometimes.
139176: The sooner you deal with this, the better. I hate having to interact with those petty land-lice.
139177: Great. You can't get the job done, so now I'll have to deal with it even more.
139178:
Ehh, politics, I believe. Oh, I never get tired of them. Dear, sweet politics. Oh, wait. No. I hate politics.

But without politics, our great democratic and free society would collapse. It's the nature of the beast, I'm afraid. And, well, the Federation has numerous laws to prevent politicians from being abusive with their politicking. Now, some dirtside political office is up for grabs after the incumbent died of a heart attack after a night at a pleasure hub. "Vice Commissioner of Waste Management for the Civic Council" or something unimportant like that.

Normally, we wouldn't even bother with something this trivial. Those silly dirtside hillhuggers and their governments aren't much to look at. But one of them had to go and break some laws, and now it's our job to clean it up. You see, someone has hijacked some broadcast waves and is sending out a constant message denouncing one of the candidates. And because it's a space-based satellite doing the broadcasting, we're the ones that have to deal with it.

Now, we don't know who it is that's making the broadcasts, and frankly, I don't care. As long as they're stopped, I'm happy with it. We've pinned down the offending satellite, so I want you to fly over there and blow it up. There might be some automated defenses, but it's just some mudsucker's place, so they can't be that great.
139180:
Someone has illegally hijacked a broadcast satellite and is using it to play a message denigrating a local politician running for office. I could care less, but those sand-sifters won't stop nagging me about it. We've found the offending satellite, we just need it destroyed — the sooner, the better. That way I'll stop having to hear complaints about it.

Oh, there might be some automated defenses, but they probably won't be that hard to handle.
139181:
The Gallente Federation is a massive democracy. It is divided up into several regions, which are subdivided into districts, which are further divided into sub-districts… which make up several individual systems, each of which has one or more planetary governments, each of which further has additional subdivisions. Though every planet follows some basic rules, such as having regular elections with universal suffrage, the systems on each planet are as varied as the Gallente people.

For most observers, planetary politics in the Federation are incredibly tedious. Some, however, count the politics of the planets as the most fascinating and vital part of the democracy. There is a huge amount of bureaucracy involved, which makes it too dense for most to penetrate. But the amount of energy put forth by many individuals (who are unlikely to be remembered once their terms are finished) exemplifies the true spirit of the Federation.
139182:
Technically, I had nothing to do with getting you into this in the first place. I was just...

Ah, never mind. What do you need?
139183: I'm too lazy to finish your mission. Sorry.
139184: Zzzz... What? Huh? Oh, you should find someone else, I guess, since your proposal's making me fall asleep.
139185: I brought the politician back, as asked.
139186: I've carried worse around. One politician shouldn't be too bad.
139191: I suppose I'll have to send someone else to do it for me.
139192: Alright, now I've got to go have a little chat with our politician. Come back to me later to see what I've discovered.
139193: Hurry over there and get him. The sooner he's back, the sooner I can get rid of him.
139194: I don't want to deal with this any more than you do. You're really quitting on me?
139195:
There's a badly damaged Gallente convoy nearby. One or two of the vessels may be capable of defending themselves, but we don't think they're up to much of a fight. We want you to head out there; finish them off and get as much of that salvage as you can. Somewhere in all that cargo and salvage there's a sealed container of great value to the Cartel, so we'll provide you with a generous bonus if you get it back to us intact.

Oh, yes, one more thing... The Gallente convoy got off a distress signal, so you might have to contend with a Gallente rescue mission. And we've heard some chatter from the Serpentis saying that they might be sending ships soon, so best be on your guard. Our intelligence says that neither of those factions has very much in the way of resources in the area, so you shouldn't have too much to do.

Things might get dicey, but I'm sure it's nothing you can't handle.
139196:
Well, it turns out that the Caldari Navy is behind those transmissions. The question is why… Why do the Caldari care who wins some meaningless election on some planetary hovel? That's what we have to find out now. The first step in taking care of this will be to question the candidate they were broadcasting about.

Now, I've received word that the man is vacationing with his family a few systems away. We've already sent word over to have him recalled as a matter of official Federation business. By the time you get there, he should be ready for pick up.

What, I didn't mention that? Yes, you get the great pleasure of taxiing that earthbounder back to us. I know you'll accept, won't you?
139197:

139200: ASAP, {[character]player.name}. See you when you get back.
139201: I can't imagine why you're complaining. You got the job done, after all.
139203: Sure, I'll give it a shot, {[character]agentID.name}. When do I leave?
139204: You were definitely low-balling the risk, {[character]agentID.name}. Here's your precious container.
139205: I think you're low-balling the risk here. I'll look for opportunities elsewhere.
139206: Holy crap, where are all those ships coming from? I'm taking too much damage. I quit!
139207: I've been busy. What've you got cooking?
139208: Really? You can't? I would never have guessed.
139209: It turns out those Caldari Navy guys are pretty tough. I quit.
139210: I'm sorry, but I'm not going to handle someone else's bully.
139211: The Caldari have learned not to mess with our local district elections.
139212: At last, something interesting! I'll do it!
139217: Nnnggg.... You're just trying to give me an aneurysm, aren't you?
139218: Good. Of course, now everyone thinks our politician's some great hero, important enough for the Caldari Navy to try and get rid of him. The fool will probably become President some day. Makes my skin crawl just thinking about it.
139219: I've uploaded the location to your NeoCom.
139220: You couldn't even take care of one lone Caldari officer? What kind of pod pilot are you?
139221:
Our politician friend managed to annoy a Caldari Navy officer back in the day and now that officer is out for revenge. He's the one behind all these broadcasts. I guess he figured since it was such a meaningless, tiny local election, the Federation wouldn't stop his revenge.

I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels.

We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out. The sooner this headache is over, the better.
139222:
No, it's true. I know I always speak glowingly of them, but really, they get under my skin.

Anyway, my questioning finally got some answers out of that damn fool politician. It turns out that there is no vast conspiracy after all. Not really. It turns out the idiot is just a little too loud-mouthed for his own good. He used to be in the Navy… before he was discharged because he kept fainting every time he went onto the battlefield. But before he demonstrated that bit of heroism, he managed to piss off a Caldari Navy officer by throwing up on him during a diplomatic summit.

Apparently, the officer in question never lived it down and still gets heckled about the event to this day. And now he's out for revenge by trying to disrupt our man, the stupid politician. It's… it's so tedious and… stupid.

Anyway, I guess this officer figured that, since it was such a meaningless little election, the Federation wouldn't bother to interfere with his revenge. Heh. I guess he doesn't know that we'll take any opportunity there is to blow up a few Caldari Navy vessels. We've tracked his base down and want you to go over there and take him out.

The sooner this headache is over, the better.
139223:
The workers in a corporate mining facility are striking, taking control of the facility's defense grid and arming their mining vessels. They have shut the mining operation down completely and locked corporate personnel out of the area until their demands are met.

This situation is not acceptable. You are to enter the facility and neutralize any armed resistance: bring the strike to an end before there is any more damage to corporate property or loss of production. Do what you can to minimize collateral damage, but ending this as soon as possible is your top priority.
139224: I certainly hope you're not a sympathizer, pilot.  You won't go far if you keep up this attitude.
139225: Good.  Here are the coordinates for the entrance to the mining facility.  Return to me as soon as the job is done.
139226: Excellent.  Hopefully the new manager of that facility will be able to get production up and running in short order.
139227: I certainly hope you're not turning this down because you sympathize with them.  I suppose I'll have to find someone else with a more realistic idea of the situation to handle this.
139228: You've taken too long: the strike has gotten far too out of control and corporate assets are in serious danger.  We've called in the military to deal with the situation. Your services are no longer needed, pilot.
139229: I couldn't wait any longer for you to decide if you could handle this for me. I was forced to call in another pilot to take care of the matter.  While I am not exactly a fan of her methods, she has been able to bring the strike to a quick end.  Perhaps next time you will make sure you get back to me in a timely manner.
139231: Wildcat strike brought to bloody end
139232: I'll deal with the strike.  You can count on me.
139233: The strike has been brought to an end.
139234: I'm not sure this is really a job for me.
139235: I've decided I don't have time to clean up this particular mess.
139237: Scientific progress grinds to a halt, thanks to you.
139238:
Well, Dr. Calus is not ready to reveal the nature of her project, but rest assured that it will be huge. However, the good doctors require some critical datacores to help them put their ideas into physical form. Sometimes scientific ideas race ahead of one's ability to fabricate the results effectively.

We need you to go pick up a unique Mechanical Engineering datacore put together for the project by one of Dr. Calus's colleagues not far from here and bring it back as soon as possible. You will be rewarded, of course, as usual.
139240: Go pick up a shipment of slaver hounds from a private deadspace compound in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They're inside the base, stored in secured containers in case those Starway freaks try anything.
139241: I got your slavers. But I don't think you'll be getting any more from that supplier-— someone bombed the place but good, just as I got there. And I'm thinking it was no coincidence.
139242:
Well, it just so happens that we're in the middle of some operations that might require a capsuleer's assistance.

The Amarrians have been busy lately, building bases and moving fleet resources back and forth along the frontier. We've done recon in several of the systems where the Amarrians have been active, but we recently observed unusual comings and goings in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We think they might be building a base in one of the system's asteroid fields, but we can't be sure as all of our ships are tied down in other locations.

I'd like to install a reconnaissance module in your ship, then have you fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2000 units of Scordite. We'll take the ore off your hands when you get back to make sure everything looks aboveboard.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Amarrian activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts.

Note, I'd advise caution. Will you do it, {[character]player.name}?
139243: We've entered the coordinates into your NeoCom, and the recon unit has been installed in your ship. Remember, you won't even know it's there.
139244:
I'd like you to fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} posing as a freelance miner; while you're out there, we'll have a reconnaissance module installed in your ship. Go to the asteroid field that we've entered into your NeoCom and mine 2,000 units of Scordite. Of course we'll reimburse you generously for your time and for the ore – the mining mission is just a cover for the recon mission.

While you're mining, the recon module will be scanning the region and monitoring Amarrian activity around the system. You'll never even notice it's there. Once you've finished, head back here and we'll recover the recon unit, take the ore, and reward you for your efforts. I'd advise caution in the area as well: There are lots of miners around, but the Amarr will be suspicious of any vessel that originates from Republic space.

139248: You should hear the reports. The Gallente are now paranoid that we're going to roll right over them! Of course our line is just that you were taking photographs for your family or something, but they're scared senseless.
139249:
Reports are that the pirates are amassing a small fleet for action against us. They have a scout scoping the place ahead of them. Only he's not going to get to the final area.

The scout will be jumping through an old, decommissioned jump gate. Take a position by the gate, and wait for him to come through. Once he does, take him out.
139250: But you stole ore! Danger is your middle name!
139251: Gate camps are groups of ships who wait outside jump gates for other ships to pass through. Once a ship comes through the gate camp bombards it, putting their target at a great disadvantage. The use of warp bubbles and scramblers can further ruin an unsuspecting target's day, preventing it from warping away from the fight. For this reason, warp stabilizers are common fitting for any ships passing through low- or null- security space.
139252: The Gallente are great lovers of wealth and luxury, and especially of beauty. They produce countless holos, from the cheapest porn flicks to high-priced stage shows and beyond. The stars of these productions are greatly esteemed for the entertainment they provide, and therefore hold influence and power in some circles.
139253: The daughter of a prominent Holder has eloped with a famous Gallente holo star, despite having a proper marriage with an Amarr man awaiting her at home. Retrieve her from this seducer and kill him.
139255:
Yes, I have work for you. The daughter of a prominent Holder has been seduced by a famous Gallente holo star. She's run away with him, likely planning to get married as soon as she is out of her family's reach.

She was already betrothed to a perfectly suitable Amarrian man, a match approved by her family and her faith. Obviously, she must be brought back into the fold.

You will be well rewarded if you can deliver her back to her family before she can shame herself any further. If you destroy this seducer in the process-- well, that's all the better.
139256: And I thought you were a true Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you fail to do these jobs.
139257: I knew you were the right person for the job. Take care, as this holo star does have bodyguards.
139258: I knew I could count on you. You are indeed a faithful Amarr; your reputation will only benefit from the work you have done.
139259: And I thought you were a good Amarr. You cannot expect to keep a good reputation if you won't put in any effort.
139260: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen without suffering any consequences.
139261: Thanks to you, {[character]player.name}, the Holder's daughter has married the Gallente holo star and brought shame to her family and to the Amarr. Do not think that you can let things like this happen and without suffering any consequences.
139265: I, uh, found the girl. You take her.

139267: I don't have time to chase down some runaway. I have more important things to do.

139269:
The Amarr Empire is ruled by the Emperor and the five Heirs. When the Emperor dies, these Heirs go through a set of ritual competitions to become the next Emperor.

In 22762 AD, Khanid was the Heir of one of the other five families, but he refused to acknowledge the election of the new Emperor. He also refused to commit ritual suicide, which is done by the remaining Heirs in order to keep resentments and past problems from interfering with the new ruler's regime.

Instead of being obedient and faithful, Khanid fled Amarr and set out to create his own empire. He formed the Khanid Kingdom, which is also known as the “Dark Amarr.”
139270: The Minmatar are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom in order to gain an ally against the Amarr Empire. This could be dangerous to the Empire, as the Khanid may know much that could help Amarr's enemies. Find, intercept and destroy the Minmatar ambassador's vessel and its escorts and bring the ambassador back for interrogation.
139272:
That is correct.

The Minmatar, deceitful devils that they are, are attempting to form an alliance with the Khanid Kingdom. Khanid is a traitor to our beliefs, and he knows much about us that the Minmatar could exploit if they manage to forge an alliance.

We cannot risk the chance that the Minmatar might succeed. Go find the Minmatar vessel and destroy it before it reaches Khanid. Take care to bring the ambassador back for questioning. Be cautious, however – the Minmatar have the distasteful habit of thinking they can fight back against us.
139273: I thought you were a better pod pilot than that. A true Amarr would understand how much this refusal could damage a reputation.
139274: Wonderful! Remember to take care – Minmatar are always hard to break.
139275: Excellent. Thank you for your efforts.  Here is your reward.
139276: I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}. I thought you would see the importance of this mission.
139277: I cannot believe that you could not find and destroy the Minmatar vessels. You are not the pod pilot I thought you were. As a result of this failure, the Khanid Kingdom may have leaked dangerous secrets to the Minmatar.
139278: You should make decisions more quickly, capsuleer. As a result of your failure to destroy the ship, the Minmatar ambassador met with someone within the Khanid Kingdom; whether or not an alliance will be forged is still unknown.
139281: Nothing would please me more than to put a stop to this plot.
139282: I found and destroyed the Minmatar ambassador's ship. I've brought you the "envoy" for questioning.
139283: I don't see this as a threat to us. Khanid might not conform as he should, but he is still Amarr.
139284: I don't have time to hunt down these Minmatar vessels. You'll have to find someone else.
139285: I heard that you needed someone willing to do a combat mission.
139286: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.
139287: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.

139289: I see.  Well, perhaps you will be of some use next time.
139290:
When the Amarr Empire first came across the Minmatar, they began raiding this new people for slaves as they had with every other race they'd come across, a practice that is sanctified and even encouraged by the Amarr religion.

Though the Minmatar have since rebelled and managed to expel the Amarr and their allies from Minmatar space, approximately a third of all Minmatar are still enslaved under the Amarr.
139291: Some Minmatar slaves have rebelled, killing several Amarr and stealing a ship. Track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.
139293:
So the news is out.

It's true, some slaves have rebelled, and their actions have caused the deaths of several people. They have stolen a ship, and thus far they've managed to evade capture as well. This is insult on top of injury and cannot be tolerated.

I want you to track them down so that they can be returned to their owner.
139294: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.
139295: God's will be with you. You will be greatly rewarded when you bring them back.
139296: I knew I could count on you to retrieve those upstarts. Stay close: I suspect I'll have another mission for you shortly.
139297: Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.
139298: Inaction speaks, pilot. Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.
139299: Inaction speaks, pilot. Be careful or people will begin to think you support the barbarians.
139302: I'll find them and bring them back.
139305: These slaves aren't worth the trouble I've gone to; get someone else to hunt them down.
139306: I've heard rumors about a slave uprising.
139307:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to the Bookmarks tab. Then right-click on the objective item (the roster) and choose "Set Destination." On your ship's control panel, click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the roster and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 1500 meters, right-click the cargo container and open it. A window will now pop up, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the item(s) into your cargo hold: Once you've done that, you will have obtained the Brutor Tribe roster. All that will remain is to return with it to your agent for your reward.
139308: What's up, {[character]agentID.name}? I take it you have some work for me.
139309: I'm encountering more difficulty than I'd anticipated. I have to to withdraw from the mission, {[character]agentID.name}.
139310: That sounds awfully fishy to me. I prefer to let other people get dirty with the propaganda machine.
139311: The Mordu's Legion fleet is defeated. And the Caldari have egg all over their faces.
139312: I'm up for anything that will embarrass the Caldari. I'll do it.
139313: That isn't what we're doing at all! But it's obvious to me you don't want the job, so forget it anyway.
139314: Excellent. Your reward has been entered into your interstellar account. Many thanks, {[character]player.name}.
139315: Well done. The system coordinates have been sent to your NeoCom.
139317:
If you're willing. Given the current state of interstellar affairs, Mordu's Legion is in the thick of things. They've been engaging in raids and reconnaissance, harassing merchant traffic, and generally making trouble for us. In this sector, at least, they're doing just what the Caldari want them to — keeping our fleet tied down so those greedy bastards can martial their own forces in relative peace.

We might have an ace in the hole, however. We have good intelligence that many Intaki inside the Caldari State are growing impatient and restless, suffering discrimination and unemployment. Many blame the Caldari for their woes, and with the right incentive they might even be persuaded to secede back to the Federation. An incident involving the State-sanctioned Mordu's Legion may be just enough to tip the scales.

We've been monitoring subspace chatter, and we think that the Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We're planning on making it known that the base is full of Intaki refugees, but just to clinch the deal, it would be best if some heroic pilot caught the Mordus in the act and drove them off before the base was completely destroyed.

What we'd like you to do is get over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along. So, what do you say?
139319:
We think that Mordu's Legion may be planning on hitting one of our bases in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What we'd like you to do is get over there and take up position near the station. When the Legion ships arrive, destroy them or drive them off. We'll be monitoring things by video drone, so we'll have clear evidence of the attack.

Oh, and the Legion may be coming in strength, so you might want to bring some friends along.
139320:
Mordu's Legion is descended from a group of Intaki military personnel who sided with the Caldari State when it chose to secede from the Gallente Federation. It was led by a brilliant Caldari officer named Muryia Mordu, who fought the Gallente with great distinction.

After the war, the Intaki were given land around Waschi City on the planet Kamokor IV, but soon racial tensions flared between them and Caldari nationalists, who called for the expulsion of all foreigners. The Intaki called upon their hero Mordu for assistance, and the aging commander emerged from retirement to lead an independent mercenary group dedicated to preserving Intaki rights and property. Mordu's Legion helped defeat the nationalists and made peace with the Caldari authorities.

Today, the Legion remains a well-known mercenary band that often works closely with the Caldari State. Many Intaki continue to suffer discrimination at the hands of the xenophobic Caldari and have grown disillusioned with life in the corporate state. Nevertheless, Mordu remains a revered character among the Intaki, many of whom see him as a savior who will one day return to deliver his adopted people from the repression and poverty that they suffer from today.
139321: Might be, {[character]agentID.name}. What have you got?
139322: I'm taking too much damage, and this is taking too long. I quit.
139323: That doesn't sound very interesting. Have you got anything else?
139324: The enemy gate is destroyed, along with some of their hardware, {[character]agentID.name}. Thanks for the mission.
139325: Sounds like a decent job. I'll do it.
139326: That's too bad, {[character]player.name}. Nothing else available right now, I'm afraid.
139328: Thanks for your help. The coordinates are in your NeoCom, along with my instructions.
139329: I expected better from you, to be honest. You are a capsuleer, right? You're not just impersonating one?
139330:
Well, we've had some suspicious activity in this system lately. We suspect that someone — Angel Cartel, or possibly Serpentis, maybe even the Amarrians — might be sneaking in and prepping the system for attack with hidden bases, supplies, and the like. There may even be a hidden jumpgate somewhere in the vicinity; we've certainly detected some suspicious warp signatures and have been able to triangulate them down to several potential locations, all quite close to each other.

If we make a move with a large fleet, though, we might spook the enemy, so we're looking for a freelancer who's willing to take a risk on behalf of the Federation. We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the acceleration gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

Mind you, if there are enemy ships, you might have to fight them too, and no one can say for sure what might come through the gate. There might even be static defense turrets or drones as well. Who knows?

Once the gate is destroyed, return here and report; do it quickly and you'll earn yourself a nice bonus. Are you in?
139331:
We need someone to fly to the possible locations of the secret gate and see what's there. I'll enter the location of the first acceleration gate into your NeoCom; you should be able to reach the others using whatever internal gate array they've put in place. Fly through each one in turn and check the area for any gates that look suspicious. If you find one, you need to blast it before the enemy can jump any more ships around in this system.

139332: Destroy the three enemy shipyards and the control tower at the specified location.  Defend yourself and destroy any resistance.  You may need backup for this one.
139333:
The Republic needs your help with this one. We've discovered one of the facilities of a corporation that's a major supplier for the Amarrian Navy. By destroying it, we'll deliver a serious blow to their military buildup, which can only help the Republic.

Expect major resistance on this-- you'll need some backup of your own. Think you can handle this?
139334: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.
139335: The slaves provided us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.
139337:
Yes. We interrogated several of the Minmatar slaves you brought back after they escaped.

It seems that the errant Minmatar were headed to a group of their own kind within the Gallente Federation. In fact, they might not have managed to escape at all without the help of a Gallente contact.

When we applied more pressure, the slaves could only provide us with a location. There was supposed to be a data chip in a dead drop at this rendezvous. In the interest of preventing further mayhem, I need you to bring me that chip.
139338: I'll have to find someone else.
139339: I look forward to seeing what you find.
139340: Good work. Let me see what this says; I may have another mission for you shortly.
139341: And here I thought you were a brave one.
139342: You've waited too long to do what I asked. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.
139343: I've waited too long for your reply. You've taught me not to mistake you for dependable.
139346: Sounds important. I'll take care of it.
139348: I don't want to risk angering the Gallente. I'll pass.
139349: Something else has come up. I quit.
139350: You said you might have more work for me?
139351: A significant percentage of the Minmatar population resides within the Gallente Federation, forming a rather powerful political bloc. This bloc is one reason that the relations between Amarr and Gallente remain constantly tense.
139352: The data cube yielded the name of a single member of the powerful Minmatar political bloc in the Federation. This man was the contact that helped the slaves escape. Kill him and any who protect him.
139354: And here I thought you were brave, {[character]player.name}.
139355: I knew I could count on you. Remember that we're setting an example here.
139358: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
139359: I hope I can find someone capable who'll be able to kill the Gallente contact before he finds out that he's a target. I am disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
139362: I'll make certain that he doesn't cause any more trouble.
139363: You won't have any more problems with that Minmatar collaborator.
139364: It isn't wise to go after someone with such high connections. I won't do it.
139365: I don't want to go after someone with such high connections. I'm done with this.
139366: Did that data chip have anything interesting on it?
139368:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} wants a massive shipment of Augumene right away, so we need you to get out there and bring some back. I've been looking for a miner who's experienced enough, with the right kind of ship, and maybe you fit the bill. Time is critical on this one. There's a big bonus for you if you can bring it in fast enough.

You may find it helpful to use a Survey Scanner module to find the asteroids in space; most standard ship scanners do not have unique listings for such worthless ores. As well, pirates and claimjumpers abound in these parts, so you should also be prepared to defend your ship from such scavengers.

Finally, this amount of raw Augumene ore may require multiple trips unless you have a Hulk or a similarly large hauler for the job.
139370:
Some Amarr officer has gone crazy - he ignored orders, broke communications with his commanding officers, commandeered an Imperial Navy vessel, and then disappeared. Our intel says he's headed our way: apparently he's not willing to let freelance capsuleers handle the fight, and instead wants to be a part of it himself.

Fix this little problem for us and you will be well rewarded.
139371:
Due in large part to the values and teachings of the Amarr faith, the Amarr have the most extensive libraries, archives, and collections of artifacts pertaining to post-Eden life and, possibly, the EVE gate.

One of the heirs of the Ardishapur family, hailed as a paragon of the faith, has amassed what may be the largest array of religious artifacts in a private collection. Some of his pieces are even suspected to pre-date the closure of the EVE gate.
139374: I knew I could count on you, {[character]player.name}.
139375: Here is your reward. You have truly earned it.
139377: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.
139378: Due to your sloth, the miners who discovered the artifact found another buyer, one from outside the faith. Thanks to your neglect, we may never discover the true religious significance of this piece of living history.
139381: I would be honored to undertake such a mission.
139382: I hope you find this as valuable as you thought it would be. The miners have already paid with their lives.
139383: I'm not going to go haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than that.
139384: I'm done haring off over some unidentified piece of ancient junk. My time's worth more than this.
139385: I thought you might have some work for me today.
139386:
Ship racing has become very popular in the past few years. Pilots race their ships to see who can complete a circuit the fastest and thus show off proper ship handling, attention to quick course corrections, and how much power can be coaxed out of a ship.

The Amarr have some of the best racers in the sector and to commemorate their successes, they are building a new racing area in one of our poorer systems to help stimulate the economy, while at the same time showcasing Amarr skill in flying the best ships in pod pilot hands today.
139387: Then I take it you've got a high-paying job for me, right?
139388: I'm getting a really bad feeling about this job, and I've learned to trust my gut. I'm out. And go easy on batting those eyelashes, {[character]agentID.name} — you'll pull a muscle.
139389: A new race track is being built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. During the final stages of building, we received reports of some ships bearing Gallente markings, and several suspicious "accidents" have occurred. Sabotage is suspected. Go find these ships and destroy them so that no harm will come to participants or viewers during the big race.
139390: If you want a clean-up job, hire a janitor.  Not interested.
139392: The Caldari cruiser is now dust. Would have been nice of you to let me know about the Guristas, though.
139393:
I have a task that must be done quickly, and it requires punitive force.

A new race track is being designed and built in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and it is supposed to be the grandest and most beautiful and complicated tracks yet ever to exist in all of the known sectors! A substantial quantity of money and work have gone into this track, and there are plans to hold one of the largest races ever as soon as the track is finished.

However, some suspicious ships have been seen in the vicinity. They evade patrols, but we've received reports that they bear Gallente markings. A couple of "accidents" have already occurred while testing the track, and investigations have led to suspicion of sabotage.

We think that these Gallente ships have been sabotaging this new track, probably in hopes of killing many Holders and their families when the time comes for the great inaugural race.

I want you to put a stop to this nonsense before it has any further impact. Destroy those ships; it's time we sent a message.
139394: Sounds simple enough, {[character]agentID.name}.  I'll get on it right away.
139395: You are not the pilot I thought you were. I'll be sure to spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.
139397: Excellent. Do take care. Our intelligence on these ships is sketchy at best, so they may be more powerful than we know.
139398: I knew you were the right pilot for the job.
139400: You are not the pilot I thought you were. I'll be sure to spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.
139402: The Gallente ships were finally found, but not before they caused further serious damage to the track. You are lucky that they were discovered before the great race, or else you would have many more Amarr lives on your conscience. You may rest assured that I will spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.
139403: The Gallente ships were finally found, but not before they caused further serious damage to the track. You are lucky that they were discovered before the great race, or else you would have many more Amarr lives on your conscience. You may rest assured that I will spread the word of your laziness and ingratitude.
139408: I've disposed of the Gallente miscreants.
139409: I'm sorry, {[character]player.name}, but the way you dress, I thought you were a janitor. My mistake!
139410: I don't have time to play hide-and-seek with some phantom troublemakers. Find someone else who has nothing better to do.
139411: Your intelligence must be wrong because I can't find these mysterious ships. Find someone else who has nothing better to do than playing hide-and-seek with phantom troublemakers.
139412: You have work for me, then?
139413: I'm so happy to hear the ship is no longer an issue for us — and especially that you're okay, {[character]player.name}. And so sorry about those Guristas. You're right, I should have said something...
139414: {[character]player.name} — you are the absolute best! I knew today was my lucky day!
139415: That's so funny, {[character]player.name}, because I just got this funny sensation behind my eyes when I saw you walk in — sort of like an ulcer, but in my brain.
139416:
I do, in fact, have a little matter that needs your attention. It's rather... delicate.

My corporation recently had a small misunderstanding with a Caldari business rival. Fortunately, after some of our folks met with the Caldari to have a… discussion, our people managed to limp back here; unfortunately, they left the wreckage of the Caldari ship intact, including the ship's log.

Now, it would impact any future dealings we might have with the Caldari if this dispute became known to their authorities. I'm sure they'd insist on petty things like vengeance. So we'd rather that didn't happen. We'd like you to go destroy all evidence of the Caldari cruiser. It can be found at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

So, will you be a pal and do this for me?
139418: Destroy the Caldari cruiser at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} along with any other hostile ships you may encounter. No witnesses!
139419:
The worst enemy is the one who was once an ally. This is a lesson not lost on the Caldari Navy, for it was from within their own ranks that the seeds of the Guristas pirates were born.

The Guristas were founded by two ex-Caldari Navy members now known only as "Fatal" and "The Rabbit." Utilizing their knowledge of the Navy's procedures — and thus its weaknesses — these two renegades have confounded their previous employers for many years with their persistence and ingenuity.

The Guristas cannot totally disown their militaristic origins: among pirates, they remain arguably the most honorable among a dishonorable bunch. Yet spacefarers shouldn't take too much comfort from that fact, or from their amusing bunny-skull logo. The Guristas will still slit your throat if there's profit involved.

Honor, as many have learned, goes only so far when LUX is concerned.
139420: Funny you should mention the Guristas, because I kind of wanted an explanation about that. You knew they'd be there?
139421: I've just done the math, {[character]agentID.name}. Bunch of Guristas + me not trusting you = I quit.
139422: Sorry, {[character]agentID.name}, but no thanks. You seem about as trustworthy as a Thukker ship salesman. Go play some other sucker, 'cause I'm gone.
139423: I destroyed those Guristas, {[character]agentID.name}, and I got the ship log. But, uh, I checked it to make sure it's the right log, and it… well, it has some interesting information. Is there something you want to tell me?
139424: This job just keeps getting better and better. And yes, that's sarcasm. But yes, I'll do it — for the LUX. I can't spend your gratitude.
139427:
Hey {[character]player.name},

Just a quick note to let you know your laxity in retrieving that ship log has led to several Caldari vigilante attacks on my corporation. At last count, 200 people are dead. Have a nice day!
139429: I did say I was sorry about forgetting to mention the pirates… but it seems obvious you're just afraid to fight. Run along then, little egger, run along.
139430:
Oh, yeah, {[character]player.name}, about that....

Listen, give me a minute to wrap this up, and then come back and I'll explain everything, okay?
139431: It speaks very well of you that you aren't running away when things get hot, {[character]player.name}. I like that in a capsuleer.
139432:
You surprise me, to be honest. I would have thought that kind of complex addition quite beyond you.

Bye now.
139433:
I'm so sorry about those Guristas! You're right. I should have said something... but I knew you'd be able to handle it.

Anyway, it seems they boarded that Caldari cruiser before you arrived and took the ship's log. Now they're threatening to turn it over to the Caldari Navy if we don't pay up. We've got enough on our plate at the moment without fomenting open war with Caldari. Amarr'd just love that, huh?

So, we've tracked them to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you could go and take care of them, I'd be really, really grateful.
139434: Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and destroy the Guristas pirates there. Don't forget to recover the ship log that they stole from the Caldari cruiser. They won't be there long, so please hurry!
139435: Well, maybe. Kinda depends on what it is you tell me now and what you want next, really.
139436: I've just had a sudden attack of common sense, {[character]agentID.name}. I'm out of here before I end up in either a casket or a rubber room.
139437: Newsflash, {[character]agentID.name}! You're obviously out of your mind. I'm putting as much distance between you and me as humanly possible. See ya, crackpot!
139438: Well, it's done. Maybe not the way you wanted, but it's done. The buyer is dead, the pirates are dead, you've got your secret package back, and I need a drink. Now pay up!
139439: You've lied to me, you've manipulated me, and you've almost gotten me killed. I've got to admit, {[character]agentID.name} — I'm starting to like your style. I'm in!
139442:
{[character]player.name},

It seems unfortunate that you would go so far in this operation only to wander off right at the end. And since you had the prototype, we couldn't get paid, either. Not a good idea to upset Covert Ops that way, you know? Really Bad Idea.
139443:
{[character]player.name},

How difficult was it to just deliver the prototype? What, the thought of a few Guristas out for revenge stopped you? Maybe you just didn't want it enough. Ever think of that? Very, very disappointed, me.
139444: But I'm really in deep with Covert Ops! I have an honorary badge and everything! And a set of spy glasses, too. I'm the real deal!
139445: Congratulations, {[character]player.name}! Not only have you done the impossible, but you've made me 100,000 LUX in a side bet! My partners thought you'd die long before this! Thanks a bunch! Here's your reward, and a little extra besides! Don't spend it all in one place, champ.
139446: I knew you'd never let me down, {[character]player.name}.  Just hurry before this buyer comes to his senses (or you do…). Oh — did I say that out loud?
139447: Wow. What a build-up to the letdown you turned out to be, {[character]player.name}. Oh, well — there must remain some expendable suckers out there I can use, I'm sure.

139478:
We have a bit of a problem, {[character]player.name}. A corporate executive seems to have used some rather unorthodox methods to try to speed up production in his mining fields, and the strain this placed on the labor force there has led to a wildcat strike which has shut down production in that field entirely, causing materials shortages all the way up our supply chain. Of course, this is entirely unacceptable; it is imperative that this strike be brought to a close immediately and production resume as soon as possible.

Corporate security is stretched rather thin in this sector, so we would like you to go to the mining facility in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and eliminate any threats to corporate assets. You should be aware that the striking miners have taken control of the facility's defense grid and armed many of their mining vessels with makeshift weapons, so you should expect heavy resistance.

Avoid any collateral damage to corporate assets if possible; we don't want this strike to cost us any more than it already has.
139479: You expect me to go in there and risk life and limb just to rescue some snotty little rich kid?! Uh, no. You're crazy, {[character]agentID.name}.
139480: While mining ore in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, a small group of mining pirates uncovered a religious artifact of uncertain origin. Find these rogues and retrieve the artifact from them.
139481:
I always have work for a good pod pilot.

It has recently come to my attention that a small group of nearby pirates stumbled across something rather unusual. While mining for ore, they made a lucky discovery-- they uncovered what appears to be a religious artifact.

As you know, such an object is of great importance to all Amarr. There are many Holders who would pay large sums to get their hands on such a find; even better, there are collectors among the royal family who would give large rewards to add such a thing to their private collections.

I want you to find these rogue miners and retrieve this artifact from them. Bring it here, and you will be well rewarded.
139482:
The attack on the meeting between the Gallente and Minmatar emissaries went perfectly. Now we need to finish the job. After escaping the scene of the attack, the Minmatar ambassador was whisked away to a nearby staging area.

A raid on the Minmatar delegation now will look like a reprisal raid from the Gallente delegation, and since the Minmatar know they weren't responsible for the initial attack, they'll be even angrier. We have reason to believe that the enemy diplomats have been transferred aboard the Minmatar flagship to ensure their safety. It's the only battleship in the delegation, and it must be destroyed.

139609:
All hell's broken loose out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The Amarrians have chosen to create an incident that they're hoping will escalate into war.

A group of Ammatar "nationals" in a small outpost out there claim that they were beaten up by our security guards and then arrested on trumped-up charges. The Empire has dispatched a fleet to blockade the outpost "in protest," they say, "on behalf of our friends and allies"; they are demanding that the prisoners be turned over to them.

We're in a no-win situation: If we hold the Nefantar, the Amarr fleet will bombard the station and force a confrontation, but if we turn them over it will be seen as a sign of weakness. We need to raise the blockade, while at the same time avoiding direct official intervention in the situation. That's why we need a capsuleer. We need you.

{[character]player.name}, please — fly to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and take out the fleet that is amassing there. It's a tough job, but from what we've heard you're up to it. What do you say?
139610: The prisoners should be safe to pick up now, {[character]agentID.name}. Oh, by the way, the Imperial Navy is also down a few warships.
139611: I shall do my best to serve the Federation's ideals.
139612: One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here.  We're not certain about their intentions, but we'd like you to take them out just incase.  Those damned Mordu's assassination squads have been known to murder our members in the past, so we keep a good eye on them.  We know their exact location this time, and I'd like you to take them out before they know what hit them.  I'm counting on you {[character]player.name}.

139614:
Recently a thief stole some valuable documents from a high ranking officer and friend of mine in {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}.  These documents are very sensitive and we fear they were stolen by someone working for an enemy of ours.  
Fortunately, the information stored within the documents was encrypted using the very latest encryption software.  The thief probably did not expect this, and we believe the information has not yet been revealed to him or his 
employer.  Should it leak out however then the leader of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} will be ... less than forgiving.  Would you please save my friends career?  I have been told by a reliable source of a shady 
person who docked here yesterday and was spotted near my friends apartment, and is most likely the thief of whom I speak.  This person has very recently left this station.  I will pay you {[numeric]rewardQuantity} 
{[item]rewardTypeID.name} if you intercept the thief, destroy his ship if he offers resistance and bring the documents back to me.  I know you probably do not want to harm someone who may not be guilty, but I assure you 
that this scoundrel has a history of criminal offenses within {[location]agentRegionID.name}.  The people of {[location]agentRegionID.name} will be glad to know of his demise.  You have only 24 hours to complete the mission, but 
he will most likely be located in this very constellation.
139615: Our counter-intelligence service has indicated that the Gallente Federal Intelligence Office has erected a covert listening post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. While our communications are encrypted, the presence of Gallente intelligence operations in our space poses both an insult to Caldari sovereignty and an unacceptable risk to communications security.
139616: The Gallente FIO answers directly to the Gallente President. Its works are shrouded in secrecy and covert operations. Among their spying operations are the construction and operation of numerous small, covert listening posts designed to glean information from enemy signals and communications.
139618:
Our counter-intelligence service has indicated that the Gallente Federal Intelligence Office has erected a covert listening post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. While I assure you our communications are encrypted, the presence of Gallente intelligence operations in our space poses both an insult to Caldari sovereignty and an unacceptable risk to communications security.

Your task is simple: go there, overwhelm whatever forces are defending the post, and destroy it. Can I count on you to see this through?
139619: Well, at least you tried. Good luck in your travels, {[character]player.name}
139620: Glad to hear it.  But be careful out there; you're not dealing with amateurs.
139621: Good work, {[character]player.name}! The agent who recommended you to me may not have praised you highly enough!
139622: So, what, we're just supposed to let the Gallente spy on us? I'll have to inform the agent who recommended you that you're less reliable than advertized. Get out of my sight.
139623: Perhaps I did not impress upon you the importance of the matter we discussed, but your delay in performing this simple task is unacceptable. I have taken the liberty of giving the job to someone who understands the importance of rooting out spies.

139627: Of course you can count on me.
139628: The Gallente spies have been destroyed.
139629: This doesn't really sound like my kind of thing, sorry.
139630: I'm afraid I'm not going to be able to complete this job for you.
139631: I'm always ready to do my part. How can I help?
139632: In order to maximize the element of surprise for our raid, all enemy pickets and patrol ships must be destroyed. Go to the assigned location in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and destroy all the ships you find there. Beware of enemy reinforcements!
139633:
The time has come to strike a blow against the arrogant Gallente. We're going to stage a raid deep into Gallente territory. In order to mask the movements of our forces, however, we first need to wipe out their pickets and patrols. We could do this with our own ships, of course, but that might alert the enemy to our plans. A lone, talented capsuleer, on the other hand, would make short work of them and raise less suspicion.

I've uploaded the coordinates of the stepping-off point of our raid into your nav-computer. I want you to go there and destroy all of the enemy ships you find. Be advised that they may try to bring in reinforcements, but that should be no problem for someone of your caliber. Are you up to the task?
139634: This is terrible! Our operations time-table is totally disrupted. I hold you personally responsible, {[character]player.name}
139635: Excellent. Get out there and make it happen. The sooner those enemy patrols are out of the way, the sooner we can launch the raid.
139636: Well done, {[character]player.name}. You'll no doubt be happy to hear that early reports indicate our raid has been a stunning success!
139637: Suit yourself, though I'd like to remind you that the details of our discussion are to be kept in the strictest of confidence. Operational security, you understand. If it gets back to me that you've been blabbing about this raid, there will be hell to pay. You are dismissed.
139638: Due to your inability to deal with this assignment in a timely fashion, the entire raid has been scrubbed. It may be quite some time before another opportunity this good arises. Whatever you were doing, I hope it was important.
139639: Based on your lack of response, I take it that this assignment did not interest you. Had you been considerate enough to simply tell us that up front, we could have gotten someone else. As it is, we've had to scrub the entire raid.
139643: All opposition has been swept away. Where's my reward?
139644: Hmm, this isn't really what I had in mind. Maybe next time.
139645: I'm afraid you're going to have to find someone else to deal with your problem. I have more important things to do.
139646: I hear you've got some important work to be done. How can I help?
139647:
Even in times of conflict with an external enemy we still find ourselves in competition with other “friendly” corporations. One such corporation is providing security for a repair outpost. They got that security contract by underbidding us. Go to the site, destroy their entire security force, then destroy the repair outpost. With such an abysmal failure on their record, they'll never get another security contract in this sector again.

And who knows, maybe we'll get the reconstruction contract for the replacement outpost as well.
139648:
As a matter of fact, I do. As I'm sure you're aware, even in times of conflict with an external enemy we still find ourselves in competition with other “friendly” corporations. One such corporation is providing security for a repair outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. They got that security contract by underbidding us. I want you to head out there, destroy their entire security force, then destroy the repair outpost. With such an abysmal failure on their record, they'll never get another security contract in this sector again.

And who knows, maybe we'll get the reconstruction contract for the replacement outpost as well.

So what do you say? Do you think you can handle this job? I can make it worth your while.
139649: I knew you couldn't hack it. Maybe you should look for a different line of work.
139650: Good. Now get out there and wreck something.
139651: You really are a ruthless one, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is always looking for pilots like you. Look me up again if you ever need work.
139652: Too bad. I guess I'll have to find someone with a stronger stomach or looser morals. You are dismissed.
139653: I take it from your inability to complete the job we discussed that you had second thoughts about it. I'm not paying you to grapple with your morals. Next time, just decline the job so that I can find someone with the guts to actually pull the trigger.
139654: When you didn't respond to my offer, I found someone willing to undertake the job. He did what we asked of him, but got caught in the process, implicating us in the attack. Amateur. I wish you'd been able to help us, because I know you'd have done the job right. Oh well, maybe next time.
139657: No problem. I'll do this job and sleep with a clear conscience.
139658: I've taken care of your little problem. Now pay up.
139659: I don't think I'm cut out for that kind of work, sorry.
139660: I've had second thoughts. I'm not going to do this job after all.
139661: Yes. Do you have an assignment for me?
139662: Head for your assigned patrol sector coordinates. Wait there and destroy any enemy ships that show up. Make sure none of them escape!
139663: As you may be aware, the Gallente Navy has been making increasingly bold reconnaissance patrols into Caldari space. This is unacceptable and must be stopped immediately. Unfortunately, given our own Navy's operational tempo, we don't have the forces to spare to cover every avenue of hostile approach. That's where you come in, {[character]player.name}. I want you to patrol an area where we've had reports of hostile recon patrols recently. Think you can handle that?

139677:
Recently a long-range reconnaissance patrol was sent out deep behind enemy lines. While trying to exfiltrate to friendly lines, our recon ship inadvertently jumped into the middle of a pitched battle. The ship and its cargo were lost. Go to the site of the battle, find the wreck of our reconnaissance ship, and salvage the data chips from the remains. This task will require the use of a Salvager module.

Beware that there may be other scavengers or interested parties in the area. Take whatever steps you feel are necessary to bring the data back safely.

While trying to exfiltrate to friendly lines, our recon ship inadvertently jumped into the middle of a pitched battle in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. 139692:

We could quadruple our security, but that might tip them off. Instead, I want you to go there and keep an eye out for them. If you see anything suspicious, you are authorized to destroy the vessel in question immediately. We don't want to take any chances.

Our team has cracked the enemy communications and found the information we need. It turns out our spy is alive and under heavy guard in a detention facility in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. We had no idea they even had a facility here; I'm not sure how they managed to sneak one there without us knowing, but that's not important. The spy's last reports hinted at him getting close to something very disturbing. The information he has could prove invaluable to us.

Our limited intel on the area has revealed it to be a high security facility. They obviously consider our man a high priority. I want you to break into the detention facility, fight your way to the prison and retrieve our man. Expect some serious resistance here.

The Sisters of EVE are a religious humanitarian aid organization. They believe that heaven resides on the other side of the EVE gate, and if they can get back through the gate, they will be able to talk to God. Allying their religion with science, they frequently experiment on the EVE gate, with the goal of one day unlocking its secrets.

The Sisters are politically neutral, with members from every faction. They have been providing aid to those in need since the Gallente-Caldari War. They have a number of stations set up outside of empire borders.
140115: A Caldari pilot who has been helpful to the Empire in the past was ambushed by Gallente ships and managed to limp away to the safe haven of a station run by the Sisters of EVE. Go make sure that the lingering Gallente ship that is waiting for her to leave will not be a problem.

She managed to reach a station operated by the Sisters of EVE, who provided her with help. However, her ship is still damaged, and there is a Gallente ship that is waiting to finish her off as soon as she leaves the station's shelter.

I would like you to assist her by making certain that the Gallente ship will no longer be a problem.

After all, what's the value of taking over territory if all your planets are uninhabitable? Of course, our foes have found counters to most of the known chemical agents. So the key to victory will be new compounds.

That's why I want you to acquire a big bunch of Augumene for us. The stuff is insanely toxic, hence its absence on the market. But in this case, its very toxicity is what we want to harness.

140250:
There are few who can deny the majestic beauty of an ice field: the slowly rotating towers of glistening blue-green ice set against the colder backdrop of the stars can give even the most jaded pilot pause. Yet such beauty hides a darker truth: if you are not prepared, an ice field can quickly become your very own sparkling graveyard.

While some ice fields can be found in Empire space, the rarer– and more profitable– ice ores are found in 0.0 space. As always, low sec can promise more LUX– or it can promise the dubious thrill of seeing your ship pounded into dust by eager pirates. Far too many inexperienced pilots have seen their mining barges blown apart-- with the hours and LUX needed to outfit them-- now so much vapor floating around their blinking pod.

Yet for most, the lure of the ice fields is too much to resist. With the sure promise of such treasures as Strontium Clathrates and Liquid Ozone, to name a few, the dangers of low sec will be dared. And even if it all ends in a fiery explosion, pilots can still enjoy the way their ship's destruction makes the ice sparkle all that more beautifully, if only for a few, rare seconds.
140251: {[character]player.name}, I need you to go and procure 10 units of a very particular ice-- Azure Ice, I believe, is what you're looking for on your scanner. I also need it within the next 24 hours, so get to that ice field!
140252: Cold Beauty: The Irresistible Danger of Ice Mining
140253:
I've been having a spot of bother filling an order, {[character]player.name}. It's starting to affect my usually sunny disposition. I'm hoping you can clear this off my docket, and bring the smile back to my face.

My client requires hydrogen isotopes to run her control tower, and she's getting a little snippy about the time it's taking me to provide it. She's even sent along a few assassins to vent her displeasure. No patience, that woman.

{[character]player.name}, I need you to procure 10 units of a very particular ice-- Azure Ice, I believe, is what you're looking for on your scanner; I can extract the hydrogen myself. I've lost a few good ships and a few incompetent pilots in the ice fields trying to fill this order, and I really need you to live up to your reputation, {[character]player.name}-- within the next 24 hours. Can I count on you, {[character]player.name}?

140275:

Now that the conflict between the Amarr Empire and the Minmatar Republic has heated up, though, we're getting pressure from both sides. The Minmatar have been pushing hard in some places, and now we've decided that it's time to push back.

We've been working with representatives of the Khanid Kingdom to give the Minmatar a surprise. The Republic has been building up forces in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. In exchange for some generous financial compensation, we've agreed to help the Khanids push the Minmatar out. But we need a good capsuleer to keep the light Minmatar escorts busy while we help the Khanids destroy the larger vessels.

Will you do it?

140279:
The Khanid Kingdom is a small empire of a dozen or so systems that was founded by the renegade Amarr Heir Khanid II. Rather than commit ritual suicide when he failed to attain the imperial throne, Khanid declared independence from the Empire. The next few years were spent fighting a rebellion by Khanid's brother and fellow heir Dakos, and turning back an invasion by the Empire.

Since then, Khanid's rule has continued, his small empire has prospered, and trade relations with his former imperial enemies have expanded considerably. The Kingdom acts as a small point of contact between the secretive people of Amarr and the rest of civilized space. Today, the kingdom's primary enemies are the Minmatar, who, despite Khanid II's secession, still see it as an ally of the hated Amarr Empire.

140292: Well, you gave it your best, {[character]player.name}. Keep telling yourself that. It'll ease the sting of cowardice you should be feeling.
140293:
A job, eh? Hm. Yeah, I've got something for you. Pretty urgent, too.

Seems the Amarr have been broadcasting holo-reels of their military "victory" over the Elder Fleet when that Sarum bitch returned to power. Thing is, we've found that someone has set up a broadcast hub to send the damned holos out here — into Minmatar space! I guess they're trying to intimidate us, or to play some kind of psychological war. Well, you know how happy that makes me. Which is to say, not at all.

Anyway, {[character]player.name}, I'd like you to head out there and blow that broadcast array of theirs to bits. Take your favorite ship, along with a couple friends, maybe, and head to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

Time to disrupt a lot of bedtime stories...
140295: Infiltrate the secret Amarr deadspace complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and destroy the communications hub found there.
140296:
A key element in sustaining an Empire is maintaining control, however illusory. This lesson of Imperial longevity has been much on the Amarr Empire's mind of late.

The Jovian War. The Minmatar Rebellion. Gallente interference. The Caldari threat. All of these and more have seemed to herald the twilight of the Empire, and even with the miraculous return of Heir Apparent Jamyl Sarum, many Amarr are skeptical. Faith can hold one for only so long, it seems.

The last thing the Amarr Empire needs now is civil unrest, and what better way to occupy the minds of its citizenry than a good, righteous war? To that end, Amarr Intelligence frequently provides footage of Amarr's victories over the rebellious Minmatar for an eager and appreciative public. The fact that certain critics claim much of the footage is (re)constructed by skilled holo-efx techs is irrelevant: All that matters is that the people are happy and not asking questions.

Because the last thing any Empire wants is people asking too many questions. The wrong questions can be hard to control.
140297: Well, you've got my interest: What's happened?
140298: This is getting way too hot for me, {[character]agentID.name}. To hell with the politics — break out the Fleet if you want that code bad enough.
140299:
You want me to take on the Angel Cartel? Here's an even better idea: you pay me for the holoreel job, and I walk away from this one.

Yeah… yeah, I like that idea better.
140300: I got a little singed, but the job's done. Here's the data chip — just wipe the Angel blood off and you're good to go.
140301: Now this is more like it! Consider that code acquired.
140302: Data Chip? Encryption Codes? Not in My Hand?
140305: Fine, {[character]player.name}. Some champion you turned out to be. You know, you could do with a new wardrobe. Something in yellow would be appropriate, I think.
140306: You are amazing, no lie — and it looks like we need to you keep it up: More trouble, it seems.
140307: I'm happy you're happy, {[character]player.name} — but the timer's ticking. Now go!
140308: Fine, just fine.  But a question before you go: How do you fit your tail between your legs inside that egg of yours? Is it kind of cramped? Or just kind of embarrassing?
140309:
Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and retrieve the data chip with the encryption codes from the Angel Cartel ship there, and then return to your agent with the chip. 
<font color = #EE3B3B>Be sure you check the timer for this mission; you won't have too long before the Angels are sure to clear out.</font>
140310:
Whatever their other gifts, the Amarr are very good at two things: piety and self-justification. Both of these qualities, but most assuredly the second, come in handy when one considers the issue of slavery.

Since slavery is a consistently inherent theme in their religious doctrine (and how can something be wrong if faith allows it?), the Amarr must contend at all times with the disgust other races feel toward slavery. Chief among their opponents are the Gallente, whose displeasure is undoubtedly fueled by the many transplanted Minmatar flooding their homeworlds and stations. In the halcyon days of the Empire, the Amarr would easily have dismissed such concerns — but recent history has brought to some Amarr, at least, both humility and prudence.

Yet the need for slaves has not diminished — and in fact, since the recent Elder Fleet "recovery" effort in Amarr space, that need has grown terribly. However, the Amarr tradition of collecting slaves has necessarily become problematic for those Heirs and Holders, who may face trade embargoes and similar punitive actions from other nations. So many Amarr look surreptitiously to more "independent" sources of slaves — sources who don't care for any optics outside of their own bank balances.
140312:
My techs here have come across some disturbing information. We were monitoring that holo-reel hub and its vicinity, and just before you neutralized the array, we intercepted a garbled message from a nearby Angel Cartel ship… sent to the Amarr homeworld. It was pretty broken up, but we did make out the words "Minmatar" and "payment." We must know more.

We've managed to track the Angel ship that made that broadcast to an outpost that's, surprisingly, not too far from here. We need the code to decrypt that message, and that ship seems our best bet.

Go to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and get that ship's log, no matter what it takes.

And you'll have to make it snappy, 'cause I'm pretty sure the Angels won't hang around there too long — you won't have much time once you accept this mission!
140313: Yeah, I'm up for it. What do we need done?
140314: I think I've done enough for the Minmatar people, don't you? It's someone else's turn to step up. I'm done with this job.
140315: If rescuing our own people from slavers isn't a job for the Republic Fleet, then what is? I'm not risking my ship because the navy refuses to do its job.
140316: I've returned with the rescued slaves. And I've wiped out every single Cartel ship involved in their abduction. You have to admit, {[character]agentID.name} — I am pretty awesome.
140317: There are no worse scum than slave raiders. It'll be my pleasure to wipe them from the stars.
140320:
You leave me speechless, {[character]player.name}. I would have thought rescuing your own people from slavery would be a priority. Obviously not….

I just don't know what more to say.
140321: I rather hope you're dead, {[character]player.name}, because there's no other excuse for allowing our people to be enslaved. I'd hate to think you just decided you couldn't be bothered.
140322: If blaming others helps you rationalize your cowardice, {[character]player.name}, then so be it. Take your "worthy self" and get out of my sight.
140323: I'd have to agree with your rather modest assessment, yes. You have served both the Republic Fleet and our people with honor. Such exemplary work deserves an appropriate reward. Enjoy, hero!
140324: Spoken like a true warrior, {[character]player.name}.  Now make those pirate dogs beg for mercy. And offer none.
140325: Fine. Know this, though: Your blatant selfishness may have condemned those poor souls to indentured servitude, or worse. Let that comfort you at night.
140326:
My techs decrypted the rest of that message, thanks to the code you recovered. It seems those Cartel ships you destroyed were part of a gang that've been moonlighting as freelance slave raiders. They're supplying the Amarr with slaves from outlying worlds! They've been abducting entire families living in isolated areas so the alarm won't be raised for weeks to come.

That ends now.

We've managed to track the Angel slaver ships to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, with — according to the message — a hundred of our people on board. We could send in the Fleet, but frankly they're still reeling, and they just might not get there in time. I need you to rescue those people, {[character]player.name}. Bring in whoever you need to help you on this one: Just get it done.
140328:
Eradicate all pirate ships at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, and then rescue the slaves from the Cartel ships.
