143293: After only being able to make off with a fraction of the civilians from their raid, The Seven were tracked back to their hideout.  Attacking them there should eliminate their local base of operations and allow for the remaining hostages to be rescued.
143294: There's hope yet for the small entrepreneur! ORE's dismissive attitude toward miner claims in that system has brought a lot of bad publicity on the corporation. Your efforts have gone a long way toward causing that.
143295:
The Seven? I was hoping it wasn't that particular gang again.

While we're very grateful that you managed to prevent most of the civilians from being kidnapped, there is still the issue of the ones that were taken. When they warped away from the last encounter, we were able to track them down and obtain the coordinates of that hideout. I'm prepared to grant you the authority, on behalf of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}, to hunt down these criminals. What do you say? Are you still willing to help?
143296: Great!  You should depart at once if you're going to catch the Seven before the hostages are moved to another facility.
143297: Whatever.  I'll find someone else to clean up your mess.
143298: Hey, I understand.  We all have priorities in life.  Mine just happen to be productivity, compassion, and loyalty, while yours appear to be somewhere between lethargy and unscrupulousness.
143299: It might be a good idea to maintain radio silence during this particular mission, don't you think?
143300: I'd flatter you with congratulations, but there's still work to be done.
143301: Phenod, the resident idiot of The Seven's organization, has stranded himself on his way to pick up some hostages.  With his DNA, a suitable transponder disguise can be forged allowing some undercover work against the gang.
143302:
One of those hostages you rescued turned out to be quite resourceful. While aboard the pirate's vessel, she hacked into its communication logs and discovered something interesting. One of The Seven's core members, a man named Phenod, has managed to strand himself in space on his way to pick up some victims that were kidnapped some time ago.

We have a golden opportunity here to not only strike a blow to The Seven, but recover some of our earlier losses as well. Head out to these coordinates at once and blast Phenod to pieces, but be sure to scrape some of his DNA off the front of your ship before returning. We'll use it to forge an identification transponder for your next mission.
143304: Am I going to have to take care of this myself?
143305: Seriously?  Phenod is too much for you to handle?  I've heard he's The Seven's resident idiot.
143306: Do you have a sample of Phenod's DNA yet?
143307: Stick around, there's more to do.
143308: Using Phenod's DNA to concoct a disguised transponder beacon, the shuttle provided by the agent should be large enough to retrieve the additional hostages and bring them to safety.  The only problem is that, if whoever shows up to drop off the hostages isn't fooled, the shuttle will be unable to respond.
143309:
I hope you didn't have too much trouble with Phenod.

Our engineers have completed the fake transponder and installed it in a shuttle, which is ready for you to take it to the rendezvous point. The story is that Phenod's ship was disabled and he's been forced to limp to the rendezvous point in an ordinary shuttle. I don't know who's going to meet you there, but it'll probably be another officer from The Seven, so try not to pick a fight. Remember, this shuttle is unarmed and doesn't have any real defenses, so if your disguise fails, you'll have to make a run for it.

Oh, and there's one last thing: That shuttle doesn't have the oxygen capacity to hold that many people for very long, so you won't be able to make it back here. We're sending a rescue vessel to linger nearby, but for obvious reasons it can't be anywhere inside sensor range of this meeting. Use the acceleration gate in the area to meet up with it and drop off the hostages.
143310: Not many capsuleers volunteer for this kind of duty outside the comforts of their preferred ship.  I admire your courage.
143311: So you've gotten this far only to give up now?
143312: Oh well, let's just hope CONCORD doesn't see you in that shuttle broadcasting a pirate faction signature.  Good luck!
143314: Now that was some really impressive flying, I have to admit!  The hostages are quite grateful to have been returned safely.  In fact, I have a message for you from one of them, if you can stick around for a minute or two.
143315: One of the hostages rescued during the previous mission has offered a reward for destroying Locced's ship and provided coordinates to his current location.
143316:
Here's the rescued hostage's message:

“Brave Capsuleer,

Allow me to offer my sincere thanks for your efforts to rescue me and my fellow hostages from the clutches of The Seven. If you would be interested, I've offered {[character]agentID.name} a sum of LUX to pay you in exchange for doing me a little favor.

During my time with The Seven, one of their officers was so cruel that I‘m inclined to seek revenge on a personal level. Seeing as you have become quite familiar with their organization and tactics, I can think of no one better suited for carrying out this task. Please destroy his ship for me.

If you‘re interested, the target‘s name is Locced and I happen to know where he‘ll be in the near future, as one of his lieutenants let the information slip during casual conversation when I was nearby.

Once again, thank you for freeing me from The Seven‘s clutches. I hope you find my offer appealing.“

Well, {[character]player.name}, what do you say?
143317: The former hostage will be very excited to hear you accepted the offer.  Here are Locced's coordinates.
143318: That former hostage is going to be heartbroken.
143319: I'm going to assume Locced beat you down like a helpless child, at least that's what I'm going to tell every other capsuleer I deal with from this point forward.
143320: The former hostage is eagerly awaiting news of your victory.
143321:
What am I, your receptionist? Here's another message from that hostage you rescued:

“Trustworthy Capsuleer,

It's going to take Locced quite a while to replace that ship. Well done, and thank you again for all of your efforts against The Seven.”
143322: Travel to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} here a disabled ship is in jeopardy. Save the crew by addressing whatever problem afflicts the vessel.
143323: {[character]player.name}, a mission of mercy needs your immediate attention. One of our ships has suffered an almost complete power loss near a spatial rift, and is adrift toward the anomaly. There's no time to lose. Get to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, find the ship, and help get it operational again.
143324: {[character]player.name}, what are you doing? Our people are going to die out there. “Can't do it?” You mean “Won't do it”! Bloody pirate!
143325: Good. You have no time to lose.
143326: What are you doing? Our people are dying in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. There's no time for this!
143327: Good work. Your efforts have not gone unnoticed. We'll try to get that model upgraded to avoid this kind of problem again.
143328: What? Maybe I didn't make myself clear. There are lives at stake!
143329: I should have known. Your kind disgusts me.
143330: What? You're telling me profit is more important than innocent lives?
143331: You're doing the right thing. Countless lives depend on you.
143332:
We have an unfortunate situation on our hands. One of our officers has apparently been targeted by a Mordu's assassination squad. We aren't sure who hired them, but we suspect that it's an internal dispute, i.e. they were hired by someone inside the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}. We need the bounty hunters eliminated ASAP, before they are able to do any permanent damage. We would rather that the {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name}'s good relationship with the Mordus Legion will not be tainted by this incident, so keep it clean and leave no evidence of the battle behind if possible. The Mordus Legion are a powerful mercenary organization that we sometimes rely on, but obviously that does not deter all of their members from targeting our people if the price is right...

Just a word of warning though, these Mordus goons are no laughing matter. Don't underestimate them.
143333:
One of our patrols spotted a Mordu's Legion strike force not far from here. We're not certain about their intentions, but we'd like you to take them out just in case. Those damned Mordu's assassination squads have been known to murder our members in the past, so we keep a good eye on them. We know their exact location this time, and I'd like you to take them out before they know what hit them. I'm counting on you {[character]player.name}.

Just a word of warning though, these Mordus goons are no laughing matter. Don't underestimate them.

143343: Unless you've been sent here by one of my subordinates, I have nothing for you.  If you're interested, you can find them in Data Centers in Kamokor, Ahtulaima and Saikanen.

143345: Unless you've been sent here by one of my subordinates, I have nothing for you.  If you're interested, you can find them in Data Centers in Muer, Abenync and Ekuenbiron.

143347:
There's a difference between being taken seriously and letting the inmates run the asylum. Diplomacy must resume, even if to only keep things just below war being declared.

It's a strange game, friend. I don't think even the diplomats fully understand it. Still, this is one of those times diplomats are useful again.

Take our envoy over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. From there he will meet with the Gallente envoy to begin non-public negotiations. If all goes well, the situation will simply vanish from the public's consciousness and life will continue as normal.
143348: This situation snowballed. Diplomacy must resume, even if to only keep things just below war being declared. Take our envoy over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. From there he will meet with the Gallente envoy to begin non-public negotiations. If all goes well, the situation will simply vanish from the public's consciousness and life will continue as normal.
143349:
We need to move fast. The situation is evolving in unexpected ways. No no, don't sit down. I'll explain this as fast as I can.

While you were out on your last assignment, Ekire himself was mortally wounded in an assassination attempt by unknown assailants. We suspect Wiyrkomi, of course - they have the most to gain from his death, both politically and pragmatically speaking. Likewise, if he dies we stand to take a massive political blow.

Ekire is currently at the Egonics Inc. Development Studio at Parchanier V, bleeding severely and fading fast. Due to a rare blood condition he contracted in an Umokkan jungle while serving as a Legion marine a decade back, transfusion via normal means would kill him. For the procedure to be at all possible he needs an aortal purifier, a seldom-used piece of medical equipment which they don't have at that particular station's med bay.

I need you to head out to Auderne immediately, to the Poteque Pharmaceuticals Biotech Production plant there, and pick up what may be the only aortal purifier available in this whole damn constellation, then bring it out to the doctors in Parchanier. His life - and our success in our campaign here - may very well depend on your speed in this matter.

Go! Fly swiftly.
143350: Green Arisite is relatively worthless because of the high costs of reprocessing; one is far better off mining Gneiss instead. As a result, you won't find the former ore on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Arisite at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Green Arisite is shown by enabling "Gneiss".
143351: You met MIO investigator Kandus Sandar.
143352: Kandus Sandar, an MIO agent in Nahyeen, requires aid.
143353: Excellent. There are at least three survivors who escaped in life pods. Find them, and we'll be able to figure out what went wrong. And be careful out there - it's an experimental ship, and we don't know what kind of threat it might pose.
143354: Have you rescued the crew of The Paryi yet? I've got some very important people breathing down my neck about this.
143355: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.
143356: That's your call. Honestly, I don't blame you for backing out now - I'm not superstitious, but this situation spooks me out.
143357:
Dr. Ateshi has provided proof that The Anomaly is active and dangerous. The experimental warp drive successfully opened a wormhole, but it was unstable and the resulting radiation fried the crew's equipment, and their brains. They've been trapped in the darkest parts of space for two decades, slowly succumbing to the sickness - there's nothing human left about them. Now that they're back in our space, the radiation is a risk not just to us but everything for hundreds of kilometers around.

My superiors have determined that it's not worth the risk of retrieving the warp drive; you need to destroy the ship entirely before the damage spreads. Fortunately, we know where they went: They jumped into the middle of a rogue drone hive. Dr. Ateshi thinks they're trying to feed off the rogue drones' power to recharge. If you can get her to one of the surrounding ships, she can jam their equipment and make them vulnerable.
143358: I'm so relieved to hear that. Keep your wits about you and you should do just fine. Remember, don't bother shooting until Dr. Ateshi has deactivated their shield rechargers.
143359: Have you destroyed The Anomaly yet? It's essential that you do it before it has the chance to jump away again!
143360: Shame about Dr. Ateshi, but she knew the risks. Good job - you've earned everything coming to you.
143361: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?
143362: After coming so far? Do you know what they're going to do to me when they find out you quit?
143363: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.
143364: Can't say I blame you, though I'm going to have to let you go for now. Getting these kinds of jobs filled can bring an agent like me to the notice of important people, you know? Talk to you later.
143365: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?
143367: Good job, {[character]player.name}. Enjoy your reward, and the limelight for being a hero to those folks – you've earned it. You should know, however, that the folks you didn't save have already made it very clear that they're not happy with you.
143369: The Prophet of the Seventh Sphere
143373: Since the scouting party is dead and gone, we've got the primary fleet hanging around in space and practically begging for someone to blow them to pieces. Seeing as how you did such a thorough job with their scouts, you were naturally our first choice for taking on their big guns. Once you're finished with them, Okelle won't have anyone to help him except his brother. And once our interrogators are done with Okelle, he'll have given us all the information we need to hunt down Martogar. It's only a matter of time - that is, unless the primary fleet manages to deploy more scouts and continue their murderous rampage, so you better get on your way to stop them.
143374:
I'm glad I can rely on you for something like this, {[character]player.name}. It seems so many capsuleers are becoming more risk-averse these days. It's a mindset I simply can't understand.

Remember that our cargo is precious and there is zero room for error here. If that formula goes missing, so will my desire to work with you. That is our LUX, and the entirety of our business together. Prepare yourself accordingly.
143375:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places and go to "Bookmarks." Then right-click on the objective item (the relic) and choose "Set Destination." Then go to your ship's control panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate star system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click on the relic and select "Warp to within 0." Once you've arrived at the location, look at your Overview and find the cargo container; right-click on it and select "Approach." Once you've approached to within 2500 meters, right-click the cargo container and select "Open." A window will now open, displaying the container's contents. Click and drag the relic into your cargo hold. Now return with it to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name} for your reward.
143376:
Hmm... Yes, I do have some work for you.

Although the Cartel usually has a firm grip over the criminal strata in our system, Sansha's Nation has been poking its ugly nose in here of late-- which is perfectly fine with us. In fact, watching the two outlawed organizations duke it out is one of my favorite pastimes. If we're lucky, it will give both sides a good bruising, which will only work in our favor.

Of course, there's also bad news. An InterBus ship traveling to {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} got caught in the middle of one of the pirate warzones. The ship was damaged beyond repair and can neither warp out nor navigate away from the crossfire. Your task is to rescue the ship's crew. Please retrieve them before any more harm is done; they're already scared out of their minds. The faster you get this done, the better.

Oh, and before you leave I'd like to give you a word of advice. When you venture into this particular deadspace area, the warpgates are not locked, which gives you the chance to avoid most of the conflict, if you're not up to the fight. However, I'm told only frigate and destroyer-class ships can activate the first gate.

Good luck.

143386:
Quitting a mission invariably results in a loss of faction standing; it is almost always in a character's best interest to complete all missions he or she accepts.

However, a character may freely decline a mission when it is first offered, as long as it isn't one of those rare "storyline" missions; after that, declining another mission within four hours of the first does result in a loss of standing. Still, in general, a capsuleer's career is usually long and eventful enough that a few such minor hits to standing may not be too large a price.
143387:
Your last assignment is to scan down a Gas cloud. We've created an artificial cloud pocket for you, and while you'd usually reap it with a Gas Cloud Harvester, our only concern is that you make it through to the second area and bring back the Proof of Discovery document.

The materials found inside these clouds are used to make biochemical enhancers known as boosters. It is a dangerous industry, populated by dangerous people. You're safe this time, but Gas clouds will occasionally be inhabited by pirates. Stay alert if you're on the prowl for them.

As soon as you accept the mission, we'll provide you with the passkey into the second area.

143407:
Banidine is normally all but worthless, so real miners don't usually bother with the stuff. Still, I've found a buyer who's willing to take whatever we can mine. So, get me 20,000 units of Banidine and I'll make it worth your while.

There's an asteroid field near here that's lousy with the stuff – I've bookmarked it for you. Get back as soon as you can and I'll arrange a little bonus.

Remember to fit a decent miner to your ship before you go. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, loading the "Mining" default overview will show all ores. If you're familiar with creating custom overview settings, Banidine is shown by enabling "Veldspar".
143408: You've destroyed a pirate ring that would have taken us months to work through. High marks all around.
143409:
Harkan?! Terrus Harkan is the traitor? Harkan, former head of Lord Miyan's security and hero of the countless military campaigns, is the traitor?

This is very bad.
143410: Yes, don't worry.  I've no more tricks up my sleeve, you'll definitely get what you want when you're done with this simple courier job.
143411: I need you to help out. There is fierce fighting going on in a nearby system and we have marines here that need to be moved out there as soon as humanly possible. Are you willing to help our cause?
143412: The local news recently aired a story on poor immigrants in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Apparently some of the families have fallen on hard times and lack the funds to even buy the most basic necessities.  A few concerned citizens in {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name} asked me to have these clothes delivered to the needy in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, which they can make use of.  I'd like you to make the first leg of the trip, which is to drop off the goods at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.  Officials at the station will take care of the rest.
143413: Take these people to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't tell anyone they were here.
143414: Deliver the secure coded package for your agent.
143415:
Well, it's my sister. I mean, I remembered her birthday this time, I swear. I planned out the gift, got it ordered in advance — and it was not cheap, let me tell you. I found a specialty perfume maker, and it turns out my sister likes the smells of really damn expensive things. And of course the fancy-pants perfumer has a ridiculous waiting list. But I got everything done in time!

I just need you to deliver it. I'll pay you, okay?
143416:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in the middle of constructing an outpost in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Our engineers there claim to lack a few loads of construction blocks to finish the work, and I was asked to deliver some blocks to that station.

Could you please take the material straight to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}? Our people in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} will take care of retrieving them from your hangar there for the construction project.
143417: They'll offload the chemicals immediately. You should be fine on your ship. They'll be gassing every corner of the structure, though.
143418:

143419:
Now what I need you to do is deliver a batch of veldspar ore to a location not far from here. I was supposed to drop off the batch there for one of my clients, but Gatti's attack 'complicated' matters. I dare not leave my current location, if an agent of the Zhara family or Kazka Bandits spots me, I'm done for.

I managed to smuggle the ore out of the asteroid belt during my escape, so as long as you can bring an industrial over here then you're all set to go.

143426:
I have not been very impressed by your performance, and as a result this will be your last task for me. I have another student arriving soon, somebody who I'm hoping will not fail me like you have. Everything must be in order when he arrives, and for that to happen I'm going to need you to bring me some electronic parts. Replacing and rebuilding the things that were stolen from me will take some time.

Even though you are not competent enough to become my disciple, I do appreciate your interest. If you complete this quickly, maybe I'll reward you with a little bit extra.

143436:
We've got a shipment of vaccines that need to be delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} in a hurry. I'm willing to provide a substantial bonus if they're delivered right away. Regardless, the meds need to be delivered soon, though.

Be sure to move the medicine into your cargo hold before you set out. And note the hasty delivery required — you don't have much time!
143437:
Well, you're pretty green, by the look of you, but I've got no choice. You may have heard all the rumors. The entire frontier is buzzing with reports that we're pretty much at war with the Amarrians. I can't say either way, for sure, but I do know that all this war talk has led to some big headaches when it comes to commercial traffic and trade-route management. Passenger liners are all booked, haulers have been pre-empted by the military or by wealthy clients... god, it's just a mess out there.

Anyway, as you may have seen, the docks here at {[location]agentStationID.name} are filled to overflowing with tons of goods, and we can't seem to find enough transport to get them to their destinations. I need to get some of this stuff out of here.

Ah, here: we've got a shipment of vaccines that need to be delivered to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} in a hurry. I'm willing to provide a substantial bonus if they're delivered right away. Regardless, the meds need to be delivered soon, though.

Say the word and you can move the stuff into your cargo hold. Can you do it?
143438: The {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} station manager has reported a lack of mono-cell batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. Deliver the batteries to them as quickly as possible.
143439:
"The deal," as you so quaintly put it, my young friend, is this: The station manager of {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} recently reported to us a serious lack of mono-cell batteries in their supply depot, a situation that could result in a temporary shutdown of the entire station. We need to help them out, and I'd like you to deliver the necessary goods to them.

Simple enough, eh? Well, are you interested or not? I know of several others who would happily take this offer in your stead.
143440: It's tough to quit smoking when you've got a warehouse full of cigarettes within arm's reach. Take every crate of that crap you can find in that warehouse over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and leave it there. Quickly, before I change my mind!
143441:
A convoy of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} ships stumbled upon a stash of viral agents in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name} while passing through the system. They dropped it off here so that a specialist can take a look at it and perhaps trace it to a particular individual or corporation. Now that they're done, I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for further research.

Don't worry about getting busted by customs for transporting the viral agents: We've cleared the matter with them and they'll be expecting you.
143442: One commodity we all have a hard time living without is oxygen. One of our buyers is on a station that's close to running out of air, so I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and give them  a bit more.
143443: A friend of mine, Professor Tsulmeki, has asked me to safely transport his most recent graduating class to a seminar. Could you go over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me? Bring them there on time; I don't want them to be late.
143444: A friend of mine, Professor Tsulmeki, has asked me to safely transport his entire research team to an important seminar. Could you go over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me? Bring them there on time; I don't want them to be late.
143445: Deliver these crates of long-limb roes to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}  station.
143446: We've been having some trouble with deliveries ending up at incorrect destinations. I guess these shipping companies can't be trusted to do their job properly, so I need you to fill in for them. Take these holoreels to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I will reward you for the effort.
143447: Have you seen the price of oil around here lately? It's absurd! Our clients are demanding more, but all we've got is the synthetic stuff, so take a load of it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
143448: We've been having some trouble with deliveries ending up at incorrect destinations. I guess these shipping companies can't be trusted to do their job properly, so I need you to fill in for them. Take these holoreels to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I will reward you for the effort.
143449: Somebody broke into my brother's home yesterday and stole his entire gun collection. He'll get into heaps of trouble with his superiors if they find out, so I want you to help him make the problem go away. Fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off a new set of weapons. I'll modify the ID codes on the guns, and nobody will suspect a thing.
143450: My friend is getting married. We need entertainment for his bachelor party tomorrow, but I can't just show up with the dancers myself. Take these "performers" to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Be sure to get them there on time so we can start the fun!

143452: A short while ago, we had a huge problem with rodents that required us to hire an army of janitors. Now that the job's done, however, we need to reallocate these people to a place where they could be more effective. Take them to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop them off for me.

143456:
Well, our little gambit worked. The bigwig's been driven out of Wiyrkomi and a blow's been struck for the little guy. Thanks so much for your help.

One last favor, if you will. Some of our guys are founding an environmentalist education facility on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and they need some construction materials brought over. You think you could do this for me? I'll pay you well.
143457:
I need a shipment of Silicate Glass delivered to this station as soon as possible. It's currently stored in one of our warehouses in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}; I'll give you the coordinates, of course. Just warp to our outpost, navigate to the warehouse, and pick up the shipment, and then return it to {[location]agentStationID.name}. Simple, ain't it?

Just make sure you keep a lookout for any suspicious activity. You can't be too careful these days.
143458:

143459: Looks like food supplies are dwindling fast at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I think people are consuming a lot more than they were before. Take them a shipment of frozen food so we can feed the hungry.
143460: One commodity we all have a hard time living without is oxygen. One of our buyers is on a station that's close to running out of air, so I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and give them  a bit more.
143461: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  and retrieve the missing war dead. Destroy all Caldari standing in your way.
143462: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and clear the area for the humanitarian convoy.
143463:
Just when you think scars from the first Gallente-Caldari War begin to heal, something comes along and the old wounds reopen. We recently intercepted chatter about a missing contingent of Federation soldiers from that conflict who were recently recovered. They were stranded out in a 'roid field after engaging the enemy. Supplies ran out. Neither side came to the rescue.

It's a depressing story, sure, but there's a happy ending if you want to be a part of it. The Federation is willing to pay for secure, respectful transport for our war dead so they can finally be laid to rest in their respective homeworlds. This may sound easy, but it's not. The Caldari have also become aware of the battle site, and already have forces onsite. They refuse to allow us a proper retrieval.

You must go to the battle site and clear out the Caldari forces. Remember, they are invaders still, and recovering our soldiers is of paramount importance.
143465: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.
143466: Glad to have you onboard. I appreciate that you're willing to do this for the Gallente people. Symbols are important in these politically volatile times.
143467: Good flying, egger. Thanks to you, we'll be able to put these soldiers to rest. It's long overdue.
143468: Well, they've waited this long. They can wait a little longer yet, I guess.
143469:
We need someone to escort a convoy running humanitarian aid into {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Well, mostly humanitarian aid. We're moving medicine and food, as well as aid workers from the Sisters of EVE. But, there're also military personnel and equipment hidden among those ships. There's a big operation planned in that system, and our forces will need all the help that they can get.

Essentially, there's sensitive cargo onboard, and not everybody needs to know about it. We're posing this convoy as a peaceful operation to keep the State off our backs, but that doesn't mean other groups would be interested in the convoy as a potential target. We don't want to lose it, and we certainly don't want to lose it to someone like the Syndicate or the Serpentis. Unfortunately, we don't have a lot of time before these things are needed, so please forgive me for omitting classified details. This is one of their “blanket operations,” whatever that means. We need you to make sure the coast is clear and that the convoy makes it to their destination safely.
143471: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.
143472: That's all right. We can find other pilots if you don't like this job. Thanks for your time.
143473: “When you made a mistake as a child and you were in a rush to hide it, what did you do? You covered it with a blanket and hoped that nobody noticed. Sometimes, we never grow out of this line of thinking.” –Sister Evetelle Boun, organizer of Operation Hope.
143474: You'll be joining them in the most dangerous leg of their journey, right in the middle of a remote outpost. I can't give you many details about this place, though. Push through this deadspace pocket and make sure the convoy gets to their destination. More instructions will follow when you get there.
143475: You actually lost a few ships, but things could have been much worse if you hadn't been there. We'll consider this matter closed, though it looks like the navy will disavow any knowledge of this event ever taking place.
143477: Destroy the Blood Raider installation and any ships trying to defend it. Bring back any tourists that are somehow still alive and in one piece. Remember, the Blood Raiders treat their victims like cattle to be drained and consumed. Therefore, search any cargo containers you discover. Each ship may have its own supply.
143478:
In the past several months, several cruise ships carrying close to 100,000 Amarr citizens have vanished without a trace. Of course, we first believed these disappearances to be accidents. We enlisted the help of several LUX-strapped capsuleers to poke around neighboring systems and scan the planets and moons for something.

One of these pilots discovered a Blood Raider installation in a system three jumps from the last known transport ship disappearance. Over the local comms channels, this brave pilot overheard the Raiders refer to it as a "Blood Farm."

We know now that the ships were hijacked and our citizens taken to this installation. There, they were systematically butchered.

I need you to go to this Blood Farm and eliminate anything that even smells like a Blood Raider operation. Don't stop until every last heretic has been utterly and completely destroyed. If there are any tourists still alive, bring them home.
143479: Make sure that the Blood Farm can never be used to massacre our people ever again.
143480: We can't let them massacre any more of our citizens. Get to that station and wipe it from existence.
143481: Too much Amarr blood for you, eh?
143482: I understand. Defending the blood of our ancestors is a serious task. Most capsuleers simply cannot find the strength for that type of commitment.
143483: So few left alive. I can't imagine the horrors they faced. Thank you for your service. Now I must inform the families of those who didn't make it.
143485: Stop the dissidents' fleet by destroying every last one of them.
143486:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.
143487:
Perhaps you know the history of Further Foodstuffs? It provides food and supplies to both the Sarum Family and the Ardishapur Family, as well as to the Imperial Navy. Some dissidents, however, believe that this organization denies the military essential supplies that are necessary in the continuing struggles against our enemies.

Some of these low-life dissidents are attempting to disrupt the food supply to the royal families who run this corporation as a way of emphasizing their belief systems. How the scum were able to procure a fleet of ships is beyond my understanding. Perhaps they had help from members of the military who actually believe their propaganda? Regardless, they have amassed a great deal of firepower. If they hurt Further Foodstuffs, they hurt themselves. Does that make any sense to you?

Eliminate this rag-tag fleet.
143488: Time is of the essence. Get going, {[character]player.name}.
143489: Better now than later. At least I still have time to find someone dependable.
143490: Are you kidding me? I spent a great deal of time searching for a good pilot.
143492: Good job. Now the two most prominent families in the Empire (and our hard-working military, of course) won't feel the loss of their favorite delicacies.
143494: Further Foodstuffs is a small agricultural company jointly owned by the Ardishapur and Sarum families. The products of Further Foodstuffs are mostly used by the subjects of these two families, while what little surplus is left is sold on the open market. This has curbed the expansion opportunities of the company, though it means the fleets of Ardishapur and Sarum will never lack for food.
143495:
Apparently, a rival corporation is afraid of our rapid growth in the field of starship design. An “associate” of ours has informed us that a shipment of datacores heading to one of our research stations is to be intercepted by a fleet of Guristas mercenaries. What's disturbing is that an Amarr corporation has allegedly hired the pirates to do this dirty work. If that's true, there is a major shift in philosophy among our adversaries, both in the boardroom and in space. We need more information before we can act upon this.

We want you to intercept and eliminate the Guristas threat. Find out, if you can, who is behind this. What we need is proof that our rivals are pulling their strings or that they have nothing to do with this whatsoever.
143496: A job well done, friend! Here is that reward I promised.
143497:
It appears the Gallente have been making hostile moves again in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. They've been continuously launching attacks from a command vessel somewhere in a deadspace pocket. Our scouts have located the Federation admiral responsible for these raids and now we just need her taken care of.

We've dealt with this thing before, so we're confident that removing her from the picture will disrupt the rest of the Gallente operations in our area. The only issue is that the Navy won't be able to mobilize against her in time – they're the Navy after all, not a hit squad. I've been asked to recruit a capsuleer if possible, so we can bypass internal military procedures altogether.

That's where you come in {[character]player.name}. We need you to travel over to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enter the deadspace pocket our scouts have found, then kill the commander and her fleet.

She'll undoubtedly be back at some point even if your mission is successful. The Gallente are a persistent enemy, so after you've killed her, leave the body in the communication array she's been coordinating the forces out of. That should send a message. It might even spook her into seeking reassignment elsewhere, away from our corporation's space.
143498: Coward! I knew I shouldn't have trusted you.
143499:
Good to see you again, {[character]player.name}. We've got something you'd be perfect for.

143500: Excellent. I have uploaded the coordinates to your journal.
143501: I thought a patriot like you would be up for this. I'll leave your name out of my report to the Navy, but I am a little disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
143502: I'm afraid your name was already put forward to deal with this. This won't reflect well on you, {[character]player.name}.
143503: The admiral isn't going to stay in that location for very long. Take her out as quickly as you can.
143504: Great work, {[character]player.name}. Intel places her at a cloning station deep inside Federation space. I imagine it will be a while before she tries that move again, and if she does, you've left a reminder on how it will end.
143505: A hefty award awaits you upon successful completion of this mission.
143506: Great to hear. I've uploaded the coordinates.
143507: I'm surprised that someone like you would be afraid to take on a few rogue miners.
143508: I will have to find someone else more capable, then. I'm surprised you couldn't handle this, {[character]player.name}.
143509:
Within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} , citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further.

Slip past the Navy forces from their rear flank and destroy the Gallente command ship and its escorts.. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in.
143510: Great work; hopefully those thieves won't come back any time soon.
143511:
Sometimes it's easy to forget we're at war with the Gallente. Maybe not for you, of course, since it's you capsuleers who are doing most of the fighting, but for the rest of us things can seem awfully “business as usual” at times.

I'm saying this because we've had a development recently; something that's reminded a lot of senior people there's a war still going on. They've asked me to scout for capsuleers willing to deal with this situation, and that request has brought you to me, {[character]player.name}.

We have credible intel that sometime within the next week the Gallente Federation will officially claim sovereignty over the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and relocate an entire Navy division to support this claim. They will justify these actions by citing a recent worker's riot as proof of “a desire for democracy”. In reality, they just want to inflame the few unhappy people further and cost our entire corporation massive amounts of LUX in the process. They have no desire to genuinely help anyone but themselves.

The Federation has moved a division of their Navy into the system, and if we don't forcibly push them out soon the riots could escalate further. We must do everything we can to avoid a repeat of the Brothers of Freedom. The State has seen enough high-profile dissenters in recent years; yet another would not help our people. We obviously cannot allow this claim to ever happen, or for this Federation task force to gain any momentum whatsoever.

We need you to slip past the Navy forces and destroy the Gallente command ship leading them. This will throw the rest of the division into disarray momentarily, and at that point, the Caldari Navy will move in. We've discovered a deadspace route that will allow you to strike the command ship and its escorts from a rear flank. They shouldn't even see you coming.
143512:
I knew I was right to choose you for this. I've uploaded the command vessel's location to your journal.

I'd expect a difficult battle, {[character]player.name}. You're about the draw the attention of an entire Federation Navy division. You will likely have to fight your way through to the commander once they realize you've breached.
143513: I set this task aside just for you, and you repay me by throwing it back in my face? We're done here.
143514: You've made us both look bad, {[character]player.name}, and if we don't stop that force, the entire State will look even worse. We do not have the luxury of failing. Someone more reliable will have to be found to replace you.
143515: The Navy is waiting on you to take out that command vessel. As soon as you do, they'll make their move.
143516: Great job {[character]player.name}. We've already taken care of most of the forces in one decisive sweep. The Federation will surely be on the retreat soon.
143518:
Formerly an extremist labor movement in the State, the Brothers of Freedom led a widespread revolt against corporate security forces on a number of Caldari planets in YC 109 – some time before Tibus Heth's vastly more successful revolt of a similar nature -- after 65,000 protesters were killed by Caldari paramilitary forces while trying to force their way onto a CEP station in the New Caldari system. After months of dogged pursuit by Caldari authorities, the riots were put down and most of the leaders were killed or arrested.

Some of the leadership, including the ringleader Melarius Torvil, did manage to escape the final Caldari Navy operation that crushed the Brothers' movement. Torvil and a small group of associates fled to the Minmatar Republic and applied for asylum from Caldari persecution, which was granted by the late President Midular's Gallente-friendly government.

Today, though they have been largely eliminated as a major force in the State, the Brothers of Freedom continue to spread anti-corporate propaganda and speak out against the CEP's government in the Gallente Federation and the Minmatar Nation, as well as outlying State settlements and facilities.
143519: A Minmatar merc plans to kidnap an Amarr young noble, so we need you to take him out before he can even make the attempt.  We know where he is preparing his plan.  You need to get in and dispose of him before he can even make his attempt. . He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds.
143520:
A confidential informant has warned us of an impending kidnapping attempt on a young noble by a notorious Minmatar mercenary. One of my associates, who owes me a lifetime worth of favors, discovered the plot during a card game. The merc's mouth and ego are both the size of New Eden itself. He talked openly about his plan without a second thought. We need your help in stopping him before he can carry out his plans.

His staging ground is at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Find and kill him with any and all means at your disposal. He's a crafty SOB, so expect not just a fight, but some unorthodox challenges when he realizes you're on to him. He's especially fond of drawing pursuers into hazardous clouds. Odds are good he'll have some ex-Navy Minnies flying back-up. He might be a braggart, but he's still a paranoid merc. Be careful.
143521: Too tough for you, eh?  This merc has defeated greater men than you, so don't let it hurt your ego too much.
143522: The merc's sneaky.  He will use every trick he knows to escape.  Keep your eyes open for clues he may leave behind!
143523: I have to find a braver pilot than you, apparently.
143525: A significant number of Minmatar make their living on the darker side of the law, acting as pirates, smugglers and peddlers in all kinds of illegal goods. Many of the larger criminal groups in the world of EVE are run by Minmatar.
143526: The Amarr Empire thanks you for your assistance in this matter. Please use all speed and discretion in apprehending this degenerate.
143527: Great job, {[character]player.name}.  The Amarr Empire is in your debt.
143528: Still nothing from the maintenance team.  Advise me on your status.
143529: It had to be done.  We'll get another gate built out there and a military presence to protect it.  In the meantime, the citizens at the listening post will have to make due with the supplies they have.  Rest assured that we will do everything we can to get back to them as quickly as possible.
143530: Damn, just what I need.  Another political firestorm.  I had better find a way to fix this quickly.
143531: Very well.  I will find someone else.
143532:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.

You have your orders. Will you execute them to the best of your ability?
143533: As to those citizens stationed at the outpost, yes, they will be cut off from all outside contact until a new acceleration gate can be built.  The good news is that the outpost is equipped with a Stealth Emitter Array that will keep it hidden until we can return.  The not-so-good news is that those citizens could experience some long term side effects from the energies emitted by the array, but they knew the risks when they signed on.  Secrecy is paramount, both from a political and a military perspective.
143534: Excellent.  Remember, this operation is classified as top secret.  You are not to discuss it with anyone.
143536: A portion of the fleet is preparing a set of protracted war games  in the next few days. There was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about. Collect the custom circuitry from the production line in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The level of piracy in the area is unknown.
143537: I don't have anything else for you {[character]player.name}. What are you waiting for?
143538: You're kidding. This is one disaster after another.
143539: You were attacked? What would they want with training drone AI ? Wonderful, now we'll have to hold up the war games   for a security check of the entire shipment. I didn't realize Angel Cartel could be subtle. Given how this went for them, maybe they should stick to the direct approach.
143540: Well so much for all that wasted time.
143541: Production for all types of goods can be found in all corners of New Eden. Every so often, though, something of a specific design is required that must be produced from a specific area. Sometimes this is due to patents, sometimes it's more to do with a sudden requirement for obsolete or cutting edge equipment.  Desperation on the part of the buyer can lead to major holes in market security.
143543: I'll thank you later. Please get going.
143544: The Blood Raider Covenant is a particularly gruesome sect of the generally reviled Sani Sabik cult. While some modern Sani Sabik rituals use blood in some manner or another, the Covenant places particular value on the blood of cloned humans, and they are utterly ruthless in obtaining it, regularly boarding other spacecraft and abducting all aboard. From their base in Delve they launch lightning-fast raiding parties and surprisingly well-coordinated incursions deep into Empire space in pursuit of their goals.
143545: Move quickly, {[character]player.name}. Every hour that passes means more profit lost.
143546:
I'm glad to see you made it over, {[character]player.name}. I have a problem with some Gallente miners that I think you'd be perfect for.

The Gallente have set up another mining operation near one of our asteroid belts. They bring in semi-mobile reprocessing stations and then mine the location dry. You have to recognize this as just another act of war, {[character]player.name}. {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has lost millions of LUX to these Federation parasites. It's almost as damaging as a direct attack, but it doesn't draw the sort of military response an overt assault would, which is why we need capsuleer assistance to deal with this quickly.

We know they've set up mining outpost at one of the smaller deadspace asteroid pockets {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} frequents. They do this in the hope that nobody will come after them. I need you to send the Federation a message that they're wrong – that the State will pursue them every time. You must show them that there's no profit to be made from illegally mining belts we have claimed.

Go to the outpost and destroy absolutely everything; all the miners and any reprocessing stations you see. Level the place entirely. The loss of personnel and equipment will set them back and send a clear message to stick to their own space.
143547:
