143548: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, drop the band off at their manager's station, and take care of the pirates.
143549:
Have you ever heard of the band Quantum Entanglement? They're a heavy metal rock opera group with a theatric, costumed stage presence. Seriously, they're all the rage among the Federation's youth. The front man is none other than Halo Axegrinder, who was one of the founding members of Starved Fedo. Remember them?

Okay, personally I can't stand that garbage, but billions of fans can't be wrong, right? Anyway, their manager is one of my old school chums and he's asked me for a personal favor. He says they thrive on adrenalin, and since most of their songs are about war, he thinks they might be inspired by experiencing a little combat action.

Coincidentally, I've got a little pirate attack that needs to be dealt with in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system; it's a task I would usually allocate to some rookie capsuleer far below your standing with the corporation. If you're packing the kind of firepower I think you are, you should be able to take this installation down without breaking a sweat. Let a few hits bounce off of your defenses to give these guys the ride of their lives and that should give them enough inspiration for a lifetime of edgy, hard-hitting chart-toppers. I think that's the right terminology.
143550: Thank you for doing this. Entertainment is becoming more and more important to the citizens of the Federation, and it's widely believed that whatever troubles may befall us, we'll overcome them based on our willingness to defend our culture.
143551: Well, thanks for your time. I'll just have to tell their manager to hold on while I find another reputable pilot. Lucky me.  You cap-pilots are common these days, but not ones I'd be willing to work with.
143552: What went wrong? You've put me in a spot here. I can't say I appreciate this but it's not like I can do anything about it.
143553: Are they getting on your nerves yet?
143554:
Outstanding work, egger. The label was still willing to pay your fee, and the producer was recovered and brought up on charges.

On a side note, the entire band was psyched about what you did. I think you inspired a real creative explosion in them, and I hope we can look forward to better music.
143556: This heavy metal rock opera band was made famous by their first album's cover, which depicted two naked individuals engaging in sexual intercourse while floating in space without spacesuits. Gallente politicians tried to have the album, called Unprotected, banned. Not because of the adult content, they claimed, but because it promoted unsafe extravehicular activities.
143557: Find the lost fleet in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and recover the data cores; destroy anything that stands in your way.
143558:
We just lost a fleet out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's a waste of hardware and personnel, but at the very least, we'd like to recover the data cores of each ship. If the vultures haven't started in on the carcass yet, they will soon. We can't afford a whole recovery effort, but we'd rather hire a capsuleer like you then let those blood-suckers run off with our data.

Keep anything else you like from the site, and if a few raiders and pirates end up dead, I doubt anyone would complain, if you know what I mean.
143559: It's all yours. We'll upload the identification beacons to your ship now.
143560: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.
143561: Damn. We were hoping to attract someone of your reputation and firepower. We'll see if we can't settle for someone else.
143562: Time is running out. By the time you get there, it might already be picked clean.
143564: Go pick up the Caldari operative from the penal station in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring him back.
143565:
I've got a delicate yet dangerous task that just wouldn't suit anyone other than a capsuleer. Here's the situation:

We caught a Caldari operative trying to walk out of the University of Callie with, and I say this literally, an armful of data cores stolen from the university's research hospital. We've had him locked down at a penal instillation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} since then, but our more convincing interrogators have changed his mind about giving up some information.

The catch is that he's demanded to be transferred to a more "dignified" location before he offers his full cooperation. That's where you come in.

Pick up the Caldari operative and bring him back here immediately.
143566:
Good. Head out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. I've sent word, so they should know to hand him over to you when you get there. They haven't responded yet, but it's an old installation, and a busy one, too. I'm sure it's nothing.

When you get him, bring him back here.
143567: Sorry to hear that. You sure? Simple, lucrative work doesn't come around every day.
143568: You're leaving me in a spot here. I'll have to get another trusted courier and contact the jail again.
143570: Good work. You really thought on your feet for that one. We'll be debriefing the operative shortly. Your payment is well deserved, unfortunately the Caldari did get away with a lot of prisoners.
143571: A drone network virus seems has taken over a mining colony and is infecting any ship that approaches. Eradicate all infected ships and destroy the virus before it infects yours.
143572:
A rogue drone virus has gone live at a mining colony. The machinery is malfunctioning and the problem spreading throughout the entire network. We sent a small rescue crew and it took over their systems. The crews are still alive but they're held hostage by their own ships. Unfortunately, we can't let that cloud our judgment. The infection must be destroyed… completely.

We have reason to believe your capsuleer vessel will be able to withstand infection long enough to eradicate the problem.
143574: Can't say I blame you, but it still doesn't help me out any. You'll have to excuse me.
143575: That doesn't leave me many options. You couldn't have told me earlier? No matter.
143576: Please try to maintain radio silence during this mission; I don't want that virus ending up in our computers here on the station!
143577: That was close. A shame for those that lost their lives, but you did incredible work out there. We'll send a scuttle crew out to sweep up and find out what happened.
143579: Rogue drones and wild drones are the terms used over advanced drones that mutated out of control. A few years ago some ingenious Gallente inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own - in essence acting in every sense like a regular space ship except being unmanned and computer controlled. First prototypes were encouraging, but then disaster struck. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Some of these were huge - the largest drones ever constructed, these drones were even equipped with warp drives and equipped with the latest advancements in artificial intelligence. These mother drones, as they were called, along with several lesser drones soon managed to spread out, not only within the same system as the research facility that birthed them, but also to other systems. Only later men discovered exactly how - the drones attacked and took over space ships, then used them to jump to other systems, the drones themselves safely hidden within the ship. Needless to say the super-drone research was soon abandoned by the Gallente.
143580: A pirate faction in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system has taken hostages and plan on executing them shortly. The innocent people need to be rescued and returned to the agent as soon as possible.
143581:
I can tell you're a bit more experienced than the average capsuleer, which means you might be interested in something a little more challenging than the usual chores.

A small gang of pirates has carved a niche for itself in the evidence disposal business. They've setup a base near an uncharted acidic cloud, which allows them to charge huge sums of money to other pirate factions that need to get rid of salvage, bodies, data cores, or whatever in a discrete location.

Unfortunately, they're currently holding some hostages that we need to have recovered. I think you can figure out the rest on your own.
143582: I don't think I need to remind you that, if you fail, a bunch of innocent people are going to get jettisoned into a cloud of acid, where they will be simultaneously decompressed, frozen, and dissolved.
143585: I'm no starship pilot, but it seems like it would be a good idea to avoid the acid cloud.
143586: Clever capsuleer, you've done it! On behalf of my corporation and the hostages you rescued, thank you very much!
143587: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and look for signs of the missing passenger ships. Evacuate any survivors you find and bring them back here.
143588:
We've gotten reports of missing passenger ships in and around {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We've lost track of three of them just this week. We'd like you to go out and see what's happening to the ships. If possible, recover the crew as well. Thousands of people are missing because of these lost ships – the worst incident so far. I'm afraid that this situation could gain a lot of unwanted attention very quickly.

I want you to look into it. I'd like to be optimistic and say that they've simply had technical difficulties, but we're past the breaking point here. Bring back any survivors you can find.
143589: Thank you.  I have no idea who would be disrupting our space lanes like this. Whoever it is, they're bold to take on the Federation. We'll have medical specialists on standby to take of the survivors.
143590: The Federation will not look kindly on your inaction.
143591: Sorry to hear that. You'll be happy to know that CONCORD has taken notice of this case and they'll be dispatching a squadron to look into the disappearances.
143593: This mission was a bigger story than I imagined. Looks like the State was using these mercenaries as a source of domestic warfare within the Federation. That's low, especially for the State. But you know what they say about war, right? Anyway, I'll report this incident to the higher-ups in the FIO. They'll be very interested in the State's recent activities.
143594: A Quote from Admiral Edan Gore, Federation Navy
143595: "Honor does not exist in this day and age, not out in space and especially not among the capsuleer communities. The only honor left is down here, planet side, where we do not resort to domestic terrorism, and where respect for the basic rights of the private citizen still exists. The stars shine on fear."
143596: Hunt down the rogue Minmatar in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  Destroy his pirated prototype ship and deliver his corpse to Minmatar caretakers.
143597:
You've shown a great deal of loyalty to the Republic, {[character]player.name}. I wonder if that speaks as much to your feelings towards the Amarr, or if it's a matter of convenience. It's been my experience that the older a capsuleer is, the more uncertain his or her motives become.

Mortals are slightly less difficult. Fervent extremists particularly. A particularly troubled Minmatar has apparently taken it upon himself to conduct a personal war against the Empire. Ordinarily, my superiors and I would quietly applaud his effort and wait for word of his death. This particular person, however, managed to commandeer a prototype stealth ship to carry out his war.

We can't let the ship fall into Amarrian hands, but we can't send the fleet in either. With him already in Amarr territory, they could easily construe it as a sanctioned act of war. As much as I want to cut out my tongue for saying it, we need you to help the Amarr kill one of our own. We'll have to smooth out the political mess through our liaison with CONCORD.

Reports place him somewhere in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. If you can manage it, bring back his remains. I don't want to think how those pious... how the Amarr would treat him.
143598: I hope you won't mind if I don't thank you outright. Oh, and don't expect the Amarr to welcome your assistance either.
143599: You're leaving us with dangerously few options, {[character]player.name}.
143600: I understand how distasteful the whole deal is, but this doesn't help.
143601: I have nothing else to tell you, {[character]player.name}. Please just contact me when this is finished.
143602: Our rampaging kinsman is gone? His ship, too? If you'll take a bit of advice from a lowly mortal, {[character]player.name}; when unethical decisions are made, eventually you're left with nothing but unethical options.
143604: Reflecting on the personal toll invariably endured, a wise figure once offered this advice to anyone considering a career in politics: “Don't.” In New Eden, with so many different factions all delicately counterbalanced, such sage advice may have never been more humanitarian.
143605:
A maintenance team assigned to a top secret acceleration gate in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} has stopped transmitting progress reports. As this gate leads to one of our new listening outposts, alarm rang out in military circles.

Travel to the acceleration gate. Destroy any hostiles. Use the acceleration gate and check on the outpost. If the outpost's location has been compromised, you are ordered to eliminate the hostiles and then destroy the gate. You must ensure that the enemy cannot return to the exact location of our outpost.
143606: Fly out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}  to monitor and disperse the slave trading operation that has set up shop there.
143607:
We have a lead on a potential slave trade in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and I need someone to patrol that area and find out what's happening. We think they're trading Gallente citizens, which is an open act of hostility against the Federation, so we need to shut this ring down as soon as possible. But first, we have to know who's behind it.

Understand that you won't be trying to actually stop the slavers; all we need is information on who's behind it. If you encounter any hostiles, however, please take care of them.
143608: That's what I like to hear. A capsuleer will really be able to send these slavers a message. Thank you for agreeing to be the voice of our culture.
143609: I'm sorry to hear that. Some other time.
143610: You're aware of what you're doing? These people need immediate help.  We'll scramble some pilots now, but you're leaving us high and dry.
143611: Interesting that you should contact me. Is it done?
143612: I've dispatched ships to pick up the slaves. They'll receive counseling and be sent back to their respective home worlds, courtesy of Interbus. It's safe to say I'm not satisfied with this outcome. I've never heard of the Serpentis dealing in human traffic, but I hope that this isn't indicative of a larger trend in that organization. But we've got the information we need, and the Federation can move forward based on your intel. Good work.
143613: Wipe out the Sansha hijackers in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. The more humiliating, the better.
143614:
There is an old saying: “Money makes the world go round.” Actually, it's gravity and thermodynamics, among other things, but money and physics all come together in a big way when you're talking about wormholes.

However, wormholes rarely occur in civilized space; take a wild guess what that means. I hope you have some experience in dealing with pirates, {[character]player.name}. Specifically, the Sansha. They seem particularly fixated on wormhole research, so much so that they've been a major pain for scientific ventures regardless of ownership.

There's no word of sanctions against the “Nation,” so we'll have to take care of it ourselves. More work for you, anyway.

We'd send a fleet detachment to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} to reclaim a wormhole we've been studying recently, but we'd rather outsource to a capsuleer like you and humiliate them.
143615: Good hunting. Personally, I suggested we just spray the area with used motor oil.
143616: I expected someone with your reputation to jump at the chance for a little rough play. I'm sure some up and coming fleet captain will be eager for the assignment.
143617: You were supposed to embarrass those androids, not your employers. I'll call in the fleet.
143618: Our scientists can't safely get back to work until you've sent the cyborgs running, {[character]player.name}.
143619: What do you mean they came through from the other end? You're suggesting they were able to predict of the most random, unpredictable pathway in existence?
143621: The inner workings of a wormhole were apparently well understood at one time. Since the Dark Ages, however, the best New Eden has managed is basic reverse engineering of ancient jump gates, significantly less powerful than the natural phenomena. This makes the appearance of a natural wormhole a dangerously valuable occurrence, over which factions will openly oppose each other in order to study and utilize the anomalies exclusively.
143622:
Glad my invitation reached you, {[character]player.name}. A portion of the fleet  is preparing a set of protracted war games in the next few days. I've been put in charge of constructing decoy ships and structures, but there was some mix up with a circuitry order that I only just found out about.
I found a replacement vendo. All my subordinates are too occupied to retrieve it.
You'll be picking up the goods direct from a production line, not through their public market. I haven't had time to check reports on local piracy though. There may be hostiles. Be ready for a fight. I don't care if you have to blow the storage facility apart, we need those chips.
143623: A rogue drone infestation in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system is causing problems and needs to be taken care of.
143624:
Hang on, I need to finish this call.

Really, another one? That same station, huh? Well, I don't know what the capsuleer was flying. What do you want me to do, hold their hands? No, don't even joke about that. One more? Do you really think it's going to be any different? Okay, but don't blame me if this one fails, too.

Okay now, where were we? Oh, yes, the exciting opportunity I have for you today! It's a bit run-of-the-mill, but I think you've earned an easy one, friend. It's just a tiny little rogue drone problem. There couldn't be more than half a dozen of the little bastards. I'll bet if you just zip in there and rattle off a few shots at the infested station, they'll scatter like frightened children. What do you say?
143625: Perfect! Run over to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and clean up those pesky drones.
143626: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?
143627: You flew all the way out here just to decline a simple task like this?
143628: How is that cleanup coming along?
143629: You actually did it? You destroyed that infested station? Do you have any idea how many capsuleers lost their- Uhm, I mean, great work! I'll keep you in mind when I come across important missions like this in the future.
143630: Find the tainted tattoo chemical being developed in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.  The exact location of the chemical is unknown.  Be prepared to destroy any number of large structures.
143631:
Tattoos are more than art to the Minmatar, {[character]player.name}. We have entire ceremonies built up around the markings we come to wear in our lives. Not to bore you with details, but ours aren't the simple ink-and-needle hatchet jobs most people think of. Exactly how the chemical process works is a closely guarded secret even within our own culture.

Word has reached my office that some Amarr splinter faction is working on their own chemical in order to contaminate Minmatar ceremonial supplies. It could mean anything from the appearance of Amarr propagandist symbols to some unexplored form of chemical dependence on the Empire.

The logistics of such a plan actually working are laughably impossible, and of course we'll never be able to tie anything back to mainline Imperial channels. Still, any threat to our freedom must be treated seriously. Well, that and the whole concept is just insulting.

We want you to bring us a sample of this chemical. I can't pinpoint exactly where the chemicals are being made. Our best information points to a deadspace complex in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

I mentioned the insult of the program. Tear through the place. I don't care how many structures you have to obliterate, just bring us this new ink.
143632: Discretion can be the better part of valor. I'm sure there's a less scrupulous capsuleer out there somewhere.
143633: I didn't expect a capsuleer to have a weak stomach.
143634: If you felt the least bit heartless blasting through them, remember which side consciously chose to use innocent victims as living shields, {[character]player.name}. We've already sent teams in behind you to rescue who we can. Or capture, as the case may be. I'll be interested to learn exactly what this substance is supposed to do.
143636: The Minmatar coming-of-age ceremony, known as the Voluval, involves an injection of a hallucinatory chemical which puts the youth in a trance. As the visions wear off, the individual finds him or herself marked with a tattoo of an unpredictable pattern on an unpredictable portion of body. The chemical used to induce trance and create the mark is so well guarded, even some Minmatar wonder if there is not more to the process than their elders admit.
143637: According to your agent, a convoy was sent out with a group of pirates pretending to be security. Intercept the convoy and take out its escort.
143638:
Please, you have to help me! I hired a group of mercenaries to escort a friend's cargo shipment; however, I just learned that the people I sent are pirate agents!

I know it would be helpful if you knew who you were going up against, but all I have is a few fragments of information here; there are no specifics so be ready for anything!

I need you to intercept that convoy and eliminate the pirates!
143639: Thank you for doing this. The convoy should be passing through {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} very soon. There's still time to head them off!
143640: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.
143641: Damn it. I need to find someone to help and quick. Time is running out.
143642: What are you doing? Time is running out!
143643: I cannot properly express how helpful you've been, so hopefully this reward will do.
143645: It's a common misconception that it is CONCORD that engages pirates with below -5.0 security status in high security space, while it is in fact the local navy that does so. CONCORD will only engage if the outlaw has incurred a GCC (Global Criminal Countdown) caused by committing a crime in Empire Space. The local navies are not as powerful as CONCORD and it is possible to survive their onslaught and limp back to the gate, or even escape before they warp scramble the ship.
143646:
Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts holding above the detention facility, and they're tapping communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further.
143647:
I'm glad you're here {[character]player.name}, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is in desperate need of your help.

Only a few moments ago the CEO from one of our subsidiaries was attacked and ransomed by Guristas, right in front of our trade delegation, too. Local security forces were overwhelmed and the pirates managed to escape. Our scouts pursued the Guristas vessels back to a Federation detention facility, which suggests the Guristas are only acting as mercenaries and the Gallente are really the ones to blame.

We have scouts hidden near the detention facility, and they're monitoring communications to look for evidence of a connection, but in the meantime we want to make an attempt to get our people out using capsuleer assistance. We're concerned that more reinforcements could be on the way, and that if they arrive, we'll lose our people for good. You need to act quickly.

Your assignment is to assault the facility and return our people to us before things escalate any further. Can we count on you for this?
143648: If that CEO dies, it'll be on your head! I don't know how you sleep at night.
143650: Time is of the essence. Get moving {[character]player.name}!
143651: What? I pray to the Maker that I can find someone else in time.
143652: Understood. Be careful how you approach this, {[character]player.name}; the Guristas must be getting paid a fortune for such a brazen attack, and they will fight to the death for that money.
143653: The best possible result, and proof once again that hiring capsuleers is the way to get that. Thank you, {[character]player.name}, you've made us both look good. I'll be sure to pass my recommendations along, right after I take a few calls about some pay adjustments of my own.
143654: The Guristas are famous for their raids into civilized territory, something that very few pirate clans are willing or able to do. The mission of these raids is most often simply to steal cargo or passengers (for ransom) from freighters, but on numerous occasions their main intention seems to be to sabotage empire installations (mining facilities, sentry guns, and the like). This has led to speculations that some unscrupulous empire companies or even governments are hiring the Guristas to take out property of the competition.
143655:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

During a routine system scan, some of my people stumbled upon something that may be a significant archaeological find. I can't just call in anyone to confirm it, though, that would risk a leak. I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

What we could do is rig your vessel's camera drones to relay a live feed of the site back to me and my people. From there, we would be able to direct you around the area to observe places of interest. What you relay back could help us confirm or disprove our earlier findings. The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. The only problem my scouts reported was a light pirate presence. I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this.
143656:
Ah, {[character]player.name}, I'm glad to see you received my mail. I have something that requires complete discretion. It's entirely legal of course, but this will need to be kept quiet all the same. You've proven yourself trustworthy so if you want the assignment I'll hand it over to you.

During a routine system scan, some of my people stumbled upon something that may be a significant archaeological find. I can't just call in anyone to confirm it, though, that would risk a leak. I don't want anyone else claiming this discovery as their own, especially if it turns out to be a lucrative one.

What we could do is rig your vessel's camera drones to relay a live feed of the site back to me and a friend of mine at the House of Records. From there, my friend would be able to direct you around the area to observe places of interest. What you relay back could help us confirm or disprove our earlier findings. The site is in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, so you wouldn't be travelling very far to investigate, either. Our scouts reported there was a light pirate presence, and interference was making the use of microwarpdrives impossible in there, but I'm sure you can deal with a few Guristas and using afterburner.

Not the usual assignment I know, but one of potentially great importance…and profit. It would be ideal if we could rely on capsuleer assistance for this. What do you say?
143657: Fine. I will find someone else.
143658: Then it would be in your best interests to forget we ever had this discussion.
143659: An arms dealer passing through the system just sold us a cache of weapons. I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Don't worry, we've already acquired a permit for them, so you won't have any trouble at customs.
143660: An arms dealer passing through the system just sold us a cache of weapons. I need you to take it to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for me. Don't worry, we've already acquired a permit for them, so you won't have any trouble at customs.
143661:
I knew I chose the right person. I'm uploading the coordinates to you now.

Once you arrive at the archaeological site, I will issue further instructions.
143662:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. Exceptionally well. It will take a little longer to fully confirm, but we believe we've discovered an ancient Caldari outpost – one of the first established after we broke away from the Federation. If true, this would be a welcome injection to the system's local tourism industry, and we'll get a commission on the money earned there. Here's your cut of the deal.

Even if it turns out to be a false discovery we're insured against the LUX, so I see no reason not to give it to you now. Thanks once again.
143663: We stand to make a lot of LUX if that site is what we think it is.
143664: Shortly after jump gate technology was jointly discovered by the Gallente and the Caldari a little over five hundred years before the Federation formed, the Caldari corporations had started their own interstellar surveying and colonization, separate from that conducted by the Gallente. It was these colonies, kept as a secret from the Gallenteans, that became the source of friction between the Gallenteans and the Caldari, culminating in the latter's defection from the Federation and an ensuing war between the two races.
143666:
Your agent's corporation suspects a rival corporation may have caused a transport crash. Go to the location in your journal and investigate the wreckage you find. Bring any evidence back to your agent.

You will require a salvager.
143667:
Glad to have you here, {[character]player.name}. I have some work for you.

A few days ago, a passenger vessel was passing through an asteroid belt, when it had a critical failure of its navigational computer. The vessel slammed into the asteroids and suffered critical damage. Before the vessel's reactor went critical, {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} personnel evacuated the passengers and got them to safety.

While this story has a happy ending, there seems to be something suspicious about the crash. A small corporation with alleged ties to the Guristas is having money troubles, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} suspects the incident may have not been an accident. Things just seem a little too perfect and well-timed.

{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} needs you to go to the crash site and investigate the wreckage. Look for any evidence that might hint at the real cause of the accident. Bring any evidence back to me and I will submit it to the proper authorities.

I don't want to tell you how to do your job, but a salvager might help you get to the bottom of this a little faster than just looking around with your on-board sensors.
143668: I was relying on you to figure out what went wrong. I just hope the evidence is still there by the time I find someone else.
143669: Great to hear, {[character]player.name}. I have uploaded the coordinates to your NeoCom.
143670: There are millions of LUX resting on this investigation. Who I am supposed to find to do this?
143671: I have a feeling there might be a cover up in the works, so get moving.
143672: This is some interesting evidence. Now we can bring some people to justice.
143673: I heard you were having problems dealing with this. Well, thanks for letting me know of your failure first-hand, I suppose.
143674: Excellent. Here are the coordinates. Don't hesitate out there, {[character]player.name};  be ready for a fight.
143675: Great Work, {[character]player.name}. It should be a long time, or a lot of LUX in bribes, before they can re-establish themselves around here again.
143676: Very well, if you're not interested I can find others. An unexpected refusal though, I must say.
143677: There's a number of ships holding outside the station. They won't be able to dock until you inspect them for contraband. Try not to keep the innocent ones waiting.
143678: Fly to the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system and obtain the salvaged electronics, then return them to your agent in {[location]agentStationID.name}. Destroy any Angel Cartel ships that get in the way.
143679:
You're just the kind of capsuleer I've been waiting for, {[character]player.name}. If you're interested, I've got something important that needs to get done, something I can't trust just anyone with. Your loyalty to the Republic is becoming legendary.

We're working on something big, {[character]player.name}, something very big. I can't go into specifics, but I can tell you that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has been tasked with gathering materials from anywhere we can find them. Luckily, two of our objectives coincide.

It just happens that our old friends, the Angel Cartel, are sitting on a veritable treasure trove of spare parts and salvage out in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. What do you say we kill two birds with one stone? Swing out there, vaporize all the Angel clowns you like, and bring us back some salvaged electronics. Sound good?
143680: I see your reputation was well-deserved! I look forward to adding my name to your list of recommendations, {[character]player.name}.
143681: I can't imagine what you have to do that's more important than this, but I understand.
143682: Oh, so you're too good to help out the Republic when it needs you? You capsuleers are all the same.
143683: Sometimes I regret taking this desk job. Hey, while you're out there, blast a few Angel goons for me, would you?
143684: Yes, this is perfect. You've done the Republic a great service, {[character]player.name}. When the time comes and you witness our greatest accomplishment, you'll be able to say that you had a small part in paving the way for the future of all Minmatar!
143685: Don't expect them to roll over and hand you the formula. Leave no stone unturned, and what I mean by that is don't be afraid to destroy every structure you see in search of your objective.
143686: Why haven't you brought me the chemical yet? Did you turn every structure inside out, because they probably won't be hiding it in some ship's cargo bay.
143687:
Though I doubt she'll run from a fight, you might want to bring a warp scrambler or disruptor to stop her from running deeper into cover.

Oh, and if you see some merchant vessels loitering around, hold your fire. That's my surveillance team. They may have some further intel once you arrive.
143688:
Have you ever heard of Anire Scarlet? Well, she's practically an urban legend among the local pirates. It seems any outlaw with a clone bay and rhetorical skills can amass a following these days. The sorts of degenerates that hang around this area are easily impressed too, so apparently has built quite a posse, but then, that could just be another one of the myths about her.

As for where you come in: all this attention has earned her a CONCORD bounty. I'd very much like to claim that LUX, {[character]player.name}, with your help. I've hired an undercover surveillance team to locate her, and they've had some luck turning up a lead. If you're able to follow it up and take her out then we can split the bounty money equally. The surveillance team found her flagship vessel, The Crimson Dawn. She is sure to be either inside it, or very close by. If you think yourself capable of eliminating her, then I'll trade you the coordinates.
143689: Nicely handled, {[character]player.name}. I'll keep you in mind for another bounty contract if she ever shows her head again.
143690: Well, I can't say I blame you. I hear Anire Scarlet's pirates are pretty rough. They're all hell-bent on impressing their “Queen.”

143702:
Hello {[character]player.name}, up for some action? I have just received an offer from followers of the notorious pirate Zazzmatazz. The mission is to break him out of a private prison, Consolidated Holdings Inc. , which has a contract with Concord. Zazz is being held there, somewhat unexpectedly, for a very short time.

The client warns that once you have broken into the prison complex you will need to FINISH IT IN ONE run. Retreating is failure! The upside is that the client has promised some significant rewards if you prove capable and as a bonus, Consolidated Holdings Inc. is rumored to hold many secrets.

Are you up for it?
143703: Good! There are several deadspace acceleration gates that and need to be unlocked one at a time in isolated deadspace pockets while a strike force moves in through the complex and finds Zazzmatazz.
143704: Alright! It is a little disappointing, but it's your call. This kind of mission doesn't float by every day.
143705: I guess I overestimated your abilities and the strength of your network of friends.
143706: Bring Zazzmatazz back as soon as you spring him out. There is a lot of heat on us because of this and I'm trying to stay out of the limelight.
143707: Zazzmatazz may have eluded you but our client might settle for his DNA instead. It is better than nothing at least. Contact me soon for his response, it shouldn't take long.
143708: Deliver Zazzmatazz – or his DNA, to be more exact – to either Consolidated Holdings, Inc., or to the pirate Ragnar Bloodthorn. Consolidated Holdings has set up a meeting with your agent, and Ragnar Bloodthorn said he will be in touch. Both clients are very angry over the turn of events: Bloodthorn was expecting Zazzmatazz himself from your initial services, not his DNA, and Consolidated Holdings has lost a lot of assets and taken a blow to its reputation. Both have a score to settle with you, but they desperately need your cooperation as well, at least until they have secured Zazzmatazz's DNA.
143709:
Hello {[character]player.name}. Our client was furious about Zazzmatazz not being retrieved, but is willing to negotiate for his DNA. However, Consolidated Holdings, Inc., also contacted me about making a deal to get his DNA back. I'll leave it up to you who to deal with. I have arranged a meeting with Consolidated Holdings, but the pirate contact said he will be in touch with you. His real name is Ragnar Bloodthorn. When you've met them, make a decision quick, please — this is one problem I'd like out of my hands!

So, do you want to go to the meeting?
143710: Alright, the locations for both targets are in the mission briefing. I'll see you around.
143711: Alright! Keep Zazzmatazz's DNA for yourself, then. I don't want anything more to do with it.
143712: I thought you were taking care of that DNA business! Now I have both Bloodthorn and Consolidated Holdings breathing down my neck because of you.
143713: Get back to me when you have delivered Zazzmatazz's DNA to either party.
143714: Good job, {[character]player.name}; this played out nicely. Consolidated Holdings, Inc., and this Ragnar Bloodthorn now have something to yell into the emptiness of space – they both got what they deserved!
143715:
Have you heard those crazy prophecies which have been picking up publicity? No, not Macaper's, I mean the ones delivered by this “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak?

In any case, all you need to know is that this fool is trying to create his own religion, and he's had some successes recently in building up his numbers. It seems each new day he lures more discontented people into his cult, and recently we've been affected by this new trend.

One of his acolytes set up shop in our little corner of the universe and began preaching to the locals. This “priest” is not exactly causing trouble, but he's making certain powerful people uncomfortable. Not only that, but we've heard reports of violence against this cult in other sectors. We'd like to quietly remove this preacher from the picture to avoid any possibility for backlash in our own areas. At the same time, we don't want to make a martyr out of him and build further support for this cult. The situation needs to be handled discretely.

He's currently preaching on Yunshin Z, a refining complex. This is a low population industrial center with little contact to the outside world. We can afford to make bold moves here. Your task is to find this preacher and return him to us. We'll handle the rest.
143716:
Have you heard those crazy sermons that people are talking about? The ones delivered by this self-proclaimed “prophet” who calls himself Tolmak? Yeah, that freak who's trying to create a religion. People who might try to kill him. Thing is, certain powerful people find him useful. A nice distraction from more political pursuits. They'd like him alive.

143718: Very well, I'll find someone else.
143720: I hope the capture of this preacher is worth the cost of hiring you.
143721:
Ah, you have him? Good work, {[character]player.name}. I hadn't heard any reports of conflict at the refinery, so I can only assume the mission went smoothly.

In fact, I'd rather continue to keep on assuming that, if you get me. My paperwork is going to indicate that Tolmak's friend came willingly, without a struggle, and that the entire operation was conducted peacefully and with the utmost respect to all involved parties.
143722: Great job, risking your neck like that! I mean, I'm sure there was no risk at all - in any case, we've already spoken with Dr. Ateshi about how to proceed.
143723: Finally, we have all the information necessary to make an informed decision. I'll see what Dr. Ateshi has to say.
143724: Destroy The Anomaly before it can do further damage. Bring Dr. Ateshi to the rogue drone hive where the ship is hiding so that she can deactivate its shields.
143725: Good. Dr. Ateshi will accompany you to the ship and give you details on delivering the scanner. Get in, drop the scanner, get out.
143726: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.
143727: Travel to The Anomaly and deliver the Neurowave Pattern Scanner.
143728: Have you delivered the Neurowave Pattern Scanner yet? There's a lot of pressure on me to get this done.
143729:
We've spoken with Fajah Ateshi about The Anomaly, and I'm afraid things look dire. Her readings were damaged from the explosion aboard The Paryi, and she needs to return to The Anomaly to get further information. Since the two of you are the only ones who've come near the ship and retained both your lives and sanity, we have to send you out again.

We're still not entirely sure if anyone is alive aboard there, though Dr. Ateshi insists that she heard garbled transmissions from survivors disoriented from radiation sickness. I tell you, all this mystery doesn't make me comfortable, and it makes the people at the top very, very unhappy. If you find survivors, excellent, but your survival and Dr. Ateshi's readings are more important. You need to attach her Neurowave Pattern Scanner to The Anomaly.
143730: I don't think you understand what you're turning down here. The fate of The Anomaly is important to a great many very powerful people, and they won't be happy.
143731: You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors and learn what they know. The Anomaly was a very expensive project and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.
143732:
{[character]player.name}? Good. I have a job that's probably outside your normal scope. This one is humanitarian.

A pandemic has broken out on a planet in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. Fortunately, a cure was already developed and mass-produced. The contagion originated on another planet nearby, you see, so the people of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} already have experience in dealing with this particular disease.

The Sisters of Eve sent a medical drone with the vaccine onboard down to the planet, but some degenerate pirates have intercepted the craft, disabled it, and are now trying to demand a ransom for its release. The Sisters say that if the drone is destroyed it could be days before we can mass-produce more vaccine – something about being unable to accelerate the bacterial cultivation. A few more days with this disease uncontrolled could mean everything. We must recapture the drone.

We're depending on you here, {[character]player.name}. Once you've secured the drone, they can deploy repair teams and send it back on its way.

Hey there, {[character]player.name}. I've got a routine run for you...just a second. I've got emergency messages coming in. Hm. You up for a rescue mission?

I just received an alert across multiple communication channels asking for evacuation help. A diplomatic station, not far from here, is undergoing a traumatic systems shut-down cascade. It's all going, and people need off that station. The rescue requires a smaller ship than what they have available to get in past the field of debris now ringing the station.

That's what happens when none of the empires will trust the others enough to allow them to send in their best station engineers and construction teams, and so they all agree on a third-party freelance company to build their stations. Happens all the time, I hear. Ridiculous.
Anyway – are you interested?

143746: Great. You get out there, and you've got some rescue money coming your way. I don't really care who you rescue, just so long as you rescue someone. Fair warning, though – the ones you don't rescue are likely to remember it.
143748: Really? That's it? You're quitting? Why'd you agree to do it in the first place, then?
143750: You will lose standing with those factions you choose not to rescue. Fair warning.
143753:
Ever heard of The Anomaly? Lots of superstition around that name - it's one of our ships that vanished completely while testing an experimental jump drive. A trading vessel heard The Anomaly's signal last week and so we sent out a salvage crew, The Paryi, to investigate the site where it reappeared, but something went wrong. We received The Paryi's distress call yesterday and can't make sense of it. It seems some of them were killed in an explosion near The Anomaly, and the survivors escaped in life pods but are trapped there by gravity waves exuding from the ship. But the other things they said… well, some of them must have cracked under the stress. If there were any survivors from The Anomaly, they would've contacted us, after all.

You need to rescue The Paryi's survivors, especially Dr. Fajah Ateshi. Once we learn what they uncovered, we'll have a better sense of how to proceed. The Anomaly was a very expensive project, and some very powerful people are invested in figuring out how it vanished.
143754:
There's been an influx of neural boosters to our area recently, and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is trying to stem the flow. We normally turn a blind eye to light drug trafficking but that only seems to have encouraged the local smugglers, who are now flooding the area with cheap, more dangerous drugs.

We know where they base out of, however, and have already taken the liberty of blockading their station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system. What we need is a capsuleer who can go in there and check out some of the larger vessels currently in holding. You are of course cleared to engage anyone caught with illegal boosters in their cargo, although if you catch anyone be prepared for them to start shooting.
143755: Who doesn't love a nice fat slice of beef? Well, vegetarians and vegans aside, I suppose, but they're a dying breed in this era, eh? Anyway, one of my clients loves his beef, and that's why I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and deliver a shipment of cattle to him.
143756: Who doesn't love a nice fat slice of beef? Well, vegetarians and vegans aside, I suppose, but they're a dying breed in this era, eh? Anyway, one of my clients loves his beef, and that's why I want you to fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and deliver a shipment of cattle to him.
143757: Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent stuffy by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.
143758:
Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units. Unless a drastic improvement in the quality and durability of this body armor can be found, we will continue to suffer the consequences.

This morning I received a priority communication from an Amarr Intelligence Officer claiming that his team had just “obtained” a revolutionary new fabric that, if properly processed, could literally double the strength of our existing armor. I know this officer only by reputation, and it is best not to pry any further into how his team came across this “miracle cloth.” Nonetheless, we have been advised that they will arrive at this station within moments to transfer the fabric here for transshipment to a more secure facility.

So, pilot, will you transport this prototype body armor fabric to the station facility we designate?
143760: Quitting mid-mission is not something I expected from you. Now I am going to have to answer to the intelligence team. Oh, and don't expect any further jobs from me until your failure here has been long forgotten. Damn… I need a stress pill….
143761: I must say I am disappointed in your decision to turn down this mission. I vouched for you personally, given what I have seen in your files about your excellent mission completion record. I will not soon forget your refusal.
143762: Lightweight body armor is a common and often required element of any police or security forces' operational gear. Modern armor of this type can stop most projectile, laser, and other light weapon fire. However, as small arms weaponry continued to evolve with regard to the amount of damage it can inflict, so to must the defensive technologies designed to maintain parity with these weapons. On rare occasions, a corporation, military laboratory, or other entity will produce a light body armor system that represents nothing short of a generational leap in design and protection. The multilayered fabrics used in these latter applications are usually amongst the most highly guarded secrets of any civilization, for many reasons. The most advanced of these contain nanotechnology which also can change color and density depending on ambient conditions and/or input from the wearer.
143763: Outstanding, pilot. You were even a bit ahead of schedule. Our offloading team is en route to your ship, and the Intel guards will stay with the shipment until that has been completed. I will keep your name in my “go to” list should any more missions come up in the future.
143764: Thank you for the update pilot, but no need to contact me until you arrive. The Intel security team on your ship is keeping me quite well informed.
143765: A small, platoon-sized Caldari special operation team is in hiding on a Gallente planet and in danger of being captured or killed. They are low on water, food, weapons, and other equipment and will not last long unless they are extracted. We have a rescue standing by; however, we need you to deliver the required materials to their station so that they can then proceed with this critical rescue mission.
143766:
One of our Caldari Navy Special Forces units conducting clandestine reconnaissance of a contested ocean planet – a Gallente-claimed planet, by the way, with extremely rare seabed minerals – sent an emergency burst communication to the covert ops ship in orbit above the planet, requesting immediate extraction. This signal was, in turn, transmitted to the classified comms center here on this station. When we attempted to contact both the team and the ship, however, we received no response. Our immediate reaction was to divert one of our long range Crow-class interceptors, which was in the region on an unrelated mission, to investigate. Soon after its arrival, its sensors confirmed that the covert ops ship had been destroyed.

There is nothing we can do for our lost covops ship; however, this series of events has left the Special Forces team alone and without a means to evacuate the planet. Even worse was a fragment from the original communication indicating that the team was on the run and low on food, water, weapons, and ammunition. They have taken refuge in a disused ocean mining facility, though it is doubtful that they will stay hidden for long. There simply aren't many places to hide on that planet, given the fact that it is mostly covered by massive oceans, with very little land mass. It will not take long for the Gallente to track down our team and either kill them or, worse, capture them for interrogation.

The good news in all this is that we have an extraction team in place, along with a shuttle-equipped vessel to deliver them to the planet. However, given the immediacy of this mission, they had to leave their original base without much of their usual equipment and weaponry. This is where you come in. We need you to transport several containers of highly specialized small arms and related equipment to the station at which the extraction team is currently located. Once you drop off this cargo, the team will gear-up and shuttle down to the planet to rescue the stranded team.

So, pilot, what is it gonna be? Will you help us?
143767: Do not contact us until you have completed this shipment. There is simply no time for idle chatter, not to mention the likelihood that the enemy is almost certainly listening in.
143768: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our military personnel at great risk. It is doubtful that we will be able to find anyone else to get this critical shipment to the station in time.
143769: Your refusal to accept this mission will almost certainly result in the loss of this Special Forces team, not to mention placing the now-dangerously unequipped extraction team at great risk.
143770: Thank you for accepting this important, time-sensitive mission. You have been given priority clearance for station undock, so please leave as soon as possible.
143771:
Due to a recent series of inspections by the regional mine monitoring commission, we have found it necessary to purchase a large quantity of the latest generation of environmentally-friendly drills and related equipment.

In order to avoid financial penalties and the possible loss of our mining rights, that company must get these quite expensive new drills into the hands of the miners as soon as possible. If you can deliver this cargo to the station that serves as our logistical hub for this system, they can then have their own pilots transship them to the required planetary mining locations.
143772:
Let me start at the beginning. As you have probably seen on the news channels, a prominent Caldari mining company is in the middle of a very nasty battle for economic survival with a new, up-and-coming mining company from within the same large conglomerate. Both of these companies specialize in the extraction of ores from some of the more inhospitable and dangerous locations in this and several adjoining systems. While this can be hazardous with regard to men and equipment, the profit potential from these largely untapped ore reserves can be quite significant, which brings me to our current predicament.

As you may know, the specialized manual labor required for some of these mines can be significant in terms of numbers. Well, the Mining Health and Safety Commission, or MHSC, for this region recently conducted a survey of the first company's operations, and found that their mining practices at certain locations may have resulted in excessive pollution, then further alleged a corresponding link to long-term miner health problems. The company has loudly complained that this is a ridiculous witch hunt brought about by their new competitor, which happens to have several “friends” on the commission. While they work to ensure they are equally “represented” on that commission, the recent finding has mandated that they immediately improve worker conditions and reduce pollution or risk losing their mining rights. To remedy this problem, they recently purchased a large number of the latest environmentally-friendly – and obscenely expensive – manportable drills, which seems to have assuaged the MHSC for the moment. They do, however, have a deadline for actually putting these new drills into the hands of the miners, which brings us to the reason I contacted you.

We need you to deliver a rather large shipment of drills and other related equipment to a station that serves as a central service hub. From there, logistics pilots will deliver this and other items to the various mines in the system. Will you take on this important job?
143773: We are shocked to hear that you have chosen to quit this job in the middle of the contract. We will now have to pay another pilot double to pick up where you left off. You should have let us know from the outset that you could not take on this important job. Hopefully, we will never have to rely on you again.
143774: Well, I must say we are quite disappointed that you would turn down this very easy contract. We shall find another pilot and move your name to the bottom of our list. Don't call us, we'll call you.
143775: I certainly do appreciate your help, pilot. Hopefully, if we can get these drills into the hands of the miners in short order, the company should be able to retain its mining rights and return to profitability.
143776: You seem to be on schedule and we look forward to the prompt delivery of the equipment to the designated station. Contact us through the usual channels after you have offloaded this gear.
143777: Job well done. Our logistics teams are loading your shipment into their transport vessels as we speak, and we should have the drills and equipment in place shortly. We will definitely contact you again, should we require your services.
143778: There has been an uprising at one of our slave Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRCs, near a rather large ore mine. The slaves are almost wholly Minmatar, so we cannot afford to have this incident continue for even one more day. The longer it goes on, the greater the chances that some reporter or news agency will get wind of this and splash the story all over the region. Given that the Minmatar Republic may feel compelled to take action to aid their brethren, this can only lead to dire consequences. That, of course, is unacceptable. We do have a plan in place, however, that should end this uprising before it has a chance to truly take root. We need you to transport a large contingent of Riot Interdiction Team (RIT) personnel to a designated station. From there the assembled security teams will join up and embark a small fleet of frigates and cruisers to race to the prison, where they will use all necessary force to terminate this uprising before it gets completely out of control.
143779: Bah – I should have known you wouldn't help us. I could tell when I first met you that you were beyond salvation.
143780: Good job, pilot. Please make all possible haste to the station as the other teams are waiting on you. The assault phase will begin after you deliver the RIT personnel and their equipment.
143781:
The Amarr Empire, realizing many centuries ago that it could not simply work slaves to the point of death, instituted a number of improvements to worker conditions in an effort to prolong the usable lifespan of its slaves. These changes were not universal across the Empire, due in large part to the Empress's unwillingness to create what might have amounted to significant friction between slave -based companies. Therefore, these decisions were largely left to the Five Heirs and their subordinate regional offices. Thus, we can state here that history has shown a lack of consistent application of these worker improvement programs across the Empire. Those Amarr systems that have chosen to incorporate these adaptations have, however, consistently derived greater revenues due to these enhanced and ongoing pacification efforts.

These shortcomings led directly to the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC). An LRC is designed much like a multilevel prison, with facilities for low, medium, and high risk inmates. The inmates are those slaves who consistently exhibit defiance or even outright hostility towards the managerial staff at the mine, construction site, or other location to which they are assigned as slave labor. Once we have identified these persons they are immediately removed from their job site and taken to the nearest LRC for corrective behavioral conditioning. This conditioning can include a wide variety of attitude modification methodologies, from intensive drug assisted counseling, to religious indoctrination, and from advanced torture techniques and a concurrent system of rewards - the so-called “carrot and stick approach” - and any number of programs in between. In this way, we break the individual slave's will so that he may be returned to the workforce as a docile and useful component in the labor pool.
143782: Bless the Empress – I am very glad to hear you've decided to help. The RIT personnel will meet you in the hangar bay shortly.  Please feel free to take any of our religious literature with you for your enlightenment during the flight.
143783: You soulless coward! Without the men you agreed to deliver our assault on the prison will undoubtedly lead to unnecessary casualties on all sides.
143785: Following a string of suicide terrorist attacks yesterday, we managed to capture a high ranking member of their organization. Interrogations have revealed, however, that a devastating viral weapon, based on nanotechnology, is already in place and primed for release. We need you to deliver the only known countermeasure to this agent, manportable electromagnetic weapons. If we are successful, these weapons could eradicate the virus before it has a chance to spread and infect the entire station.
143786: Pilot, there is simply no time to discuss this any further. Deliver the cargo to the station immediately, before that horrible weapon kills thousands of innocent men, women, and children.
143787:
Last night, a strike team of suicide terrorists from the Anti-Corporatist Revolutionary Front, or ARCF, struck at more than twenty Caldari offices and stations throughout the region. During one of these attacks a terrorist was captured with a well-shielded, improvised nuclear device hidden in his rucksack. Obviously this event represents an entirely new level of threat from the ARCF, now that they have proven themselves willing to carry out such a horrendous and indiscriminate mass casualty attack.

The only upside to this is that the terrorist has turned out to be the most notorious operative of the ARCF, a woman known as Commander Rachendia. Having her in custody has offered us an opportunity to gain information related to her group's future plans to strike at the Caldari State. During one of the more aggressive interrogations, she disclosed information about a pending attack against one of our nearby stations. The nature of the attack is not entirely clear; however, we know with certainty that it involves the surreptitious introduction of a viral agent into the life support and air circulation systems.

Our initial searches for these hidden canisters at that station have, so far, been fruitless – with the exception of one small aerosol-type canister. A preliminary test revealed that these viral weapons appear to be based on a self-replicating nanotechnology. Once released from stasis in their container, they seek out and consume human tissue, and leaving behind little more than dust. Our medical scientists have calculated that just one container, released into the central air processing vents, could result in the deaths of all human life aboard a medium-sized station within no more than four hours. The only good news is that these nanos are programmed to self-terminate within 12 hours. Of course, this would be far more time than would be necessary to kill everyone aboard all but the largest of stations.

Your role in this desperate situation is to deliver a cargo of electromagnetic weapons, modified to emit a short-range pulse that will literally "fry" any nanos within its range. So, we are asking: will you deliver these containers to the station immediately? Thousands of lives may depend on your answer.
143788: We had placed all our hope in you completing this mission. It's too late now to find another pilot and another ship. I fear many thousands of lives may be lost due to what can only be your cowardice. Obviously, you are not a man of your word, and we won't forget that.
143789: Your bravery and skillful piloting without question, saved the lives of untold numbers of innocent people. We will definitely move your name to the top of our list for any future time-sensitive missions!
143790: We're very glad to hear you are willing to take on this important mission. If we can get these EM devices to the station in time, I know we can save many innocent lives.
143791: We are all terribly disappointed in your refusal to transport these electromagnetic weapons to the station. We shall now have to find another pilot and another ship, and I fear even then we will be too late. I doubt you will be sleeping very well after you see what may become of that station.
143792: Terrorists, working with criminal scientists, have developed a strain of viral weaponry that is based on nanotechnology. When combined, the "hive mind" of the viral strain works to seek out human tissue at which point the microscopic nanos begin to quickly disassemble the tissue, leading to a slow and painful death. Research into electromagnetic pulses has provided some promising leads with regard to countermeasures, but these have not yet been field tested.
143794: The Imperial Navy recently made a final attempt to scour the battlefield graveyard of The Battle of Vak-Atioth. This battle pitted our brave Navy against the Jovian enemy; however, due to a number of unforeseeable factors, we did not emerge victorious. The graveyard itself has been picked over for decades by scavengers and others seeking some quick LUX. The Amarr ships sent to perform this duty were attacked by pirates, and only one ship eventually returned. But when it did, it brought with it a valuable icon of Amarr military history: a selection of data chips holding recordings of a small part of that legendary battle. We need these chips delivered to a distant station for proper cleaning and processing.
143795:
As you almost certainly know, many decades ago our Grand Fleet met the hated Jovians on the field of battle in a system known as Vak-Atioth. Most unfortunately, our fleet was destroyed by the technologically superior Jovian ships and their advanced weaponry, marking one of the darkest moments in our history. Still, we learned much from this encounter, and the lessons learned there continue to benefit our military to this day, which brings us to why I called you here.

Several days ago, Imperial naval intelligence mounted a highly classified effort to revisit the Vak-Atioth system, now known simply as Atioth, to conduct a final intensive search for any remaining debris that might provide some insight into the tactics and weapons used by the Jovians. Needless to say, this once-massive floating graveyard has long since been picked over by not only our own salvage fleets, but by scavengers and opportunists alike. All has not been lost, however.

Much to our surprise, the Anathema covert ops ships sent to scan this system returned with a damaged but still readable supply of TIL-1A Nexus Chips. A preliminary review of the information they contain reveals only a portion of the great battle. We are hoping, however, that a more thorough analysis of these chips will reveal some insight into Jovian tactics and technology. If nothing else, they provide a very rare first-hand accounting of the battle which will add greatly to our historical archives and, when displayed at one of our leading military academies, will provide a stirring motivational icon for future generations of brave Imperial naval warriors.

Now that you understand the importance of these chips to the Empire, I must ask: will you transport this invaluable cargo to the designated station?
143796: Many decades ago, a large portion of the Imperial Grand Navy met the Jovians in combat at what today is referred to as The Battle of Vak-Atioth. It was our intention in opening that battle with the as-yet untested Jovians to destroy their fleet utterly, thus forcing their subjugation, as we had done with so many enemies in the past. Without going into great detail, the fearless Amarr fleet was utterly surprised by an enemy that possessed incredible destructive power and remarkably advanced battle tactics. This, coupled with the unforgivable impetuousness of our fleet's leadership, resulted in the near-total annihilation of our warships, at an estimated cost of only one-third of the Jovian armada. We were never again to take to the field of battle against that most dangerous and mysterious opponent. However, while some ships escaped, in less than six hours of battle we left behind a vast field of our dead and dying ships. Today, this system – known now only as Atioth – holds almost none of these battlefield remains, having long since been swept clean by Amarr salvagers and various scavengers. Nonetheless, this system remains an eternal reminder of the vigilance and bravery of our Grand Fleet and the sacrifices they are often called on to make in service of the Empire.
143797: Well, pilot, I could have at least understood refusing this mission in the first place. At least that would have been somewhat understandable given the value nature of the threat. But to quit in mid-shipment is something we did not expect from you. We shall retrieve the chips and deliver them ourselves.
143798: Thank you, pilot. You will be doing the Empire a great service in even such a brief undertaking as this.
143799: You have made a significant contribution to the Empire, pilot. We cannot thank you enough. Of course, no record will be kept of your part in this episode, as we cannot be seen to have been even slightly concerned over the risk of attack and the potential loss of these chips. We will, however, fulfill our financial obligation, as outlined in the mission contract.
143800: I can understand your reluctance to undertake this mission, as we do not know who or what might be out there waiting to attack you in order to obtain these chips. This is a rare moment in that we bear you no malice for your fear.
143801: Please remain off this comms channel, pilot. While your voice is encrypted, the communication itself can be hacked. Contact us only after docking, or, of course in the event you are attacked.
143803: Some decades ago, Amarr veterinary scientists achieved a milestone in genetic manipulation with the creation of hybrid slaver hounds. These new breeds are specifically designed to live and work in extreme climate conditions, which is a boon for all those slave labor facilities on ice planets and other harsh environments. Demand for these animals has been overwhelming and we are struggling to maintain our delivery schedule. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station. From there they will be transshipped to a desert planet and put to work as guard animals.
143804: I really am surprised that you're declining this one. It was a good chance to make some quick LUX with very little risk. Well, no bother. There is no shortage of pilots looking for an easy trip.
143805:
Amarr slavers on Syrikos V first learned to breed and train slaver hounds to provide an extra layer of low-cost security for their slave labor operations. These animals soon proved their worth, particularly as a last line of defense for any slave that managed to bypass a facility's security controls and escape into the whatever wilderness lay beyond the facility's walls. So keen are the senses of these animals, and so lethal their attacks, that most slaves will give up any hope of escape before even making the attempt. One problem that arose, however, was that many slave labor operations were located in some of the harshest imaginable environments, often so harsh that they were unsuitable for your average slaver hound.

So, it was with tremendous satisfaction that Amarr veterinary scientists reported recently that they had managed to create stable, obedient hybrids of the breed, each type adapted for a different geographic or atmospheric condition. Thus, if you are a slave owner on an ice planet, for example, you can now purchase slaver hounds with thicker pelts, greater body fat, and higher overall tolerance to cold and freezing wind. These new hybrids have proven remarkably adaptable, and have long since spread to slave labor facilities throughout the Empire.
143806: Good to know the hounds haven't caused you any trouble. Please contact me when you reach the station. Offloading has already been arranged.
143807: You're quitting this mission? You should know that quitting a mission as simple as this one does not look good on a pilot's record.
143808: The Origins of Hybrid Slaver Hounds
143809: See? I told you this one was a no-brainer.  I would suggest, though, remaining in your ship until the hounds have been safely offloaded. I wouldn't want to be hanging around your cargo bay if one of them got loose, as the sedatives will have worn off by now.
143810: I had a feeling an easy job like this one might interest you. Good chance to flip on the autopilot and take a nap.  Just make sure the cages are secure and locked and your cargo bay doors are sealed.
143811:
I'm not sure how much you know about Amarr slave labor installations, such as mines, agricultural harvesting fields, moon mineral extraction zones, and the like. Well, I can tell you that these facilities are often of such size and complexity that they cannot always be wholly secured against slave escape attempts. Certainly, all but the most primitive and poorly administrated of these locations feature any and all manner of perimeter alarms, security cameras, remote sentry drones, microwave motion detectors, infrared barrier fences, you name it. As you can imagine, though, this can get quite expensive given not only the capital outlay for the equipment, but for the manpower needed to operate and maintain them year-round, 24 hours a day.

It was during this search for lower cost alternatives to these technologies that the animals we call slaver hounds were introduced to the overall security plans of select slave labor facilities, used to detect, track, and interdict runaway slaves. Their acutely tuned senses coupled with their remarkable natural endurance and speed made them an ideal choice for many Amarr slave operations. However, it was not long before it was realized that the standard, purebred slaver hound was not suitable for all environments. This resulted in the creation of genetically modified breeds more at home in harsher environments such as swamps, frozen wastelands, jungles, and the like. Today, these more adaptable variants can be found on many such installations throughout the Empire, despite their comparatively high cost when compared to your usual slaver hounds.

This brings us to the reason I contacted you. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station for transshipment to an Amarr desert planet. As long as the hounds remain sedated and don't find their way out of their cages, this should be a simple, trouble-free courier job.
143812:
Yes, I think I have some work for you.

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
143813: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.
143814: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.
