144096: Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.
144097: You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.
144098: While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.
144099: Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.
144100: That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.
144101: Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.
144102: Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!
144103: Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.
144104: During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.
144105:
I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?
144106: Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.
144107: We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.
144108: We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.
144109: Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.
144113: I haven't received confirmation of your delivery yet, {[character]player.name}. Is there a problem?
144115: Smaller ships rely upon their speed and smaller signature radius to make it difficult for larger ships to track and target them. The heat output from propulsion systems increases signature radius, making a small target much easier to track; the greater the speed, the greater the heat production. Specialized coatings help to reduce the effect and prevent expansion of the parts within propulsion systems, helping them to operate much more efficiently.
144116: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. The testers have already submitted a preliminary report. The results seem favorable towards our new design, and we've received permission to begin a small first-run production.
144117: This shipment of Mesarchonite needs to be taken to the manufacturer on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. The cargo is radioactive, and while the containment units are good enough for a short period, the mineral really requires an industrial containment in a stable and controlled environment.
144118: Okay, take a look at this. You know what this is? Yes, yes, it's a rock. It's a rare mineral, actually, called Mesarchonite. It has industrial applications, but it's mostly used in security systems. The reason it's in a special containment field is that it's also fairly radioactive. Take this shipment over to the manufacturers at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and don't bloody open it!
144119: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. Do try to hurry, you don't want this stuff sitting around too long in your cargo hold.
144122: Have you delivered that Mesarchonite, {[character]player.name}? You don't want to expose your ship to it for much longer.
144125: Security systems on stations are all-in-one, monitoring room occupancy, ambient temperature and humidity, and the gas mix from environmental control. It can be set to go on alert for various stimuli, and contains several redundant systems to ensure that an interrupt on one line does not prevent a problem being reported. Small pieces of radioactive material which are sensitive to various stimuli are an integral part of such systems.
144126: One of {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}'s archaeological teams has uncovered a load of pre-Federation relics. I need you to transport the pieces to a laboratory for analysis.
144127: One of our archaeological teams has unearthed a load of pre-Federation tech from a moon in this system. We're really excited about this; I don't think I need to explain to you how the results of this find could give us a leg up on the competition. Get this lot over to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and don't tell anyone!
144129: Sad. I thought you'd have more interest than that.
144131: {[character]player.name}, have you delivered those artifacts yet?
144132: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. The minerals that society was focusing on are pretty worthless to us -- it's just crystalline octenase, borealt and the like -- but it looks like they were used in the basic construction of the ship they used for the outpost. Who would have thought of coating low-density tritanium panels with a lassenium compound? With a little work, we can find out where their culture came from, and why they're not here anymore.
144134: Corporations often sponsor archaeological and research projects, paying for work permits and equipment when the people involved need them. In exchange, the corporations obtain exclusive rights to any discoveries which are made. This includes the right to display and charge viewing fees, or to make new developments based upon information obtained from the artifacts.
144135:
Oh! {[character]player.name}, perfect timing!

One of our research outposts in Molden Heath came under attack by rogue drones last week. This is highly unusual, since drones are rarely seen beyond Etherium Reach. The outpost's defense systems managed to keep our scientists safe, and the downed drones were retrieved for examination. They found unusual mineral deposits replacing the drones' original microboard networks, which appear to work far more efficiently.

Of course we don't want anyone else getting ahold of the samples before we can replicate them. The samples have been in transit via a series of drops in order to keep them safe. Take them on to the labs at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
144136: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! I can't wait to see what we've got.
144137: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.
144138: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I thought I could trust you for this.
144139: {[character]player.name}, have you done what I asked?
144140: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. We're one step closer to the forefront of technological advancement!
144141: While examining wrecked rogue drones following a failed attack, strange minerals were found which replaced some of the drones' usual systems. The compounds seem to run more efficiently than the parts they replaced, and your agent has hired you to take the find to researchers for examination.
144143:
Rogue drones began innocently enough, as part of a Gallente scientist's research into drones that could learn and operate independently. The artificial intelligence he created was in itself fairly primitive and non-threatening, but in its self-perpetuation it developed beyond the scope of the scientist's work, and the drones began to truly think for themselves.
Using the justification that the results had produced extreme and life-threatening risk to human life, CONCORD declared all research into artificial intelligence illegal unless performed in a controlled and isolated environment under the watchful eye of DED experts. Proposals for engaging in such research are vetted carefully and the scientists presenting the proposals are subject to extreme background scrutiny.
144144: Against my better judgment, I've been asked to order several sets of educational packages of the Amarr Scriptures for the children of families who have been released by the Empire. It leaves a sour taste in the mouth, but maybe we can use the teaching materials to our own ends.
144145:
I'm in a bit of an awkward position here, {[character]player.name}. With all the people being released from slavery in the Empire, we're getting more and more families who practice the Amarr religion. No thanks to Jamyl, she knew this would happen. The edict from our government is that we need to respect the poor deluded people and gently introduce them to a new way of thinking. It won't be easy, and it's putting a strain on all of us.

My problem right now is that a bunch of the refugee families have requested that some Amarr Scriptures be included in the course structure at the schools we've set up for their children. It's our own people doing the teaching, so we can slowly steer the education in the right direction, but we all still feel dirty for having to use it.

Do you think you'd be willing to take a shipment of books over to one of the schools?
144146: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. I knew I could count on you.
144150: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. I know it's an unsavory business, but our instructions from on high are to try to get along and help these people adjust.
144152: With the release of several generations of slaves from the Empire, Jamyl struck a blow at the heart of Minmatar culture, forcing the Republic to accept those who have known only the ways of Amarr and what little Minmatar tradition they had been able to maintain through the years. Inducting such people into modern Republic society has proven troublesome and at times outright frustrating; allowing released slaves to practice the religion they grew up with has been a bitter necessity as counselors struggle to help the people adapt to their new lives.
144153: A nearby station has suffered a life-support failure. They got the atmospheric regulators working again, but the interior temperature is starting to drop. Get the heating units over there quickly, before the place gets too cold.
144154:
A severe accident has occurred on another station, {[character]player.name}; they suffered a freak blowout in primary life-support, and the station's environmental control shut down entirely. No, don't panic, they stabilized the atmosphere as soon as they could, so the people on the station won't asphyxiate. But the internal heating units have yet to be replaced. People are bundling up as their heat bleeds out – the external insulation is some protection, but it's not enough.

Fortunately for them, we've been developing some hyper-efficient portable heaters here. Donating a bunch will be good publicity for us. It'll also be a good field test for the heaters, and we may get a few preorders from it if people like them. Take these over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and make sure you let them know who donated them.
144156: Well, I'm certain we can find someone who values their job more.
144157: You're heartless, {[character]player.name}. What about all those people?
144158: Have you delivered the heating units yet?
144159: Thanks, {[character]player.name}! The field-test was invaluable. Turns out the units couldn't handle consistent use for more than 16 hours, something we never tested for in the labs. The next version of the heaters will be much better!
144161: The most vital systems on a space station or starship, life-support covers everything from atmosphere generation and recycling to environmental control to the recycling of drinking and pumping water. Originally a series of tanks containing specialized filters, as residence in space extended from long-term to lifetimes, advances in bioengineering developed hydroponics systems for stations which both produce and recycle air and water efficiently. Environmental control, which cycles water and air through the station and maintains an even internal temperature despite the cold of space outside nibbling at the edges, runs off the same generator as the internal electrical circuits. External electrical devices, such as guide-lights, shielding and containment fields, security systems and communications, run from separate generators with extensive backup arrays.
144162: One of our planetside subsidiaries has recently lost a lot of farming equipment to a storm. I need you to take these parts to the assembly plant so we can recoup our losses.
144163: One of our subsidiaries has recently suffered a major setback, {[character]player.name}. A hurricane wiped out half their planetside crops and wrecked the equipment. Most of it was already falling apart, the storm just finished it off. Obviously, this is a big problem for them, and us, but it's still the early part of the first growing season. Deliver these parts to the assembly plant at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} so we can replace the equipment before they lose too much from this harvest.
144167: Have you delivered those parts yet, {[character]player.name}?
144168: Thank you for your help, {[character]player.name}. Our subsidiary has managed to save more than they first thought of the initial crops and they're good to go for the second growing season.
144170: Despite the increasing popularity of fully-automated hydroponics farms, many planetary economies continue to rely on large-scale land-farming to provide jobs and food for local populations. On particularly fertile worlds even small start-up farms can be instantly successful, but in order to compete with larger farms in the market, these smaller farms frequently approach large corporations, offering to supply certain vital organic produce in exchange for controlling market shares.
144171: A Nefantar House is relocating to a planet within the Republic, and we've had a tip-off that they're working against us for someone in the Empire. We've planted surveillance nanobots in a shipment of materials for their planetside home; take it over to the depot. The logs will show nothing amiss.
144172:
I hope I can trust you to be discreet, {[character]player.name}.

As part of a goodwill gesture to the Nefantar tribe, the Republic has offered allotments of planetary territory within our space on which to build embassies or summer homes or whatever else they need land for. I don't care what it is, I don't trust ‘em, but the government is determined to make sure we all get along.

Yesterday I got an alert from one of my colleagues; it seems one Nefantar house is in collusion with elements from the Empire. Obviously we can't just point fingers without evidence, but I'm in a perfect position to obtain that. The contractor they hired to design and build a house on their new property is a friend of mine. He's given us one shipment of interior facing materials to seed with nanite spyware. Take the load to the depot at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}; I know I can trust you to keep quiet about the additions to the cargo.
144173: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. If anyone asks where those came from, the manifest will show their usual station.
144175: I'm beginning to question your loyalty, {[character]player.name}.
144176: Have you delivered your cargo for me, {[character]player.name}?
144177: Thanks to your assistance, {[character]player.name}, we've been able to record some rather incriminating communications from these people already. They wasted no time in contacting their associates in the Empire to let them know they were settled in.
144179:
The day Drupar Maak struck down Arkon Ardishapur on Starkman Prime with the Heir's own sceptre began the darkest night for his people. In retribution for the death of his father and their attempted rebellion, Idonis Ardishapur ordered the annihilation of the Starkmanir tribe.

At the same time, the Nefantar tribe approached the Empire with an offer, making a bargain for mercy in exchange for assisting in the subjugation of the Minmatar. The tribe took on many aspects of the Empire, including open practise of their faith and owning Minmatar slaves, themselves. Despite the recent revelation that their conversion helped to protect the last Starkmanir to survive the purge, many within the Republic are hesitant to forgive the Nefantar for their actions.
144180: {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has a number of outposts in w-space systems, exploring what lies beyond known space. They've turned up some unusual pieces which I need you to take to a more extensive laboratory for identification.
144181: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. Hurry up! This could be our biggest breakthrough yet!
144182: If it's not worth your time, you could have just said so.
144184: I've not received a receipt for the cargo yet, {[character]player.name}.
144185: The strangest thing happened when they got all the pieces slotted together: the light inside them stopped flickering and turned blue. We're not certain what that means, since nothing else happened, but it appears to be a sign we're on the right track!
144187: Capsuleers aren't the only people to explore the systems accessible via wormholes. Every corporation wants to be the first to make the Next Big Discovery, and then market the developments from researching it. Most corporations will categorically deny that this is what they're doing, creating an atmosphere of both paranoia and plausible deniability if their explorations turn up nothing of value.
144188: A small startup that {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} has recently invested in has been hired to build a water garden for a Gallente politician, but the frogs he wanted are too dangerous to the fish. Fortunately, there's a variety that are just as ornamental without the side effects. I need you to take them over before we lose our investment.
144189:
Yes, yes, perhaps you could help me out.

A well-known politician is having a vacation suite commissioned in another station, and decided that he just could not live without an ornamental water-garden. One of our daughter-companies was hired for the work, and it could be just the break they need to make a name for themselves in the interior design industry.

Thing is, on stations, such gardens need to be self-supporting ecosystems in their own right. He had a load of very pretty frogs shipped in to add color and control the inevitable insect populations, but those lovely little Leina's Darters are also beautifully toxic, and the fish that eat them are dying. We've finally discovered a variety that won't prevent the fish from reproducing. Take this load over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and quickly, before His Honor decides he wants a rock garden instead and we lose our investment.
144191: I'm sorry to hear that, {[character]player.name}. I'll just have to find someone else.
144193: Have you delivered those frogs yet, {[character]player.name}?
144194: Thanks to your work, it looks like Holistic Habitat, LLC is on its way up. The politician can't praise the quality of his water-garden enough.
144196: Nothing boasts of a flexible wallet than a private garden within the walls of one's apartment. Society's elite will spend a great deal of money to obtain a perfect replica of the Intaki rainforests or Mannar seaside in which to entertain guests and impress prospective clients. Extra emphasis is placed on making such gardens self-supporting, including specially-engineered fauna to keep the flora happy.
144197: Our salvagers have built up a load of industrial-quality scrap metal to be used in ship building. I need you to take it to the reclamation facility so we can recover the useable parts.
144198:
Okay, here's one for you. Don't look at me like that. Yes, it's a load of metal scraps we need taken to a reclamation facility at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Contrary to popular belief, our ships are not made solely of scrap-metal, utility adhesive and chewing gum, but we do recycle extensively.

The reason I'm asking you to do this rather than hiring a much cheaper regular captain is that these bits are industrial quality, or they will be once they've been processed. They're worth a lot of cred on the black market – peanuts to you capsuleers, but a year's wages to anyone else.
144199: Thanks, {[character]player.name}. It's not a glamorous job but someone's gotta do it.
144201: Sad, {[character]player.name}. I had hoped you were the reliable sort.
144202: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?
144203: Good! You've been a big help, {[character]player.name}.
144205:
Since its dawning days, New Eden's landscape has been riddled with conflict, both political and physical. Battles waged and lost have left scars upon planets and littered constellations with floating wrecks. Close to where the Eve Gate lies in Genesis, abandoned stations pose navigational threats to pilots, and many stars are developing orbital rings of human-made space junk.

Despite the risks inherent in a single scrap of metal the size of a man, hurtling through space at just below light-speed – never mind something as vast as a wrecked starship – governments either cannot afford or cannot be bothered to send teams to clean them up. The most dangerous pieces are towed out of the primary space-lanes, then left adrift in deadspace, marked with tracking-beacons. Scavenging is publicly discouraged, though authorities tend to turn a blind eye when various pieces end up on the market. Most of the finds end up in the hands of artists, inventors and archaeologists. One large piece of hull-plating found on the market, still bearing the much-corroded legend MAF Commandant Aurora, was identified as belonging to one of the earliest Gallente interplanetary shuttles, and now forms part of a wall in a museum on Gallente Prime.
144206: A friend and I are running a small holoreel bootlegging operation on the side. The shipments are bound for Syndicate, but I only need you to take them on to where my business partner is operating from. The cargo has been disguised as standard holoreels, an effective disguise provided nobody looks too closely at the contents.
144207:
I like nice things, {[character]player.name}. Who doesn't? Handing missions out to you people all day doesn't offer nearly enough to cover my expenses, so a friend and I run a shipping business out to Syndicate space. Nothing big enough to interfere with the Syndicate itself, mind you. We provide a humanitarian service importing the latest holos from the heart of civilization. It's the only way they can get the things for a reasonable cost – buying them direct from the companies in the Federation incurs immense shipping charges.

Our usual courier is out of commission today, with her ship in for repairs after a pirate attack. If you want to make yourself useful, take the latest shipment over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and ask for Amelyn. They'll know who you mean, just say that “Imba” sent you.
144208: Good, good. Get going, would you?
144209: Fine. It's not like anyone would believe you if you told them, anyway.
144210: What? Why now? Couldn't you just have refused at the start? Now we'll have to move our operation elsewhere.
144211: Amelyn hasn't contacted me yet, {[character]player.name}. What's the hold up?
144214: Founded by Intaki exiles after the first Caldari-Gallente war, Syndicate rapidly became a safe haven for criminals and the more unsavoury sorts of businesses which can't operate as freely in Empire space. Anything and everything can be found on the market, including things people would rather not be shared openly. Secrets – both personal and professional – fetch a good price, and the sellers rarely care who the money comes from.
144215: A pair of civilians too wealthy for their own good are holding a decadent reception for their wedding, and ordered a tremendously expensive champagne to keep their guests entertained. A regular pilot can't be trusted to ship the drinks in, but what's a thousand-LUX bottle of wine to a capsuleer?
144216:
Do you read the gossip rags? I wouldn't expect you to; you capsuleers obviously have greater concerns than who's mocking whom this week. The big news right now is this wedding being planned by Ahvir en Foilien, the former co-star of Under Wraps. He's not been heard from since he got canned as the host of the Sugar Sweep game show, but now he's caused a ruckus by arranging a marriage to the daughter of Material Acquisition bigwig Hemy Selvah. A lot of money obviously changed hands to manage this, since Selvah's daughter isn't quite ten years old, and en Foilien already has a wife, a husband and a few playmates on the side.

If you believe what the tabloids say, that is. Who knows what the truth might be?

En Foilien has arranged a lavish party on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} which is undoubtedly meant to encourage the public and the reporters to overlook the dodgy circumstances and remind them that he used to be important. It doesn't really matter. He's ordered several crates of Feille d'Marnne champagne to loosen them up and assist with the memory loss.
144217: Thanks, {[character]player.name}, I knew we could count on you.
144218: Fine, I'll find someone else, hopefully before it's too late.
144219: I'm not laughing, {[character]player.name}. I have a reputation to maintain, you know.
144220: I haven't received a receipt for that champagne yet. What's the hold up?
144221: Thank you, {[character]player.name}. That party isn't one the glitterati will soon forget; Selvah's daughter threw her entire glass of champagne in en Foilien's face and called him some very unflattering schoolyard names. Of course it was all caught on camera, and the media is having a field day.
144223: Nobody loves a good party more than the Gallente. The hedonistic stereotype is one that the Federation revels in and flaunts shamelessly. Public figures actively compete to host the wildest and most fashionable affairs, vying for the attention of news services and gossip magazines. Among the celebrity elite, a wedding, birth or even a funeral is simply another excuse to splash out and stand in the limelight. Occasionally, an event will be engineered so a falling star can make a desperate final grasp at publicity and salvage a faded career.
144224: One of my clients asked me to send over drones to replace the ones his company's been losing in the line of work. That's all he said. He never said anything about needing mining drones; of course I sent him a set of scout drones, and he was very upset at me for not being able to read his mind. People should be more specific about things. Take these mining drones over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for him, and if he asks why the paint looks new, tell him they're fresh off the production line.
144225: Just make sure to tell him how sorry I am, okay?
144226: Fine. I can always find someone else.
144227: I am very disappointed in you, {[character]player.name}.
144228: Have you finished your work for me, {[character]player.name}?
144229: Excellent. I've been trying to get those old things off my hands for months.
144230: I accidentally sent a client the wrong set of drones because they never specified what type he needed. Take the right cargo to him. Hopefully he won't ask too many questions.
144232: The most common mining drone, the Spider Drone, is manufactured by Ishukone. The brainchild of Chief Foreman Jaartu Mediuri in the early days following the first Caldari-Gallente war, the first mining drones were little more than immense strip-mining factories which were deposited on the surface of an asteroid to chew through the surface and process useful minerals until their belly holds were full, then sending an alert to the foreman for uplift and unloading. It wasn't until advances simplified the operation of the mining laser that Mediuri proposed automating a laser and attaching directional thrusters. The project was shelved indefinitely after the initial models failed repeatedly, but after Ishukone headhunted the prodigy roboticist Vayan Hemitaru from Sukuuvestaa, the programme restarted with renewed energy and interest. Eventually a self-powered, mobile mining laser was produced. Some contention was held over its need for basic guidance from an operator, but Ishukone argued that full autonomy was unnecessary, particularly since use of capsule-controlled ships had become common and a capsuleer controller could, through experience and training, more than accommodate for the lack.
144233: Planetary officials have asked me to bring in a team of mercenaries they've hired to deal with a terrorist threat. Your job is to keep them in line en route.
144234: We have a planetary situation we need your help with. A group of pro-Amarr terrorists is wreaking havoc in outlying provinces, and the local government's hired a group of mercenaries to deal with them. You know mercs, I'm sure; they never really listen to anyone they think is softer than they are. We're having trouble finding an ordinary captain who's willing to ferry the guys over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for transit planetside. I think they'll be more likely to behave if the captain is someone who can and will follow through on a threat to vent the ship to vacuum. Someone like you, in other words. Can we count on you to keep the unruly lot in line?
144235: Good to hear, {[character]player.name}! Don't actually vent the ship, though. We need these guys.
144236: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.
144237: Sad. Now I'll have to find someone else. You were the best option, too.
144238: Those mercs aren't giving you too much trouble, I hope.
144239: Excellent, {[character]player.name}! I'll let the local government know their solution is on its way.
144241:
Despite centuries of enslavement and the systematic erasure of half their culture, some Minmatar advocate a return to “the old ways,” total service the Amarr. Many of these are adherents to the Amarr religion, others are simply willing to do anything for the right pay.

Activism can be as tame as preaching on street-corners or door-to-door, or as extreme as acts of violence and sabotage. The general population of the Republic resents being proselytized and threatened, and in some parts of the Republic clashes have occurred between demonstrators and bystanders. One notable clash on Huggar left 39 dead and hundreds hospitalized for shrapnel wounds and burns.
144242: There has been an uprising at one of our slave Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRCs, near a rather large ore mine. The slaves are almost wholly Minmatar, so we cannot afford to have this incident continue for even one more day. The longer it goes on, the greater the chances that some reporter or news agency will get wind of this and splash the story all over the region. Given that the Minmatar Republic may feel compelled to take action to aid their brethren, this can only lead to dire consequences. That, of course, is unacceptable. We do have a plan in place, however, that should end this uprising before it has a chance to truly take root. We need you to transport a large contingent of Riot Interdiction Team (RIT) personnel to a designated station. From there the assembled security teams will join up and embark a small fleet of frigates and cruisers to race to the prison, where they will use all necessary force to terminate this uprising before it gets completely out of control.
144243: Bah – I should have known you wouldn't help us. I could tell when I first met you that you were beyond salvation.
144244: Good job, pilot. Please make all possible haste to the station as the other teams are waiting on you. The assault phase will begin after you deliver the RIT personnel and their equipment.
144245:
The Amarr Empire, realizing many centuries ago that it could not simply work slaves to the point of death, instituted a number of improvements to worker conditions in an effort to prolong the usable lifespan of its slaves. These changes were not universal across the Empire, due in large part to the Empress's unwillingness to create what might have amounted to significant friction between slave -based companies. Therefore, these decisions were largely left to the Five Heirs and their subordinate regional offices. Thus, we can state here that history has shown a lack of consistent application of these worker improvement programs across the Empire. Those Amarr systems that have chosen to incorporate these adaptations have, however, consistently derived greater revenues due to these enhanced and ongoing pacification efforts.

These shortcomings led directly to the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers (LRC). An LRC is designed much like a multilevel prison, with facilities for low, medium, and high risk inmates. The inmates are those slaves who consistently exhibit defiance or even outright hostility towards the managerial staff at the mine, construction site, or other location to which they are assigned as slave labor. Once we have identified these persons they are immediately removed from their job site and taken to the nearest LRC for corrective behavioral conditioning. This conditioning can include a wide variety of attitude modification methodologies, from intensive drug assisted counseling, to religious indoctrination, and from advanced torture techniques and a concurrent system of rewards - the so-called “carrot and stick approach” - and any number of programs in between. In this way, we break the individual slave's will so that he may be returned to the workforce as a docile and useful component in the labor pool.
144246: Bless the Empress – I am very glad to hear you've decided to help. The RIT personnel will meet you in the hangar bay shortly.  Please feel free to take any of our religious literature with you for your enlightenment during the flight.
144247: You soulless coward! Without the men you agreed to deliver our assault on the prison will undoubtedly lead to unnecessary casualties on all sides.
144249: Our security and military ground forces have been experiencing a slow but steady increase in the numbers and severity of injuries suffered during a wide range of armed conflicts. A recent stuffy by Amarr military scientists has determined that the primary cause of this has been a failure to adequately improve the lightweight body armor worn by millions of our soldiers, Marines, police, and other fighting forces. As fate would have it, one of our intelligence units has obtained what they claim to be a revolutionary new fabric that could provide fifty percent better protection across the board in all types of engagements. We need you to deliver this very sensitive cargo to a station we designate.
144250:
Thank you for coming, pilot. As you know, the Amarr Empire is in a constant state of conflict. Our enemies have included organized criminal gangs, drug traffickers, terrorists of every conceivable motivation, pirates, unpacified slave populations, and even the occasional low level skirmish against our fair-weather friends, the Caldari, Gallente, and, lest we forget, the Minmatar. This requires the Empire to always remain vigilant to any situations that may call for the use of force on levels ranging from simple urban pacification to outright military combat. What you do not know is that a high-level internal Empire report has revealed that our casualty levels have been steadily increasing over the last several years, often requiring evacuation to more robust – and already overburdened – medical facilities.

In the “recommendations” section of this report, the researchers concluded that the single most identifiable cause of these excessive casualties is a systemic problem with our lightweight body armor. This armor is standard issue for millions of police and security personnel, as well as our military reconnaissance units. Unless a drastic improvement in the quality and durability of this body armor can be found, we will continue to suffer the consequences.

This morning I received a priority communication from an Amarr Intelligence Officer claiming that his team had just “obtained” a revolutionary new fabric that, if properly processed, could literally double the strength of our existing armor. I know this officer only by reputation, and it is best not to pry any further into how his team came across this “miracle cloth.” Nonetheless, we have been advised that they will arrive at this station within moments to transfer the fabric here for transshipment to a more secure facility.

So, pilot, will you transport this prototype body armor fabric to the station facility we designate?
144252: Quitting mid-mission is not something I expected from you. Now I am going to have to answer to the intelligence team. Oh, and don't expect any further jobs from me until your failure here has been long forgotten. Damn… I need a stress pill….
144253: I must say I am disappointed in your decision to turn down this mission. I vouched for you personally, given what I have seen in your files about your excellent mission completion record. I will not soon forget your refusal.
144254: Lightweight body armor is a common and often required element of any police or security forces' operational gear. Modern armor of this type can stop most projectile, laser, and other light weapon fire. However, as small arms weaponry continued to evolve with regard to the amount of damage it can inflict, so to must the defensive technologies designed to maintain parity with these weapons. On rare occasions, a corporation, military laboratory, or other entity will produce a light body armor system that represents nothing short of a generational leap in design and protection. The multilayered fabrics used in these latter applications are usually amongst the most highly guarded secrets of any civilization, for many reasons. The most advanced of these contain nanotechnology which also can change color and density depending on ambient conditions and/or input from the wearer.
144255: Outstanding, pilot. You were even a bit ahead of schedule. Our offloading team is en route to your ship, and the Intel guards will stay with the shipment until that has been completed. I will keep your name in my “go to” list should any more missions come up in the future.
144256: Thank you for the update pilot, but no need to contact me until you arrive. The Intel security team on your ship is keeping me quite well informed.
144257: Some decades ago, Amarr veterinary scientists achieved a milestone in genetic manipulation with the creation of hybrid slaver hounds. These new breeds are specifically designed to live and work in extreme climate conditions, which is a boon for all those slave labor facilities on ice planets and other harsh environments. Demand for these animals has been overwhelming and we are struggling to maintain our delivery schedule. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station. From there they will be transshipped to a desert planet and put to work as guard animals.
144258: I really am surprised that you're declining this one. It was a good chance to make some quick LUX with very little risk. Well, no bother. There is no shortage of pilots looking for an easy trip.
144259:
Amarr slavers on Syrikos V first learned to breed and train slaver hounds to provide an extra layer of low-cost security for their slave labor operations. These animals soon proved their worth, particularly as a last line of defense for any slave that managed to bypass a facility's security controls and escape into the whatever wilderness lay beyond the facility's walls. So keen are the senses of these animals, and so lethal their attacks, that most slaves will give up any hope of escape before even making the attempt. One problem that arose, however, was that many slave labor operations were located in some of the harshest imaginable environments, often so harsh that they were unsuitable for your average slaver hound.

So, it was with tremendous satisfaction that Amarr veterinary scientists reported recently that they had managed to create stable, obedient hybrids of the breed, each type adapted for a different geographic or atmospheric condition. Thus, if you are a slave owner on an ice planet, for example, you can now purchase slaver hounds with thicker pelts, greater body fat, and higher overall tolerance to cold and freezing wind. These new hybrids have proven remarkably adaptable, and have long since spread to slave labor facilities throughout the Empire.
144260: Good to know the hounds haven't caused you any trouble. Please contact me when you reach the station. Offloading has already been arranged.
144261: You're quitting this mission? You should know that quitting a mission as simple as this one does not look good on a pilot's record.
144262: The Origins of Hybrid Slaver Hounds
144263: See? I told you this one was a no-brainer.  I would suggest, though, remaining in your ship until the hounds have been safely offloaded. I wouldn't want to be hanging around your cargo bay if one of them got loose, as the sedatives will have worn off by now.
144264: I had a feeling an easy job like this one might interest you. Good chance to flip on the autopilot and take a nap.  Just make sure the cages are secure and locked and your cargo bay doors are sealed.
144265:
I'm not sure how much you know about Amarr slave labor installations, such as mines, agricultural harvesting fields, moon mineral extraction zones, and the like. Well, I can tell you that these facilities are often of such size and complexity that they cannot always be wholly secured against slave escape attempts. Certainly, all but the most primitive and poorly administrated of these locations feature any and all manner of perimeter alarms, security cameras, remote sentry drones, microwave motion detectors, infrared barrier fences, you name it. As you can imagine, though, this can get quite expensive given not only the capital outlay for the equipment, but for the manpower needed to operate and maintain them year-round, 24 hours a day.

It was during this search for lower cost alternatives to these technologies that the animals we call slaver hounds were introduced to the overall security plans of select slave labor facilities, used to detect, track, and interdict runaway slaves. Their acutely tuned senses coupled with their remarkable natural endurance and speed made them an ideal choice for many Amarr slave operations. However, it was not long before it was realized that the standard, purebred slaver hound was not suitable for all environments. This resulted in the creation of genetically modified breeds more at home in harsher environments such as swamps, frozen wastelands, jungles, and the like. Today, these more adaptable variants can be found on many such installations throughout the Empire, despite their comparatively high cost when compared to your usual slaver hounds.

This brings us to the reason I contacted you. I need a large shipment of these hybrid slaver hounds delivered to a nearby station for transshipment to an Amarr desert planet. As long as the hounds remain sedated and don't find their way out of their cages, this should be a simple, trouble-free courier job.
144266: Due to a recent series of inspections by the regional mine monitoring commission, we have found it necessary to purchase a large quantity of the latest generation of environmentally-friendly drills and related equipment. In order to avoid financial penalties and the possible loss of our mining rights, that company must get these quite expensive new drills into the hands of the miners as soon as possible. If you can deliver this cargo to the station that serves as our logistical hub for this system, they can then have their own pilots transship them to the required planetary mining locations.
144267:
Let me start at the beginning. As you have probably seen on the news channels, a prominent Caldari mining company is in the middle of a very nasty battle for economic survival with a new, up-and-coming mining company from within the same large conglomerate. Both of these companies specialize in the extraction of ores from some of the more inhospitable and dangerous locations in this and several adjoining systems. While this can be hazardous with regard to men and equipment, the profit potential from these largely untapped ore reserves can be quite significant, which brings me to our current predicament.

As you may know, the specialized manual labor required for some of these mines can be significant in terms of numbers. Well, the Mining Health and Safety Commission, or MHSC, for this region recently conducted a survey of the first company's operations, and found that their mining practices at certain locations may have resulted in excessive pollution, then further alleged a corresponding link to long-term miner health problems. The company has loudly complained that this is a ridiculous witch hunt brought about by their new competitor, which happens to have several “friends” on the commission. While they work to ensure they are equally “represented” on that commission, the recent finding has mandated that they immediately improve worker conditions and reduce pollution or risk losing their mining rights. To remedy this problem, they recently purchased a large number of the latest environmentally-friendly – and obscenely expensive – manportable drills, which seems to have assuaged the MHSC for the moment. They do, however, have a deadline for actually putting these new drills into the hands of the miners, which brings us to the reason I contacted you.

We need you to deliver a rather large shipment of drills and other related equipment to a station that serves as a central service hub. From there, logistics pilots will deliver this and other items to the various mines in the system. Will you take on this important job?
144268: We are shocked to hear that you have chosen to quit this job in the middle of the contract. We will now have to pay another pilot double to pick up where you left off. You should have let us know from the outset that you could not take on this important job. Hopefully, we will never have to rely on you again.
144269: Well, I must say we are quite disappointed that you would turn down this very easy contract. We shall find another pilot and move your name to the bottom of our list. Don't call us, we'll call you.
144270: I certainly do appreciate your help, pilot. Hopefully, if we can get these drills into the hands of the miners in short order, the company should be able to retain its mining rights and return to profitability.
144271: You seem to be on schedule and we look forward to the prompt delivery of the equipment to the designated station. Contact us through the usual channels after you have offloaded this gear.
144272: Job well done. Our logistics teams are loading your shipment into their transport vessels as we speak, and we should have the drills and equipment in place shortly. We will definitely contact you again, should we require your services.
144273: Following a string of suicide terrorist attacks yesterday, we managed to capture a high ranking member of their organization. Interrogations have revealed, however, that a devastating viral weapon, based on nanotechnology, is already in place and primed for release. We need you to deliver the only known countermeasure to this agent, manportable electromagnetic weapons. If we are successful, these weapons could eradicate the virus before it has a chance to spread and infect the entire station.
144274: Pilot, there is simply no time to discuss this any further. Deliver the cargo to the station immediately, before that horrible weapon kills thousands of innocent men, women, and children.
144275:
Last night, a strike team of suicide terrorists from the Anti-Corporatist Revolutionary Front, or ARCF, struck at more than twenty Caldari offices and stations throughout the region. During one of these attacks a terrorist was captured with a well-shielded, improvised nuclear device hidden in his rucksack. Obviously this event represents an entirely new level of threat from the ARCF, now that they have proven themselves willing to carry out such a horrendous and indiscriminate mass casualty attack.

The only upside to this is that the terrorist has turned out to be the most notorious operative of the ARCF, a woman known as Commander Rachendia. Having her in custody has offered us an opportunity to gain information related to her group's future plans to strike at the Caldari State. During one of the more aggressive interrogations, she disclosed information about a pending attack against one of our nearby stations. The nature of the attack is not entirely clear; however, we know with certainty that it involves the surreptitious introduction of a viral agent into the life support and air circulation systems.

Our initial searches for these hidden canisters at that station have, so far, been fruitless – with the exception of one small aerosol-type canister. A preliminary test revealed that these viral weapons appear to be based on a self-replicating nanotechnology. Once released from stasis in their container, they seek out and consume human tissue, and leaving behind little more than dust. Our medical scientists have calculated that just one container, released into the central air processing vents, could result in the deaths of all human life aboard a medium-sized station within no more than four hours. The only good news is that these nanos are programmed to self-terminate within 12 hours. Of course, this would be far more time than would be necessary to kill everyone aboard all but the largest of stations.

Your role in this desperate situation is to deliver a cargo of electromagnetic weapons, modified to emit a short-range pulse that will literally "fry" any nanos within its range. So, we are asking: will you deliver these containers to the station immediately? Thousands of lives may depend on your answer.
144276: We had placed all our hope in you completing this mission. It's too late now to find another pilot and another ship. I fear many thousands of lives may be lost due to what can only be your cowardice. Obviously, you are not a man of your word, and we won't forget that.
144277: Your bravery and skillful piloting without question, saved the lives of untold numbers of innocent people. We will definitely move your name to the top of our list for any future time-sensitive missions!
144278: We're very glad to hear you are willing to take on this important mission. If we can get these EM devices to the station in time, I know we can save many innocent lives.
144279: We are all terribly disappointed in your refusal to transport these electromagnetic weapons to the station. We shall now have to find another pilot and another ship, and I fear even then we will be too late. I doubt you will be sleeping very well after you see what may become of that station.
144280: Terrorists, working with criminal scientists, have developed a strain of viral weaponry that is based on nanotechnology. When combined, the "hive mind" of the viral strain works to seek out human tissue at which point the microscopic nanos begin to quickly disassemble the tissue, leading to a slow and painful death. Research into electromagnetic pulses has provided some promising leads with regard to countermeasures, but these have not yet been field tested.
144282: A small, platoon-sized Caldari special operation team is in hiding on a Gallente planet and in danger of being captured or killed. They are low on water, food, weapons, and other equipment and will not last long unless they are extracted. We have a rescue standing by; however, we need you to deliver the required materials to their station so that they can then proceed with this critical rescue mission.
144283:
One of our Caldari Navy Special Forces units conducting clandestine reconnaissance of a contested ocean planet – a Gallente-claimed planet, by the way, with extremely rare seabed minerals – sent an emergency burst communication to the covert ops ship in orbit above the planet, requesting immediate extraction. This signal was, in turn, transmitted to the classified comms center here on this station. When we attempted to contact both the team and the ship, however, we received no response. Our immediate reaction was to divert one of our long range Crow-class interceptors, which was in the region on an unrelated mission, to investigate. Soon after its arrival, its sensors confirmed that the covert ops ship had been destroyed.

There is nothing we can do for our lost covops ship; however, this series of events has left the Special Forces team alone and without a means to evacuate the planet. Even worse was a fragment from the original communication indicating that the team was on the run and low on food, water, weapons, and ammunition. They have taken refuge in a disused ocean mining facility, though it is doubtful that they will stay hidden for long. There simply aren't many places to hide on that planet, given the fact that it is mostly covered by massive oceans, with very little land mass. It will not take long for the Gallente to track down our team and either kill them or, worse, capture them for interrogation.

The good news in all this is that we have an extraction team in place, along with a shuttle-equipped vessel to deliver them to the planet. However, given the immediacy of this mission, they had to leave their original base without much of their usual equipment and weaponry. This is where you come in. We need you to transport several containers of highly specialized small arms and related equipment to the station at which the extraction team is currently located. Once you drop off this cargo, the team will gear-up and shuttle down to the planet to rescue the stranded team.

So, pilot, what is it gonna be? Will you help us?
144284: Do not contact us until you have completed this shipment. There is simply no time for idle chatter, not to mention the likelihood that the enemy is almost certainly listening in.
144285: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our military personnel at great risk. It is doubtful that we will be able to find anyone else to get this critical shipment to the station in time.
144286: Your refusal to accept this mission will almost certainly result in the loss of this Special Forces team, not to mention placing the now-dangerously unequipped extraction team at great risk.
144287: Thank you for accepting this important, time-sensitive mission. You have been given priority clearance for station undock, so please leave as soon as possible.
144288: Suicide terrorists have been attacking and destroying our commercial convoys as they have passed through their usual transit zones, despite the presence of heavy security escort vessels. A communications intercept, partially decoded, indicates that these individual intend to step up the level of their attacks by targeting the stations themselves. While we can defend against some of these attackers, based on analysis of their previous attack profiles, we have never had to defend against pilots and ships who fully intend to die by throwing themselves against us without regard for their own lives. Tactical analysis indicates that they will get through our defense and may cause catastrophic damage, likely killing hundreds if not thousands of our civilian workforce and their families. We need you to help us evacuate them immediately!
144289: We have virtually no information on these new threats, other than that they have access to very fast ships filled to the brim with high explosives. Their tactics are simple – they seem to appear out of nowhere, then accelerate their ships to maximum velocity and, ignoring defensive fire, fly directly into the cargo bays of our freighters and other haulers. We are currently working with Caldari Naval Intelligence to determine the source of this scourge; however, early indications from their ship markings are that they belong to an extremists environmental cult that views the Caldari State as the ultimate evil in the universe. They will stop at nothing to destroy us, especially as we expand planetary industry and resource harvesting.
144290: You are quitting on us now? In the middle of an evacuation? Fine. Just deliver those men, women, and children to the nearest safe location, and we will send someone to get them. You are a despicable coward and you'd better hope you never need to transit through this system ever again.
144291: I will never be able to thank you for helping us in our most dire hour. The Caldari Navy should be arriving soon to provide additional security, but that's no guarantee that the terrorists won't follow through with their insidious plans. I will be sure to pass the word throughout the comms networks of the great service you did for all of us today.
144292: I cannot believe what I'm hearing – you are refusing to help save these people? Well, I don't know where we are going to find another ship at this late hour.
144293: Thank you. That is a big load off my shoulders. We need all the good pilots we can get to help us get these people to safety before the terrorists attempt any suicide attack against this station.
144294: Thank you for the update. I am glad to hear the passengers are doing well. I can't tell you how much it means to us that you are willing to divert from more profitable ventures to save these innocent lives.
144296: The Imperial Navy recently made a final attempt to scour the battlefield graveyard of The Battle of Vak-Atioth. This battle pitted our brave Navy against the Jovian enemy; however, due to a number of unforeseeable factors, we did not emerge victorious. The graveyard itself has been picked over for decades by scavengers and others seeking some quick LUX. The Amarr ships sent to perform this duty were attacked by pirates, and only one ship eventually returned. But when it did, it brought with it a valuable icon of Amarr military history: a selection of data chips holding recordings of a small part of that legendary battle. We need these chips delivered to a distant station for proper cleaning and processing.
144297:
As you almost certainly know, many decades ago our Grand Fleet met the hated Jovians on the field of battle in a system known as Vak-Atioth. Most unfortunately, our fleet was destroyed by the technologically superior Jovian ships and their advanced weaponry, marking one of the darkest moments in our history. Still, we learned much from this encounter, and the lessons learned there continue to benefit our military to this day, which brings us to why I called you here.

Several days ago, Imperial naval intelligence mounted a highly classified effort to revisit the Vak-Atioth system, now known simply as Atioth, to conduct a final intensive search for any remaining debris that might provide some insight into the tactics and weapons used by the Jovians. Needless to say, this once-massive floating graveyard has long since been picked over by not only our own salvage fleets, but by scavengers and opportunists alike. All has not been lost, however.

Much to our surprise, the Anathema covert ops ships sent to scan this system returned with a damaged but still readable supply of TIL-1A Nexus Chips. A preliminary review of the information they contain reveals only a portion of the great battle. We are hoping, however, that a more thorough analysis of these chips will reveal some insight into Jovian tactics and technology. If nothing else, they provide a very rare first-hand accounting of the battle which will add greatly to our historical archives and, when displayed at one of our leading military academies, will provide a stirring motivational icon for future generations of brave Imperial naval warriors.

Now that you understand the importance of these chips to the Empire, I must ask: will you transport this invaluable cargo to the designated station?
144298: Many decades ago, a large portion of the Imperial Grand Navy met the Jovians in combat at what today is referred to as The Battle of Vak-Atioth. It was our intention in opening that battle with the as-yet untested Jovians to destroy their fleet utterly, thus forcing their subjugation, as we had done with so many enemies in the past. Without going into great detail, the fearless Amarr fleet was utterly surprised by an enemy that possessed incredible destructive power and remarkably advanced battle tactics. This, coupled with the unforgivable impetuousness of our fleet's leadership, resulted in the near-total annihilation of our warships, at an estimated cost of only one-third of the Jovian armada. We were never again to take to the field of battle against that most dangerous and mysterious opponent. However, while some ships escaped, in less than six hours of battle we left behind a vast field of our dead and dying ships. Today, this system – known now only as Atioth – holds almost none of these battlefield remains, having long since been swept clean by Amarr salvagers and various scavengers. Nonetheless, this system remains an eternal reminder of the vigilance and bravery of our Grand Fleet and the sacrifices they are often called on to make in service of the Empire.
144299: Well, pilot, I could have at least understood refusing this mission in the first place. At least that would have been somewhat understandable given the value nature of the threat. But to quit in mid-shipment is something we did not expect from you. We shall retrieve the chips and deliver them ourselves.
144300: Thank you, pilot. You will be doing the Empire a great service in even such a brief undertaking as this.
144301: You have made a significant contribution to the Empire, pilot. We cannot thank you enough. Of course, no record will be kept of your part in this episode, as we cannot be seen to have been even slightly concerned over the risk of attack and the potential loss of these chips. We will, however, fulfill our financial obligation, as outlined in the mission contract.
144302: I can understand your reluctance to undertake this mission, as we do not know who or what might be out there waiting to attack you in order to obtain these chips. This is a rare moment in that we bear you no malice for your fear.
144303: Please remain off this comms channel, pilot. While your voice is encrypted, the communication itself can be hacked. Contact us only after docking, or, of course in the event you are attacked.
144305: Amarr scientists, working at a clandestine engineering laboratory in a nearby system may have developed the hardest metal yet known to science, known as Ditanium. The potential applications for warfare, specifically, in hardening our warships, is simply too tempting to pass up. Therefore, the full weight of the Amarr military science machine is waiting eagerly for the results of the pending tests, in which the Ditanium plates will be affixed to a specially modified frigate for flight testing. Therefore, we need you to deliver a large quantity of these plates to a nearby station where it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship.
144306:
As you know, Amarr warships rely heavily on the various armors that we use in the construction and upgrading of our ships. For the most part, we rely on the same metals and alloys found in markets and hangars found in virtually every corner of the populated regions. Thus, it is a rare thing when a wholly new metal appears – and rarer still when only one race discovers it, unbeknownst to the others.

Such an occurrence, I can tell you now only in the strictest confidence, has indeed taken place at a remote clandestine Amarr metallurgical research facility. Masquerading as a routine ore processing laboratory near an otherwise uninteresting Veldspar-laden asteroid field, this facility has been conducting advanced research exclusively into an extremely rare and highly classified metal, found only in the ore of a small fraction of the asteroids present in that specific field: a new metal we call Ditanium. To date, this is the strongest naturally occurring metal yet encountered by our scientists. While we are confident that this metal exists elsewhere in space, to our knowledge, we are the first to actually find it.

Given the rarity of this metal and the significant complexities of its mining and processing, it has taken two full months to produce just enough finished metal plates to fit a single Punisher-class frigate. We intend to use this ship for Phase I field testing, which includes flight handling characteristics, radar cross-section analysis, temperature extremes testing, and other critical operational parameters. If successful, we are confident that we may be able to begin full scale production and ship fitting within two years.

However, before this test can take place, we need someone to courier these Ditanium plates to a station we designate. From there, it will be transshipped to a military shipyard for fitting to the Punisher testbed ship. We do not anticipate this shipment will present any problems, particularly given the high level of secrecy relating to the project, but with potentially many hundreds of billions of LUX riding on the successful integration of Ditanium into our armor plates and other protective ship components, we are taking no chances.

We need to know immediately if you will deliver this Ditanium to the designated station.
144307: I was just informed that you have chosen to quit this important mission prior to the agreed on completion conditions. Please return the Ditanium plates to the nearest Amarr station and we will consider this arrangement terminated.
144308: Well, it is unfortunate that you've chosen not to help us. We trust that you will not discuss this meeting with any other parties, though we are confident that if you did, they would likely laugh you out of whatever station bar you frequent. And if we do hear of you babbling your mouth about this, be assured that we will find you and liquidate any chance of a future partnership, if you catch my meaning.
144309: Outstanding news, {[character]player.name}. Our scientists have verified receipt of the Ditanium plates and are right now moving those pallets to other ships for transshipment to the final destination. Well done and please contact us again in the future should you seek further employment. And remember: you were never here.
144310: Yes, well, we were quite confident that this would be a fairly routine mission, so we were glad to hear that is indeed the case. Fly safe, pilot.
144311: The daughter of a Caldari executive was kidnapped this morning by a group of slavers while she was on holiday. They are demanding we provide them a large quantity of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium, in exchange for her life. There is no time to mount a rescue operation, so our only choice is to provide this shipment immediately. We will deal with those criminals once the girl has been released to us. However, time is of the essence, and our primary mission now is to deliver this shipment to a transshipment station for further transportation to the slavers' designated rendezvous point.
144312:
Time is a factor here, so I will get to the point. The daughter of a prominent Caldari industrialist, CEO of a large scrap metal corporation, was kidnapped while she was on holiday with her school classmates. At the time of her abduction, she was in a lowsec system she should not have been in, one well known for its hedonistic night life. Apparently, the girls each told a bit of a fib to their parents, indicating they were traveling to a much safer, highsec destination resort. Well, early this morning we received an urgent call from the executive's chief of security telling us that the daughter had been grabbed and thrown into a vehicle by some dangerous-looking men outside a bar after a night of drinking.

While we had hoped it was part of some prank or a misunderstanding as to what the girls really saw, our worst fears have been realized. We have been contacted, through a circuitous channel, by a notorious band of slavers. As proof of life, they have transmitted the daughter's DNA sequence to us. Analysis of this information has verified her identity.

The kidnappers have given us a very short window in which we can secure the girl's safe release, after which they will sell her into slavery – and I don't want to even imagine what horrors that might entail. As expected, they are demanding a very large payoff in exchange for her life. Specifically, they want our entire stockpile of our rarest and most expensive metal, quantrium – one found only in the wiring of electronic countermeasures (ECM) equipment of the Caldari Navy's Rook-class combat reconnaissance ships.

What I need you to do is to quickly move this quantrium to the designated station for transshipment to the slavers' rendezvous point. We will take it from there.
144313: Please, pilot, do make haste. The quantrium must be delivered as soon as possible. If we are even one minute late to the rendezvous, the slavers will assume we have involved the authorities, and we will never see the young girl again.
144314: The kidnappers have been listening to our comms, and have heard that you have chosen to quit. They have let us know that we will not see the executive's daughter again. I hope your reasons for quitting are worth the life of an innocent young girl.
144315: We were counting on you. You were our only hope for the safe return of the CEO's daughter. I hope your cowardice here today will haunt you for the rest of your miserable life!
144316: We just got word from the hotel security staff – the executive's daughter was returned to them safe and sound, as the kidnappers promised!  We owe you a debt I hope we can repay one day! We will not forget you!
144317: A small fleet of unidentified frigates has attacked one of our remote communications outposts, killing and injuring dozens of our personnel. Those who survived the attack managed to pilot a high-speed shuttle to the nearest station. However, we have strong reason to believe that a team of assassins is en route to their location to eliminate them before they can pass along the information about the organization responsible for this attack. We need you to make all possible haste to their location and rescue the survivors before this hit team arrives.
144318: We are disappointed that you have chosen not to complete this critical mission; you've left our contractors at great risk. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere, though I doubt this will be possible at this late stage.
144319: Your refusal to accept this mission will undoubtedly result in numerous civilian casualties. We must now try to find someone else to undertake this rescue operation.
144320: Your skillful handing of your ship in this vital rescue mission has saved the lives of many civilians who would have otherwise surely perished in the damaged outpost. We knew we could count on you and we will now move you to the top of our list for future missions.
144321:
Earlier today, a small, unknown group of frigates attacked one of our remote signals intelligence (SIGINT) communications outposts, causing catastrophic damage and killing dozens of our personnel. This station belonged to a small Caldari corporation with a poorly hidden contractual link to our military intelligence services. Fortunately, the survivors managed to escape, via their high-speed emergency shuttle and are expected to arrive at a nearby station within the hour.

As you might expect, we are working hard to determine the identities of the aggressors, but as yet we have no solid leads. Of course, this is not your concern. What is your concern, should you choose to help us, is a report we just received indicating that the surviving team of SIGINT contractors have been targeted for immediate assassination by the same mysterious organization behind the outpost attack. Apparently, someone does not want these individuals to provide us with whatever information they must have obtained during the course of their recent duties.

Within the last few hours, we intercepted a poorly encrypted communication indicating that a covert hit squad is en route to the station aboard an unspecified vessel, or may actually be at the station already! This station's security force, while well armed and highly trained, is insufficient to detect and defeat the kind of lethal operatives that we believe intend to kill our contractors. Therefore, we need you to rescue this team immediately and bring them back to us for an emergency debriefing and to ensure their safety.

After running a check of qualified pilots in our office database, your name was near the top of the list. We estimate there will only be sufficient time for this one rescue attempt before the assassins strike.
144323: The Caldari Navy, much like the military services of other races, operates a covert network of signals intelligence outposts along the borders of the Caldari State. The specific, primary mission of these stations is to provide advance early warning of any hostile incursion by the Gallente military. Beyond this vital mission, however, the outposts are also tasked with gathering intelligence on a wide variety of other targets, both military and civilian. Of particular interest is the regular provision of information on the movement of the commercial and industrial fleets of other races, given the competition between the Caldari corporate system and foreign companies. In this way, the outposts not only provide an essential early warning system for any hostile forces, but also provide data of immense economic value, thus better enabling the Caldari private business sector to better compete in the merciless realm of interstellar business.
144324: There is no time to discuss this mission further given the haste with which you will need to accomplish this. Please contact me only when you have delivered the contractors safely to the final destination.
144325: Thank you for agreeing to attempt the rescue of our civilian contractors. You must leave very soon if we are to have any hope of reaching them before the hit team arrives.
144326: Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. During a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's sensor cross-section, making it much easier to detect and attack. Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Therefore, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet.
144327:
Greetings, {[character]player.name}. Several days ago, an internal security team identified a Gallente deep cover saboteur working at one of our clandestine shipyards producing the current generation of Widow-class Black Ops battleships. He swallowed a hidden poison tablet as we moved in to arrest him, so he is no longer a threat.

However, during a routine quality control check, the shipyard's scientific team was shocked to discover a highly advanced nanite swarm that the saboteur had somehow introduced into the shipyard's stockpile of advanced adhesives used to bond sensor-absorbing coatings to the hulls of our newly-constructed Widows. The effect of this harmful agent is to slowly erode this protective coating, thus increasing the ship's signature radius, making it much easier for our enemies to detect and attack.
