Given the slow-acting nature of this particular breed of nanite, it is unlikely that this gradual loss of stealth capability would be noticeable under routine operating conditions, thus placing the ship and its crew at mortal risk when operating in hostile space. Essentially, the Widow's commander would not know that his ship had lost its critical operational advantage until he was detected and targeted by hostile combatants. Given the very specialized role of this ship, not only would the Widow be compromised, but it is possible than any ships he might be bridging in via its covert jump portal generator could be unknowingly hot dropped near a waiting enemy fleet, instead of empty space.

In order to remedy this critical situation, we need you to immediately transport a large quantity of our new aerogel counteragent to a station for further distribution to the fleet. This shipment represents our best and only hope to quickly repair the damage done by the Gallente spy and ensure the safety of our brave Widow pilots and crew.
144328: Do not contact me on an open channel until this mission is complete. Remember, this is a clandestine operation!
144329: Your successful delivery of the prototype nanites will undoubtedly save the lives of many Black Ops pilots and crew. You have the makings of a good counter operative!
144330: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our Black Ops teams at great risk. We will have to find another operative elsewhere.
144331: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to accept this critical mission. We will have to find another pilot elsewhere.
144332: Produced by the Kaalakiota megacorporation, the Widow-class Black Ops battleship represents the current edge technology for Caldari military vessels used in covert operations. The primary function of the Widow is to conduct infiltration and espionage behind enemy lines. Specifically, when equipped with covert cynosural field generators and covert jump portal generators, the ship can create a “bridge” through which conventional ships are instantly transported, much like a jump gate. The effect of this is to surprise an enemy by instantly “hot dropping” a combat fleet into what was, moments prior, only empty space. In addition, it can also be fitted with ECM modules and cruise missiles such that it can provide jamming capabilities and supporting firepower if necessary. Using this technology, the Widow represents a significant force multiplier in the ongoing conflicts faced by the Caldari State.
144333: We are relieved to hear that you've accepted this important mission. It is imperative that you deliver this cargo with all possible haste.
144335: A team of mercenaries led by a man calling himself “Black Dog” has killed one of our senior managers as he toured an asteroid field not far from here. Intelligence has indicated that he intends to continue these operations into the foreseeable future. To remedy this unacceptable situation, we need you to transport a trained assassin and his entourage to a station closer to the scene of the crime. Once this is done, you will have completed the terms of this contract. We appreciate your discretion in this endeavor.
144337: We are disappointed that you've chosen not to complete this critical mission. You've left our executives and even our miners at significant risk from these mercenaries.
144338: Your unwillingness to assist us in this matter is going to cost this corporation a great deal of LUX until we can find some other way to resolve it. Mr. Smith may soon take a personal interest in you, as you've now disrupted his lucrative contract. I certainly don't want to be in your shoes once he gets the word.
144339: We all know the saying, “business is war.” Nowhere is this adage practiced more seriously than in the Caldari corporate world. The soldiers in this fight are typically thought of as the salesmen, managers, executives, and other boardroom warriors. However, from time to time a very special skill set is required to deal with an equally specific threat. For these situations, corporate assassins are sometimes required to resolve issues that cannot be otherwise remedied through conventional channels. In the most extreme cases, these highly-trained operatives, most of whom served particularly arduous and dangerous careers in the Caldari Special Forces and intelligence groups, are hired to carry out very selective missions with very limited goals. The missions they are paid, - highly paid at that - to undertake would rival any holovid espionage movie, though the consequences are, of course, much more serious. You don't want to mess with these guys, and gals, as it is usually the last thing you'll ever do.
144340: We just received word from Mr. Smith that you did indeed deliver him on time and without attracting any unusual inquiries. We hope the compensation for this mission was worth your time. The Caldari State can use more competent and discretionary pilots like you.
144342:
Before we begin, I must make one thing perfectly clear: You were never here, and this meeting never took place. You do understand what I mean, yes?

We are in need of a pilot who can deliver a very sensitive cargo from this station to a nearby station, without attracting any undue attention. You may have heard in the news or the local gossip channels that a Caldari regional director for mining operations was murdered yesterday by unknown assailants while touring an asteroid field in his personal shuttle. That much is indeed true. However, what has not been reported is that we have, in the last few hours, learned the identity of the assassin, a mercenary who goes by the name “Black Dog”, and that he and his team have already begun to plan for an ongoing hit-and-run campaign designed to try and scare off Caldari corporations from any future mining activities in the region.

Of course, we cannot allow this kind of disruption to what has proven a highly lucrative endeavor – the Board and our shareholders simply will not tolerate any further dips in revenues. To remedy this interruption, one of our sister companies that specializes in, shall we say, discrete solutions, has loaned us one of their most highly trained specialists to resolve this issue. His name, as you might expect, is Mr. Smith. His mission, in brief, is to liquidate Black Dog, along with any associates that may be operating with him at the time.

What we need from you, and need soon, is for you to transport Mr. Smith and his entourage to a station closer to the action – one with a hangar walkway the leads directly to an unmarked office. Once you have dropped him off, your role in this action will be complete.

So, what is it going to be, pilot? We need a yes or no right now if this operation is to stay on schedule.
144343: In order to get around the laws pertaining to the transportation of illegal drugs through Amarr Empire space, we have been forced to create new and unknown substances for use on, or by, rather, our various slave labor enclaves. This new drug, Blue Paradise, does away with many of the harmful chemicals previously used while actually increasing the pleasurable effects. We are certain that, properly controlled and distributed, introduction of this drug into the slave labor workforce will increase productivity by a substantial margin. We are counting on you to deliver it to the designation transshipment station as soon as possible.
144344: Biochemical Agents for Improved Slave Workloads
144345: Well, you have certainly wasted my very valuable time. I thought we could count on you, but obviously I was misinformed. Don't count on working for me any time soon.
144346: Excellent. We are transferring your cargo to a dozen smaller ships equipped for high speed runs to the more remote work sites in the region. I see a lot of profit in your future, {[character]player.name}, if you stick with us.
144347: There are few things I despise more than a quitter. If you come back to my station I am sure we can find you a position on the station slave labor gang, scrubbing the personal hygiene tanks with a toothbrush for the next six months.
144348:
History has shown us that a properly motivated slave work force can work harder and longer - especially in harsh conditions - if they are provided the means to enhance their everyday lives. Well, for many decades, the provision of various stimulant drugs to slave laborers was considered a standard method of doing business. However, the downside to this was that, while the use of stims typically increased productivity, more often than not it resulted in significant long term health problems for the slaves leading to shortened lifespans and, more importantly, to decreased profits. So, while the use of stimulants has largely been discontinued, the idea that drugs could increase slave output never entirely went away, though it did require a new approach.

To this end, my company recently developed an inexpensive new drug that works on the pleasure centers of the brain, providing what we might call a “reward” for hard work. Importantly, this drug, known as Blue Paradise, or "Beep" as the techs call it, has been proven in real-world testing to increase slave labor output by as much as twenty percent across the board, without any known long term health problems. As you can guess, the increased profit potential here is, well, staggering. Equally important is the fact that we have not reported this new drug to the various control boards; nor do we intend to at this juncture.

We need you to deliver a very large shipment of this drug to a forward logistics hub station from which it will be transshipped to ore mines, agricultural farms, and other slave-intensive operations. I can give you my guarantee that this cargo will not be flagged by customs or the police, as it is not yet deemed an illegal substance.

So, can we count on you to deliver this?
144349: Good, glad to hear it. I will immediately order the refrigerated secure containers moved into your cargo hold for your prompt departure.
144350:
We all know that there have been a long series of proclamations, laws, and rules banning the transportation of illegal drugs (and some legal drugs) in Amarr space for use in slave labor. These prohibitions have typically had no real teeth, unless of course the Empress herself sets forth an official decree specifically banning a given substance. The logical, time-tested way around this has been to create entirely new generations of performance enhancing biochemical drugs.

As slaves are typically wary of any pills or other obvious means of altering their behavior (recalling, as we must, the various slave uprisings that have occurred when we tried to openly force drugs on them), we've had to resort to less obvious methods. For example, we have surreptitiously and gradually delivered the drugs into laborer's systems through aerosols in their habitat ventilation systems, impregnated substances into their foodstuffs and water supplies, and other rather clever means, I won't go into here. What is important is that the result has almost always been a positive one, with significant increases in worker productivity.

The downside to this, however, has been a decline in overall slave lifespans due to the long term effects of these drugs. Normally, this would be considered simple attrition; a cost of doing businesses. However, as it continues to become more and more difficult to obtain new slaves (particularly given the intolerable and unjust interference of the other empires), this solution is less and less viable. We need them to live as long as possible. This reality, of course, leads us to the only other benign option – drugs as a part of a rewards system for those slaves who meet a certain work quota each day.

To this end, we shall continue to develop new substances to both avoid interference by Customs and police forces and to ensure the maximum possible output by our slave laborers.
144351: We know the mission is proceeding well, as we've got a cloaked Covert Ops ship following you at a discrete distance. Please contact me only in the event of an emergency.
144352: I'm glad to hear you're going to help us out here. We aren't expecting any trouble with this one, but with corporate espionage, you never know – keep your eyes open.
144353: By quitting mid-mission you've singlehandedly compromised the whole operation! I doubt we'll be able to flush out the spy now, given the fact that you've interrupted the shipment – no doubt he will sense something is up and simply remain unknown to us.
144354: Well, we are disappointed that you've turned this one down. We'll have to use one of our own transportation pilots to get this done.
144355: Outstanding job, {[character]player.name}! As you may have heard by now, the spy was caught trying to remove the device from the offload cargo bay on the station. Needless to say, he has a very uncomfortable future ahead of him in one of our interrogation facilities. Thanks to your piloting skills and discretion, our work on the new cloak remains a well guarded secret.
144356: We have reason to believe that a small team of Gallente saboteurs has managed to destroy one of our new – and not yet fully operational – Command Centers on a nearby ice planet. These facilities are critical elements in our overall plan to dominate the planet such that we can then exploit the vast and lucrative materials that we have identified there in abundance. We need you to deliver a large complement of Arctic Warfare Marines to a forward station so that they can then be transferred down to provide the security we so desperately need. Their massive amounts of equipment will be brought in on other ships, so we need you to deliver these men safely and securely – everything depends on their safe arrival.
144358: Are the Marines behaving themselves? Good. Please continue to make all possible haste in delivering them to the station. They tend to get a bit rowdy when they are cooped up too long.
144359: How you can quit this mission mid-stream is absolutely beyond me. Do you have any idea the mountains of LUX that this is going to cause my department and the Planetary Exploitation Division as a whole? Don't ever come back here for a while.
144360: I'm glad to you hear that you've agreed to help us out on this one. If you'll just confirm this manifest, we'll rally the Marines and have them report to your ship immediately. You'd better get moving – don't want to keep the troops waiting.
144361: We have so far managed to keep this event a closely held secret, as we do not want to discourage the senior management of the company from further exploiting the extremely valuable materials that are in largely untapped abundance on the sea floor. If word of this was to get out at this critical stage, it might give them reason pack up and move to a safer location - perhaps even to another planet. Well, this would simply be unacceptable, as our new planetary industry efforts have so far generated record revenues - the one thing keeping our shareholders and investors happy. And we want to keep them happy, if you understand my meaning. We must allow nothing to interrupt that flow of LUX into our corporate coffers.
144362: I just got word that you delivered all the Marines safely to the station, great job! However, I must now coordinate the follow-on shipment of their equipment and weapons, which is going to mean another all-nighter here at the office. Oh well, business first, yes?  We will be in touch for future missions, so thanks again.
144363: That you have chosen to decline this mission has put this company in a very difficult position, to say the least. Well, get out of here then; let us hope the Marines don't hear about this and decide to give you a rather rough send-off.
144364:
Two days ago, a covert Gallente strike team infiltrated and destroyed a brand new Command Center on a nearby ice planet. We think they managed to infiltrate as local civilian workers due the fact that the facility's Personnel Security Identification Systems had not yet been fully brought online. This unforgivable lapse in security enabled the four-man team to gain access to a highly secure area that contains the controls for the counter-harmonic stabilizers which, in short, keep the entire facility level and secure in the very harsh climates encountered on that planet. A series of well-placed explosives damaged these stabilizers, however, taking them offline and causing the entire command center to collapse and sink through the ice to the ocean floor some two kilometers below. Fortunately, the bulk of the work force was not scheduled to arrive for two more weeks, so casualties were very light. The financial and economic costs were, however, staggering.

Now that you understand the gravity of the situation, we can proceed to the reason that we contacted you to help us in this critical moment in the company's ongoing rapid expansion phase. We need you to very quietly transport a company of our best Arctic Warfare Marines from this station to the destination station with all possible haste. From there they will flown to the ice planet to provide a very high level of security for this and other nearby command centers and facilities. It is just a matter of time before this disastrous event becomes public knowledge, and we need to prove to the senior management, shareholders, and investors that we have the security situation resolutely in hand.

So, {[character]player.name}, are you willing to help us out by delivering a large number of Arctic Marines to the designated station?
144365: During a high-level security assessment, a decoy maglev train designed to mimic the regional governor's chartered train was destroyed by unknown saboteurs while traveling at very high speed. Our investigation has yet to uncover the traitors; however, we are confident that a prompt scientific examination of the wreckage will provide the clues we need to resolve this internal security matter. We are sending a team of senior investigators to the wreck site so that they might help determine the identities of the attackers. We are counting on you to fly them to the designated station.
144366:
I know the security screening process at this station has been time-consuming and a bit, well, intrusive. Now that you have passed our various tests, however, I feel confident that I can now let you in on the reason you are here.

One of our regional governors had recently been planning an unannounced visit to one of the new planetary command centers in a nearby system. For security reasons, this information was restricted to only those in the governor's inner circle, to include the commander of his personal security detail. Well, this commander decided to test his internal security prior to this event, to best ensure the governor's safe travel. So, for this exercise, he created a painstakingly detailed agenda, identical in every detail to an actual state visit. In this scenario, the governor was to travel by chartered high-speed maglev train to a number of the new planetary command centers.

As the Governor's decoy train traveled through a large canyon, however, a series of explosive charges detonated on the rail line, sending the train off its track and into the canyon wall. As it turned out, the security commander's ruse had worked perfectly; someone in the governor's inner circle had tipped his or her hand and provided information to unknown assassins.

So far, however, we have not been able to determine the traitor's identity, and each member of the inner circle is vehemently denying any involvement, despite our best chemical interrogations. So, what this investigation will likely boil down to is to what clues can be solved from the train wreckage, the destroyed maglev track sections, and the soil around the site of the blasts.

We need you to transport several investigative teams, along with a considerable amount of equipment, to a nearby station where they will then be transported via shuttle to the planet. Will you take on this mission?
144367: Thank you for agreeing to aid the Empire in this matter. My assistant will provide you all the details you will need to deliver these personnel to the designated station.
144368: We are extremely disappointed in your decision to leave this mission. I am quite sure the Regional Governor's office will not soon forget this offense to the Empire.
144369: We are disappointed in your decision not to assist the Empire in its hour of need. However, we do have another pilot waiting in the next room, so you may leave. And I need not remind you of the consequences should you discuss any of what you have been told here today.
144370: Excellent work, pilot. The personnel you transported for us have already developed some interesting leads, and it seems – at least at this early juncture – that the assassins may be of Minmatar descent. Further testing, we expect, will confirm this. We will retain your contact information, should this incident require more of your courier skills.
144371: Thank you a million times over, pilot, for taking on this mission. The hearts and minds of the Amarr faithful in that station and elsewhere will benefit immeasurably from your prompt delivery of these hallowed holoreels.
144372: Well, I was not expecting this. All we needed was for you to make a simple run from this station to the designated station and drop off our cargo. Well, suffice to say, you will not be receiving any prayers of blessing from me tonight!
144373: Our hearts are glad to know that you are en route to the station and will be docking there shortly. Please contact me on arrival.
144374: While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class strategic cruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.
144375: Excellent news, pilot, thank you for updating us as to your position and condition. Please make all possible speed to the destination so that we can then dispatch the combined rescue team package.
144376: We've received confirmation that you did indeed fulfill your promise and deliver the Marines to the station. As we speak, the combined rescue team is loading into other ship for immediate transport to the Harbinger. Hopefully, we will reach them in time.
144377: Quitting? Now?  You have placed our marines and hundreds of other personnel in grave danger by abandoning them mid-mission. We will have to find some way to get them to our damaged strategic cruiser, though I feel it is now too late.
144378: We will not forget this – the moment you chose to abandon our people in a time of great need. Your assistance could have turned the tide of this whole disaster. Do not contact me again.
144379: Our deepest thanks for taking on this mission. I can tell you that our best analysts feel that you should be fairly safe in this mission, as the terrorist will have to focus all their efforts on targeting the stricken cruiser. They simply won't have the ships or the time to even attempt to interdict your ship as you make your way to the destination station.
144380: We have recently been experiencing an increase in terrorist attacks by groups seeking to free Amarr slaves in this region. Their raids have become more complex and lethal, resulting in the loss of untold millions of LUX worth of valuable property. More importantly, one of the regional governors is having his annual gala event as his estate on a nearby planet. We need you to deliver a cargo of elite conditioned slaves to a station we will designate. From there they will be transported to the governor's estate by heavily armed ships.
144381:
You are aware, no doubt, of the rumors of extremist antislavery terrorist groups within the Amarr Empire itself. Well, you know then that their loyalty to the Empire is indeed secondary to their overarching desire to see all slaves freed and made equal members of society. This is a condition that we, as the greatest state in all of New Eden, simply cannot tolerate. However, our efforts at arresting and reeducating those insurgents have largely failed to permanently change the mindsets of these rather fanatical individuals.

This system has been particularly hard hit by this and other like-minded groups. Most recently, an Anathema-class covert ops ship, specially configured to transport elite slaves to the estates of senior Amarr leaders in the region, was somehow decloaked, its weapons and sensors jammed, and ruthlessly attacked to the point of near-total structure failure. The terrorists then demanded the pilot transfer the slaves to this mystery ship, on threat of the total destruction of the covert ops vessel. The pilot complied, though he has since been punished for his cowardice.

It is for this reason that I called you here today. I need you to transport a new shipment of elite slaves to a nearby station for further transshipment to the residence of one of the regional governors. This shipment is of particular urgency as the governor is hosting his annual gala event at his estate, and the usual staff of slaves simply will not do. We need these specific slaves, as they have been trained in protocol, proper food and drink service, entertainment, and numerous other talents that I need not mention here.

Will you take on this courier mission on behalf of the Empire and deliver these highly trained and extremely expensive slaves to the designated station?
144383: While it might seem impossible at first glance, there are indeed small bands of terrorists who seek to upset the very core foundation of our society by working to eliminate slavery throughout the Empire. We have had significant success in disrupting these groups, with many members killed or taken prisoner. Nonetheless, like a hydra they continue to grow and adapt to our tactics and operations, making them a quite annoying thorn in our side. The Amarr Empire is devoting increasing resources to the eradication of these groups; however, even the most optimistic analysts concede that it may be quite some time before this nascent insurgency can be eradicated.
144384: Thank you for the update pilot, it is rather reassuring that you are flying without any interference from our unwanted friends. Please contact me again when you are being towed in to the dock, as only then will I feel assured that this courier mission was a success.
144385: You must be kidding?!? I have already guaranteed the governor's office that you are en route and will arrive at the scheduled time. This act on your part is probably going to get me reassigned to some asteroid in an uncharted system a million light years from here. Well, I will make sure I'm not the only one who will feel the heat for this failure.
144386: While I must say I am rather shocked at your refusal to undertake this mission, we are fortunate in that we do have contingency plans in place. So, while we will have to risk the crew and slaves in another run, I feel confident that only you will bear the negative feedback for failing us here today.
144387: Great job, {[character]player.name}. The slaves are being offloaded now and will be en route to the governor's estate shortly. I can't thank you enough for your reliability and promptness.
144388: That is very good news, pilot. I will contact the governor's aide myself to let her know that you have accepted and will be departing shortly.
144389: Suicide terrorists have been attacking and destroying our commercial convoys as they have passed through their usual transit zones, despite the presence of heavy security escort vessels. A communications intercept, partially decoded, indicates that these individual intend to step up the level of their attacks by targeting the stations themselves. While we can defend against some of these attackers, based on analysis of their previous attack profiles, we have never had to defend against pilots and ships who fully intend to die by throwing themselves against us without regard for their own lives. Tactical analysis indicates that they will get through our defense and may cause catastrophic damage, likely killing hundreds if not thousands of our civilian workforce and their families. We need you to help us evacuate them immediately!
144390: We have virtually no information on these new threats, other than that they have access to very fast ships filled to the brim with high explosives. Their tactics are simple – they seem to appear out of nowhere, then accelerate their ships to maximum velocity and, ignoring defensive fire, fly directly into the cargo bays of our freighters and other haulers. We are currently working with Caldari Naval Intelligence to determine the source of this scourge; however, early indications from their ship markings are that they belong to an extremists environmental cult that views the Caldari State as the ultimate evil in the universe. They will stop at nothing to destroy us, especially as we expand planetary industry and resource harvesting.
144391: You are quitting on us now? In the middle of an evacuation? Fine. Just deliver those men, women, and children to the nearest safe location, and we will send someone to get them. You are a despicable coward and you'd better hope you never need to transit through this system ever again.
144392: I will never be able to thank you for helping us in our most dire hour. The Caldari Navy should be arriving soon to provide additional security, but that's no guarantee that the terrorists won't follow through with their insidious plans. I will be sure to pass the word throughout the comms networks of the great service you did for all of us today.
144393: I cannot believe what I'm hearing – you are refusing to help save these people? Well, I don't know where we are going to find another ship at this late hour.
144394: Thank you. That is a big load off my shoulders. We need all the good pilots we can get to help us get these people to safety before the terrorists attempt any suicide attack against this station.
144395: Thank you for the update. I am glad to hear the passengers are doing well. I can't tell you how much it means to us that you are willing to divert from more profitable ventures to save these innocent lives.
144397:
So get this: There's some big high society party going on. All the best and brightest are there. So this one Gallente dignitary is completely hammered and starts mouthing off to everyone. He even goes right up to an admiral and calls our side, "a bunch of humorless egg-jockeys." Right to his face!

So now it's this whole thing. The higher-ups are protesting by pulling out of the embassy. I think it's a stronger statement than they really should be making, but they're going ahead with it. They need you to provide security while they pull out. Rumor has it some jingoist factions of the Gallente will try to make a move on the ambassadors to spark more conflict. Patrol the area outside the embassy until the dignitaries have completed their withdraw.
144398: There's a fitness initiative going through Federation schools. I'm sure you've heard about it? A weird luddite group called The Natural Way wants to get kids to stop relying on modding to stay in shape, and they're tossing cred around like water to do so. No school would turn down money in exchange for a couple hours' fitness classes a week. Take these {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} over to one of their facilities at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll see some of that money, too.
144399: There's a fitness initiative going through Federation schools. I'm sure you've heard about it? A weird luddite group called The Natural Way wants to get kids to stop relying on modding to stay in shape, and they're tossing cred around like water to do so. No school would turn down money in exchange for a couple hours' fitness classes a week. Take these {[item]objectiveTypeID.name} over to one of their facilities at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll see some of that money, too.
144400: The Natural Way is a group which promotes a lower-tech way of life. They're throwing around a lot of cred to start a fitness initiative encouraging kids to stay away from body modding, and I see nothing wrong with encouraging them in exchange for a little LUX.
144401: Body modification, or "modding," is widely accepted throughout the Federation, primarily for cosmetic purposes. Color-changing tattoos which move, programmable "makeup" which is implanted in subcutaneous layers, piercings and body-shaping are the most common forms, so normal they're barely worth mentioning. The wilder forms of modding, however, can frequently give people the wrong idea. Parents who want to discourage their children from engaging in extreme modding may sometimes turn to groups which support lower-tech ways of life for educational programs, particularly in the tumultuous teenage years when youngsters start to seek their personal identity.
144402: Just don't watch those, okay? They gave me nightmares.
144403: You haven't WATCHED those, have you?
144404: Thanks a lot, {[character]player.name}. My mother's been giving those to my kids for their birthdays every year, and I was afraid I'd never get rid of them.
144405: As before, I need another data fragment from Amolah Kesti's message.  Scour Zimse for any traces of it, or use scanner probes to find its cosmic signature.  Return to me once you have completed your objective.

144409:
I've been begging my handlers to let me get a hold of you. Just look at you, a genuine capsuleer . We have a lot of pretenders around here. They'll do a few things for us here and there and then they'll blow some of our boys out of the sky for the bounties on their heads.

I have my doubts, but we'll see.

I was sent to the Venal region a bit ago. The Navy and other State corps are moving in and trying to clean us honest rogues out, which is why we need to teach them fear.

Ytiri has a base they've built up in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We'll be taking it, but that's not where you fit in. It's not enough to simply take the base: We need to curtail their ability to operate in this region. We need to destroy all of the ships assigned to this base, let them know it's not worth the wasted time and resources in trying to reclaim their property or their territory.

We're going to take that station over in the name of Gurista, and I have just the men to do it. I'll hand over a platoon of soldiers, trained professionals within our ranks. They're known as the Dread Guristas, and this is their strike force. Take them to the base, and let them do their magic. Wait for the strike force to take control while you eliminate any enemies in the sky. Don't worry: They know what they're doing.

But so do you, I guess. Well, I'll give you the reins on this one.
144410:
{[character]player.name}, thanks for stopping by. Every now and then I get handed another assignment to clean up our spacelanes and clamp down on narcotics smuggling. I was hoping I could count on you to handle this one as we've had some problems in the past with other capsuleers.

There's been an influx of neural boosters to our area recently and {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} is trying to stem the flow. We understand that boosters will never truly go away; we're not trying to be overbearing here, quite the opposite in fact. We normally turn a blind eye to light drug trafficking, and usually this has proven to be good business, but that only seems to have encouraged the local smugglers in recent times. They've been flooding this system and others nearby with cheap, more dangerous drugs, which is absolutely not good for business.

We know where they base out of, a station in the {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} system which we've already taken the liberty of blockading. We'd rather have the matter dealt with on a corporate basis though, before anyone goes alerting the Chief Executive Panel or CONCORD authorities, so your discretion is important here.

We've set up a check point outside the station. What we need is a capsuleer who can go in there and check out some of the larger vessels currently in holding. We're concerned that some of these vessels are not only heavily loaded with boosters, but also heavily armed. It would be best to have someone like you on standby for the inspection process. You are of course cleared to engage anyone caught with illegal boosters in their cargo, although if you catch anyone, be prepared for some shooting.
144411: Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.
144412: Trust me, pilot, we are watching you, and we know you are on time and flying via the preprogrammed waypoints. Contact us only on your arrival.
144413: Looks like food supplies are dwindling fast at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I think people are consuming a lot more than they were before. Take them a shipment of frozen food so we can feed the hungry.
144414:
I'm supposed to transport these reports to the Caldari Navy station in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}, but I really have a tight schedule at the moment. The contents of the reports are confidential, something about the new recruits we've been getting. Apparently the Navy has been on the lookout for some pilots to hire for various jobs, and they want some background info. That's why I couldn't just send this information via a transmission: Caldari law prohibits doing that with personal information since such transmissions can be hacked.

If you do the job for me, I'll give you a nice reward. And even a bonus if you get it done quickly.

144420:
The bank manager at the local State and Region vault has heard some worrying rumors that some thugs are planning a run on his bank. He is in no position to investigate the matter himself, so he sent for the cavalry. The Caldari Navy, that is. I was sent here by the Navy to check out the validity of these rumors. I haven't dug up anything of interest yet, but just to be on the safe side I'd like to put some heat on the bandits roaming in the area. I've asked my buddy Jali Tanaka to help me out too, but he's busy setting up a surveillance system, so I don't want to take too much of his time.

The Kazka bandits over in Sakkikainen seem like likely candidates for this sort of an operation. I don't know for sure, but it doesn't hurt to stir things up a little. You seem like a hardy pilot more than capable of roughing them up a bit. How about you get in there all guns blazing and bring me back, say, 30 drifter spurs? That should shake them up, hopefully enough for one of them to spill his beans into the wrong ear.

Finally, be very careful. The Kazka bandits are rough. Make sure you only target their grunts, the others are too tough to be worth the hassle.
144421: You found him!  I'll notify his family immediately.  I'll also report our success here directly to my contact in The Scope. Thank you for your assistance.
144422:
As you know, there are many hundreds of thousands of Minmatar slaves working to provide essential services to the Empire, just as they have for centuries. Given their considerable natural physical abilities, they have always made up one of the most important and valuable ethnic groups within the vast Amarr slave workforce. One unavoidable consequence of this, however, is that we have had to invest a considerable amount of money, not only in the health and welfare of these slaves, but also to ensure their obedience.

One important aspect of this latter effort has been the establishment of Labor Reeducation Centers, or LRC's, which are designed to house some of the more problematic slaves in order to facilitate their eventual return to the workforce. In recent months, however, there has been a significant increase in violent disobedience at certain LRC's, with some of the more severe instances leading to near-riots.

Our immediate problem is that one of these facilities, LRC-12A, has been taken over during just such an uprising. The slaves have reportedly killed and injured dozens of our personnel and taken the remainder hostage. They are demanding the immediate release of their fellow slaves at a nearby Amarr mining operation, along with transportation to a destination of their choosing. We have, so far, managed to keep this incident quiet; if the Minmatar Republic leadership were to learn of this, it could very easily lead to much more severe consequences for both races. The only way to ensure this does not happen is through the immediate application of overwhelming force.

Therefore, we need you to deliver a large contingent of specially trained Riot Interdiction Teams to a nearby station, from which they will join up with other security elements for final transportation to LRC-12A. Will you assist us?
144423: The teams have begun to embark on a small fleet of frigates and cruisers for LRC-12A. With this amount of men and lethal weaponry, there is no doubt that we shall prevail!
144424: The teams have begun to embark on a small fleet of frigates and cruisers for LRC-12A. With this amount of men and lethal weaponry, there is no doubt that we shall prevail!

144429:
Our engineering scientists, working at our highly secure, clandestine R&D facility on a nearby planet have produced a new type of cloaking device that, when fitted to Covert Ops ships, could theoretically enable them to jump through stargates without uncloaking! And yes, I can see by the look on your face that you must think I've had far too many Extra Strength Quafe sodas today. However, I can assure you that, while it may be many years before this technology is perfected and suitable for even experimental use, the science behind it is quite real, and this is where this story takes a very important twist.

Our internal security teams have managed to uncover a plan formulated by one of our competitors to steal the prototype cloaking system at some point between the time it leaves the lab up until it arrives at the field testing facility over in the next system. Problem is, we don't yet know who the spy is, so we devised a plan to get that spy to expose himself so that we can then move in and make the arrest.

To this end, you will be delivering is a very detailed mock-up series of the actual prototype, one that will withstand an initial visual and electronic scrutiny on the part of the thief. In all practical terms, however, these devices could no more cloak a ship than it could cook your morning breakfast. We are naming this event Operation Doorstop, which is our planning team's attempt at humor, given the uselessness of this particular lump of metal and wires. What we do need, though, is your absolute confidentiality on this shipment. If the spy gets any whiff that this is a set-up, we will likely never know who he or she is, and we will remain at ongoing risk of one of our most important R&D projects potentially falling into the wrong hands.

So, what do you say, {[character]player.name}? Willing to take on this rather interesting assignment?

Yes, I have some work for you.

We have several research outposts in various w-space systems. It's common, one of those things that nobody discusses but everybody knows about anyway. A while ago, they recovered bits of ancient technology which seemed to have unusual properties.. We thought for a while it might be some sort of Sleeper computer core, but now it appears to be Talocan in origin. Another of our laboratories has more pieces, and they're suggesting it's actually the core of a station's life-support system, with multiple redundant modules that can back each other up and be easily replaced if they fail. They're setting up to test their theory right now at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. I need you to take our samples over so they can complete the network they've pieced together.
144453: That is very good to hear, thank you. We will transfer the cargo to your hangar immediately, along with a small element of the intelligence team, who have stated that they will provide security through to the final destination station. You'd best head to your ship quickly, as I wouldn't want those guys on board my ship without an escort, especially as the rather unique weapons they usually carry are easily capable of punching a nice little hole in your hull.

144455:
As you probably know all too well, speed is the lifeblood of the Republic's defense fleets, particularly for the smaller frigates and cruisers. There's a lot that goes into it: low-density reactor cores, kinesthetic maneuvering thrusters, hyper-responsive gyroscopic stabilizers. All the housings are built using nano-alloy rather than the more heavyweight materials the other empires use; it was simply more convenient back when the ships were first designed, but it gives them that little bit of extra boost that's become our signature.

Our R&D specialists have been working on a new formula for the C-86 thermal epoxy resin used on engine housings and other parts of the propulsion systems; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

The lighter construction does have the drawback of making the systems more fragile. Our R&D specialists have been working on a more efficient design for the inertial compensators which keep the drive components from shaking themselves to bits; I want you to take this batch over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} for application and field testing.

144464:
Ah, {[character]player.name}! It is good to see there are freelancers who still maintain some loyalty to the Federation. It pleases me greatly that capsuleers like yourself still prove willing to help us out at need. Anyway, if you are looking for something to do, I know a little job that might just mix profit with pleasure.

The Serpentis are setting up a little shop in this area where they are training their fighters, intending to bring them into the tournament. Now, we aren't afraid of a little competition, but these fighters aren't all-natural, if you know what I mean. We're going to need them kidnapped and brought back here. Chances are you're going to find the substance the Serps have been feeding their fighters as well, and I know some people who are very interested to see it recovered. Purely for research, of course. I wouldn't dream of touching the stuff myself....

OK, OK, so maybe years ago when I was younger I might have tried some, but everyone experiments a little. No harm in that. Right? Just don't let me find out that you've kept a little for yourself. I need ... I mean, I want it all. To give to our researchers, of course. Ahem. Yes.

So, well, before you go ... listen, I would appreciate it if you could keep this matter to yourself. I'm sure you'll agree that not everybody needs to know about this, hm?
144465:
Thanks for meeting me in person, {[character]player.name}. We have a problem: My superiors have transcripts of our earlier communication and know about the drugs you brought back. It's okay, though, they've given me a chance to get rid of the stuff.

I need you to head out to Q-UA3C. The Serps have had a small shipping checkpoint there for a while, one which our investigative reporters have been monitoring for a big exposé on the way Serpentis supply chains work. Since my bosses want this little "mistake" of mine rectified quietly in order to prevent a scandal, they want the drugs taken there and the outpost destroyed. And that's what will happen.

Between you and me, though, I can't stand the idea of letting such a valuable commodity go to waste. So what I want you to do is head out there and kill everything you see, but leave the drug disposal to me. I'll convince my superiors and anyone else who asks that the drugs were destroyed at the outpost, and everyone will be happy ? at least, assuming that you can keep this a secret. And that is what you will do, I trust.

We have data sheets miles long on the Gallenteans. While a lot of it is complete crap, it does give us good information on their typical ship load outs, including the ships flown by pirate groups working in Gallente space, such as the Serpentis.

Serpentis ships favor Kinetic and Thermal weapons, so be prepared for that. Their armor is tough, but cannot turn a point: Using an ammo type that does Kinetic damage should do the trick. Scourge light missiles or rockets work well.
144470:
The Amarrians were busy out here. It seems they were up to a lot more than just scouting. One of their missions was apparently to place mines along some of our major shipping routes. {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, in particular, is full of the blasted things, and we've got a convoy coming through within four standard hours. We need to get someone to both systems and clear out those mines!

These "mines" are quite something, though. They are highly explosive proximity charges built into structures, but when they blow, they also launch a bunch of drones into space to finish off anything not torn entirely apart by the explosion. It's a tough job, but if they're not cleared by the time the convoy gets there, our people are in serious trouble.
144471: The Amarrians now know that we're manufacturing high-tech EMP smart bombs in this vicinity. They can't attack this station -- it's too well defended -- but they also know we need Mexallon to produce the bombs, and they are trying to cut off our supply. We need you to deliver some Mexallon to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}.
144472:
We recently found a number of new mining fields in adjacent systems, and the usual assortment of pirate trash has come out of the woodwork to exploit it. We'll need them mined soon because even those thieving bastards have friends in places high enough to put the legal status of these sites in doubt. For some reason they've taken an interest even in Banidine, too, and we'll need to find out why; all my workers are busy with the more profitable fields, but I'm not taking any chances.

I'm uploading a bookmark to your People & Places databank; it shows the location of a Banidine mining operation. I need you to head out there and mine all the Banidine. Should be 18,000 units, my foreman tells me. Once we've made an undisputed claim, we're free to mine there again without interference, and I'll provide you with a little something for your trouble.
144473:
My boss wants Banidine; something to do with manufacturing cheaper parts for refrigeration units or something. I don't know. Point is, he's made it my job to get the ore. And now I'm makin' it your job.

There's a few Banidine rocks out at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, enough for 20,000 units, the scouts tell me. Go out there, mine it, bring it back. Should be easy enough, right?
144474:
We've gotten word of the location of a bunch of Mercium ore here in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but we believe that our information has also been leaked to other factions, including the Gallenteans. It's vital that you collect all the Mercium: It cannot be allowed to fall into enemy hands.

You may want to use a Survey Scanner module to find the right asteroids in space; also, be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
144475: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.

144478:
We've found an old mining post in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. But, the thing is, we can't find who used to own it: There are no records of its being built or even existing. It's simply empty. No sign of anyone left there, dead or otherwise. Our initial investigation found extensive fire damage, gas leaks; you name it, it went wrong. Lots of explosive damage, though we can't tell if that was accidental or intentional. And some marks... well, we just don't know what could do that to metal. It's damn creepy, that's for sure.

Anyway, near as we can tell, the miners were working on a large Lyavite deposit. They didn't finish, because there's still about 5,000 units of it at the site. Now, I know Lyavite isn't the most popular rock, but nobody just leaves that much ore lying around. And besides, the brains at the lab figure they can use the stuff for some of their research, so this opportunity is too good to pass up.

That's where you come in. Warp in, mine the Lyavite, and warp out. It's that easy.
144479: You've heard of Parriaval Mastes, the infamous troublemaker? Well, he's escaped from the prison camp where he was held. We need someone to locate him and bring him back here discreetly. If word of his escape gets out, political dissidents from all across the Empire will start causing trouble. Fortunately, we've tracked the ship he stole and located its signal at a suspected terrorists' outpost in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Are you willing to fly out there and retrieve him? There's a significant reward.
144480:
Your agent has placed a bookmark in your NeoCom to help you get to the correct location. Open People and Places, go to Bookmarks, right-click on this mission objective, and choose "Set destination." Then go to your Ship Control Panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click again on this mission, and select "Warp to location." Once you've arrived at the fugitive's location, you'll see him as a red target icon on your Overview. Engage and destroy his ship. Once the fugitive's vessel has been destroyed, a cargo container will eject from it. This is Parriaval's escape capsule. Once you're within 1,500 meters, right-click on the cargo container and select "Open" (or use the "Open" icon above your Overview). A window will now open displaying the contents: Click and hold the prisoner and drag him into your cargo hold.

Congratulations, you've recaptured Parriaval Mastes! Now return to {[character]agentID.name} for your reward.

There's a significant reward.
144482:

Then go to your Ship Control Panel and click the Autopilot icon. Your ship will now travel to the appropriate system. Once you've arrived, your Autopilot will deactivate.

Now go back to your Bookmarks, right-click again on this mission, and select "Warp to location." Once you've arrived at the fugitive's location, you'll see him as a red target icon on your Overview. Engage and destroy his ship. Once the fugitive's vessel has been destroyed, a cargo container will eject from it. This is the spy's escape capsule. Once you're within 1,500 meters, right-click on the cargo container and select "Open" (or use the "Open" icon above your Overview). A window will now open displaying the contents: Click and hold the prisoner and drag him into your cargo hold.

144485:
Since we've drawn so much attention to the plight of the Matari, there's been a news leak: one of the slave colonies has staged a rebellion. Now, the Amarr always respond to rebellion with brute force, so those people are pretty much doomed. But we can save them, and still make it look like they all perished once again at the hands of the Amarrians.

Destroy the mining colony before the Amarrians do, and bring the survivors back here for safekeeping.
144486: Trade is a booming industry. Humanity is spread out over such a vast area of space that everything is rare somewhere, and there's always someone willing to make that journey for a profit, however small.
144487:
Unbeknownst to us, a botanist here named Horei Falcosis took one of the seeds for examination before you shipped the package; a short time ago, as he worked with it, it shot out a tendril and sank it into his flesh. It was several minutes before he was discovered, and by that time, the seed's tendrils had penetrated his body in several locations. Falcosis was unconscious by this time, and the seed had pulled itself close to his body and started to secrete a protective resin.

Sadly, this station does not have the proper facilities to care for him. And since this tree has now been designated noxious and dangerous--the other seeds were all incinerated safely, I understand--Falcosis has been placed in cryogenic stasis for transport.

Deliver him to the station I've uploaded to your Journal, would you?
144488: We couldn't wait for you any longer. We sent someone else after the book. Because of your delay, it will now be months before we can reclaim that part of the station, if not the whole thing. Who knows?
144489: We couldn't wait for you any longer. We sent someone else after the book. Because of your delay, it will now be months before we can reclaim that part of the station, if not the whole thing. Who knows?
144490:
No doubt you've see that little furrier that's been bouncing around the station for the last few days, {[character]player.name}? You haven't? Well, I certainly have. Nasty little creature. It bites, you know.

In any event, it was part of a shipment of exotic pets intended for delivery to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, but it got left behind because I spilled a drink all over the cargo manifest. We need someone to take this furrier, special delivery, over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and get it the hell out of our hair. We need a special pilot, a pilot with skill and daring, a pilot who doesn't know the meaning of the word "fear"… and who isn't allergic to furriers. You interested?
144491:
One of the functions of my job is to ensure things operate smoothly in this region. I have a number of informants that keep me in the loop of the less visible happenings. They tend to be skittish by nature, but recently one of my informants was noticeably shaken. He won't send the information, and he won't meet me in person. He's insisted that I send a third party to pick up the data.

Normally I'd just find another informant, but this one was on the trail of a particularly virulent heretic. The man can't be anything but mad--he calls himself The Crackpot, for one thing--but it's damned hard to track a madman. He's been attracting attention, even followers from among the weak-minded, and it's long past time to put a stop to his nonsense.

If you'll go and pick up that data, it could help us track this menace down.
144492: {[character]player.name}, because of your inaction, the drone swarm found the Banidine. This rare mineral is now even rarer because you let those automatons get to it first, and that can't be good for any of us.
144493:
It's not a well-kept secret that as rogue drones get more advanced, they're becoming more unpredictable. Talk to any seasoned pod pilot and they'll tell you about the dozens of rogue drones they've had to fight off just in the course of their regular business. Even more disturbing are reports of drone hives, massive constructs of debris that no one can quite figure out, but which are always full of haywire drones.

So what's their interest in Banidine? Who knows?! Most humans don't go looking for the stuff: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. In fact, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother giving it its own entry in their mining packages when they produce ship scanners. (If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in your mission's Journal entry and select "Add to Overview.")

So, again, why the interest from the drones? Well, none but the drones can say, and they're not talking. Suffice to say that their interest can't mean anything good for the humans that share their space.
144494:
{[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name} wants a massive shipment of Augumene right away, so we need you to get out there and bring some back. They seem to think they might be able to find some use for the stuff for chemical warfare, I guess? But that's just between you and me, right?

Anyway, I've been looking for a miner who's experienced enough, with the right kind of ship, and maybe you fit the bill. Time is critical on this one. There's a big bonus for you if you can bring it in fast enough.

Seriously, we need a mountain of this stuff, so get on it. I've uploaded the location to your People & Places databank.
144495: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions that more than negate any profit to be made from refining the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
144496: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes extremely expensive safety precautions — which more than negates any profit to be made from reprocessing the stuff. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
144497:
Turns out someone got the bright idea that if mining drones mine more ore, bigger drones would mine even more ore. This guy's team slapped some mining drone's AI into non-regulation heavy combat units and threw some mining lasers on. He even hacked the firmware so that the mining brains could control the weaponry, making some sort of self-sufficient mining machines.

Now there's a bunch of haywire drones zipping about this rare mineral that we want. Our guys in the lab need it for research, I guess. The drones aren't even mining the rock, last I heard, but they have tried to bore through any ship we send out there....

It's getting ridiculous. If you can, get out to {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, neutralize the drones, and bring back all the Mercium; we'll pay you well for your efforts.
144498: Someone else got to the Mercium before we did; most likely those drones, which have also disappeared. You better start getting on the ball.
144499:
Mine 20 units of Crystalline Icicles. Oh, and watch out for pirates or rogue drones. Lots of them around these parts.

You will need an Ice Harvester module to complete this mission. Also, be aware that this amount of raw Crystalline Icicles ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
144500:
Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, a respected Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, and hence unmanned.

Unfortunately, the drones became unruly, then unmanageable, and soon developed the ability to "infect" other drones, and eventually even ships, with their capricious artificial intelligence. Needless to say, Gallente soon abandoned this line of research.
144501:
Drones scare the daylights out of some people. To be completely honest, the big hives even scare me a little. The smaller drone groups are annoying, but more manageable. Usually.

Anyway, there's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting these wild drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. So the best solution is to just remove the cloud: no cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.
144502: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.
144503:
Well, we've located some asteroids that contain substantial amounts of Polygypsum. It's a comparatively rare mineral, and almost completely unknown in this system. Our guys want to have a look at the stuff and see if they can figure out some way to make use of it; however, we don't have anyone who wants to deal with the stuff. So guess who I thought of first?

You'll need to grab all 2,800 units of the stuff and get it back here. So what do you think? Are you in?
144504:
Polygypsum is widely considered worthless because of the dangers associated with storing and reprocessing it. As a result, you won't find this ore on the market. In fact, for this reason, most sensor manufacturers don't even bother putting it as a unique entry in the computers when they install standard ship scanners.

If you're having trouble finding the correct ore at the mission location, you can right-click the "Polygypsum" icon in your mission's Journal entry and select "Add to Overview."
144505:
No, no. There are no Gallente. It's those cursed rogue drones. If the Gallente hadn't made those things way back during the Caldari-Gallente War, I wouldn't have this headache to deal with.

Here's the odd thing: There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that seems to be attracting drones. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just end up replacing them. We've figured out that, for whatever reason, they're attracted to the gas. The best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. If you can harvest that cloud out, it'd be a big help.

You must own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to complete this mission. If you do not or cannot, please just decline; note that you can decline one mission every 4 hours without standing loss.

A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.
144507: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.
144514:
Following the widespread release of cloning technology, as it became both financially viable and CONCORD-sanctioned, Zainou Biotech enjoyed a period of unprecedented profits. Securing almost one third of the market share in clone sales, the corporation was set to become one of the most important Caldari corporations in the cluster, which would only have added further influence to its parent company, Ishukone.

In those days, Zainou handled all cloning, though, then as today, only the fabulously wealthy could afford the technology. However, since the event known as the "Insorum Imbroglio," when Zainou lost the trust of the other State corporations, the CEP has mandated that the highest levels of office and those of great value to the State would have their clones stored in other facilities.

Little is known about these cloning centers. Details such as their number, location, staff, administrative structure, and resources all remain closely guarded secrets.
144516: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.
144517: I'm afraid that my datapad went missing on your watch, {[character]player.name}. It is an unfortunate thing, very unfortunate indeed. I'm afraid, also, that I'll have to hold you responsible for its contents and any action--or in this case, inaction--they might have inspired.
144518:
There's been an increase in Caldari activity in surrounding systems. We think those self-righteous bastards might be up to something. Of course, that's nothing new.

We've placed passive reconnaissance units in several nearby locations, but we don't want any direct transmissions from them for fear of attracting Caldari attention. So we've decided to dispatch "unofficial" vessels like yours to pick up the data chips from their base and bring them back here. The Caldari are less likely to suspect--or at least less likely to interfere with--a capsuleer, so they should leave you alone.

If you do get jumped, however, remember that the recon unit is the top priority. Get it out of there if you can. Do it fast and there'll be a substantial bonus.
144519:
A number of the mega-corporations have joined together to produce SPLET: the State Personnel Life Enrichment Tour.

The first thing we need is food, and there are crates of frozen food waiting not too far from here. Bring the food here so our chefs can start to figure out how to stretch it into an appropriately festive-- but still economical-- dish.
144520:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission.
144521:
One of our intelligence technicians has gone rogue. He isn't a very high-level operator, but he has access to some sensitive passwords, code keys, and patrol routes. We think he was bought off by the Caldari and is headed out of system.

We've located him in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and we need someone to stop him and grab his ship's log if possible. It may contain information about his destination and, more importantly, about who recruited him. It's an important mission. Are you game?
144522:
There has been an outbreak of commerce raiding in this sector. We strongly suspect the Caldari are behind it, either directly or through proxies such as Mordu's Legion. They've hit a convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but there was too much cargo for them to loot immediately. We suspect that they'll be returning in a few hours with a transport and some escorts.

We want to strike back, but also to learn something about who these raiders are and whether the Caldari are really behind the attacks. Take out the transport and escorts when they arrive in-system, and return to us with any logs or transponders you're able to recover. The lost cargo is yours if you want it. Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.
144523:
There's been an outbreak of commerce raiding in this sector. We strongly suspect the Caldari are behind it, either directly or through something like Mordu's Legion. Whoever it is, they've hit a convoy in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}, but it seems there was too much cargo for them to loot immediately. We suspect that they'll be returning in a few hours with a transport and some escorts.

We want to strike back, of course, but also to learn something about who these raiders are and whether the Caldari are really behind the attacks. Take out the transport and escorts when they arrive in-system, and return to us with any logs or transponders you're able to recover.

Take these guys down and we'll make it worth your time. You might even get a piece of the action if we find out who's behind the raids. The lost cargo is also yours if you want it. Insurance has already covered those losses, so consider that a little extra bonus for yourself.
144524:
There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

I won't lie, it's risky.The depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.
144525:
An Amarrian slaver has found a way to hack the Egonics signal, at least at short range. Security cameras in a nearby station show hundreds of people--all of them wearing Egonics devices--simply walking into the cargohold of an Amarrian Bestower. It wasn't until after the ship had departed the station and the missing persons reports starting coming in that we realized anything was amiss. Security found that this Amarrian "citizen" had inserted subliminal commands into the Egonics signals at the station.

If you can get all of those citizens back, there's a big reward for you.

There are over 1,000 people missing. You will need a large cargo capacity to carry them all at once, unless you intend to make multiple runs to the deadspace location where the Amarrain ship is located.
144526:
There's a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating illegally out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. We need you to go take them out. Leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny its actions in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight.
144527:
A short time ago, Minmatar terrorists in a combined fleet of frigates and cruisers attacked one of our Harbinger-class battlecruisers as it was transporting slaves from a recently closed mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in a nearby system. While all but one of the attackers was annihilated, our convoy's escorts were destroyed and our cruiser is burning. Making a bad situation worse, we are anticipating that the terrorists will return in force within the next several hours to attempt the theft of our slaves, as they almost certainly know the cruiser is alone and all but helpless.

Our concern is that if the terrorists feel that they have a window of opportunity to recover these slaves, it is likely that they will throw everything they have into the effort. Our intelligence assessments of the terrorists' fleet assets are even less reassuring: we believe that they could send as many as four battlecruisers into this fight – more than enough to wipe out the arriving frigates and forcefully board our heavily damaged strategic cruiser. However, we have calculated that if we can delay any terrorist boarding parties long enough, this should give us enough time for the much larger main rescue fleet to arrive.

The only bright side to this situation, in what is unquestionably an act of divine providence, is that a large contingent of marines are aboard this station as we speak, having just completed specialized refresher training in counter-boarding operations. We need you to deliver them to the station closest to the last reported position of our cruiser. From there, we will transport a combined team of marines, engineers, medics, and other essential personnel to hopefully stop the fire and save the ship - along with its cargo of highly valuable slaves. However, this mission must be undertaken immediately. Any delay will surely doom the Harbinger and her brave crew.
144528: While transporting Minmatar slaves from a recently close ore mine to a new mineral harvesting facility in nearby system, the convoy was attacked by terrorists, destroying the escort frigates and heavily damaging the Harbinger-class battlecruiser carrying the slaves. We believe it is likely that the terrorists will return, and in larger ships, to attempt a rescue of the slaves before we can respond with reinforcements. The window of opportunity for the terrorists is short, so it is imperative that we immediately render as much help as possible. What we need you to do is deliver a contingent of heavily armed marines recently trained in counter-boarding operations to a station closer to the site of the battle. From there, they will join other Amarr military and rescue teams for immediate transportation to the damaged cruiser.
144529:
{[character]player.name}! Glad you could make it on such short notice. Let me get right to the point: Yesterday, as you almost certainly know, a regional governor delivered her State of the Region address. Needless to say, we were quite excited and thus put forth a maximum effort to ensure that her speech was broadcast on every possible channel and to the maximum ranges of our civilian and military communications networks.

However, for various reasons at many remote locations, this signal did not reach many who would have otherwise benefitted from this opportunity. For all our efforts, there are some locations that can only be reached the hard way -- ferrying holoreels directly to each and every one of them. We have already dispatched messengers, primarily in interceptors and other fast ships, to these more dangerous destinations.

We need you to transport a quantity of holoreels containing the State of the Region speech to one station in particular and hand them over to an agent who will be waiting for them there. He will then handle all further distribution of the 'reels.

So, can you help us with what should be a straightforward courier job?
144530: The regional governor herself delivered an important State of the Region speech yesterday to all her billions of faithful followers. Due to technical problems, however, this message did not reach as many citizens as it should have. Fortunately, we have managed to correct this rather quickly through dispatching a small fleet of interceptors to the problem locations. We need you, however, to take a shipment of holoreels to the station we designate, as our usual contact there is indisposed at the moment and may not be available for some time. When you deliver these to that station, our contact's second-in-command will take charge of the cargo and facilitate further broadcasting.
144531: Thank you so very much, {[character]player.name}. The Amarr representative has already informed us that he is offloading the holoreels as we speak. We will not forget this service to the Empire.
144532: I must say we are quite disappointed. As you know, all of our pilots are gone, taking these 'reels to the faithful. Your refusal leaves a gap in this coverage that will leave many faithful Amarr without this important message from the governor.
