144537:
Impetus is considering putting out a new holoreel about the enslaved Matari. Now that people think the Amarr would rather blow up CONCORD ships than allow the public to see how slaves are treated, there's talk of a major project, not just a documentary. This is exactly what we need!

News and documentaries are useful, but this would really reach the public. The average person needs things black and white, and that's what holos are for.

This is the last thing I'm going to ask of you, and it won't be easy. Since we've drawn so much attention to the plight of the Matari, there's been a news leak: one of the slave colonies has staged a rebellion. Now, the Amarr always respond to rebellion with brute force, so those people are pretty much doomed.

But we can save them--at least a good number of them--and still make it look like they all perished, once again at the hands of the Amarrians. And it's unlikely Amarr will even bother to deny responsibility since everyone knows they'd destroy the whole colony anyway. Remember, if you leave it to the Amarr to destroy the colony themselves, those Matari will only suffer further torture and degradation, and then be killed anyway.

Can you do this final task for the cause?
144538:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all… it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends… I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me--for us--if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?
144539:
It's those damn Gallente, what else!? They're not even trying to maintain the appearance of peace between us anymore! I'm deadly serious, {[character]player.name}. If this isn't a direct act to provoke all-out war, then I don't know what is. We are dealing with a blatant assault on one of our most important facilities, right within our own borders!

Alright, here's the deal: They've somehow discovered one of our secret cloning facilities, and I'm told their orders to attack it have come from the most senior of Federation military officials.

I can't stress enough the importance of this mission. If those clone bays go down, we'll have a huge problem on our hands. Hell, for all we know this could be only the first step before key individuals are targeted, without clones to save them. I don't have the clearance to know exactly whose clones are being stored where, nor if they are the only copies. All I know is that they are holding important people, very important.

You need to fly over there immediately, and destroy any and all hostiles you see. Once the facility is secure, we can send in the relocation fleet and move it all safely away. You must move quickly, though! This initial force is undoubtedly just the scouting party since they're not attacking the facility yet. We need them cleared out before we have a fleet of Navy Moros besieging the facility.

If we can't trust you with this, {[character]player.name}, then I don't know who we can trust anymore.
144540:
We've got some more information from the data you brought back. It seems that these enemies are indeed Mordu's Legion, with their squadron insignia obscured. That means the Caldari are likely behind the raids and we need to send them a message that we know about it.

There's a Caldari supply depot located at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} that we want destroyed. We can't offer you much support, but we know you don't really need it. That's why we're sending you in, and not some Navy rookie. We want the Caldari to know that we can cause them grief with only a single ship. It doesn't take us a whole fleet.

So, you want to go in? I won't lie, it's risky--the depot is likely to be guarded, and they may send reinforcements once the action begins.
144541:
There's been a lot of Amarrian activity along the frontier lately. We think they're preparing for war with the Minmatar, but there's no love lost between them and us, as you know. Or perhaps they want to start a conflict that will involve all four major powers. We can't say.

What we do know is that there is a flotilla of Amarrian ships operating out of {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. To avoid the political confrontation, we'd been leaving them alone until now, but they've been snooping where they aren't welcome, and we think they may even be raiding some of our supply convoys. We need you to go take them out--leave as much wreckage as you can so the Empire can't deny it had an illegal military outpost in our space.

Now, we're not sure how many fleet resources they have in the region, so it might be a tough fight. A real tough fight. Are you up for it?
144542:
I found this woman in a bar in the Lai Dai station in Otitoh, and she seduced me. The next morning, I woke up with a terrible hangover in her bed--a bed which also happened to belong to Officer Eteri Tazaki of the Lai Dai Protection Services.

I've been running ever since. The fact is, every law enforcement officer in this system seems to be corrupt, and by the virtue of his position alone, Tazaki has managed to convince the authorities that I raped his wife. I'm now a wanted man, hunted by those I once trusted with my life. I'm still trying to come to terms with what has happened, but it's hard. I just hope my family doesn't hear about this until I have time to explain everything in person.

Your first task will be a difficult one. The sheriff of Otitoh, Togany, has been snooping around the area looking for me. I think he must have been tipped off by one of the locals, because he's currently scouring the asteroid belts near here, where I usually run at the first sight of law enforcement officers. You must take him out. Destroy his ship or whatever; just prevent him from finding me. I fear that if he's not taken care of soon, I will be caught. If he catches me, he'll call in back-up, and there'll be no stopping them. He's currently located near one of the moons of Otitoh VII. Bring me proof of his demise and you will be rewarded.
144543:
The corporations of the State have many friends, as you know... many friends in many interesting and useful places. Why is this relevant, you ask? Well, it's not at all... it was merely an idle thought I had today that I wanted to impart upon you.

But actually, now I come to think about the topic of friends... I am reminded of a particular friend of mine in a very difficult situation. He's due for a promotion, you see. More accurately, he would be if there weren't a few other promising individuals ahead of him in line. Such promising individuals, indeed, that I am sure their superiors would miss them dearly if anything were to happen to them. But it would be very, er, helpful... for me--for us--if this friend of ours were to get what he wants.

However, you see, they are all Gallente officers, and for any agent of the State to interfere in Federation matters would be quite wrong, now, wouldn't it? Of course, with all the random third party violence these days, it's not terribly uncommon for valiant officers, Gallente or otherwise, to meet quite unfortunate ends in any number of... well, mishaps. Yes, {[character]player.name}, it's not uncommon at all, is it? So I'm sure things will work themselves out somehow.

Anyhow, your mission. Right. Well, this is quite embarrassing... I've completely forgotten any mission I might have had for you. Come to think of it, I've forgotten everything I was just talking about. Goodness, I think I better go and lie down for a while.

But... I don't suppose you could look after my datapad here while I rest? It's quite important, you see, for it has the current coordinates of one of those promising Federation individuals, one of the ones we just discussed. And I wouldn't want that to fall into the wrong hands, now, would I?

And you... you look like you could use a break, too. Maybe a leisurely cruise out into space somewhere nearby, a chance to relax and, oh, I don't know, enjoy some scenery? Maybe pay someone a visit? And by the time I wake up, maybe my worries will have taken care of themselves, hmm?
144544:
Welcome back. Now we're going for speed.

You can use two types of active propulsion modules: Afterburners and their bigger brother Microwarpdrives (or MWDs). We're about to teach you how to use Afterburners.

Afterburners don't increase your speed as drastically as MWDs, but they suffer less penalties: They use only a moderate amount of capacitor to run and cannot be disabled by Warp Scramblers. Afterburners are also much easier to fit to your ship - they use less power grid and less CPU, and have no fitting penalties.

We've got an area riddled with dangerous electromagnetic interference that will damage your ship periodically. Your task is to fly through the clouds of EM disturbance using an Afterburner, and make it to the other side in one piece.

Zira Cobalus, the slave leader you dispatched for us, might have been a Minmatar agent sent into our slave population to foment rebellion among the masses. This is intolerable. However, we must verify that she was indeed a spy, and our databanks here are inadequate to this task.

Take this data chip for examination at {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. Intelligence personnel there will compare our data with theirs, and hopefully we will get a match.

144562:
Your agent wants you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}.

And you might want to keep an eye out for the Guristas. They might be a little peeved with you.
144563:
We have a serious situation on our hands, pilot.

A few weeks ago we dispatched a small squadron of Amarrian vessels that had made it inside our borders to a contested sector. We thought the job was finished and the area secure but it seems we've been duped. The entire regiment we cleared was just a decoy, and they've been massing hostiles in a nearby location with the use of covert technology.

The situation is not only embarrassing; it's undoubtedly boosted their own morale to have deceived us so effectively. We relocated all of our forces from there only days ago and re-establishing a presence will be admitting to our own people that those Imperial scum outsmarted us…or one of them in particular, actually.

Various sources of ours have pointed towards one of their Field Commanders being the key strategist behind these latest maneuvers. We need her assassinated, pilot. Not only will her death impede their progress, but it should send a message to other commanders inside the Empire. Fly out there and make it clear to them: we have capsuleers ready and able to strike down their best and brightest. Let that be the first thought in their mind before they step up to lead fleets against our people.
144564:
One of the key advantages we've had so far in this sector is our extensive cynosural field network, which allows us to drop our capital ships in on the enemy almost at will. The enemy, meanwhile, is forced to leave their ships vulnerable during cynosural field generation.

Unfortunately, our advantage may be crumbling. Yesterday, a task force engaging an Amarr blockade suffered serious losses when three enemy carriers dropped on them. The disturbing part is that the cynosural field was activated by a beacon, not by an Amarr ship. That means the Amarr have put up a limited cynosural field network to compete with ours. No doubt they're expanding it as fast as they can.

The network needs to be destroyed, but we need to know where those beacons have been deployed so that we can get all of them when we do a sweep. In order to do this, we want you to penetrate the security at the Amarr outpost nearby and get the tactical information sheet there. Bring it back here, and we'll have Republic Intelligence find those beacons. Understood?
144565:
Amarr forces have begun to deploy a cynosural field network in this sector.

In order to find the beacons comprising this network and destroy them, we need to get the records on where those beacons have been deployed. To find that, we need to get the tactical information sheet from the Amarr outpost not far from here. You'll need to fight your way to the outpost and grab the sheet. Bring it back to me as quickly as possible.
144566:
It's time to act fast, {[character]player.name}. We've just received reports that the Caldari Navy has established a forward outpost in the Otitoh system, in preparation for a strike at our complex in the area. According to our information they have a sizable force there already, and are preparing to move in more people. We're happy to tell you, however, that the EMP charge you placed at the Lai Dai station had its desired effect, severely damaging a substantial number of support vessels and equipment the Navy had meant for use in Otitoh. Now is therefore the time to strike, while they are weakened and working to compensate for the loss of backup assets.

We need you to go in there and take out the Navy's Command and Control center in the area. Any losses you can inflict on them while doing so will be most appreciated, but the primary target is the C&C center. If that is taken down, the Navy will have to retreat from the area, and our plans for this constellation will be that much closer to fruition. Once the building is destroyed, report back to me and I will see to it that you are rewarded handsomely for your efforts. The Guristas will not forget this one, {[character]player.name}. Good luck.
144567:
I've just received word that a fleeing civilian convoy was destroyed by the Amarr, pilot. There were over two thousand fatalities before a Fleet search-and-rescue force was able to reach the scene and recover the survivors.

In addition to the utter disregard for human life that this act displayed, evidently the daughter of a prominent Elder and her family were on board one of the industrial ships with the convoy. They are still missing, but the Fleet isn't hopeful that they will be found. We are outraged, and they want to show those terrorists that they can't get away with this kind of butchery.

I've been asked to find a pod pilot capable of taking out the sector commander who ordered this massacre. His battleship group is currently resupplying, and is temporarily vulnerable. It won't be easy; despite his cowardly choice of targets, he's quite capable and has a significant force at his disposal.
144568:
An Amarr task force destroyed a civilian convoy fleeing the front lines. Included in the missing and presumed dead are the daughter of a prominent Elder and her family, and the general staff is outraged by the attack. We must have revenge for this brutal massacre.

The sector commander responsible for ordering the attack is currently resupplying, leaving him temporarily vulnerable. We don't intend to let him get away. Fly to the base at the coordinates you've been given and make sure the sector commander does not survive. Any other targets are secondary, but don't hold back. Blow those slaving bastards out of the sky.
144570:
We've decided to do our agents in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name} a favor. They've been complaining for quite some time of being overworked and underpaid, so we've decided to send them the perfect gift to soothe their nerves. A few packs of tobacco should do the trick, heh heh. It's at least something, until we come up with a better solution.

Deliver the batch to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and a local supplier will pick it up from there and deliver it to where they're staying.

144572: Zainou has requested a batch of silicon for their production facility in {[location]objectiveDestinationSystemID.name}.  Deliver the goods there on time and you'll be eligible for a bonus reward.
144573:
You've done well, {[character]player.name}. You can continue working for various corporations in {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.name} as long as you like. I suggest finding an agent that has a greater variety of tasks available. Simply search the stations that are owned by a corporation within {[npcOrganization]agentFactionID.nameWithArticle} and you are bound to find an agent to your liking. You can also search for agents who will speak to you by checking the database information for the corporation of your choice. To do that simply open the People and Places menu through your NeoCom and search for the corporation name. Right click on it and choose 'show info'. There you should find a list of all of its agents that are available. Their division should give you a hint as to what type of mission they are associated with.

Take care!
144574:
It's those damned rogue drones again! They never seem to get enough!
This time it's big. Two of our main mining facilities in the system have been completely overrun by rogue drones. If you can go clear them out we can save some of the miners and perhaps even the facilities themselves. Please don't fail me on this one. Those facilities provide a large portion of both our incomes and it would be a big loss to both of us if they were lost
144575: It's tough to quit smoking when you've got a warehouse full of cigarettes within arm's reach. Take every crate of that crap you can find in that warehouse over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and leave it there. Quickly, before I change my mind!
144576:
I'm so glad to see you {[character]player.name}. I had almost given up hope on finding a skilled mercenary to do some dangerous work for {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. I've looked everywhere in this run-down system but you're the first ray of hope that I've encountered so far.

We have a serious problem on our hands at the State And Region Bank in Ihakana. A gang of hooligans has been terrorizing passersby in the area, allegedly causing damage to our property and pestering our customers. We haven't been able to pin anything major on them yet, but our patience has worn out. I will pay you a large sum of LUX if you take care of these pests yourself, before they do any serious harm.

The deadpsace pocket is hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan down the Kazka blockade.

144578:
I just received a transmission from my family on Otomainen XI, apparently the Kazka Bandits have erected a blockade at key areas around the planet to prevent anyone associated with me to leave or enter in one piece. Of course the local authorities haven't lifted a finger yet to stop these pirates from going along with their business, since XI is so sparsely populated and the Kazka Bandits have close ties to some of the corrupt officials here.

Since the planet is not technically habitable, my family has to live inside an enclosed bio dome, and we are totally dependant on supply convoys to survive. We have a little agriculture going on down there inside the dome, but not enough to feed the entire population. I'm afraid that if the Kazka become desperate, they might cut off our food supply and force the mayor to order my family to leave. That would surely be their death sentence.

The blockade is comprised of Kazka thugs, lead by one of their leaders, Pata Wakori. Kill their leader, and I'm sure you'll kill the blockade.

The deadpsace pocket is hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan down the Kazka blockade. Take care of them quickly will you, time is of the essence here.

144580:
The most important task is behind us, but there are a couple more assignments that I'd like you to accomplish before you leave. The first of these assignments is to destroy a small armory near G5ED-Y II. It's being used to re-supply Guristas fighters in the system, and therefore must be destroyed. You may keep any of the supplies found inside, but do bring back some evidence of its demise.

The armory is in a deadspace pocket hidden from passive sensors. You will need to use probes to scan it down.

144584: Gallentean society is currently enjoying the fruits of unprecedented economic prosperity and growth, undergoing a cultural and spiritual revitalization. President Foiritan, still popular despite being ousted by President Roden, takes credit for ushering in this age, expanding trade with other nations and pouring money into massive projects. In all of New Eden, no other nation has as many concurrent terraforming initiatives underway as the Federation; the demand for labor has grown so great that it now draws immigrants from many other nations, especially from the Minmatar Republic.

144586:
We have a big problem, and very little time to deal with it, {[character]player.name}. Four days ago, two of our squadrons conducted a strike on a small outpost not far from here, not realizing the place was a key tactical and scientific asset belonging to the Federation. In retaliation, Fed Navy HICOM has issued three platoons of combat ships to attack the Fountain region. According to our intel, they will be striking several vital targets of ours in the next twenty-four-hour period. Rumor has it the order came from President Roden himself, so we can expect them to bring big guns and larger numbers.

Losing these outposts is something we cannot afford, so we have to move swiftly and meet them head-on before they do their damage. Two teams have already been sent to intercept the first two squads. I want you to handle the third. We believe that they are currently residing at 4-EP12. Get over there and send them back to Yulai.

144601: Pirates are a blight on New Eden. Make sure you kill every last one, or they will scatter and regather somewhere else.
144604: You're a little twisted. And I'm okay with that. Yeah, I'll get you your Augumene.
144605: Excellent. Go get me some of that magnificent ore.
144606: You seem happy. What is it?
144607:
I was talking to some blowhard in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} when his station was destroyed. So, I'm thinking raiders, right? But no, it's even better. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh!

It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me! I want you to go out there, and bring me back all of that Augumene.

Oh, you'll want to bring a survey scanner to find the rocks out there: Lot of station debris and blowhard bits floating around.
144608: Here's the Augumene. Where's my LUX?
144609: Ah, it even feels like providence. And cold, hard kredits. Speaking of which, here's yours.
144610: You seem entirely too happy with all this. And that troubles me. I'm going to decline, I'm afraid.
144611: What? You don't like free LUX?
144612: Augumene is an extremely toxic ore; fortunately, it is also extremely rare. It can be mined safely from a starship, but proves very deadly when handled directly unless one takes very expensive safety precautions. For this reason, even black market operators generally won't deal in it, and it is never found for sale on the open market.
144614:
I'm on the comm, talking to this blowhard I knew back from my days at the academy, right...? So he's going on and on about how his corporation in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is going to make LUX hand over fist mining some rare ore, blah blah blah. Then all these alarms start going off on his end. And I'm thinking his stupid corp is getting raided or something. Then, all of a sudden, the wall behind him disappears and he's ripped away from the screen! The blowhard got spaced right in front of my eyes!

Now, here's the best part. I send a few probes out that way, 'cause I want to know who to send the thank you card to. Turns out there were no raiders. Turns out that the whole damn station was hit by an asteroid full of Augumene! Luckily, I know a guy who's willing to pay decent kreds for the stuff, even though it's pretty much worthless! Heh! It's like some angry, ironic god came down and crushed that jerk with a giant wad of kred notes, all for me!

So, anyway, I want you to go out there and bring me back all of that Augumene. Do that, and I'll have a nice reward here for you when your come back, alright? Oh, and you'll want to bring a survey scanner to find the rocks: Lot of station debris and bits of blowhard floating around out there, I imagine...
144615: I don't have time to wait for you to decide whether you like LUX or not. I'll get someone else to mine my lucky rock. So you can just get lost, okay?
144617: This is more than a little weird. I'm not mining this Augumene anymore.
144618: Don't tell me you're scared of a little rock?
144619: Great. You took just long enough for some other vultures to get all the Augumene. That rock was meant for me, but no, you had to prance around until it was too late. Thanks for nothing.
144621: Sounds like a good deal. I'm in.
144622: Remember, move fast. Time's of the essence, huh?
144624:
Seems like every government around wants some of this Mercium stuff. I don't know why, but if they all want it, then it might be worth a bundle to me down the road if I can get it first. I mean, no one's willing to pay for it now, but I'm thinking ahead: All four sides bidding, you got any idea how high that might drive the auction prices?

Now, I happen to have the location of some of this stuff. Thing is, I don't have a ship to handle it, so I need you, and I'm willing to put some money up front against this future "investment." Get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.

You may want to use a Survey Scanner module to find the right asteroids in space; also, be aware that this amount of raw Mercium ore may require multiple trips unless you have a large amount of cargo space.
144625: Here's your Mercium. So, where's my cut?
144626:
Here you go. Oh, this is gonna be just like hacking into that SCC station computer and making LUX for myself!

Uh, I mean, not that I've ever done that....
144627: I'm not interested in getting caught in a four-way crossfire just to mine some rocks that might be worth something to someone at some point.
144628: Not everybody's got what it takes. I knew that when I first looked at you.
144630:

Alright? You gotta get in, get me that ore, and get out before somebody else pops in there for it. Simple.
144631: I don't have this kinda time, {[character]player.name}. I gotta move on this Mercium before it's gone.
144633: Selling to all four of the big empires? Uh... even I don't want to piss off that many people. Nah, I quit.
144634: Don't worry, I'll find someone who's willing to make some decent LUX.
144635: Somebody else already beat you to that Mercium, bonehead. Way to go.
144637: Though Mercium is not commercially viable at present, it remains of scientific interest (and thus potentially of future financial interest) to agents of virtually all factions.
144639: Get it quick. I don't like waiting.
144641: Mine 18,000 units of Banidine at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} and bring it to {[character]agentID.name}.
144642: I've got your Banidine right here, pal.
144644: I don't work for crazy people.
144645: Most people don't go looking for Banidine: It's virtually worthless, so you won't find it on the market. If you're having trouble finding the Banidine at the mission location, you can right-click the "Banidine" icon in your mission's Journal entry and select "Add to Overview."
144647:
Look, I need some… ah, building materials, but I've got a client who's a bit particular. He wants it special, from some asteroids that already destroyed a shuttle of his, I guess. He gave me a location; you just go there, mine all 18,000 units of the Banidine that's there, and bring it back. Now, you won't find this stuff anywhere else, so don't go looking to bring me back something similar and easier to come across — you try and rip me off on this, and I'll know. Got it? Alright.

So, you game?
144648: I got no time for games. I'll find somebody who can get it done.
144650: I'm done with this weird stuff. Banidine? It's worthless! So I get to wondering… who the hell wants this stuff, and for what? And I decide, maybe I ought not to do this, huh?
144651: Thanks a bundle. I didn't pay ya to think. That's my job. Remember that next time.
144652: I need this done yesterday. I found someone else who can do the job faster.
144655: Thank you. You wouldn't believe how difficult it is to find a good gas harvester around here.
144656: You know me, ready for anything.
144657:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta fit a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. And you also gotta deal with any drones there. Fair enough?
144658: I've harvested the gas cloud. Hopefully the drones won't be so interested in the area now.
144659: Great. We'll keep an eye on the area, but I think you've fixed our drone problem.
144660: I'm afraid I can't do this. So... "no thanks."
144661: Damn. I'll have to find someone else. Hey, thanks for being honest, though.
144663:
There's a Chartreuse Cytoserocin cloud over in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It's attracting all sorts of drones to it. I don't know why. It's like insects to a flame or somethin'. We keep clearing them out, but new drones just take their place. It's annoying as hell.

I figure the best solution is to just remove the cloud. No cloud, no drones. Simple. If you can harvest that cloud out, I'll pay you well.

You gotta own and be able to use a Gas Cloud Harvester to do this mission. If you don't or ya can't, just say "no thanks." You can decline one mission about every 4 hours without pissing me off, so no worries.
144664: Rogue drones and "wild drones" are the terms used for advanced drones that have mutated out of control. A few years ago, some ingenious Gallentean inventor had the idea of creating super-advanced drones that could think and act on their own in every sense like a regular space ship, except for being computer controlled, hence unmanned. The drones became unruly, then unmanageable. Needless to say, this research was soon abandoned by the Gallenteans.
144665: The career advisor agents will be able to help you choose what skills to train, and how to specialize as a capsule pilot.

Time for you to see for yourself. We've chased a pirate down to a nearby hideout and we want you to pin him down. We'll provide you with a Civilian Stasis Webifier, and you may want to fit an afterburner, too.

Do not get too close to any CONCORD police vessels when using a Stasis Webifier - they may see you as a threat and destroy your ship.

144949: Take your time at the academy, {[character]player.name}. There is a lot to see out there.

144954:
Excellent. These are the coordinates of the nearest training center, and here are your clearance papers. Take them with you to the station.

Good luck, {[character]player.name}, and remember: I'm never far if you need help.
144955: Excellent work, {[character]player.name}. You've arrived. I'm relaying further instructions to you now.
144956: You should travel out to the career advisors as soon as you can.
144957: Colonists eking out a living on godforsaken rocks in space are finding it hard to maintain food production, so we're giving them a boost. The moment you've brought those crates of frozen plant seeds over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, our caravans will pick them up and haul them to those thankful pioneers.
144958:
You capsuleers spend so much time in the midst of mayhem and destruction, and you leave countless wreckages in your wake. Now, though, you and I have an opportunity to help sustain new life. I want you to transport some large crates of frozen plant seeds for me.

It will not surprise you that we are always trying to establish new colonies in even the most desolate parts of space. Colonization is always an exciting opportunity, not only for the settlers who dare venture out into space and stake their fortunes on some desolate rock, but for local entrepreneurs, businesses and politicians to support them. You won't hear of these, because your kind is so far up above piddly little local events, but it's a big deal for those involved.

Unfortunately, local support can't last forever. After the initial interest has waned, the citizens on those colonies have to fend for themselves. Sometimes they manage to create self-sustaining habitats where no outside intervention is needed. Occasionally they get lucky, and the outcome of their scientific experiments, ore search, or whatever else they were up to, makes them enough money that they can buy whatever they need off local orbitals.

All too often, though, we have to step in. Your cargo, once delivered to their colony, will hopefully enable them to bootstrap themselves to a self-sustaining life cycle. Colony life is hard enough as it is.
144959: Really? Ah well, back to destruction it is.
144960: I am greatly disappointed. Their food stores were already running low.
144961: Take care to keep those seeds frozen at all times.
144962: Excellent. Caravans will take the seeds to the colony. You have earned back some of your karma, capsuleer.
144963: Some entertainment-hungry collectors out there are waiting for a lot of specially ordered holoreels that were manufactured, stamped, signed and compiled in special editions elsewhere in the cluster. I need you to bring these large holoreel crates to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} before they risk starting something silly like reading books.
144964:
Most often we leave the shipment of entertainment material to the more slow-moving vessels in our employ. Every so often, though, we receive sufficient premium orders from other stations and the planets in their vicinity that we dispatch a special courier with the payload.

That courier is you, and the payload is huge stacks of holoreels, most of them ordered on some manner of timed interstellar delivery offer.

This isn't the primary business of our own corporation as such, but we have enough ties to the producers of all this material - as would any corporation large enough to have gone interstellar - that it's incumbent on us to find ways of delivering it to the customers.

Believe me, I wish we could just transfer all of this digitally, but for most of this cargo that is simply not an option. Some of these holoreels are under trade restrictions that prevent them from being beamed over and saved or stamped on the spot; others are special collectors' editions that may include anything from specially signed copies to boxed sets weighed down with any number of collectable objects.

Please ensure your crew doesn't open any of the crates, either. These people are collectors and paid a galactic premium for their items. If they so much as smell another human being's presence on the merchandise, they will resort either to lawsuits or assassinations.
144965: Very well. They'll just have to watch empty screens for a little longer.
144966: The customers will not be happy with this.
144967: Don't open any of those sealed special editions, you hear?
144968: Excellent. Your crew left the holoreels untouched, I trust.
144969: We have come into possession of large amounts of garbage, and since we can't legally rid ourselves of it here, I need you to transport it over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}. They have some good people there who don't have ethical qualms about destroying any kind of trash, even if a limb or two is dangling out of the crate.
144970:
In all honesty, I find it just unbelievable that in this day and age we are expending actual capsuleer man-hours, not to mention the time and effort of your crew, and asking actual spaceships to travel interstellar distances only to shift around a cargohold of something as pitiable as actual garbage. Garbage. Especially the type we've got here, which takes up a bunch of room, has to be stored in nonporous containers, and, frankly, is starting to smell.

Nonetheless, here we are. We could have this cargo sent down planetside and destroyed, except that while those people are perfectly happy to toss up any number of shipments with whatever trinkets the station clientele is demanding that week, they have frothing conniptions if we so much as suggest that we might want to send anything like this back down in return. The merest whisper of it is enough for them to drag out the lawyers. It's not as if they don't have the space.

You aren't too big to help out, I trust. All we need you to do is haul this smelly, half-liquidized garbage to another station, where they'll have ways to get rid of it without endless complaints or moral qualms. I swear, if the PR department would just let us stop accepting all these colony refugees, we wouldn't have this problem.

Actually, forget I said that last part.
144971: Look, it was just normal, everyday garbage. There was no reason for you not to take this on.
144972: I am disappointed. I hope you didn't root around in the cargo.
144973: If your crew tells you that anything was moving in the garbage, don't believe them.
144974: Thanks. Now we have them off our hands. The garbage, I mean.  Off our hands.
144975: We have a small outburst of violent behavior to deal with on a nearby station. Refugees from interstellar violence have begun gathering forces and are demanding compensation, hearings and whatnot. Now, this is just a damn stupid situation, and we have people who can put it right, but they need a bit of a boost. That's where you come in. Transport these large crates of small arms to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and we'll take it from there.
144976:
Our people at a nearby station are in need of more firepower. They are going to have to subdue unruly refugees from destroyed colonies and crews from recently destroyed ships.

I know it sounds ludicrous. The thing is, when you have near-death experiences of that kind, you may come to the realization that life is fickle, short and dangerous, and that everything you took for granted may be taken from you in the blink of an eye. It tends to upset people, make them aggressive and reckless.

That is, if they're mortal. You being a capsuleer, you'll just have to take my word for it. I'm sure death has a great impact on your sense of the world, but thus far in my experience, it doesn't make you half as crazy as near-death, and at least your type has the sense to take it outside when you feel the need to blow something up.

Incidentally, there are always claims - by silly local news outlets nobody listens to - that representatives of our corporation may not always react immediately when they hear that people are floating out there in escape pods, waiting in to be rescued. Do not let those claims bother you. Those same people are sitting in the midst of a deadly capsuleer battlefield and are in dire need of learning the blessed virtue of patience.
144977: Alright. We'll have to find other ways of subduing them, then.
144978: I'm disappointed. I hope you're not siding with these rebellious people.
144979: I know you have plenty of firepower, too, but let's leave this one to station personnel.
144980: Thanks! And don't feel bad for those people - I'm sure there'll be some survivors.
144981: You have a juicy and slightly sticky mission on your hands. Quafe is conducting one of their local marketing campaigns and are in need of exotic drinks - which in this case means another shipment of Quafe manufactured in another solar system. Bring these large crates of quafe over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and you'll make a lot of thirsty people very happy.
144982:
Quafe is preparing for one of their routine planetside campaigns, and as a premium they want to offer special bottles of the ubiquitous drink.

To be honest, there is nothing special about the drink. It's the same cola, with the same water, color, sugar, additives and perfectly legal trace elements, that you'd find on any civilized planet in the cluster. What's important isn't so much the brand as the bottles themselves . They were manufactured on another planet, so their design is subtly different from what's available where you're taking them, and the labeling indicates their origins.

People go crazy for this stuff. I'm serious. This will be hard for a capsuleer to understand, but most people don't even travel that much between the continents on their own planets. To hold in your hand an item that was manufactured in another solar system is an experience that's truly special to a huge number of people.

This only works for things like Quafe, mind you. Taking anything this thoroughly familiar and changing it just slightly has a higher excitement freakout value than even if you'd brought in some unknown artifact made by actual aliens.
144983: You sure? But everybody loves Quafe!
144984: That's a disappointment. If you and your crew drank it all, it's okay to say so. You're not the only ones with a habit.
144985: Keep moving. I don't trust the sealants on those crates, and I'd hate for the Quafe to go flat.
144986: Perfect. Help yourself to a nice, cool, fizzy drink as a reward.
144987: Our pod fluid vats in {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} are in dire need of refilling, lest you find yourself floating in something that's more like a swamp lake after a hot summer. Collect from your hangar those large crates of ectoplasm we dredged up and haul them over there as soon as you can!
144988:
You capsuleers are amazing. Not only have you got the interstellar corporations doing crazy business in ore, minerals, modules and ammunition, but you also routinely exhaust our storages for the equipment that's required to even keep you people in the air. I need you to transport something that's vital for your own continued success.

I'm not referring to the capsules themselves or the unimaginably complex electronics that help you interface with your ship. No, this is something much more mundane. We need to replenish our vats of pod fluid, and for that, we need ectoplasm. This way, whenever you visit our fair station, we can drain and replace your capsule if our tests show that its contents have become a little too stale.

Also, should you have a clone contract with any of our stations and later on find yourself inconvenienced to the point of ... well, to the point of death, we want to ensure that we can put you into a new capsule filled to the brim with pod fluid that's proper, fresh and new. Nothing's quite as disgusting as waking up in a brand new body only to realize that it's been plunged into someone else's used pod fluid.
144989: Fair enough. Keep floating in your own goo, then.
144990: Really? Alright, but don't be surprised if your pod starts to thicken up a little in time.
144991: You'll ... not want to taste the cargo. Trust me.
144992: Wonderful. We'll happily let you try out the first batch.

145009:
Excellent work! You've proven you know how to handle yourself in deadly situations. What you've overcome today represents only a fraction of the threat a skilled capsuleer poses, but the basic premises are the same: Warp Scramblers, Webifiers, Afterburners, and a weapon of choice. With these tools, the knowledge to use them, and the courage to try again in the face of ship loss, you can become much more than you are now. Remember, it is as much about your mindset as it is about the ships at your disposal.

Now, as I mentioned earlier, I've arranged to have your standings with the Minmatar Republic increased. This bump in your reputation will help you to enlist in Factional Warfare, where you can fight alongside your own people. There are many battles being fought over the occupancy of strategic systems, and every ship makes a difference.

Whether you follow that path or take another is up to you, {[character]player.name}. I would recommend that you enroll in other training courses if you haven't already, and learn as much as you can before making any long-term plans. My work here is done, though. I thank you for the help you've given us, and I hope you've learned something in return. Fly safe.

145017:
Few have the skills to enter the world of Covert Ops, and fewer still survive long once they enter it. And of those who do survive, rare are those who can claim to be totally sane afterwards.

One of the first lessons in Covert Ops is "plausible deniability"; this, along with the selective use of misinformation, allows a government and or a military entity to distance itself from its spies and operatives should their activities become known. Paradoxically, though, while every government and military organization requires Covert Ops to survive, it can be extremely harmful to admit such groups' existence, at least without a feasible back-up story — a story usually provided by the covert agents themselves.

At times, the distance between a Covert Ops agency and its parent organization can become so byzantine that funding can present a dangerous optic. When that occurs, operatives may have to raise funds themselves, in ways only they can...
145018:
Okay, I haven't been totally honest with you. I'm currently working on behalf of a Covert Ops agent for the Republic Navy.

That Caldari ship? Belonged to a disgruntled military scientist who was going to sell us a bio-weapon prototype. Unfortunately, we had a small misunderstanding over price, and now he's dead. Things happen, you know? I hired you to retrieve the ship logs so we could have a little thing called "plausible deniability" if things went badly. Like they kinda did.

{[character]player.name}, here's the new plan. First of all, the weapon is useless — the scientist was as terrible a researcher as he was a negotiator. But rumors we whispered into the right ears have got people believing otherwise. This whole operation was about raising funds for Navy Covert Ops, after all. Spy stuff isn't cheap!

Anyway, we need you to meet with the buyer at {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. Will you do this for me?

Sorry about all the fibs. Please? Pretty please?
145019:
Ok, you're now all set to speak with Arizam Gimit. You'll probably find her at her desk in the Amarr station in Lossa. And don't forget to bring your graduation certificate when you pay her a visit!

If you forget the location of this agent, you can always look it up by opening the 'show info' window for the graduation certificate.
145020:
{[character]player.name}, the Caldari have built an observation base in Gallente space. It has been designated “Station 464.” One of the structures is a relay station, and it is being used to store all the information the Caldari have collected in the system. I need you to hack the relay station so we can see what kind of information they have collected and thus the purpose of the base.

The data center is heavily protected so be ready for a real fight. I will upload the location to your Neocom.
145021:
Hello, {[character]player.name}. At the moment, all you have to fly is a capsule. Our first priority is to get you into a starship.

Your assignment: Follow the tutorial steps, I will guide you to a hidden location in space.

If you ever get lost, remember to use the back and next buttons and read the tutorial slides or you can quit the mission and start over again from the beginning.

Next up is a kind of interdiction called warp disruption. When activated on another targeted ship, these kinds of modules "tackle" it, disabling its warp drive.

Tackling only works if you maintain close distance - don't let the target slip outside your warp disruptor's range - and have sufficient strength to overpower its warp core. To successfully lock down a ship, the total number of warp disruptors attempting to tackle it must outnumber the Warp Core Stabilizers it has online.

I'll give you a Civilian Warp Disruptor to test out on a pirate that escaped from the headquarters you just blew up. Pin him down, but don't blow him up.

145158:
I'm not going to beat around the bush with you on this one, as there isn't any time. We have a developing emergency in {[location]objectiveLocationSystemID.name}. Several of our commercial convoys have been ripped to shreds in the last few months by an extremely dangerous band of terrorists. As you can see from these camera drone recordings, they have even been willing to fly their ships directly into our freighters and other unarmed haulers. And yes, before you ask, we have been escorting these convoys with heavily armed security vessels, though to little effect.

As these terrorists are obviously willing to die for their cause, they aren't bothering to attack our warships. They simply seem to appear out of nowhere, accelerate to high speeds and slam into the cargo ships. Depending on the cargo, this action can, at best, tear open the cargo bays and release the contents into the vacuum of space, or, at worst, strike a shipment of fuels or ammunition, and destroy the freighter in one huge explosion. One such explosion destroyed an entire convoy.

However, an ultra-secure communications intercept satellite recently picked up a communication that we believe indicates the terrorists are now considering turning their deadly tactic against some unidentified stations in the region. Given our huge civilian population on these stations, the decision has been made to conduct a partial evacuation of all potential target stations.

What we need from you is your help in getting these civilians – mostly the spouses and children of station personnel – to a station that is further away from the terrorists' known area of operation. Normally, I would not ask this of a capsuleer, but I am begging you: will you help us evacuate these people until this threat has passed? We need to know right now, as we have already begun to organize the evacuation fleet; can we count you in?

145160:
An infestation of nasty, biting roaches has taken hold on {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name}, and it is growing out of control. In fact, it's gotten so bad that they've considered venting the emergency airlocks briefly and allowing the station atmosphere to empty into space, but scientists tell us the little bastards can survive even in space for hours.

The only answer is to gas the entire station. The substance they want to use is a special concoction designed specifically to grant this particular species of roach a quick death. I have a shipment of the stuff; I just need you to get it there. This stuff is more dangerous than the cockroaches.

Note the hasty delivery required — you don't have much time to complete this mission.

145162: Goddamnit, what is Irichi doing? That bastard is losing his mind. He hasn't been the same since he lost his legs, and he blames me for that. Well, I guess he should. I was the one who tortured him when I was working for the Federation. But we're Guristas now, and we pirates have to stick together, right? It's the pirate's code. That, and “every pirate for herself."
145163:
Religious freaks like to spread all sorts of apocalyptic messages, and in recent times there are few who have captured the imagination of conspiracy theorists in the way that Tolmak has. The so-called “Prophet of the Seventh Sphere,” Tolmak is an enigmatic and elusive character. He has never shown himself publicly for fear of reprisal, and relies instead of proxies to spread his word. Others say his real strength comes from the media outlets that cover these preachers. Outlets that, for their own part, are mostly concerned with the profit to be made from the inevitable controversy his message brings.

Among other things, Tolmak's elaborate revelations paint a universe governed by demonic forces that secretly control the heads of all the empires. He reserves special bile for the capsuleer class, teaching that their clones are not actually the same person reborn, but are instead, demonic simulacra.
145165:
So good to see you, {[character]player.name}. I've been on a pretty tight schedule for the past two weeks, ever since we discovered the strange, and increasing, Serpentis activity in the system. Our CEO demands an explanation, yet we still don't know enough about the situation to determine what's really going on. And that's where you come in.

Serpentis activity on this scale in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} is unheard of, and quite frankly we aren't well enough prepared at the moment to deal with any major conflict with them. Not only that, but those greedy pirates are insatiable, and news of their appearance around here has sent the trade lanes into a state of panic. People are leaving this station already, making my superiors ... less than content if you know what I mean. We're losing good people because of this unacceptable situation and we need to put an end to it.

The first thing I want you to do is undertake a reconnaisance mission for us into an area where we have witnessed most of the Serpentis activity. We've already lost a few patrols that ventured into this area, so be careful. If you do find any Serpentis ships out there, eliminate them. We don't want any prisoners, interrogating these deviants won't do us any good. Report your findings to me a.s.a.p.

145168: You showed some class out there, {[character]player.name}.  Take your pay and report for your next assignment.
145169: Because of your successful reconnaissance mission, we've managed to narrow down the location of the main Serpentis activity a bit.  The data that we extracted from your system scanner also revealed to us a few Serpentis ships that were not mentioned in your preliminary report.  It appears to be some sort of convoy, at least one of their ships was clearly an industrial.  Because of this we guess that it may be a routine shipment, meaning that they might get a convoy at regular intervals.  We'd like you to fly out there, preferably with a cloaking device, and lay in wait for any possible sign of another Serpentis convoy.  If you do see one, destroy it and bring back the contents of the industrials to me for inspection.

145171: Construction blocks?  I was afraid of that.  This doesn't seem to be a mere smuggling operation, but something much more sinister.  But we still don't know what they are building ... And don't you leave just yet, I have another assignment waiting for you!
145172:
Now that we've established the general location of the Serpentis activity within {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, it's actually time to find out exactly what they are building. In your last mission you destroyed one of their construction block transports, but this brings us no closer to finding their base of operations. We've had no luck interrogating these pirates before, and the surveillance teams we have sent to investigate the area have either found nothing or disappeared. This leaves us with very few options. But after brainstorming possible solutions to our problem, I came up with a devious plan.

We have in our possession so called 'spy drones', straight from our science labs, which attach themselves to a nearby ships hull and emits a low frequency signal which is picked up by one of our beacons which are strewn around {[location]agentSolarSystemID.name}, which in turn sends a high frequency signal to our control tower in {[location]agentStationID.name}.

Now we know that an agent of the Serpentis Corporation regularly picks up shipments of Ectoplasm at a certain station near here. If we can place the spy drone into his next shipment, this might allow us to track his ship to its destination.

Our men have placed beacons throughout our constellation, so everything is in place. All you need to do is take these crates filled with ectoplasm, and our spy drones, to the station specified in your journal, our agents there will take care of the rest. With luck we'll soon know the location of the Serpentis base.

145175:
After reviewing the intel we received from the spy drones which you transferred for us in your last mission, we managed to pinpoint the location of a military outpost they are building in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name}. It appears to be a part of a defensive perimeter that they are setting up around their territory, which has elevated our fears that they have actually managed to erect a large colony inside our solarsystem.

But for now let's keep our sights on the current task, to breach a hole in their defensive wall. We believe that the outpost in question hasn't been fully built, and therefore will be a fairly easy target for you if it's defensive installations aren't complete. Contact with the spy drones was cut off before we could fully analyze the Serpentis forces in the area. But one thing's for sure, there will most certainly be guards nearby, and they will have to be dealt with. You will receive a bookmark to the location of the outpost, and your instructions are simple, destroy the habitat of their construction workers. That should slow them down a bit. Good luck.

145178: Somebody broke into my brother's home yesterday and stole his entire gun collection. He'll get into heaps of trouble with his superiors if they find out, so I want you to help him make the problem go away. Fly over to {[location]objectiveDestinationID.name} and drop off a new set of weapons. I'll modify the ID codes on the guns, and nobody will suspect a thing.
145179: Travel to the designated system and retrieve the reports from the thief.
145180: Small, independent trade hubs throughout New Eden are sometimes referred to by a most peculiar and archaic term: “Roadhouses.” Though no one quite remembers why they're called that, it's common knowledge that roadhouses are ideal locations for moving stolen goods, making underworld contacts, or getting hurt. Needless to say, these establishments are frequented by unscrupulous roughnecks for whom pain doesn't hurt.
145182: Thank you for this. You have no idea how much this means to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}.
145183: It was just as we all suspected. Please accept our thanks and all the rewards that come from loyal service to {[npcOrganization]agentCorpID.name}. Keep this up and you‘ll have more LUX than you know what to do with – I promise you that.
145184: It's alright. I'll find another capsuleer willing to bathe in all this LUX I have to offer.
145185: I should have listened to my superiors and taken care of this internally instead of thinking for a second that a capsuleer would be willing to help.
145186: Have you found that worthless bastard yet?

This incident comes at a very bad time. Political relations between our governments are extremely volatile at the moment, and there are rumors of war floating around everywhere. So I have explicit orders to tell you to keep this quiet. With your record I know I can trust you, don't speak of this to anyone. Just find the missing reporters, destroy their captors, return them to me and keep your mouth shut.

The first group of Gallente civilians went missing in {[location]dungeonLocationID.name} reporting on a story involving a group of Caldari Smugglers, who were said to have been smuggling armed terrorists to our stations in {[location]agentConstellationID.name}, to cause mayhem no doubt. I'll give you the coordinates to their last known position. Find them and bring them back, dead or alive. Their families must be informed of their fate, or they will never be at peace. If you find any hostiles at the scene, feel free to use deadly force.

234559: "The State had lost its way. The corporations forgot the principles upon which they were founded. The people suffered. The State suffered. We were an embarrassment. Our forefathers turned in their graves at the depths to which our leaders had allowed our State to fall. No more. We are strong once again. We are Caldari once again. We are the State once again, and our homeland is ours at last. We are at war. The State calls out to you, the capsuleer, for we need your strength and your leadership to fend off the encroaching Gallente menace. They seek to bring us to heel. The State! The State bends for no one and no thing. The State stands strong, The State will not fall. Join us. Fight. Win."
234560: "Millions of souls cry out for emancipation, begging to be freed from a life where they are treated no better than captive animals. The Minmatar heart sings for freedom and the Minmatar soul strives for open skies, but the Minmatar heart withers away in captivity. It is now up to you, the capsuleer. You hold the power to free our people. You are the heroes of your generation. It is finally time to make the Amarr pay for their atrocities. We will find those who called themselves "masters", and we will bring them to their knees! Look to your heart, look to our people. Join us! Death to Amarr!"
234561: "The Amarr Empire used to shine as a beacon to humanity of what it meant to be civilized: To be strong, and to lead by example. Through God's words we spread civilization throughout the stars and it is by our leadership that New Eden achieved its wings. It is up to you to carry this example, the lessons of God's chosen, and reinstate the Empire of Amarr to its former and rightful glory. We need you to reclaim the Minmatar from the drudge, chaos and inhumanity in which they currently dwell, and into God's light. We are their angels. We must be their saviors. By your power they shall be rescued from the dark. God wills it, and so it shall be."
234562: "The Federation is the standard, indeed the only example, of equality, justice, freedom and sanity in today's universe. While the rest of the Empires seek to expand in willful acts of destruction, the Federation seeks to protect its people and its borders from the deprivations of the Caldari who have shown unprovoked aggression against us. We attempted to be civilized, to talk, to travel the road of peace, but they refused. The Federation has awoken to the threat, and now its strength shall be tried. We wanted peace, and now we are faced with war. We are the Federation. We shall not stumble, we shall not falter. We shall stand victorious on the field of battle, a testament to the values of liberty and justice. The people of the Federation need you. With your strength and your conviction we shall endure."

The weekly cost is {[numeric]cost.isk} and the attacking organization will receive a bill which needs to be paid promptly to maintain the war. If the bill is not paid before it is due then the war will be cancelled.

Both sides in a war must control at least one structure in space in order to be war eligible. If either side loses their last structure, they lose their war eligibility and the war is cancelled.
The attacking side of a war must designate one highsec Upwell structure that they control as the War HQ for the conflict. If the War HQ is destroyed or removed from space the war will be cancelled.

When an active war has been cancelled, there is a 24 hour cooldown period during which fighting can legally continue.

If you are at war with a corporation that joins an alliance then the war will change from being against the corporation to being against the alliance.

If you are at war with an alliance and a corporation leaves that alliance then you will still be at war with the alliance and a new war will be created with the corporation that left. This new war is subject to its own bills and all the normal war eligibility requirements.

"I will not hesitate when the test of Faith finds me, for only the strongest conviction will open the gates of paradise. My Faith in you is absolute; my sword is Yours, My God, and Your will guides me now and for all eternity."
- The Scriptures, The Prophet Kuria, "Paladin's Creed"
236991:
Templar Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Paladin Crusader and immediately below Cardinal Lieutenant.

"War is not hell, far from it. War is beautiful. War is divine."
- Grand Admiral Mekioth Sarum, excerpt from a commencement speech to Paladin graduates of the Imperial Academy. CE 23215
236992:
Cardinal Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Templar Lieutenant and immediately below Arch Lieutenant.

"Surround yourself with the faithful, stand together, for there is no strength like it under the heavens."
- The Scriptures, Book of Missions, 71:21
236993:
Arch Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Cardinal Lieutenant and immediately below Imperial Major.

"The word of the Lord is pure,
It is a shield for the faithful,
Brought unto men by the Angels,
As a guiding light in the darkness "
- The Scriptures, Book of the Prophet Anoyia, 8:15
236994:
Imperial Major is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Arch Lieutenant and immediately below Marshal Commander.

"God's compassion is all encompassing; His vengeance, all consuming."
- Grand Admiral Sundara The Kor-Azor charge. YC 110.6.10
236995:
Marshal Commander is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Imperial Major and immediately below Imperator Commander.

"And the Lord spoke to him from the heavens,
Described to him his holy purpose,
Bestowed upon him the wisdom,
Of God's holy embrace."

- The Scriptures, Gheinok the First, 2:8
236996:
Imperator Commander is a commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Marshal Commander and immediately below Tribunus Colonel.

"To know the true path, but yet, to never follow it. That is possibly the gravest sin"
- The Scriptures, Book of Missions, 13:21
236997:
Tribunus Colonel is a senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Imperator Commander and immediately below Legatus Commodore.

"Assign turrets one through seven, radio crystals, designate target Omega-One!"
"Target Omega-One locked!"
"For the Emperor"
"Fire!"

- Opening salvo of the Battle of Vak'Aioth
236998:
Legatus Commodore is a senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Tribunus Colonel and immediately below Divine Commodore.

"By His light, and His will"
- The Scriptures, Gheinok the First, 12:32
236999:
Divine Commodore is the most senior commissioned rank in the 24th Imperial Crusade. It ranks above Legatus Commodore.

"Run and you shall be crushed.
Stand and you shall fall.
Kneel and you shall be saved."
- Emperor Arrach Sarum. CE 21423
237000:
Nation Warrior is the lowest commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks immediately below Spike Lieutenant.

"Though free I am bound by the chains of my brothers"
- Inscription from a stone in the Remembering
237001:
Spike Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Nation Warrior and immediately below Spear Lieutenant.

"At this exact junction in history we have within our grasp the means to loosen our tormentors' hold and win freedom for our kin. Opportunities are there to be taken.
Brothers, we must rise."
- Malaetu Shakor, Republic Parliament Head Speaking before the Tribal Council November 27th. YC 107
237002:
Spear Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Spike Lieutenant and immediately below Venge Captain.

"The initial volleys neutralized sixty-eight separate defense batteries while removing a mere ninety-eight thousand Minmatar from the viable worker stock. Praise unto God."
- Intercepted Amarr Navy transmission during orbital bombardment of "Eanna", Planet VI, The Hror System
237003:
Venge Captain is a junior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Spear Lieutenant and immediately below Lance Commander.

"The holder stood atop his tower and preached salvation to the baying horde of slaves below. In answer, Korgoth raised his fist and let out a roar of defiance. The throats of a thousand Minmatar joined him, tearing through the air in a wave of pure hatred."
- Battle of Ariti, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives
237004:
Lance Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Venge Captain and immediately below Blade Commander.

"Their military handbook regulated the guarding of gates, chokepoints, treelines and skies. it neglected, however, to mention sewers."
- Commander Skioth, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives
237005:
Blade Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Lance Commander and immediately below Talon Commander.

"Our people assaulted the ship en masse. Those with weapons fired at it, those without hurled whatever was at hand even though they knew such acts to be futile. This is how the last of the Amarrian ships fled our world"
- Unknown Author, "Tales of the Rebellion", Minmatar Archives
237006:
Talon Commander is a commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Blade Commander and immediately below Voshud Major.

"There were once men who stood strong against the Amarrians no matter what they threw at them. They never knelt before them, they never called them masters. These men were called the Defiants. We will carry their name into the heart of Amarr and make them tremble at the sound of it. We will stand victorious or we will die with our hands around the slavers throats."
- Karishal Muritor addressing his fleet before the strike on the Imperial Shipyards of Beloth Tor
237007:
Voshud Major is a senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Talon Commander and immediately below Matar Colonel.

"The Matari spirit is an indomitable fire. Be sure when fanning those flames that you do not burn this world of ours down. Seeds cannot grow in a soil of ash."
- "The Elder's Tome", Matari Chronicles
237008:
Matar Colonel is a senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Voshud Major and immediately below Valklear General.

"War is within our hearts. It is a raging beast which we must harness lest it consume us"
- "Teachings of Valla."
237009:
Valklear General is the most senior commissioned rank in the Tribal Liberation Force. It ranks above Matar Colonel.

"We have struggled through pain and grief; we have faced our torments with unbowed heads; we have lived as men. And in the end, what counts is not the years in our lives, but the unyielding life in our years."
- Inscription from a stone in the Remembering
237010:
Protectorate Ensign is the lowest commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks immediately below Second Lieutenant.

"Slowly but surely we are betraying the legacy left to us, the children of the Raata. The light of the Caldari spirit grows ever darker under the encroaching shadow of our would-be masters. Our very identity as a people is being subsumed by the Federation and we must act to preserve it."
- Excerpt from a National Address, delivered by Kalaakiota CEO Matias Sobaseki. CE 23154.6.26
237011:
Second Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Protectorate Ensign and immediately below First Lieutenant.

"It is rather strange that the good of the many seems to constantly coincide with whatever policies weaken the Caldari, the Intaki, and the Mannar and keep them under the heel of the Gallente."
- Caldari Senator Kiriusu Otenga, Senate session 23154/T3782. CE 23154.11.21
237012:
First Lieutenant is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Second Lieutenant and immediately below Captain.

"We will not permit you to tell us how to be Caldari, and so you leave us with no choice"
- Excerpt from the Caldari Proclamation of Secession. CE 23154.11.22
237013:
Captain is a junior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above First Lieutenant and immediately below Major.

"We survived on this world for thousands of years without the Gallente. Do they think we will starve now?"
- Wiyrkomi CEO Taaiko Wiyrkomi, Response to the Gallente blockade of Caldari Prime. CE 23154.11.30
237014:
Major is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Captain and immediately below Lieutenant Colonel.

"They will retaliate. We must be prepared."
– Vice-Admiral Orlan Mito, Caldari Navy, Morning after the Nouvelle Rouvenor attack. CE 23155.1.14
237015:
Lieutenant Colonel is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Major and immediately below Colonel.

"Caldari Prime burns, those left behind are choking on the dust and ash that fills the air, and you demand our surrender? Is this a joke? You have only hardened our resolve. Every drop of blood you have taken from us will be repaid -- with interest."
- CEP response to Federation demands for unconditional surrender after initial bombardment of Caldari Prime. CE 23155.1.18
237016:
Colonel is a commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Lieutenant Colonel and immediately below Wing Commander.

"As we make the tea, you must take it. The Caldari way demands it."
- Matias Sobaseki, CEO of Kaalakiota, Morning of Reasoning. CE 23155.2.10
237017:
Wing Commander is a senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Colonel and immediately below Strike Commander.

"Their fleet is in total control of Caldari Prime's Orbit. We're heavily outnumbered and outgunned. To be able to effectively evacuate the population we need exactly one month of complete orbital control. Ideas anyone?"
- Admiral Orlan Mito, Caldari High Command Session. CE 23155.2.21
237018:
Strike Commander is a senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Wing Commander and immediately below Brigadier General.

"High command need more time to complete the evacuation. We shall provide."
- Admiral Yakiya Tovil-Toba's personal log entry #21A231. CE 23155.3.7
237019:
Brigadier General is the most senior commissioned rank in the State Protectorate. It ranks above Strike Commander.

"Non-essential personnel, abandon ship."
- Admiral Yakiya Tovil-Toba's last command. CE 23155.3.15

PLEX - Pilot License Extension PLEX is a commodity that can be stored, transported and traded on the market or through contracts. It can be used to add Clone State Omega time to your account or to unlock special character and account services. Passes and access to select events, in game and out, can also be purchased with PLEX. Account time: One PLEX is equal to 30 days of Clone State Omega time which can be added to your account by using the PLEX directly from your in-game inventory. Multiple character training: Activate 30 days of passive skill gain on additional characters on your account with PLEX. Character transfer: Transferring characters between two accounts can be paid for with PLEX. Character re-sculpt: Customize and recreate your character’s facial appearance. Convert to AURUM: PLEX can be exchanged for AURUM, the currency used in the Noble Exchange store where unique fashion accessories are sold.
Buying PLEX You can buy PLEX on the EVE market using LUX or securely on eveonline.com using conventional payment methods.

This is the information hub for the war effort. In this panel you can enlist yourself or your corporation, and once enlisted access data and statistics about the war effort.

Individuals may enlist by leaving any current player corporations, ensuring their standing from this faction is above 0.5 and that they're not on a trial account; applications are processed immediately.

Directors and CEOs may enlist their entire corporation by leaving any current alliance and ensuring their corporate standing from this faction is above 0.5; applications are processed at downtime.

All enlisted players are in a state of permanent war with their enemies and may be attacked by enemy capsuleers at any time. They are also advised to avoid high security space (0.5 security and above) belonging to enemy factions, as those factions' navies will shoot on sight.

Enlisted players are empowered to take missions from agents in their Militia, and to assist in the capture of strategic locations. Missions are limited by ship type. Locations are exploration sites found using the onboard scanner, are limited by ship type and have proximity sensors on strategic capture sites that trigger a capturing timer.

For further information on all aspects of the war, please visit the knowledge base!

259046: The modern Caldari State was forged in war, a fact that shapes its society a great deal. They are determined and military minded, living their lives like they were at a constant brink of armed conflict. The result is a weird combination of aggressiveness and paranoia. The Caldari are widely regarded as fearsome fighters, be it in space or on the ground, and their high quality military hardware is much admired and imitated by the other empires, bar only the Jovians. The Caldari excel in missile manufacturing and very maneuverable and fast ships.
259047: The Minmatar society is a tribal one, although the widely different status of the race today has blurred this in the minds of some of them. Yet the tribal culture is very strong with most of them and they have managed to retain their customs remarkably well. So much so in fact that a Minmatar of any given tribe can travel the width of the world, visiting fellow tribesmen and always feel at home, whether he visits a wealthy merchant within the Gallente Federation, an unscrupulous pirate in the outer regions or even a slave within the Amarr Empire. The Minmatars are the most populous of the races, but also the most politically fragmented. Only a quarter of them reside in their official empire, the Minmatar Republic.
